(`Queries::productCoverage`): the items (`ix_sku_merged_into`); the matched variants grouped by item and then by their set of stores (one
pass over the index `channel_listing (sku_id, channel_id)`; the set is a number with one bit per store, or a list of ids beyond 62
stores); the items with a suggestion waiting (the index `match_proposal (status, proposed_sku_id, listing_id, band)`). They also give a
list's total, so a list without a text is never counted. (2) The page's 50 ids, in id order from `ix_sku_merged_into` (its entries end
with the id), then their rows by id. "On every store" is one EXISTS per store (the optimizer starts from the store with the fewest
variants); "Missing on <store>" is an anti-join on `(sku_id, channel_id)`, item by item, with the index named in a hint (without it MySQL
first read every listing row of the store: 107-137 ms against 2-53 ms); a search and "With a suggestion waiting" read all their ids in
one pass (they are few), which also counts them. (3) Three reads for the cells of those 50 (`productCells`): the variants matched to them
(`channel_listing.sku_id IN (…)`, with their names and the year's units from the profiles: the item's "Product: …" line comes from this
read, no query and no index was added for it), the open suggestions that propose them, the decisions waiting for them.
`0024_by_product.sql` adds the two indexes these reads need to stay off wide rows: `channel_listing (sku_id, channel_id)` in place of
`(sku_id)` (it serves the foreign key too), and `match_proposal (status, proposed_sku_id, listing_id, band)`. Both are named in optimizer
hints, which are ignored while an index is not there, so the code may run a moment before the migration (slower, not wrong). Measured on
the slot's test schema filled like staging (10 Oct 2026: the small cluster, MySQL 8.4, a 32 MB buffer pool; 15,000 items, 38,040
variants with profiles, 2,638 open suggestions; the `EXPLAIN` of every statement is in `/root/cw_work/runs/prodmap_explain_1010.txt`, and
of the second round in `/root/cw_work/runs/prodmap_explain2_1010.txt`): the counts 60-80 ms together (8 + 30 + 25); a page of All 5 ms
and 3 ms for its rows; the cells 9-17 ms; On every store 3 ms; Missing on a store 2 ms on page 1 when most items are missing, 45-53 ms
on the last page or when few are;
With a suggestion waiting 22 ms; a search by words 80 ms (it reads every item row), by CW number 1-2 ms, by barcode 3 ms; coming back
from a decision adds one read of 15-38 ms. The CSV of the whole catalogue: its ids in 18 ms, then 26-44 ms for each 500 items,
the `product` column's join of the matched variants' profiles included (that read: 9 ms for the 566 matched variants of a slice; a
slice took about 30 ms before it, so it costs little here, and more on the real, wider profiles). The picker: its suggestions
2 ms, its rows 3 ms, its search 60 ms without words and about 105 ms with words on a store of 9,000 variants. That search reads the
profiles of the store's waiting variants, as Store Products' search does; the real profiles are about four times as wide as the test's,
so expect several times that on staging. That is why a plain opening of the picker does not run it when there is something suggested to
show (U118; found in review: it ran on every opening). If it still proves too slow, a full-text index on the variants' names is the next
step (not built: U121).

**U118. The picker** (`/ui/review/products/{id}/map?channel=<store code>`: a plain page, links and one GET form, no script needed), titled
"Match <CW number> on <store>". On top the item's facts: name, CW number, brand, range, flavour, strength, size, barcodes, and what the
store has for it now. Then "Suggested for this item": the store's variants whose open suggestion proposes it, the strongest first. Then
"Other variants of <store> still waiting for a match" (not matched, not ignored, no decision waiting): a search of the fields Store
Products searches (name, option name, brand; the option number; a barcode), word by word as the Find page does, best sellers first, 20 a
page with Previous / Next and no count (the store's waiting variants are read once, not twice). The box is filled in from the item's own
words (its brand and flavour when its details have them, else the first words of its name; a strength or a size is left out, since each
website writes "20mg" its own way). **When that search runs:** on a plain opening (no `q` in the request) only when there is NO suggested
row to show; when there are suggestions they are shown, the box is filled in with its Search button, and one line says "The suggestions
are above. Press Search to look for other variants with these words." A search the person sent always runs: also an emptied one (every
waiting variant of the store), and one with no usable word finds nothing (as U116). Previous and Next always name the search they page
through, an emptied one too (`…&q=&page=2`): the first version built them from the values alone, an empty value is left out of a link, and
page 2 of "every waiting variant" fell back to the first search and showed another list (found in review). Each row: the variant's
product name and, under it, its own option name; its brand and option number; its state (or the strength of its suggestion for this
item); "Same barcode / Different barcode / No barcode to compare" (GTIN keys, as the comparison table); the price; the units sold in 30
days and a year; and ONE action, Choose. An item that does not exist (404), one that was joined into another (404, with the way to that
one) and a store code that names no store (404) are answered in words.

**U119. "Came from By Item", and back.** `Ui\ByProductContext` (QueueContext's sibling): the fixed token `via=product`, the item's number
(`product`), the store's code (`channel`; it must name a store), the list's own filter and search (`cov`, `lq`; each must be one of the
page's values) and, when the person had them, the picker's own search and page: `pq` (trimmed and cut to the search box's 100
characters; an emptied search travels as one space, because a link and a form leave an empty value out and "no `pq`" means "the picker's
first search") and `pp` (a number above 1). It travels as the variant page's `$qq`: its links, its "pick a different product" search and
its answer forms; only people who may decide get it. On that page "Back" and "leave it and go back" are the picker AS THE PERSON LEFT IT
(`pickerUrl()`: their search, also an emptied one, and their page; the first version always opened the picker's first search on page 1:
found in review). After the decision (`ReviewController::decide`) the person is sent to By Item (`listUrl()`), to the list as they left
it and `at=<item>`: the page of the list that holds the item, its row tinted with "You came back from this item." (when the filter no
longer holds it, because it is matched now, it is shown once, first, and says so), under the EXISTING notice in words: matched to CW-…,
saved but waiting for a matching lead's second OK, or marked "not this product". `pq` and `pp` are NOT part of that address: after a
decision the person is on the list, not in the picker. A refused answer stays on the variant's page with its words and the form, as
before, and keeps the whole context. Every address is built from those values and nothing else (never a return address from the
request: no open redirect; a crafted `pq` is only ever a query value of the picker, a crafted `pp` no page); an incomplete context is no
context (the page's own redirect, as before). A list (`queue=`) and a spot check (`sample=`) come first, so "next in the list" is
unchanged.

**U120. A small link.** The item page's "Website products matched to it" has "See where it is matched": By Item narrowed to that item,
for people with `linking.view`. Store Products is unchanged.

**U121. Words, look, and what was left out.** Words: `MENU`, `MENU_HELP` and `PAGE_INTRO` `by_product` (and `by_product_map`), the groups
`BY_PRODUCT` and `PRODUCT_STORE` with its tones, `ERROR` `unknown_store` and `item_joined`, `ITEM` `coverage_link`. Look: a board with one
cell per store, cards on a phone with each cell labelled by its store; section 22 of app.css; no new JavaScript. Left out: (1) a
best-seller order and sort options: an item's sales are its variants' units, a sort over every profile, so the list is by CW number;
(2) matching from the list itself, or several items at once: a match is one decision on its page, and the bulk confirm of suggestions
stays on Mapping (M46); (3) undoing a match from here: it stays on the variant's page (M53); (4) variants with the item's barcode offered
in the picker before any search (the barcode can be searched, and each row says whether it is the same); (5) counts narrowed by the
search; (6) a row for an item that was joined into another one (its own page says where it went); (7) a full-text index for the picker's
word search (U117): it reads the profiles of the store's waiting variants, as Store Products' search does; (8) grouping the list by
parent product (one heading per product with its items under it): the parent is known only for matched items and differs from store to
store, so it is a line under the item, not a level of the list.

**U122. The owner's words: items and variants (binding for this screen).** The owner, 10 Oct 2026, on seeing "By Product": "actually we
need variant mapping not product ... each variant we have treating item". So, on this screen and its picker:
- a **variant** is a store's sellable option (one flavour, one strength, one pack size): a `channel_listing` row, what the other matching
  screens call a website product;
- an **item** is the warehouse record a variant is matched to: a `sku` row, what the other screens call a warehouse product;
- a **product** is only the parent page that holds many variants (`listing_profile.product_title`).
What a person reads: the tab "By Item"; the intro "Every warehouse item and the variant it is matched to on each store."; the first
column "Item"; the cells "Matched <variant name>", "+1 more variant" / "+N more variants", "Suggested <variant name>", "Not on this
store"; "Stores matched: 2 of 3"; the button "Match…"; the picker "Match <CW number> on <store>" with "Suggested for this item", "Other
variants of <store> still waiting for a match", the column "Variant" (the product's name with the option's name under it) and "Choose";
the item page's link "See where it is matched". **The parent product** under an item ("Product: <name>") is the product name of the
item's matched variant that sold most in a year, on any store (the same number twice: the lowest listing id); it is left out when no
variant is matched, when that name is empty, and when it only repeats the item's own name. It is read in the cells' matched read (U117)
and is the CSV's column `product`. **Scope:** this screen and its picker only. The other screens keep their words (Mapping, Store
Products, the variant's own page with "Yes, same product: match to CW-…", the shared note "1 sale = N products"): they are pinned by
their own tests and were not what the owner spoke about; a person goes from "variant" here to "website product" on that page, which the
crumb "By Item: <store>" bridges. The paths, route names, keys and the context's fields are not renamed (`/ui/review/products`,
`by_product`, `BY_PRODUCT`, `PRODUCT_STORE`, `via=product`, `product=`): bookmarks and the pinned route lists stay, and only words
changed. `WordsTest::testByItemSpeaksOfItemsAndVariantsAsTheOwnerDoes` pins the naming (no "website product", "warehouse product" or
"By Product" in this screen's words; "product" only in "Product: …").

## Products › By Item: more rows, and a bulk action with a preview (slot `bybulk`, 10 Oct 2026)

The owner's request of 10 Oct 2026, on seeing By Item: "by item here bulk preview and update option easy table need more item want to
handle based on selection also all here possible options need". That is: on By Item, tick many items, choose what to do, SEE exactly what
will happen, then apply it; show more rows at once; offer every action that makes sense there. Code: `migrations/0025_by_item_bulk.sql`,
`src/Mapping/BulkDecisions.php` (the list context `item`, `preview()`, `checked()`, `itemChecks()`, `confirmScope()`, `rejectedBefore()`,
`predict()`), `src/Settings.php` (one rule), `src/Ui/Controller/ByItemBulkController.php` (new), `src/Ui/Controller/{ByProduct,Bulk}
Controller.php`, `src/Ui/{ByProductContext,Queries,Kernel,Sections,Words}.php`, views `by_item_preview` (new), `by_product`,
`by_product_map`, `bulk_bar`, `bulk_result`, `public/ui/assets/app.css` (section 22) and `app.js` (one rule: a box marked
`data-bulk-manual` is left out of "select all", U124). Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/ByItemBulkTest.php` (new),
`tests/Integration/Mapping/BulkDecisionsTest.php` (four new tests), `BulkScreensTest`, `ByProductScreenTest`, `ByProductContextTest`,
the pinned routes, sections, templates and words (`UiUnitTest`, `SectionsTest`, `UiTemplatesTest`, `WordsTest`), and the HTTP tests
`UiSecurityTest` and `UiReviewFlowTest` (slot `ui`). `DecisionService` is not touched: it is still the only thing that changes a
match. This amends M54 ("three GET routes, no POST": By Item now has two POST routes, see M55) and U121's left-out point (2)
("several items at once"). A second round the same day (a review of the first commit, and the reviewer's ruling on what a confirm may
take) changed M55's scope into M59, fixed three defects (the notes below say where) and renumbered the migration to 0025.

**M55. The bulk action of By Item acts on the suggested variants of the ticked items, through the existing bulk decisions.** A person
who may decide (`mapping.decide`: a matcher or a matching lead, as on the lists, M49) ticks items, chooses "On: All stores · <each
store>" and presses one of three actions, which are `BulkDecisions`' existing ones for each variant: **Confirm suggested matches**
(`link`: each suggested variant to THIS item, with the units per sale its suggestion says), **Not a match…** (`reject`) and **Send back for
matching…** (`send_back`). The rows of a request are every open suggestion that proposes a ticked item on the chosen store(s): the
"Suggested" cells, and the variants a matched or waiting cell counts as "Also suggested"; "Not a match…" and "Send back for matching…"
act on all of them, and a confirm leaves the doubtful ones to a person (M59; the first version confirmed every one of them). A variant
has one open suggestion, so it is suggested for one item only and no variant is counted twice (the form refuses one named under two
items). `BulkDecisions` gains the list context `item` (`SOURCES`, `ITEM_ACTIONS`; `mapping_batch.source` gains `item`, 0025). A list of
Mapping has one strength; By Item has
all of them at once, so nothing is refused for the list's strength and each row's own strength is checked as it is done: a confirm skips
a strength that `mapping.bulk_confirm_bands` leaves out (`band_not_allowed`, the existing check of every confirmed row), and Clues disagree
is skipped for a matcher (`lead_only`: DecisionService refuses it, as one at a time). Every other rule and skip of M50-M52 applies
unchanged: holds, spot checks, vetoes, flags, a failed spot check's population, a bulk link undone before, the two-person rules, the
bulk switch, listing id order, one transaction a row. **`mapping.bulk_max_rows` counts decisions, that is variants, not items**: one item
with three suggested variants is three rows, and more rows than the setting allows are refused whole, in words, by the preview and again
by the apply (422, nothing written). **Nothing is done to a Matched cell in bulk:** undoing a match stays one at a time, on the variant's
page, with a note (M53); the page says so in one line under the bar. Not offered either: Ignore (it says a variant is no real product: a
store's matter, on Store Products), Create as new item (the variant would become another item, not this one), and approving the
decisions that wait for a second OK (each is another person's look at one match).

**M56. The preview is the same checks, made read-only.** `BulkDecisions::preview()` takes what `run()` takes and returns, for every row,
what `run()` would do: done, waits for a second OK (with the reasons), or skipped (with the code and its detail). It is built from the
same code, not from a copy of it: (1) `checked()`, the checks of the whole request, MOVED out of `run()` unchanged (the list and its
action, a person who may decide, the strength rule of a list, the note, at least one row and at most the setting's): both paths call
it, so a preview is refused whole exactly when the apply would be, with the same codes; (2) `prechecks()`, as it was (it only ever
read); (3) for By Item, `itemChecks()` (M58, M59); (4) `predict()` (M57). `checked()` also refuses, for every list, a row that names a
number no variant, suggestion or version can be (a variant number or a version above 4,294,967,295, the largest an INT UNSIGNED column
holds, or below its smallest): 400 `bad_request`, nothing written. Such a row used to pass as an ordinary skip ("no such variant",
"changed") and failed only when that skip was recorded: a 500 in the middle of the batch, with the rows before it decided, the rest
never run and no audit row (found in review; the lists' own route `/ui/review/bulk` had the same gap and is closed by the same check).
`ByItemBulkController` refuses the same numbers itself (400 in the form's words), so a preview can never show such a row. `run()` then differs only by what it always did after the checks:
the batch row, the decisions, the batch rows, the audit row. **The preview writes nothing**: no batch, no batch row, no audit row, no
lock, no transaction. `ByItemBulkTest` and `BulkDecisionsTest` prove it on every table of the schema: the row count, the checksum of the
content and the next auto-increment id of each are the same before and after (a write that was rolled back would still have used an
id); only `staff_session` is left out of the screen's check (a signed-in request stamps its own session).

**M57. What the preview says of DecisionService (`predict()`), and how it is kept true.** The pre-checks do not know what
DecisionService will answer for a row they let through, and a dry run of `decide()` would write (and lock, and use up ids). So
`predict()` reads what `decide()` reads for a variant that waits for a match and applies its rules in its order: Clues disagree for a
person who is no matching lead is refused (`lead_only`); a confirm or a "not a match" of an item that is not there (`no_product`), a
confirm of an item joined into another (`product_joined`), units per sale above `DecisionService::MAX_UNITS` (`refused`); a confirm waits
for a second matching lead when the item is protected (`protected_sku`), when 1 sale is not 1 item while `approvals.match_multiple` is on
(`units_per_item`), when the pair was marked wrong before (`previously_rejected`: the item or one joined into it, `rejectedBefore()`,
the same answer as `DecisionService::rejectedAs`; a confirm from By Item has skipped such a row by then, M59, so this reason is seen
in a preview of the lists only), and while `approvals.mapping_bulk_second_ok` is on (`bulk`). These are a second statement of rules that
live in DecisionService, which this build may not change; they are held to it by tests that run the same rows through `preview()` and
then `run()` and compare every row's outcome, skip code and reasons for a second OK (`BulkDecisionsTest::testThePreviewSaysWhatRunWillDo…`,
`…KnowsTheApprovalSwitches…`, and the screen tests). A refusal that carries a number is shown with it: "must be a whole number from 1
to 1,000" (`BulkController::why()` printed the text's raw `%s` for `bad_units`, in the preview and on the result page: found in
review; a refusal whose words want a value the page does not have is said in the service's own words instead). A rule added to `decide()` later without its line in `predict()` shows as a row
the preview called "will be matched" and the result page calls skipped or waiting: never as a wrong match, because the apply is
DecisionService's. The preview therefore says "will", and the page says that everything is checked again.

**M58. The apply does what the preview showed, or less: never something else.** The preview's form carries every row again
(`row_<variant>` = item . suggestion . version . 1 or 0): the item the row was shown under, the suggestion and the `map_version` the
list showed (they travel from the list through the preview, as `ver_` / `prop_` do on the lists, M5 / M19), and whether the preview
skipped it. `run()` checks all of it again. A variant decided or renamed since is skipped (`changed`), one whose suggestion was replaced
is skipped (`suggestion_changed`), and so is one whose suggestion now names ANOTHER item than the one it was shown under
(`itemChecks()`: `suggestion_changed`; a variant is only ever matched to the item the person saw it under, also when a crafted form
says otherwise). A row the preview skipped is never acted on, whatever it looks like at the apply (a hold released, a strength the owner
allowed in between): it is recorded as skipped with the reason it has now, or as `changed` when it has none any more, because the
person said yes to "these N" and it was not one of them. So the batch holds every line of the preview, and the result page lists the
skipped ones at the end (the owner's rule). What may differ from the preview without being wrong: the approval switches are read at the
apply, so a row called "will be matched" waits for a second OK when the owner switched one on in between (and the other way round);
the result page says what was done. A second press of the button (or the Back button) sends the same versions again: every variant
has changed by then and is skipped.

**M59. What "Confirm suggested matches" leaves to a person, one at a time (second round; this replaces the first version's "every
open suggestion is confirmed").** The owner's rule is "skip anything doubtful, finish the rest, show the skipped at the end", and the
reviewer ruled what is doubtful in a confirm from By Item (`BulkDecisions::confirmScope()`, called from `itemChecks()`, so the
preview and the apply answer alike; each is a skip with its own code and words, listed on the preview and on the result page):
- **`item_on_store`**: the item already has a variant matched on that store, or a match waiting there for a second OK. "<Item> already
  has a variant on <store>: open it and decide." A second variant of one store for one item is decided on its page (some stores do
  list one item on two pages, but that is a person's call).
- **`rejected_before`**: the pair was marked "not a match" before: a `match_reject` of this variant for this item or for an item
  joined into it since. "It was marked not a match for this item before: open it and decide." One at a time such a match waits for
  a second person (`previously_rejected`); in bulk it is not sent to Second approval unread.
- **`several_suggested`** (added by the builder, for the reviewer to confirm or strike): more than one variant of that store is
  suggested for the item. Confirming them together would make exactly the second variant the first rule keeps for a person, and
  taking one of them would be an arbitrary pick, so ALL of them are left: "<Item> has more than one suggested variant on <store>:
  open them and decide which is right." It counts every open suggestion of the item on that store, also one marked wrong before
  (send that one back first, and the other becomes the only one).
"Not a match…" and "Send back for matching…" are not narrowed: they take every open suggestion of the ticked items, as before. The
lists of Mapping are not changed either: there a pair marked wrong before still goes to Second approval. These three are checked
with the other pre-checks, before the rows run (as vetoes and flags are), not again under each row's lock.
**On the list** a store's cell whose every suggestion was marked not a match before reads **"Marked not a match"** instead of
"Suggested" (red; the variant, its strength and its Review link are as before; `Words::PRODUCT_STORE` `rejected`); a cell that has
another suggestion too stays "Suggested" and names that one first; the picker's "On <store> now" line and the CSV say the same
(the CSV also notes each such variant). A row whose only suggestions are such ones keeps its tick box (to send the suggestion
back, say) but is **not ticked by "tick all"**: the header box and "Select all on this page" leave it (`data-bulk-manual`, the one
rule added to `app.js`; `all=1` without the script does the same), and a line under the bar says so. **Where it is read:**
`BulkDecisions::rejectedBefore()` answers for the page's suggestions, for a confirm and for `predict()` alike: `match_reject` by its
unique index `(listing_id, sku_id)` (the table DecisionService's own rule reads; EXPLAIN on the filled test schema: `range`,
`uq_match_reject`, "Using index", 206 rows for a page of 200 items), then the few rejected items that are not the suggested item
itself by primary key, following what each was joined into. No index was added and nothing is scanned. The confirm's other two reads
are the `(sku_id, channel_id)` index of `channel_listing` alone, the waiting decisions by their unique index
(`uq_match_decision_pending`, named in a hint: a few rows whatever the table's size) and the open suggestions by item
(`ix_match_proposal_open_sku`).

**U123. More rows: 50, 100 or 200 a page.** Above the list, at the end of the board's head: "Rows 50 100 200" (plain links, the
current one marked; another number keeps the place: the page of that size that holds this page's first item). The number a page opens
with is the setting `mapping.by_item_page_size` (0025: 50 as before; one of 50, 100, 200, a `Settings::RULES` `in` rule; changed on
Settings › System › Settings with a reason, like the other matching settings; a stored value that is none of the three reads as 50).
The person's choice is the query value `n`; the links (pager, filters, search, the way back from a variant's page: `ByProductContext`
`ln`) carry it only when it is not the setting's number, so a list nobody resized keeps the addresses it had. The CSV is every item
and has no pages. **No sticky header:** the brief allowed one "if the existing CSS has the pattern", and it has none: a list table
sits in a `.table-wrap` that scrolls sideways, and a header cannot stick to the page from inside a scroll box without script or a
second, vertical scroll box. The first (item) column is sticky as on every board, rows keep their strip and their hover tint, and the
bar and the preview's button stay at the bottom of the screen.

**U124. Ticks and the bar.** For people who may decide: a tick box on every item that has a suggested variant on some store (none on an
item with nothing to act on, as Store Products ticks only the rows an action applies to), "tick all on this page" in the header, the
existing action bar (U108, `bulk_bar`, which now takes its words and one choice from the page; `app.js` gained one rule, M59: a box
marked `data-bulk-manual` is left out of "select all", and the header box speaks for the others). The bar
says "N items ticked", then "On [All stores | each store of the `channel` table]", then the three buttons; a line under it says what
they act on, the limit (from the setting, in variants) and that matched variants are not changed here. Without the script it is a plain
form: the bar is a row under the list and "Select all on this page" a link (`all=1`). Each row that can be ticked sends ONE hidden
field with EVERY suggested variant it showed (`cells_<item>` = "variant.suggestion.version …"), not three fields a variant: a full
page of 200 ticked items is about 410 fields, well below PHP's `max_input_vars` (1,000; Kernel refuses a form that reaches it), and
the apply's form is one field a row (at most 500 by the setting's rule). **A row is never cut:** the first version sent the first 50
suggestions of an item without a word, and the store choice then said "none of the ticked items has a suggestion on <store>" where
the page showed some (found in review). What bounds a request is the whole-request limit, counted after the store is chosen. The one
bound of a row is the most `mapping.bulk_max_rows` can ever be set to (`Settings::RULES`, 500: `ByItemBulkController::MAX_PER_ITEM`
is that number, not a second one): an item with more suggested variants could never be acted on in one go, so its row has no tick
box and says "N suggested variants: more than one bulk action can take. Decide them one at a time." The preview reads only the store
of the variants sent (`Queries::variantStores`), keeps the chosen store's, checks the limit, and reads names for those. The bar's own "too many" warning is off here
(`data-max` 0): it counts ticked rows, which are items, and the limit counts variants; the server counts and refuses in words. The row
a person came back to after a decision keeps its tint under a new class, `here` (U119 used `picked`, which the bar's script sets and
clears with the tick). People who can only look, and an admin alone, see no tick, no bar and no form.

**U125. The preview page.** Pressing an action never saves. `POST /ui/review/products/bulk` (a POST because it carries the ticked rows;
`mapping.decide`, the session's CSRF token) answers with "Preview: confirm suggested matches" (or "not a match", "send back for
matching"): the summary "12 will be matched · 3 will wait for a second OK · 5 will be skipped", the store, how many items were ticked and
how many suggested variants that is, how many ticked items have nothing suggested on the chosen store ("nothing happens to them"), what
the action does in a sentence, and one line per item × store × variant, in the list's order: the item (name, CW number), the store, the
variant (its names and option number, a link), and what will happen in words: "Will be matched", "Will wait for a second OK" with each
reason as a label, "Will be skipped" with the reason in a sentence (`Words::BY_ITEM_SKIP`: the lists' reasons in items and variants).
When every line would be skipped there is no button and the page says so. When nothing is suggested on the chosen store, or more
variants are asked than the setting allows, there is no preview: the refusal in words, with the way back.

**U126. One button, and the way back.** "Yes, do these N" (N = the lines that will be done or will wait; blue), or in red "Yes, these
N are not a match" / "Yes, send these N back for matching", and "No, go back to By Item". The button stays at the bottom of the screen
(`.actions.sticky`). **The owner's rule that "Not a match" needs a second step is met by this page:** on the lists the first press
opens a second step that states the count and has one red button (U110); here the first press opens the preview, which states the
count, lists every variant, says "This is the second step of 'Not a match': nothing is marked before you press the red button", and
has that one red button. A third step would add nothing. Back is the list as the person left it: the filter, the search, the page, the
number of rows, the chosen store and the ticks (`ticked=<item numbers joined by dots>`, at most a page's 200, read back as numbers or
not at all; `on=<store code>`); every address is built from checked values (a filter that is one, a text cut to the search box's
length, numbers), never taken from the request.

**U127. The result page.** The apply (`POST /ui/review/products/bulk/apply`) ends on the existing batch page (M47). For a batch of By
Item it says "By Item · <store or All stores>" for where, speaks of variants (its headings, the skipped reasons), stays under the By
Item tab (the redirect says `from=item`; `Sections` matches it), and its way back is By Item with the filter, search, page and number
of rows the person had (carried by the redirect, each read as the list reads it). The batch's own record decides what it is: the same
page opened without `from=item` has the same words and way back, only the tab differs.

**U128. What the forms take.** Only numbers and checked values: an item's number, a variant's, a suggestion's, a version, an action of
this list (`ITEM_ACTIONS`: "ignore", "unlink" or a list where one value is expected are refused), a store's code that names a row of
`channel` (another value: 400 "We cannot find this store"; no value: all stores), the list's own values read as the list reads them.
A variant's store, names and item are read from the database, never from the form. `cells_` and `row_` must match their pattern to the
last character (bytes that are not UTF-8, a sign, a fourth number, more variants for one item than one bulk action can ever take, more
ticks than a page has rows, a value of 100,000 characters: 400 in words); a variant number or a version beyond what its column
holds is refused the same way (M56), and one within it that names nothing is a skipped line ("This variant no longer exists"). Both routes: `mapping.decide`
(403 in words for the others), the CSRF token of the session (403), GET is 405. Tested through the kernel and over HTTP (slot `ui`,
where a page of 200 ticked items is previewed and applied).

**U129. Cost at 200 rows (measured 10 Oct 2026, `/root/cw_work/runs/bybulk_explain_1010.txt`; the slot's test schema filled like
staging: 14,846 items, 38,040 variants with profiles, 2,638 open suggestions; MySQL 8.4, a 32 MB buffer pool).** No index was added:
a page of 200 reads the same indexes as a page of 50. The page's ids: 4-5 ms (4 at 50). Its rows: a range of the primary key, 4-5 ms
(2). Its cells, three reads: 16-22 ms (8-19 at 50): the matched variants by `ix_channel_listing_sku_channel` (a range of 200 values),
the suggestions by `ix_match_proposal_open_sku` (a range, "Using index": the proposals' rows are not read), each variant then by its
primary key; the suggestions' "no decision waiting" test is read per variant at 50 and, at 200, as one pass over the unique index of
the waiting decisions (the optimizer's choice on the test's 20 decisions); the decisions waiting for a second OK are read as before
(a scan of that table at 50 and at 200 alike on the test's 20 rows: unchanged by this build). `cl.map_version`, which the form needs,
comes from the row the suggestions' read already fetched. "Missing on a store" at 200 a page: 2 ms on page 1 when most items are
missing, 43-57 ms on the last page or when few are (as at 50). A preview of 100 variants: about 45 ms for all its reads (16
statements, each a primary-key or unique-index range of at most 100 values), plus 3 ms for the variants' names and 2.5 ms for the
items'. The apply costs what a bulk action of the lists costs: one DecisionService decision a row. Second round
(`/root/cw_work/runs/bybulk_explain2_1010.txt`): the list reads one thing more for its page, which suggestions were marked not a match
before (M59: `match_reject` by its unique index, 2-3 ms for the 206 suggestions of a page of 200 items, and 2 ms for the items of
the rejects that are not the suggested item's own); a confirm's preview of 100 variants is 22 statements, 61-82 ms (the three reads
of M59 are 1-3 ms each, all index ranges); a preview of "Not a match" 34-42 ms.

**U130. Words, and what was left out.** Words: `BY_ITEM_BULK` (the bar, the preview, its buttons, the refusals, the result page's
words) and `BY_ITEM_SKIP` (every code of `BulkDecisions::SKIPS`, in the same order as `BULK_SKIP`, with the same `%s`), `PAGE_INTRO`
`by_item_preview` and `by_item_result`, the setting's name and help, `BY_PRODUCT` `rows`, `note`, `note_look`, `PRODUCT_STORE` `rejected`
("Marked not a match"); all in the owner's words
(U122): items and variants, never "website product" (`WordsTest`). The reasons for a second OK are the shared `NEEDS_SECOND` labels
("1 sale is not 1 product"), as on the result page and on Second approval. Left out: (1) a sticky table header (U123); (2) anything
for Matched cells (M53) and for the decisions waiting for a second OK; (3) Ignore and Create as new item (M55); (4) ticking across
pages, or "every item of the filter": a request is what one page shows, at most 200 items, and the setting's limit in variants;
(5) the bar's live count of variants (it counts items; the preview counts variants): that needs more script than the one rule of M59;
(6) a preview for the lists' own bulk actions: `preview()` works for them too (tested), but their screens keep the second step they
have. **For whoever puts this together with the New Variants build (`mapping-new-variants`):** this build merges first and its
migration is **0025**; New Variants' is 0026. The rule for `mapping_batch.source` from here on: 0025 adds `item`; a later migration
that adds a value must restate every value the column has by then (`'review','store','item'` and its own: `MODIFY COLUMN` replaces
the whole list); an applied migration is never edited. Both builds add a list context to `BulkDecisions` (`SOURCES`, the action list
of a context, `offered()`) and skip codes to `SKIPS`; this build moved the request checks of `run()` into `checked()`, where the
bound on a row's numbers (M56) now is; the decision numbers of the two sections may collide (both start after M54 / U122).

## Products › New Variants: a store's new variants, and the "seed" on every store (slot `newvar`, 10 Oct 2026)

The owner's request of 10 Oct 2026: "new item add in any store how to here show also seed option any new each site with". That is: when a
variant is added on any store, show it in CW; and offer the "seed" (make the warehouse item from the variant, as was done once for the
main store's whole list) for a new variant of EVERY store. The facts that day, from the handoff of 10 Oct (this build read nothing
on cw_staging): every store is `off`, no store sends variants, each store's list on staging was loaded by the engineer between 26
Sep and 10 Oct, and a variant that arrives has no suggestion.
Code: `migrations/0026_new_variants.sql`, `src/Ui/Controller/NewVariantsController.php` and the view `new_variants` (new),
`src/Ui/Queries.php` (the New Variants reads), `src/Mapping/BulkDecisions.php` (the list `new`, the seed's skips, the checks of what
was posted), `src/Matching/Gtin.php` (`forms()`), `src/Mapping/DecisionService.php` (one check of the note's text, M60),
`src/Ui/Controller/{Bulk,Review}Controller.php`, the view `bulk_result`, `src/Ui/{Kernel,Sections,Words}.php`, `src/Settings.php`.
Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/NewVariantsScreenTest.php` (new), `tests/Integration/Mapping/BulkDecisionsTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/BulkScreensTest.php`, `tests/Unit/GtinTest.php`; the pinned navigation, templates, words and routes in
`SectionsTest`, `UiTemplatesTest`, `WordsTest`, `UiUnitTest`, `MenusTest`, `HomeScreenTest`, `DuplicatesScreenTest`,
`ByProductScreenTest`; the HTTP tests `UiSecurityTest` and `UiReviewFlowTest` (slot `ui`). The page uses the owner's words of U122: a
store's sellable option is a VARIANT, the warehouse record it is matched to an ITEM.
This section was written beside By Item's bulk action (the section above), which was merged first and holds M55-M59 and U123-U130:
the points here are M60-M62 and U131-U138, and the migration is 0026 after its 0025. Where the two builds met in the code: both
add a list to `BulkDecisions` (`SOURCES` is now review, store, item, new; `actionsOf()` names each list's actions; `offered()`)
and skip codes to `SKIPS` (By Item's three, then the nine of a bulk "create as new": each has its words in `BULK_SKIP` and, because
By Item's words are pinned to hold every reason, in `BY_ITEM_SKIP` too); the checks of the whole request are By Item's `checked()`,
for `run()` and its `preview()` alike, and this build's two (a New Variants request names its store; the note is text) sit there;
the batch page takes its words from By Item's `$words`, with New Variants' action and list in them.

The first version of the same day seeded any ticked variant that had no suggestion, on a barcode check alone. An independent review
(eight findings, each confirmed by a second reviewer) showed what that makes: items from page headings, drafts and binned pages
(their state WAS stored), a second item for a variant whose name an item already has, and a second item for a variant whose seed had
been undone. The owner's rule is "skip anything doubtful, finish the rest, show the skipped at the end", and a duplicate item splits one
product's stock over two records and is never deleted. So the rule of M61 replaced it before anything was merged; the eight findings
and what answers each are named where they belong below. A second independent check of that second version (the same day) found
the rule still trusted an open "new" suggestion for as long as it stayed open: round 2b added the guards that look at what
happened after the check (an item made from the variant, a name taken since, a change on the website), made them the rule of every
bulk "create as new", and corrected the words that promised more than the check does (M61, U133, U135, U138).

**M60. No new way to decide: the seed is BulkDecisions' `new_item`.** New Variants only reads (two GET routes; `UiUnitTest` pins that no
POST route starts with `/ui/review/new-variants`). Its tick boxes post to the EXISTING bulk route (`POST /ui/review/bulk`,
`mapping.decide`) with `source=new`, and `BulkDecisions::run` does what it does for the other lists: one `DecisionService::decide`
per ticked row, in listing order, each in its own transaction, with the version and the suggestion the page showed, a batch
(`mapping_batch`, `screen:<id>` on every decision) and the result page (M47, M52). So the roles (M49: whoever may decide one may tick
many), the two-person rules (M50: units per sale, a protected item, the owner's switch `approvals.mapping_bulk_second_ok`, which makes a
new item wait for a second matching lead: nothing is made until then) and the most rows at a time (`mapping.bulk_max_rows`) are the
existing ones. What `BulkDecisions` gained: (1) the list `new` (`SOURCES`) with its actions `NEW_ACTIONS` = create as new items,
confirm match, ignore (`actionsOf()`, `offered()`); (2) the seed's own skips (`seedCheck()`, M61): it never makes an item the existing
new-product check would not make, it only skips more; (3) a request of this list that names no store, or a code that is none, is
refused whole (400, nothing written): the list is one store's. `mapping_batch.source` gains the value `new` (0026), so the result page
says where the rows were ticked and leads back there.
Two checks of what was posted, for every list of the route (found in review; both were there before this list and ended on the error
page): a ticked listing number or version above 4,294,967,295 (no listing and no version has one; recorded as a skipped row it did
not fit its column, after the rows before it had already been decided) is refused whole with the existing 400 `bad_form`
(`BulkController`), and `BulkDecisions` refuses the same before anything is written (400 `bad_request`: ONE bound, in `checked()`,
which By Item's build brought with its M56; both builds had found it); a note that is not valid UTF-8 text is refused there too,
before the batch is written and before a preview is drawn (400 `bad_reason`; Ignore's second step is shown again with "The note has
characters this system cannot read"). And the route itself reads the list a form names as one of review, store or new: By Item's
`item` is in `BulkDecisions::SOURCES` but is NOT taken at `POST /ui/review/bulk` (its bulk action has its own route, with the
preview first), so a form that names it there is read as a match-strength list's and refused as one (`NewVariantsScreenTest` pins
it). `DecisionService::reason` has the same check of the note for the one-at-a-time path: that is a
check of what was typed (the database refused the row anyway, as an error page), not a rule of matching; no decision, role or
two-person rule of `DecisionService` changed.

**M61. What a bulk "create as new" takes, and what it skips: one rule for every list.** New Variants' "Create as new items" and
the New products list's "Create as new product" are the same check (`BulkDecisions::seedCheck()` and `nameChecks()`; Store Products
offers no such action). It takes ONLY a variant with an OPEN suggestion that says "new product" (band `New item` and
`proposed_new_item`, the two marks the existing new-product check asked for). What that suggestion says, exactly: when the computer
check ran, it compared the variant with the MAIN STORE's list of variants (`tools/first_match`: two export files, no database) and
found nothing like it. It does not say "nothing like it in the warehouse now". The check never sees an item made since by "create as
new" from another store's variant, nor the item made from this very variant, nor the other rows ticked with it; and it speaks of the
variant as it was that day. (The second version of this paragraph, the screen and the tests said "checked against the warehouse's
items": wrong, found by the second independent check on 10 Oct, which confirmed five gaps. The guards numbered 1, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10
below close them; nothing had been merged.) A done row: a new item (a `sku` row, its CW number, origin `new_item` and the variant
as `origin_listing_id`) made by `DecisionService` from the variant's own profile (`cardFrom`: the name is the variant's own title, else
its product's; the brand; the details the matching features hold), and the variant matched to it, with the suggested units per sale.
Skipped, each with its reason on the result page, nothing changed on it, in this order (the first that applies is the one recorded):
1. an item was ALREADY MADE from this variant (`made_before`, with that item's CW number: "An item was already made from this
   variant (CW-…): open it and decide."): `sku.origin_listing_id`, whatever became of the match since (undone, the item joined into
   another) and whatever suggestion is open now. One read over the ticked ids on the index of 0004 (`BulkDecisions::madeFrom`). It
   is the first check because a later computer check says "new" again of a variant whose own item it cannot see: a seed that was
   undone would be made a second time after the next check (in either order: the check imported after the undo, or while the
   variant was still matched);
2. New Variants only: its open suggestion is a MATCH to an item, of any strength (`suggested_match`: "The computer suggests it is
   CW-…: open it and decide."; the detail keeps the item's CW number);
3. a page heading of the website (`page_heading`: the stored features' `is_placeholder`: a landing row, or a parent row that only
   holds its options): "It is a page heading on the website, not something that is sold.";
4. its state on the website is known and is not Published (`not_published`, with that state: Draft, Bin, …): "It is not published
   on the website (Bin).". The state is the stored features' `variant_status`; when they give none, the `variant_status` the open
   suggestion recorded when the computer checked it (its evidence, decoded in PHP; `BulkDecisions::siteState`). The features are
   stored when a store's list is loaded together with a computer check (`bin/mint_vpg.php`, `bin/import_proposals.php`), and they
   are WIPED when the variant's titles, brand, attributes or barcodes change (`ListingIngestService`): before the fallback, a binned
   variant that was renamed read as "state not known" and was seeded. Known from neither: says nothing and skips nothing;
5. NO open suggestion, whatever came before (never looked at, sent back for matching, a suggestion marked wrong and then sent
   back): `not_checked` on New Variants ("The computer has not checked this variant yet. Open it and decide."), `no_suggestion` on
   the New products list (as before). "No suggestion" never meant "new": it means nobody compared it with anything;
6. an open suggestion that is not "new" and names no item. On New Variants two reasons (round 4 told them apart):
   - a MATCH that names no item (strength Strong or Likely with no item: `bin/import_proposals.php` stores a suggestion so, with
     the flag `target_not_minted`, when the main-store variant the computer matched has no item, which is the ordinary case for a
     thing the main store added after its first seed): `match_no_item`, "The computer matched it to a variant of the main store
     that has no item yet: open it and decide." The strength is what is asked, not the flag (`BulkDecisions::matchNoItem`). Until
     round 4 such a row read "The computer could not say what it is (Strong match)", which contradicts itself;
   - one the computer could not decide (Not sure, Clues disagree, a renamed range, one left to a person): `not_new`, with its
     strength in words ("The computer could not say what it is (Not sure – you choose): open it and decide."; before round 2b
     such a row ticked for Create was explained with the confirm action's sentence "…not one that may be confirmed together",
     which names a setting that cannot change the outcome).
   On the New products list both are `band_not_allowed` (as before: that list holds one strength);
7. it CHANGED on the website after the computer checked it (`changed_since_check`: "It changed on the website after the computer
   checked it: open it and decide."), told from two signs, either is enough (`BulkDecisions::changedSinceCheck`):
   - the suggestion has a record of what it was made on (`match_proposal_basis`, M27, read by its primary key) and the identity
     recorded there (titles, brand, attributes, barcodes: the profile's `identity_hash`) is not the variant's identity now. The
     suggestion stays open through such a change (only the variant's version moves on), so without this a variant renamed to
     anything was seeded on the check of its old name. A suggestion with NO such record (made before 0012 and never proved
     unchanged) skips nothing by this sign;
   - the suggestion's evidence holds the title the computer judged (`title`, a text that is not empty) and it is not the variant's
     title now (`KeyEligibility::sameTitle`: the option's title, else the title, compared without letter case and spacing; the
     comparison the Key bulk confirm uses for the same question, M28 `evidence_title_differs`). Evidence with no title skips
     nothing by this sign. It is needed (round 4) because the record of the first sign dates from the IMPORT of a suggestion,
     on the variant as it is then, while the run that judged it was exported earlier: a variant renamed between the two (the
     store's list loaded again, or its connector's push) gets a record on its NEW identity, read "New", and was seeded on a
     check of a thing it no longer is, with the old features the import writes back.
   What this does not see: a change of the brand, the attributes or the barcodes between a run's export and its import (only
   the title is in the evidence), and any change at all when the evidence holds no title. The lasting answer is at the source:
   the import should not take a suggestion (or write a run's features) onto a variant whose title is no longer the run's; that
   is the import tool's, not built here;
8. its barcode is on an item or on another variant of any store (`barcode_elsewhere`, the existing rule of M51, with the wider
   look-up below);
9. the name its item would get is the name of an item that is not joined into another (`name_elsewhere`, with that item's CW
   number: "An item with the same name is already in the warehouse (CW-…): open it and decide."). The name is the one `cardFrom`
   gives (the same trim and collapse of white space `mint()` stores); it is compared as the item table compares names (letter
   case and accents do not tell two names apart), one look-up per name on the index `sku (name)` of 0026, 50 names a statement
   (`namesTaken`). This is what stops the second of two stores' variants of one thing when they share no barcode, and a variant
   whose name an item made since already has;
10. two or more of the request's rows that would otherwise be made have the same name, compared without letter case
    (`name_twice`, every row of the group: "Another row you ticked has the same name, so the two may be one item: open each and
    decide."). Ticked one at a time, the first is made and the second then finds its name (`name_elsewhere`);
- and, as before: a matched one (`linked`), one with a decision waiting for a second OK (`pending_second`), an ignored one
  (`not_waiting`, with its state), one that changed since the page was drawn (`changed`, `suggestion_changed`), one of another store
  than the page's (`other_store`), one held back or in a spot check (`held`, `in_spot_check`), one with no name at all (`no_name`),
  and any refusal of `DecisionService` (by its code).
A skipped variant is not lost: "Open" leads to its own page, where a person who sees its details may still match it by hand or
create its one item (also one the computer never checked, one of a name there is, one an item was made from before:
`DecisionService` is unchanged, and the tests pin that each of these can still be made there). An item made by mistake is not deleted
(the owner's rule): the match is undone on the variant's page (M53) and the item stays, unmatched; no bulk action makes a second
item from that variant afterwards (1).
**One rule for every list (decided at the second check, 10 Oct; it reverses "the existing lists keep their rules" for these
guards).** Until round 2b the New products list made its ticked rows whatever the stored features said, and the guards above were
New Variants' own. The same hazards live on that list (a duplicate item, an item for a page heading), so a bulk "Create as new
product" there now skips `made_before`, `page_heading`, `not_published` (with the fallback of 4), `changed_since_check`,
`name_elsewhere` and `name_twice` as well. What counts as a suggestion to make on that list is exactly as it was (`no_suggestion`,
`band_not_allowed`); `not_checked`, `suggested_match` and `not_new` stay New Variants' own. The tests that pinned the old behaviour
were changed with it (`BulkDecisionsTest`: the draft on the New products list is now skipped). The single-variant page is untouched.
**The name is read twice (round 4).** `nameChecks()` reads the guard once, before the first row. Each "create as new" then reads
its own name again immediately before its decision (`BulkDecisions::one()`, one look-up on `ix_sku_name`): an item of that name
made in between is found, and the row is skipped as `name_elsewhere` with that item's CW number. "In between" is an earlier row of
the same request whose name differs by an accent only (the item table calls the two one name; `name_twice` compares without
letter case only), another person's create on a list or on a variant's page, or an approval in Second approval, once it is
committed.
**What the name guard does not do.** It finds exact names only (white space, letter case and accents apart): two stores that
title one thing differently still both seed. **It is a read, not a lock**: two creates of the same name decided within the same
instant (another person's bulk create of that row at that moment, a create on a variant's own page, an approval in Second
approval) can still both make an item, because neither sees the other's item until it is committed; no named lock is taken. With
two people using the system this is accepted (decided at the final check, 11 Oct 2026); such a pair can be joined afterwards. A
new item that waits for a second OK (the owner's switch) is not an item yet, so a same-named row seeded
meanwhile is not caught: the second person sees each one. And the item's name is the variant's OWN title when it has one: on a store
whose variants are titled with the option only ("Blue Razz / 20mg") many rows will share a name with an item and be skipped
(`name_elsewhere`); they are then made one at a time on their own pages, where the person types a name.
**The barcode rule's look-up (for every list, and for the variant page's "also on" list):** `Gtin::forms()`: each barcode as it is
stored, its key (leading zeros gone) and that key padded with zeros to every length up to 14 digits, so "5056168800073" finds a record
that holds "05056168800073" and two different paddings of one code find each other (before: only the ticked variant's own two forms,
so a clash was missed in one direction, and in both for two paddings). Every barcode of the variant is looked up (before: the first
20), each an exact match on an index (`sku_barcode`'s primary key; the multi-valued index of 0005). The bulk rule asks 200 forms a
statement and stops at the first hit (`BulkDecisions::barcodeElsewhere`); the variant page's list sends every form in ONE statement
per table (`Queries::barcodeElsewhere`: its ORDER BY and its limit of 10 stay exact that way; a variant holds at most 100 barcodes,
so at most about 1,400 values). A code that differs by more than leading zeros (a hyphen inside) is still another code.

**M62. Confirm match and Ignore… on this list are the existing actions.** Confirm match is offered while `mapping.bulk_confirm_bands`
allows any strength and the filter is not "New" or "Not checked yet" (nothing there has a suggested match); each row is then checked
on its own as M51 says: its strength must be one the setting allows (`band_not_allowed` otherwise), no veto, no flag, no failed spot
check, no undone bulk link; a row without a suggestion is skipped (`no_suggestion`). Ignore… has its second step with the count and
the note (U110): it is how a page heading or a binned page leaves the lists. "Not a match", "Take off the ignored list" and "Send
back for matching" are not offered here (posted by hand: refused whole, 400).

**U131. The tab and the list.** Products › New Variants (`/ui/review/new-variants`, `linking.view`), after By Item in
`Sections::MAP`. One store at a time, chosen with the store selector of the matching pages (`store_seg`; the stores are the `channel`
rows that have variants, by name, the first by default; a code that names none of them is answered 404 in words). Its variants FIRST
SEEN in the period, newest first (`channel_listing.created_at`, then the id): the moment CW made the row, which a later push of the
same variant never changes. Columns: Variant (the product's title, under it the variant's own title and the brand), Option number,
Barcode (up to three, "+N more"), Price, Sold (30 days), Sold (1 year), First seen (UK time), Match (a chip that says what the row
is, U133), "What the computer found" (why, U133) and Open (the variant's existing page: match by hand, or create one item with its
details checked; coming back from there is not built). The selector's number beside a store is its variants first seen in the
period, whatever they are. 50 a page with the existing pager.

**U132. The period and its setting.** `mapping.new_variants_days` (a whole number, 30 by default, 1 to 365; Settings › System ›
Settings › Matching products, changed with a reason as every setting, Y4; its baseline is in 0026): the period the page opens with.
The page offers 7, 30 and 90 days, the setting's own number when it is another one, and "Any time". A period is counted back from now,
to the second. The link of the default period carries no period, so a bookmark follows the setting; a value the page does not offer is
the default.

**U133. What a row is, the filter, the search, the CSV.** Each row says what it is, so a person sees before ticking which rows the
seed takes (`Queries::NEW_KINDS`, `Words::NEW_VARIANT_STATE`): **New** ("When the computer checked it, it found nothing like it.": an
open "new product" suggestion, M61), **Suggested match** (its strength and the item's CW number and name; "Strong match, to a
variant of the main store that has no item yet: open it to decide." when it is a match that names no item, from the same condition
the seed skips on, `BulkDecisions::matchNoItem`; or only its strength in words when the computer could not settle on an item: Not
sure, Clues disagree), **Not checked yet** ("The computer has not checked it
yet: open it to decide."), Matched ("Matched to CW-…" and the item's name; "On hold: shows as out of stock"), Waiting for a second
OK (what waits), Ignored. A row still to match also says what the seed would find, from the SAME conditions the seed skips on
(`BulkDecisions::madeFrom`, `changedSinceCheck`, `siteState`, `isPlaceholder`: the row and the skip ask the same functions, so
they cannot disagree): "An item was already made from this variant (CW-…): open it to decide." in place of the New or Not checked
sentence (under a suggested match: as a line below it); for a row marked New, "It changed on the website after the computer checked
it: open it to decide." in place of "found nothing like it"; and below, what the website said (from the stored features, else from
what the check recorded): "A page heading on the website, not something that is sold." or "Not published on the website (Bin)."
(nothing when it is published or not known). A row marked New with one of these is a row the seed skips, and the row says why. A
name that an item already has is NOT shown on the row (it would be a look-up per row on every page): it is found when the row is
ticked. The filter (`Words::NEW_VARIANT_FILTER`): **All not matched** (the page opens with it: New, Suggested match and Not checked
yet together), **New: the computer found nothing like it** (the rows the seed can take, less the ones it skips), **Suggested
match**, **Not checked yet**, **All**, each with its count in the period; the counts are not narrowed by the search
(as Store Products'). Search is Store Products': a text in the product's title, the variant's title or the brand, an option number
whole, a barcode; white space of any kind around the text is dropped, and text that is not UTF-8 finds nothing. Export is a CSV of
every variant of the store, period, filter and search (not only the page; at most 50,000), newest first, read 500 at a time:
`store`, `option_number`, `product`, `variant`, `brand`, `barcodes`, `price`, `sold_30_days`, `sold_1_year`, `first_seen_utc`,
`state` (what the row is), `cw_number` (the item matched, or the one suggested), `details` (the row's sentence and its lines). A
file that was cut ends with "Only the first 50,000 variants are in this file.": decided from the read of the ids alone (one more
than the file may hold is asked for, and the line is written when that one came back; `NewVariantsController::csvText`). The
second version compared the ids with a count read a moment earlier, so a file that was NOT cut could end with that line while
someone was deciding rows (found by the second check). The counts are an input of `csvText` (its last parameter; read there when
not given), so the test can hand it counts that are wrong, as they are when a row is decided between the two reads: counts that
say 99 for 55 rows under a limit of 60 give no line, counts that say 1 under a limit of 54 give the line. The first version of
that test passed under the old rule as well (found by the final check): in one thread the count always equals the list.

**U134. The action bar, per person.** People who may decide (`mapping.decide`) get a tick box on every row still to match (New,
Suggested match, Not checked yet; a matched, on-hold, waiting or ignored variant changes on its own page), "Select all on this
page", and the existing bar (U108): "Create as new items" on every filter, "Confirm match" (M62), "Ignore…". One line beside the bar
says what the seed takes: only the rows marked New; every other ticked row is skipped and listed afterwards with the reason (not
checked yet, a suggested match (also one to a variant of the main store that has no item yet), one the computer could not decide, a
page heading, not published on the website, changed on the
website after the check, an item already made from it, a name that an item already has or that two ticked rows share, a barcode
that is already on an item or on another variant). The form carries the list as it was (store, period, filter, search, page), so a refusal and the second step of Ignore lead
back to it; the result page leads back to New Variants for that store. Everyone else with `linking.view` sees the list, Open and
the CSV, no boxes, no bar and no such line ("You can look; … change this.").

**U135. Where new variants come from, in honest words.** A box on the page (`Words::NEW_VARIANTS` `where_from`): each store's
connector sends the variants the store adds or changes to CW (`PUT /v1/listings`), and a variant shows here from the moment it first
arrives; the first load of a store's list counts too; nothing is made up, a variant the store has not sent is not here. Then one
sentence about THIS store, decided from what CW records and nothing else (`Queries::storeLink`, `NewVariantsController::sending()`):
its mode in CW (`channel.mode`) and its connector's latest heartbeat (`channel_health`, by the index (channel_id, id)):
- mode `off`: `store_off`, "<store> is Off in the warehouse system (Settings › Stores), so its connector sends nothing yet: its new
  variants arrive only when its list of variants is loaded on the server (ask …)", whatever its connector reports;
- switched on AND heard from within the time the Stores page calls recent (`Sites::STALE_AFTER_SEC`, 180 s) AND the website itself
  did not report `off` (the lower of the two modes applies): `store_on`, "<store> is in contact with the warehouse system: its
  connector sends its new and changed variants.";
- switched on but never heard from, not heard from lately, or reporting `off`: `store_quiet`, "<store> is switched on in the warehouse
  system, but its website is not sending now (Settings › Stores shows why): its new variants arrive only when its list of variants is
  loaded on the server (ask …)". The first version said "sends" for every store that was not `off`, also while nothing could arrive
  (an empty allowlist, no key, a connector that is not installed): found in review.
And the day the store's newest variant was first seen.
**A store the computer check has never marked a variant New on** gets one more sentence in the box (`never_new`,
`Queries::everFoundNew`): "The computer check has not marked any variant of <store> as New so far (it may not cover this store yet),
so "Create as new items" will skip every row here. To make an item from one of its variants, open the variant and create the item
on its own page." Why: the only tool that writes a "new" suggestion is `bin/import_proposals.php`, for the store a check judged,
and `tools/first_match/run.php` refuses the main store as the judged side (it is the list every other store is compared WITH). So
no tool can mark a main-store variant New: its unmatched variants read "Not checked yet" for good, and the bulk seed has nothing to
take there; each is created on its own page (or, on the server, by the first seed's tool for published main-store variants). The
rule was not changed for it; the words were made true (the second version's "not checked yet … ask for a check" promised a check
no tool performs for that store). The sentence is decided from data, not from a store's name (CW has no "main store" setting): the
store has no suggestion of the strength New product in any state (open, decided, or replaced by a later check's). It is therefore
also shown for a store no check was ever run for, and for one whose checks found nothing new: the words say only what the data
says ("has not marked … so far (it may not cover this store yet)"). The read is asked only when the period on the page shows no
row marked New (U136).
On staging on 10 Oct 2026 every store is `off` and, by the handoff's dates,
each store's whole list was loaded within the last 30 days: the default period then shows every variant still to match of a store
there, until 30 days have passed since the load or the owner sets fewer days. For the main store those are, by the handoff, mostly
pages left out of the first seed on purpose (binned, drafts, landing rows): they have no suggestion and their features say what they
are, so they read "Not checked yet" with the website's line, the seed skips them, and Ignore… is what takes them out of the lists.

**U136. Kept cheap; what 0026 adds.** Two indexes, both built online: `channel_listing (channel_id, created_at, id)` for the list
(below) and `sku (name)` (`ix_sku_name`) for the name guard of M61. The reads round 2b added, measured the same way on the same
slot schema (11 Oct 2026; 15,000 items of which 14,648 hold the variant they were made from, 38,040 variants, 5,164 suggestions of
which 2,638 are open with a record of what they were made on, 2,597 of the strength New product: 371 open and 2,226 replaced by
later checks; every statement's `EXPLAIN` is in `/root/cw_work/runs/newvar_explain_r2b.txt`): the items already made from 100
ticked variants 2-3 ms (a range of `ix_sku_origin_listing`); the pre-check read of 100 ticked rows 15-18 ms (it now also brings
each row's titles and features, to name the item, and the suggestion's record by its primary key; 5 ms before); the name guard
0.7 ms for one name and 25-33 ms for 50 names in one statement (one `ref` look-up on `ix_sku_name` each; WITHOUT that index 2.2 s
for the same 50, each name a pass over the items: the reason the index is in 0026); the page's 50 rows 4 ms and the item-made-before
read 1 ms; the CSV's 500 rows 16 ms and 7 ms. `everFoundNew` reads the suggestions' own index of 0020 (status, strength, variant:
never a suggestion's row) and each one's variant by its primary key, until one is the store's: 1-2 ms for a store that has one;
for a store that has none it passes every "New product" suggestion of every store: 8-10 ms for 2,597 of them, 30-38 ms for
13,727 (as if thirty more checks had run). That cost grows with every check that is imported and is paid on each view of New
Variants for such a store (today: the main store); if it ever matters, the answer is a per-store mark written when a check is
imported, not a faster read. For the list: `channel_listing (channel_id, created_at, id)` (`ix_channel_listing_seen`). No
index served "one store, newest first, since a date": 0024's index starts with the item, `(channel_id, status)` is in id order within
a status, `(channel_id, external_variant_id)` in the order of the website's ids. The reads (`Queries`), each named in an optimizer hint
that is ignored while the index is not there: `seenRange` (a store's oldest and newest "first seen": the index's two ends);
`storeLink` (the store's row and its latest heartbeat, both by primary key after the index's last entry); `seenSinceByStore` (the
selector's counts: one range of the index per store in one statement); `newVariantCounts` (the filter's counts: when the period holds
every variant of the store, which the oldest "first seen" says, Store Products' three narrow reads `storeStateCounts` and one read of
the store's open "new product" suggestions by their strength's index; else one grouped read of the period's entries, with the
waiting decision probed by its unique index and the open suggestion's row read only for a variant that has one); `newVariants` (the
page's 50 ids: the period's entries backwards from now, stopping after the page. "All not matched" reads the narrow listing row;
"Not checked yet" also probes the open suggestion's unique index; "New" and "Suggested match" join the open suggestion by that index
AFTER the listing (`JOIN_ORDER`), so the list is read in the index's order whatever the tables hold; a search also reads the profile
of each variant it passes, and counts its hits in a second pass); `newVariantRows` (the 50 rows by primary key, with the two stored
marks of the website read out of the profile's features). Measured on the slot's test schema filled like staging (10 Oct 2026: the
small cluster, MySQL 8.4, a 32 MB buffer pool; 15,000 items, 38,040 variants with profiles, 2,638 open suggestions of which 371 say
"new", 3,000 heartbeats; the By Item build's generator with "first seen" added; every statement's `EXPLAIN` is in
`/root/cw_work/runs/newvar_explain_r2.txt`). A store that sends as it goes (299 of its 29,000 variants first seen in 30 days): the
two ends 4-5 ms; the store's link 3-5 ms; the selector's counts 12-22 ms; the filter's counts 16 ms (25-41 ms for 747 variants of
which 205 have a suggestion); a page's ids 2-17 ms by filter and its rows 4 ms; a search in the period 13-15 ms. "Any time": the
counts 31-59 ms (Store Products' reads and the "new" read); page 1 of All not matched 5-6 ms, its last page 126-204 ms; page 1 of
New on a store of 9,000 with 371 of them 11 ms, its last page 70-78 ms (it walks the store's variants still to match); a search
275-344 ms on the biggest store (it reads the profile of every variant, as Store Products' search does: the real profiles are about
four times as wide as the test's, so expect more on staging). Staging today (each store's whole list first seen 14 days ago): the
counts 34-50 ms, page 1 of All not matched 23-25 ms (it walks past the matched ones), of New 11 ms, of All 1-3 ms, a search 484-575
ms. The CSV: every id of a store in 41-44 ms, of its variants still to match 130 ms, then 18 ms for each 500 rows. A bulk action:
its pre-check read 5 ms for 100 rows; the barcode rule's two look-ups 1 and 2 ms for one barcode in its forms, 6 and 7 ms for 200
forms. Without the index the same page 1 took 96-186 ms (every variant row of the store read, then sorted; 450-760 ms in an earlier
run) and the two ends 83-94 ms. The plans: the list is a range or a backward scan of `ix_channel_listing_seen` and is never sorted;
the period's count groups its rows in a small temporary table; every look-up is by primary key or a unique index, the barcode rule's
by ranges of exact values. Times on that cluster vary from run to run by a factor of two or three, and the first of three runs is the
cold one (up to 1.1 s for the whole-store search).

**U137. Words.** Every word is in `Ui\Words`: `MENU`, `MENU_HELP` and `PAGE_INTRO` `new_variants`; the groups `NEW_VARIANTS` (the page),
`NEW_VARIANT_STATE` (what a row is) and `NEW_VARIANT_FILTER`, `NEW_VARIANT_ACTION` (the bar: "Create as new items", "Confirm match",
"Ignore…"), `NEW_VARIANT_DONE` (the result's count: "2 new items created and matched") and `NEW_VARIANT_PENDING` (what waits for a
second OK); `BULK_SKIP` `suggested_match`, `not_checked`, `not_new`, `match_no_item`, `page_heading`, `not_published`,
`made_before`, `changed_since_check`, `name_elsewhere`, `name_twice` (the last six are also what the New products list's result page
says since round 2b, in these words); `NEW_VARIANTS` `made_before`, `changed`, `match_no_item`, `never_new`; `BULK_ERROR` and `MATCH_ERROR`
`reason_text`; `ERROR` `unknown_variants_store`; the setting's name and help. They say variant and item, never "website product" or
"warehouse product", and "product" not at all (`WordsTest::testNewVariantsSpeaksOfVariantsAndItemsAsTheOwnerDoes` pins it, and that
no store is named). The batch page of a New Variants action says "What: Create as new items" and "Where: New Variants · <store>" in
these words; its shared sentences (the second step of Ignore, the other skips' reasons, "Products ticked") keep the other screens'
words until those are renamed together (U122).

**U138. Not done, and open.** (1) Nothing here brings new variants in: that is each store's connector (built on the proto sites,
switched off) or a load on the server; a nightly read-only refresh of staging's lists was asked of the owner, not built. (2) **No
suggestion is made when a variant arrives** (the computer check is still a batch run on the server, `tools/first_match`). So a variant
that arrives by itself reads "Not checked yet" and the bulk seed does not take it until a check has run and said "new": until a check
on arrival exists (the mapping method's build step 3), "the seed on every store" is the seed of what the last run found new, and
anything else is created one at a time on its own page. **For the main store no run can say "new" at all** (the check compares
another store's list WITH the main store's; `tools/first_match/run.php` refuses the main store as the judged side): there the bulk
seed takes nothing until a check exists that judges main-store variants against the warehouse's items, and the page says so (U135).
Whether a bulk route for new main-store variants is wanted (that check, or the first seed's tool `bin/mint_vpg.php` run again on
the server: by rules only, an item for each published main-store variant that is not matched) is the owner's decision; nothing was
built for it. (3) The check compares a
variant with the main store's list as it was on the day of the run, never with the items made since or with the other ticked
rows. The guards of M61 answer the cases that can be read cheaply (the variant's own item, an exact name read again at each row's
turn, a change of the variant since the check as far as its recorded identity and its judged title show it). What is still open
is written there: under point 7 (a change of brand, attributes or barcodes between a run's export and its import; evidence with
no title) and under "What the name guard does not do" (names that differ, and two creates of one name in the same instant). The
lasting answer is a check that compares with the warehouse's current items, and an import that refuses a run made on other titles. (4) The website's state is known only where features were stored or a check recorded
it (M61); for a variant that arrives by itself CW does not know it. (5) No count on the tab or on the Dashboard, and no note "new
since you last looked". (6) No "create as new items" for a whole filter across pages: a page's ticks, at most `mapping.bulk_max_rows`.
(7) Coming back from the variant's page to this list (By Item's U119) is not built: the brief left it out. (8) The page size, the
three fixed periods, the CSV's 50,000 and the 180 seconds of "heard from lately" (the Stores page's own constant) are not settings.
(9) A search over "Any time" costs what Store Products' search costs (U136). (10) The barcode rule does not see through punctuation
inside a code (M61).

## Products › Mapping: the rows no bulk action takes, and what a list shows (slot `newvar`, 11 Oct 2026)

What was found on staging (read only, 11 Oct 2026): on 10 Oct the owner used the bulk action on Products › Mapping › To review, store
Electrofag, list Strong match: 15 batches of 50 "Confirm match". 234 were matched. The last three batches matched nothing: page 1 of
the list then held only rows every bulk action skips, 47 held back (M30) and 3 matches of the open spot check (M28). "Tick all +
Confirm" on that page was a dead end, and the page did not say why before the button was pressed. The rule itself (M51) is right
and stays; the lists did not show it.
Code: `src/Mapping/OneAtATime.php` (new), `src/Mapping/KeyHold.php` (`IN_FORCE`), `src/Mapping/BulkDecisions.php` (it asks
`OneAtATime`; no rule changed), `src/Ui/QueueContext.php`, `src/Ui/Queries.php` (`SHOWS`, `queue()`, `nextInQueue()`),
`src/Ui/Controller/{Review,Bulk,StoreProducts,NewVariants}Controller.php`, the views `queue`, `store_products`, `new_variants` and
`one_at_a_time` (new), `src/Ui/Words.php` (`QUEUE`, `QUEUE_SHOW`, `ONE_AT_A_TIME`), `public/ui/assets/app.css` (section 21). No
