migration, no setting, no change to `app.js`. Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/OneAtATimeScreenTest.php` and
`tests/Unit/QueueContextTest.php` (new), one test added to each of `tests/Integration/Mapping/BulkDecisionsTest.php`,
`tests/Unit/WordsTest.php` and the HTTP tests `tests/Integration/UiReviewFlowTest.php` (slot `ui`), and the new partial added to the
templates `tests/Unit/UiTemplatesTest.php` lints (its two lists of templates gained the name). No assertion that was there before
had to change. `DecisionService`, `KeyBulk` and Products › By Item are not touched.

**M63. One read of what no bulk action takes.** `OneAtATime::of(db, listing ids)` answers, for each of the listings no bulk action
takes, why, in this order: `held` when a hold is in force on the listing (`KeyHold::activeForListings`), with the hold's reason, who
set it aside and when; else `in_spot_check` when the listing is one of the matches (a `key_sample_member` with a position) of a
spot check whose verdict (`KeySample::verdicts`) is not `complete`, that is waiting or failed, with the spot check's name (the
oldest such spot check when it is a match of several). It also gives the spot check's id and name, for a link.
`BulkDecisions::prechecks()` takes its `held` and `in_spot_check` skips from this read, with the same code and detail as before, in
the same place in its order (after "no such listing" and "another store", before everything else), for every action and every
list; `one()` asks it again under the row's lock (a hold found only then is `held_meanwhile`, as before). What a batch row records
and what the result page says are unchanged. The private `inSpotCheck()` became `OneAtATime::spotChecksOf()`; its read is now
ordered by spot check, so the one named is the same each time. `KeyHold::IN_FORCE` is the one text of "a hold in force" (a hold row
that no release names): KeyHold's own read is built from it, and so is the SQL the lists filter and count by
(`OneAtATime::heldSql()`). For the lists' spot-check side `OneAtATime::spotMatchesToDecide()` gives the variants still to decide
that are a match of a spot check that is not complete: the candidates are read from the spot checks to their matches to each
match's listing, and the answer is `spotChecksOf()` of those candidates, the same function a row is asked with; `spotSql()` names
them to the SQL by their ids (a few dozen numbers). The engine is unchanged: a hand-made form that ticks such a row is skipped as
`held` or `in_spot_check`, on every list.

**U139. Such a row has no tick box and says why.** Every match-strength list of Products › Mapping › To review, Store Products and
New Variants ask `OneAtATime::of()` for the rows of their page. A row it names has an empty tick cell: no box and none of the row's
hidden fields, so the page's form cannot send it. Under its name one line says what it is and what to do (the partial
`one_at_a_time`, `Words::ONE_AT_A_TIME`): `Held back on <day> (set aside by <name>). Open it to see why and to decide it.`, with the
day and the name as the row's own page says them (the job "Matching lead" when the hold names nobody); or `In spot check <name>:
it is answered in the spot check.` followed by the link "Open the spot check". The hold's note is NOT printed on a list (a build
decision of 12 Oct 2026, the reviewer's and not yet put to the owner, from staging's data: the stored notes are the screening rules' own texts, 190 characters typical and up to
480, `rule: [MEDIUM] model_number_differs: model/line numbers: EF - vs VPG 25000 …`, which under 47 rows of a page is neither plain
English nor readable). The variant's own page shows the note in full, as before, and so does the skip sentence of a bulk action's
result page (`BULK_SKIP` `held`), which is unchanged. "Select all on this page" needed no new script: `app.js`
ticks the boxes marked `data-bulk-row` and such a row has none; without the script `all=1` draws a row ticked only when it has a box.
On Store Products and New Variants the line is on the rows of the states a bulk action applies to there (Suggested, Not matched,
Ignored; New, Suggested match, Not checked yet): a matched, on-hold or waiting row had no box before and says nothing new. Someone
who can only look has no boxes, as before, and still reads the line. Products › By Item is unchanged: its preview lists such a
variant as "Will be skipped" with the reason (M56).

**U140. "Show" on a match-strength list.** Under the strength legend: Show · All · Ready for a bulk action · Held back · In a spot
check, each with how many rows it holds of this list, this store and the list's other filters (search, found by, units sold). All
is the list as it was, and the default. The query value is `show` = `ready`, `held` or `spot` (`Queries::SHOWS`); none, `all` or
any other word is All and is then written nowhere, so every address the list had before is unchanged. It is one more part of
`QueueContext` (`show`, `showValue()`), so it travels with `query()` and `pageQuery()`: the pager, a row's link to its page, that
page's way back, the hidden fields of that page's forms and so the address after a decision, and the bulk form's keep fields.
"The next one" follows it (`Queries::nextInQueue()` takes it): from the list of the ready ones the next ready one opens. It is also
kept by the search box (a hidden field), the links of the strength legend and of the store selector (which did not and do not
carry the search, found-by and units filters), the link to the next list with work, the second step of "Not a match…" and
"Ignore…", and a refused request's way back (`BulkController::back()`). The result page of a bulk action leads back to the list
as it was shown: the redirect to the batch page carries `?show=` (a match-strength list's batch only) and the batch page reads it as
the list does, By Item's way (U127); a batch page opened without it leads back to the whole list. Held back is
`OneAtATime::heldSql()`; In a spot check is `spotSql()` and not held back; Ready is neither. So the three never overlap and add up
to All. "Clear filters" clears it too; a choice that hides every row shows "No website product matches your filters" with the
choices still there. An empty list offers no choice. It changes what is listed, never what a bulk action does.
After the last row of what a list is showing, the list is not called done: when the answer saved was the last one of a list that is
narrowed (`QueueContext::filtered()`: a choice of Show, found by, units sold or a search), the notice is `shown_done`, "That was the
last one of what this list is showing.", and the page below it says what is left (the choices with their numbers, or "No website
product matches your filters" with "Clear filters"). `queue_done`, "This list is done.", stays for a list nothing narrows. (Before
this build the found-by, units and search filters ended on "This list is done." too; with Show > Held back it would have been the
ordinary end of the owner's routine.)
The counts (`Queries::queue()` returns them as `shows`): the list's own count is read once, as before, and is All; the held-back
rows are counted from `key_bulk_hold` (the holds in force, each joined to its open suggestion and its listing) and the spot checks'
rows from the listing ids of `spotMatchesToDecide()`; Ready is All less those two. The total of the page shown is one of these four
numbers: no second count of the list is made. A list with no row reads none of it.

**U141. The notice above the list, and a page with nothing to tick.** When the page shown holds rows with no tick box, and this
person has a bulk action on this list, one box above the list says so and leads on: "47 on this page are held back and 3 are in a
spot check: they are decided one at a time and have no tick box." and the link "Show only the ones a bulk action can take (863)"
to the same list with Ready for a bulk action (the count is that list's). It has its singular forms; when nothing is ready it says
"Nothing in this list is ready for a bulk action." in place of the link; on the list of the ready ones it has no link to itself.
A page whose every row has a box has no notice. When NO row of the page can be ticked (the page the owner was stuck on) the
action bar, the tick column and "Select all on this page" are not drawn on that page: its buttons could only answer "Tick at least
one product first".

**U142. What it costs; no index.** Measured on the slot's test schema filled like staging (38,040 variants, 15,000 items, 2,638
open suggestions of which 1,116 strong matches of one store; a spot check that waits with 20 matches there, 300 holds of which 260
in force, a second spot check that waits on another store, a third whose matches were decided long ago), MySQL 8.4.8 with its 32
MB buffer pool. The script ran six times that evening, each case three times in a run. The first two runs still had an EXISTS for
the spot checks' side of the filter, which MySQL answered by reading the spot checks' whole populations (`ready_explain_try2.txt`);
that form was dropped for the listing ids of `spotMatchesToDecide()`, and the figures below are from the four runs made after
that. The cluster's times vary a lot, so each figure is the lowest, the middle and the highest of those twelve
(`/root/cw_work/runs/ready_explain.txt` is the last run with every SQL and its EXPLAIN, `ready_explain_try3.txt` to `_try5.txt`
the three before it, in the first two of which the candidates of `spotMatchesToDecide()` were still read in one statement, 2 ms
either way; the script is `ready_explain_script.php` there and is not in the repository). The change of 12 Oct (the held line's
words, the notice after the last row) touches none of these reads and was not measured again:
- the rows of a page (`OneAtATime::of()`, 50 rows): 5 / 6 / 26 ms, two reads of about 2 ms each (the holds by their listing, the
  spot checks' matches by their listing); 17 / 22 / 95 ms when the page shows a spot check's match, because that spot check's
  verdict is then worked out (KeySample's five reads). The same read for 100 ticked rows before a bulk action: 7 / 11 / 26 ms (the
  two reads the pre-checks made before);
- the spot checks' matches a list names (`spotMatchesToDecide()`, two spot checks that wait): 21 / 31 / 120 ms. Its own three reads
  take about 1, 2 and 2 ms; the rest is KeySample's verdict of the two spot checks;
- a list page (`Queries::queue()`, 1,116 rows, page 1): All 38 / 63 / 86 ms, Ready for a bulk action 46 / 56 / 130 ms, Held back
  41 / 54 / 149 ms, In a spot check 28 / 56 / 95 ms. By statement (the middle of the four runs): the list's own count 8-13 ms and
  its page of ids 21-26 ms, both as before; the held-back count 6-11 ms (it reads the 340 hold rows); the spot checks' count 4-7 ms
  (it starts from the 40 listings named); the page's rows 5-7 ms, as before. With "sold at least" 43 / 51 / 127 ms, with a search
  57 / 65 / 387 ms (the list's own count reads the profiles, as before), with "found by" 52 / 141 / 601 ms (the suggestions' rows
  are read, as before). An empty list: one read, 1 / 3 / 8 ms;
- "the next one": 13 / 18 / 35 ms for every row (as before), 21 / 23 / 28 ms of the ready ones, 16 / 18 / 38 ms of the held-back
  ones, 5 / 7 / 9 ms of a spot check's.
With about ten times more of both (2,371 hold rows of which 2,291 in force, 676 of them on that list; 11 spot checks that wait, 220
matches): the spot checks' matches 104 / 164 / 431 ms (11 verdicts), the rows of a page 50 / 65 / 182 ms, the list page All 55 / 64
/ 343 ms, Ready 58 / 107 / 182 ms, Held back 55 / 86 / 157 ms, "the next ready one" 29 / 34 / 60 ms. So the cost follows the number
of spot checks that are not complete and the number of holds, not the size of the lists.
What a page of the All list reads on top of what it read before (about 45 ms on the first fill), by the middle figures: the two
counts (about 15 ms), the spot checks' matches (about 30 ms for the two spot checks that wait) and the answer for its rows (about
6 ms). The old code was not timed on this fill: "before" is the sum of the statements that did not change.
No index was added. Every read is by an existing index: the holds by their listing (`ix_key_bulk_hold_listing`) or read whole for
the count (the table is the small side: 340 rows there), a hold's release by `uq_key_bulk_hold_release`, a spot check's matches by
`uq_key_sample_member_position` (one range of 20 for each spot check) or by their listing (`ix_key_sample_member_listing`), the
open suggestion by `ix_match_proposal_open_band` (status, band, listing: the index alone), the listing by its primary key. No plan
reads a spot check's population or passes over the list or `listing_profile` for the two new counts, with two exceptions the
list's own count already had: with a search the counts read the profiles of the rows they count (a few hundred, where the list's
count reads the whole strength), and with "found by" they read the suggestions' rows.

## The check on arrival, build 1: matches by barcode and copied address (slot `newvar`, 12 Oct 2026)

The owner, 11-12 Oct 2026: "do the check on arrival next". Until now a variant arrived with no suggestion and stayed "Not checked
yet" until a developer ran the one-off first match; 6,391 of Electrofag's variants were in that state on staging (104 with a barcode
on exactly one item, 1,167 with a web address copied from a main-store variant, 5,120 with neither). This build is the safe half of
the design (`/root/cw_work/Arrival_check_design_2026-10-12.md`, rules version ar1.0), as the build's scope cut it
(`Arrival_check_build1_2026-10-12.md`): a never-touched variant whose barcode or copied web address points at an item gets a
suggestion. "New: nothing like it", the name search and the website's state are build 2 and are not started. Whose choice each
thing is, is said where it is said: the owner's rules are quoted; the scope's choices are "the build's" (made by the orchestrating
session, not yet put to the owner); the rest was settled while building and is marked so.
Code: `migrations/0027_arrival_check.sql`, `src/Matching/ArrivalRules.php` and `src/Mapping/ArrivalCheck.php` (new),
`bin/check_arrivals.php` (new), `src/Mapping/ListingIngestService.php` (the mark), `src/Mapping/OneAtATime.php`,
`src/Mapping/BulkDecisions.php` (the skip code and the read under the lock; no rule of a decision changed),
`src/Mapping/KeySample.php` (`NOT_A_MATCHING_RUN`), `src/Settings.php` (`RULES`), `src/Ui/Queries.php`,
`src/Ui/Controller/{Review,NewVariants}Controller.php`, the views `one_at_a_time` and `new_variants`, `src/Ui/Words.php`,
`deploy/staging/cw-staging.cron` and `install_cron.sh`. Not touched: `Proposals`, `ProposalBasis`, `DecisionService`, `Band`, `Veto`,
`Candidates`, `Normalizer`, `Gtin`, `StoredBand`, `Reband`, `KeyEligibility`, `KeyBulk`, `Stock`, `Reservations`, the API,
`Grants` (no new table), both hashes of a profile, `fromExport()`, `seedCheck()` / `nameChecks()`, `tools/first_match`, the other
tools, `app.css`, `app.js`. Tests: `tests/Integration/Migration0027Test.php`, `tests/Unit/ArrivalRulesTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/Mapping/ArrivalCheckTest.php`, `tests/Support/ArrivalFixtures.php` (new); added to `ListingIngestTest`,
`BulkDecisionsTest`, `KeyBulkTest`, `OneAtATimeScreenTest`, `NewVariantsScreenTest`, `WordsTest`, `QueueContextTest`, `DeployTest`,
and one op (`check_arrivals`) to `tests/Support/op_worker.php`.

**M64. When the check runs, who it looks at, what it never does.**
*When.* The listing intake (`ListingIngestService`, the push and the import alike) only leaves a mark on the profile, in the
statements it runs anyway: `arrival_state = 'queued'`, `arrival_seq + 1`, `arrival_channel_id`, when a profile is created, when its
identity changed and when its web address changed (the three things the rules read). A push that changes none of them marks
nothing. No suggestion is made inside the intake's transaction: a suggestion takes the feed clock as the last lock of its
transaction, and the intake holds up to 1,000 profile locks. The check itself is `bin/check_arrivals.php` and nothing else: no web
or API request runs it. One cron line (`*/10 * * * *`, `--apply`) takes the QUEUED variants of the stores named in
`mapping.arrival_stores`; with no store named it logs "switched off" and exits 0. The variants that were there before the check
(mark NULL) are never taken by the timer: only a hand run with `--backfill --channel=<code>` looks at them, and it marks each
`done` in that run, so they are never queued for the timer either. A store whose queue is above `mapping.arrival_queue_alarm` is
left by the timer's form (no `--channel`) for a hand run that names it: a whole store that was just loaded is not drained by the
timer. (Settled while building: the alarm applies to the form without `--channel`; a run that names a store takes its queue.)
*Who.* `Proposals::add()` supersedes whatever suggestion is open without asking, so the refusals are the check's own, made twice:
before the rules (`ArrivalCheck::look()`, no lock), and again under `SELECT … FROM channel_listing WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE` just
before `add()` (`write()`). A variant gets a suggestion only when all of this holds; the first that does not is recorded on its
profile (`arrival_outcome`): its store is in the setting; it is `unmapped`, or `suggested` by the check's own untouched suggestion
(`not_open`); no hold is in force on it (`held`); it is in no spot check, as a match or in a population (`in_spot_check`); it has
no suggestion of any state from another run, no decision other than the check's own `suggest` (so none waiting for a second
person, no ignore, no un-match, no "sent back", no "not a match") and no `match_reject` row (`has_history`); its profile has a
title (`no_title`); and under the lock its identity, its web address, its mark's number and its own open suggestion are the ones
the rules read: if not, nothing is written and it stays queued. The owner's rule (facts file): "DO NOT replace or close the open
suggestion of a variant that is in a spot check or held back". The setting the design had for "wait while a store has a spot check
to answer" is not built (the build's choice: the refusals above already keep the check away from every spot-check member, every
held variant and every variant with any history). (Settled while building: the outcomes are asked in the order state, hold, spot
check, other history, title, so the recorded outcome names the check that stopped it; the store is checked for the run, not again
under each variant's lock: a store taken out of the setting is left from the next run.)
*What it never does.* It writes Likely (`Check`), Not sure (`Can't tell`) or Clues disagree (`Conflict`), never Strong (`Key`),
Renamed range (`Manual`) or New item: `ArrivalRules::BANDS` is all it can say. It never writes an `ai` block, so
`StoredBand::inputs()` cannot read its evidence and a suggestion of it enters no spot check, no Key bulk confirm and no re-band
(`Reband` skips it as `unknown_band_version`: its run names no band version, in `engine_version` or in `detail`). Its run sources
are in `KeySample::NOT_A_MATCHING_RUN`: a run of it does not unlock an override of a failed spot check. It never confirms,
matches, ignores or creates: its caller is a system caller, which `DecisionService` lets only `suggest`. It never names an item
that was joined into another (`DecisionService::rootOf`). It never replaces anything but its own untouched suggestion. It never
locks a profile row inside its transaction (the intake locks profile, then listing; the check locks the listing and reads the
profile without a lock; its mark is a compare-and-set on `arrival_seq` in a statement of its own after the commit), and it adds no
lock after the feed clock, which `add()` takes through the `suggest` (`add()` itself then inserts the suggestion's basis, whose
foreign keys take share locks on the item and the target's listing: that is `Proposals::add()` for every import, unchanged; a
deadlock there rolls the variant's whole transaction back and `Db::transaction` runs it again, refusals included). It never
deletes, and it never scans a big table (the reads are listed under U144). A dry run (no `--apply`) writes nothing at all: no
suggestion, no mark, no run row, no audit row. A real run that looked at anything writes ONE audit row, `mapping.arrival_check`,
with its counts per store.
*Its own suggestion* is looked at again when the variant is marked again. The same answer: nothing is written (the older
suggestion and its basis stay as they are). Another answer: a new suggestion supersedes it; the variant stays `suggested`, with no
second `suggest`. No clue any more: it is replaced by a Not sure that names no item and says why (`arrival_no_longer`); a stale
one is never left open, and that Not sure is not written again at every later look. Once a person has touched the variant (a "not
a match" that leaves the suggestion open, say) it has a history and the check leaves it. A later judged run supersedes a
rules-only suggestion like any other: that is wanted.
*Two run rows* (settled while building, because of E below). A run that writes makes its `match_run` rows when it first needs
them, inside the transaction of that first suggestion (a rolled-back variant leaves no run row): one of source `arrival` for its
clean matches and one of source `arrival_warned` for everything else, under one run id `arrival-<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>` (the
unique key is (run_id, source)); a new pair for every run, because one run row holds one suggestion per variant for ever. So
"found by the check on arrival" and, of those, "with a warning" are told from the run alone, without a suggestion's flags.

**M65. The rules of build 1 (`CW\Matching\ArrivalRules`, pure, version `ar1.0`).** Two clues and nothing else. The BARCODE: the
variant's usable barcodes, by the strict cleaner of the barcode sync (`BarcodeSync::keys`: no junk, no in-store numbers), are on
an item through the item's own barcode records (`sku_barcode`) or through a variant matched to it (`listing_profile.barcodes`, the
multi-valued index of 0005; every text the code may be stored as, `Gtin::forms`); not through a variant whose item people ruled
the barcode away from (a removal, a barcode review: "The review of build 1" below, C). The ADDRESS: its web address equals a
main-store variant's (`permaKey()`, character for character `tools/first_match/run.php`'s: trimmed, lower case, no closing slash);
the address rule compares WITH `mapping.arrival_main_store` and is never applied TO a variant of it, which can still get a barcode
answer. An item the clues name is compared with the variant by `Veto::check`, both sides normalised afresh from their profiles
(stored features lack the words the comparison reads), with `s_strength_sibling` always on, so "Strength not stated" fires
whenever the variant states no strength and the item has one: stricter than the batch run, on purpose. The item's side is its
representative variant: its origin variant while that is still matched to it, else its lowest matched main-store variant, else its
lowest matched variant.
The answers, the first that applies (settled while building: a Conflict before a Not sure, a Not sure before a match; the design's
table gave the lines, not their order):

| The facts | Strength | Item named | Reason (a key of `Words::BAND_REASON`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| the barcode is on two or more items, or on a barcode record marked not usable | Clues disagree | none | `arrival_barcode_two_items` |
| the barcode is on another variant of the same store | Clues disagree | none | `arrival_barcode_same_store` |
| the barcode and the address point at different things | Clues disagree | none | `arrival_clues_differ` |
| an item is named, and a hard veto says it cannot be that item | Clues disagree | closest only | `veto_on_key` (the codes in `evidence.target_vetoes`) |
| an item is named by a barcode recorded as more than one unit a scan, or (with no barcode record of the item's own) carried by a variant matched with more than one unit a sale | Not sure | closest only | `arrival_barcode_pack` |
| an item is named by an address whose main-store variant is matched with more than one unit a sale | Not sure | closest only | `arrival_copy_pack` |
| an item is named, and another variant of the same store is matched to it, waits for a second OK to be, or has it suggested | Not sure | closest only | `arrival_item_taken` |
| an item is named, and only a pending range rename stands between the two (`Band::ALIAS_PENDING_FLAGS`) | Not sure | closest only | `arrival_renamed_range` |
| the barcode is only on variants that have no item | Not sure | none | `arrival_barcode_no_item` |
| the address is on several items | Not sure | none | `arrival_copy_several` |
| the address is only on main-store variants that have no item | Not sure | none | `arrival_copy_no_item` |
| an item is named, with a soft flag of the engine, or an address several variants share that the one with an item settles, or a barcode that is also on a main-store variant with no item, or nothing to compare the item with (`arrival_not_compared`) | Likely | the item | the clue's, with the flag `arrival_warned` |
| barcode and address name the same item, nothing against it | Likely | the item | `arrival_barcode_and_copy` |
| the barcode is on exactly one item, nothing against it | Likely | the item | `arrival_barcode` |
| the address is exactly one item's main-store variant, nothing against it | Likely | the item | `arrival_copy` |
| no barcode on anything and no copied address | no suggestion | | outcome `no_clue` |

Every suggestion carries the flag `rules_only`; everything but a clean match also `arrival_warned`. "The two clues point at
different things" is told as the batch run tells it (its flag `barcode_transfer_disagree`): two items; or one clue names an item
and the other's variants are not that item's and do not carry the barcode. A barcode that is also on a variant of a third store
with no item is no warning (two stores' copies of one new thing); only on such variants, it is a Not sure. Two things the design
did not have (settled while building): `arrival_not_compared`, for an item with no matched variant to compare with (a match that
could not be checked is a warned one, never a clean one); and a barcode shared by more than 200 other variants counts as "on two
or more items" without being read further. NOT in this build, by the build's choice: the name search (a variant with no clue gets
NO suggestion and the outcome `no_clue`), "New: nothing like it" (the check never writes New item, and the seed is untouched), and
the website's state (the answers above are written whatever the state: a match makes nothing).

**U144. The screens, the words and the reads.**
*No dead end on the lists* (the build's choice, in place of the design's "block only the ticked confirm": the owner had just had
"tick all + Confirm does nothing" fixed, M63). While `mapping.arrival_bulk_confirm` is off, a variant whose open suggestion the
check made is a third kind of row no bulk action takes: `OneAtATime::of()` answers `on_arrival` for it, after `held` and
`in_spot_check`; `BulkDecisions::prechecks()` skips it for every action and list with that code (`BULK_SKIP` / `BY_ITEM_SKIP`:
"Its suggestion was found by the check on arrival, and no AI has looked at it: open it to check and decide."), and `one()` asks
again under the row's lock, of the suggestion the row named whatever the decision has just made of it
(`OneAtATime::arrivalSuggestion()`: a confirm closes the suggestion and `of()` reads only an open one, so a setting switched
off while a batch runs would otherwise not be seen); on the three lists of variants the row has no tick box and one line under its name, "Found by the
check on arrival: no AI has looked at it. Open it to check and decide.". With the setting on, a clean match is an ordinary row
that can be ticked and confirmed; one with a warning, a Not sure and a Clues disagree stay one at a time whatever the setting. The
match-strength lists' "Show" gains a fifth choice, **Found on arrival**, with its count; "Ready for a bulk action" leaves these
rows out, so "Ready + tick all + Confirm match skips none of the kinds" still holds, and All is the sum of the four parts. The
fifth choice is offered only on a list where it holds a row (or while it is the one chosen): with nothing found by the check, the
lists, their counts, their addresses and their statements are the ones of before (settled while building). The notice above a list
names the third kind beside the other two ("2 on this page are held back, 1 is in a spot check and 3 were found by the check on
arrival: …"). The rows are told BY THEIR RUN: `OneAtATime::arrivalRuns()` gives the run rows of the check that still have an open
suggestion (both sources while the setting is off, `arrival_warned` only while it is on), and both the row's answer and the
lists' SQL (`arrivalSql()`: `p.match_run_id IN (…)`) take those numbers, so a row and its filter cannot disagree. For that the
migration adds the index `match_proposal (match_run_id, status, band, lane, listing_id)` (settled while building: the table had
its run column and the unique key (match_run_id, listing_id), which holds neither status nor strength, so a count would have read
every suggestion a run ever made).
*The variant's page.* A suggestion with the flag `rules_only` says what the strength means without "the AI thinks"
(`BAND_HELP_RULES`), its reasons in words ("Its barcode is on this item"), and the warnings about the clue itself beside the
engine's. Nothing is preselected.
*New Variants.* The chip and the filter "Not checked yet" read **No suggestion**: the old words stopped being true the day a
check could look and find nothing. Under such a row one line says why, from the mark the check left (`ARRIVAL_LEFT`): the check is
switched off for the store; it was here before the check; "Waiting for the check on arrival."; "The check on arrival found no
barcode and no copied web address for it: open it to decide."; "A person or an earlier computer check has dealt with it, so the
check on arrival leaves it: open it to decide."; and the like. A row the check suggested for says the strength, the item (or the
closest one) and the reason in words. The box at the top says whether the check is on for the store, how many variants wait and
what its last run did there. The sentences that promised "the next computer check, which suggests again" for a variant sent back
(two bulk texts) and Home's "Nothing to do now: they come in the next computer check." are corrected: the check on arrival leaves
a variant a person sent back. The skip sentence and the seed's note that said "not checked yet" say "nothing is suggested" / "no
suggestion" (settled while building, for the same reason). `AUDIT_ACTION` names `mapping.arrival_check`.
*Not done here* (build 2 or later): the words for New and "state not known", "Name search" for the lane, a "Check now" button, a
runs page, a line on Home; Store Products and New Variants have the row treatment only (no "Show", as before).
*The reads* (EXPLAIN and three timings of each on a fill of staging's size, 38,000 variants: `/root/cw_work/runs/arrival_explain.txt`).
One variant: its listing and its profile by primary key; the holds, the spot-check memberships, the suggestions, the decisions and
the rejects by their listing indexes; `sku_barcode` by its key; the other variants with the barcode by the multi-valued index of
0005; the main-store variants with the address by `ix_listing_profile_perma_key` (the index compares without letter case: a
superset, and `permaKey()` in PHP decides); the item, its origin listing and, only when that is not matched to it, one range of
`channel_listing (sku_id, channel_id)`; "is the item taken" by that index, by `match_proposal (status, proposed_sku_id, …)` and by
the pending decisions. The queue and its count: `ix_listing_profile_arrival` alone. A backfill: `channel_listing (channel_id,
status)` in id order, each profile by its primary key. The lists: the runs by the first letters of their name on `uq_match_run`,
each asked on the new index for one open suggestion; the count and the page of "Found on arrival" from the new index and each
listing's primary key.

**U145. Settings (Settings › Matching products; all provisional, the design's recommended defaults, for the owner to confirm).**
`mapping.arrival_stores` (store codes, empty = switched off: the check ships off), `mapping.arrival_main_store` (`vapeandgo`),
`mapping.arrival_bulk_confirm` (off), `mapping.arrival_max_per_run` (200; 1 to 5,000), `mapping.arrival_max_seconds` (45; 5 to
600), `mapping.arrival_queue_alarm` (300; 1 to 100,000). Each has its baseline in `config_change`, its bounds in
`Settings::RULES`, its name and its help in `Words::SETTING` / `SETTING_HELP`. The command-line options `--limit` and
`--max-seconds` exist for hand runs only. No store's code is written in the code; no setting's number is printed on a screen. The
other settings of the design (the New switches, the name search, the state's age, "wait for a spot check") are not in this build.

**The migration, and what the database server really does** (settled while building; `Migration0027Test`,
`/root/cw_work/runs/arrival_probe_ddl*.log`). The design asked for `ALGORITHM = INSTANT`. On staging's database server (MySQL
8.4.8, a managed build) that word is accepted and the table is rebuilt all the same (a new table id and tablespace, no row
version), for a plain column on a plain table too; and `listing_profile` has the multi-valued barcode index of 0005, with which
MySQL refuses to add any column in place, and, asked for INSTANT, copies the table without saying so (rows affected = every row).
So nothing but a copy adds a column to this table here, and 0027 copies it once and says so: ONE statement (the five columns of
the mark, the VIRTUAL `perma_key`, both indexes), `ALGORITHM = COPY, LOCK = SHARED`. Reads go on while it runs; a write to
`listing_profile` (a push, an import) waits for it. On a scratch table of staging's size (38,000 profiles, 120 MB) it took 9
seconds alone and 17 seconds while one connection read and another wrote without pause (2,716 reads, the slowest 0.6 s; the one
write that met it waited the 17 s and went through). Every later column on this table will cost the same while that index is
there (build 2's website state: put its columns in one statement too). The index on `match_proposal` is added in place and online
(`INPLACE, LOCK = NONE`; the table is not rebuilt: the test holds its id). The alternative that copies nothing, the mark in a small
table of its own, was not taken: the build's scope names the columns and "no new table" (`Grants` untouched), and the intake would
have needed a second statement for every profile.

**Open, and for the reviewer first.** (1) The copy above: 9 to 17 seconds during which a listing push waits. No store pushes to
staging today (every store is `off`). (2) `Proposals::add()` inserts the basis after the feed clock (above): unchanged, and the
check's write is retried whole on a deadlock. (3) A suggestion kept because the answer is the same keeps its old basis and evidence
title although the variant's identity moved; nothing in build 1 reads those for a match (the seed's "changed since the check" is
for New only). Build 2 must write a fresh suggestion when the identity moved, or a New would read "changed" for ever. (4) The
score's T2 counts "match" only where the rules offer the item; an item that another variant of the store already has reads Not
sure there too, which is the rule. (5) Settled in the review below (fix B): `BulkDecisions::one()` now asks for the third kind of
the suggestion the row named, and a test forces the setting to be switched while a batch waits on the row.

### The review of build 1 (12 Oct 2026, on the tree of `678bf3d`)

Four reviewers, each with one question (can it replace anything but its own untouched suggestion; does it write only when and
where it may; is what the rules write right and harmless; can a row and its filter, count, tick box or skip disagree), then a
refuter on every finding. No critical finding: no path replaces a person's decision or another run's suggestion, a dry run writes
nothing, the timer takes only queued rows, nothing is ever Strong, Manual or New. Each of the 21 mutations of the build was then
applied alone and killed by its own test (`/root/cw_work/runs/arrival_mutations_2.log`).

**The index order, measured.** A last change before the review led `ix_match_proposal_run_open` with `status` and read the
check's runs from the open suggestions. Its tests passed, and its plans were worse: the lists' own reads that main already had
(`status = 'open' AND band = ?`) left `ix_match_proposal_open_band` (only that strength's rows) for the new index with the
status alone (every open suggestion), and no read got faster (`arrival_explain2.txt`). It was taken back whole: the index is
(`match_run_id`, `status`, `band`, `lane`, `listing_id`) and `arrivalRuns()` asks each run of the check once. The cost of that
choice is under "Left" (the run list).

**Fixed (each with a test that failed first).**
- **A. The tool reads its command line whole or refuses it.** `getopt()` drops a word it does not know and goes on: `--apply=false`
  was an apply, a misspelt or empty `--channel` left the timer's form (every store of the setting), `--backfill=0` was a backfill,
  a second `--db` fell back to the default schema (seen on staging's PHP 8.3.6). `Ops\Cli::unreadable()` names the first such
  word and `Cli::main(..., strict: true)` ends with the usage and exit 2 before anything is connected to. Only
  `bin/check_arrivals.php` asks for it; the other jobs read their options as before. `Unit\CliOptionsTest`, the tool test.
- **B. A batch and the switch.** Above (U144, Open 5). `ArrivalCheckTest::testATickedBatchLeavesAMatchOfTheCheckOnceTheSettingIsSwitchedOffWhileItRuns`.
- **C. People's barcode rulings bind the barcode clue (M65).** A barcode a person took off an item stays on the profile of that
  item's variant, and the check found the item through the variant; a barcode a review gave to one of two items read "on more
  than one item" for ever. Now a matched variant that carries the barcode does not name its item when, for every barcode the two
  share, the item has no barcode record of its own for it and the latest decided `barcode_review` of (barcode, the variant's
  item) keeps it away (`BarcodeReviews::KEEPS_AWAY`, the read the barcode sync and the seeder make). Such a variant counts as one
  that carries the barcode and has no item. A record of the item's own wins over an older ruling. Known limit, the sync's own: a
  ruling made for an item that was joined into another since is not found. The batch tool (`tools/first_match`) reads no
  barcode ruling at all; that is older than this build and unchanged.
- **D. A clue through a pack (M65; settled while building, past the letter of the design's "pack" line and on the safe side).** A
  suggestion carries no units, so a confirm links one unit a sale. A barcode carried by a variant matched with more than one
  unit a sale, when no barcode record of the item's own says what it stands for, is the "pack" line; an address whose main-store
  variant is matched with more than one unit a sale is Not sure, closest only, with the new reason `arrival_copy_pack`. On
  staging no variant is matched with units other than 1 today, and no barcode ruling is decided: neither C nor D changes an
  answer there yet.

**Refuted.** A push that changes only the web address while the check writes: the end state is the one of "check, then push"
(the suggestion made on what was read, the variant marked to check again), which the lock test pins on purpose.

**Left, each confirmed and minor (for build 2 or a small follow-up; none lets a bulk action take a row it must not).**
(1) The check's own suggestion stays open when the variant loses its title. (2) The roll-back after `add()` and the time cap are
run by no test; the second refusal is not tested with the check's own suggestion open and a person acting in between. (3) A run
that dies in `mark()` leaves its suggestions without the run's audit record. (4) The queue alarm counts variants the check can
only leave (a matched variant that changed), and a store named for the first time starts with whatever queued since the deploy.
(5) `install_cron.sh` copies the code before it migrates (older than this build): a listing push in that gap fails. (6) A store
code that is no store is accepted by the settings and then ignored; for `mapping.arrival_main_store` that marks every
address-only variant `done` with no word, and nothing looks at a `done` variant again (no "check again" option exists yet). (7)
A barcode match whose address is shared by several main-store variants loses the "shared" warning. (8) A dry run counts two
matches where an apply writes one match and one Not sure (the second variant of a store for one item). (9) `bin/mint_vpg.php`
refuses a main-store variant that holds an open suggestion of the check. (10) With `mapping.arrival_bulk_confirm` on, a clean
row is tagged "found by the check on arrival" and is not in "Found on arrival": name the choice by what it holds before the
setting is switched on. (11) The list of run ids `arrivalRuns()` hands to the lists grows by two for every run that writes and
shrinks only as people decide: do a backfill in few large runs; if it ever reaches hundreds, tell the kind by a join. (12) The
box above New Variants shows the last run that looked at anything in any store. (13) Four lane flags that alone make a match
"warned" have no words (`transfer_ambiguous`, `transfer_target_not_in_seed`, `transfer_resolved_by_seed`,
`gtin_target_not_in_seed`): the page says a detail needs a look and not which. (14) Home and Mapping › To review still say "Not
checked by the computer yet" where New Variants says "No suggestion". (15) A dry run's `--list` lines say `written`.

## The check on arrival, build 2a: the website state (slot `newvar`, 12 Oct 2026)

"New: nothing like it" lets a person make an item with one click, so it needs to know whether the variant is on sale on its
website and whether it is a page heading. Until now the warehouse knew that only for the variants a one-off matching run had
looked at (inside `listing_profile.features`, wiped by any identity change); a variant that arrived by itself had no state, the
stores' connector does not send one, and the seed's rule for it was "known from neither: skips nothing". The orchestrating
session cut build 2 of the design (`/root/cw_work/Arrival_check_design_2026-10-12.md`) in two; this is 2a, as its scope cut it
(`Arrival_check_build2a_2026-10-12.md`): the state is stored, loaded for the variants that are there, and read by the seed. It
suggests nothing new by itself. The name search and "New" are build 2b and are not started. Whose choice each thing is: the
owner's rules are quoted; the scope's choices are "the build's" (the orchestrating session's, not yet put to the owner); what
was settled while building is marked so.
Code: `migrations/0028_arrival_site_state.sql`, `src/Mapping/SiteState.php` (new), `src/Mapping/ListingIngestService.php`,
`bin/import_listings.php`, `src/Mapping/BulkDecisions.php` (`seedCheck()`, `prechecks()`), `src/Mapping/ArrivalCheck.php` (the
evidence and the snapshot; no rule), `src/Ui/Queries.php`, `src/Ui/Controller/NewVariantsController.php`, `src/Ui/Words.php`,
`src/Settings.php` (`RULES`). Not touched: `Proposals`, `ProposalBasis`, `DecisionService`, `Band`, `Veto`, `Candidates`,
`Normalizer` (asked, never changed), `Gtin`, `DuplicateSweep*`, `StoredBand`, `Reband`, `KeyEligibility`, `KeyBulk`, `Stock`,
`Reservations`, `ArrivalRules` (`ar1.0` stays), `OneAtATime`, `Grants` (no new table), the band ENUM, the `IDENTITY` list and
both hashes, `fromExport()`, `tools/first_match`, `bin/import_proposals.php`, `bin/mint_vpg.php`, `bin/sync_barcodes.php`,
migrations 0001 to 0027, the API layer, the stores' connector, `app.css`, `app.js`, every view. Tests:
`tests/Integration/Migration0028Test.php`, `tests/Unit/SiteStateTest.php` (new); added to `ListingIngestTest`, `ImportToolsTest`,
`BulkDecisionsTest`, `ArrivalCheckTest`, `NewVariantsScreenTest`, `BulkScreensTest`, `WordsTest`, `UiReviewFlowTest`, and one
helper (`siteState()`) to `tests/Support/MappingTestCase.php`.

**M66. The website state: where it lives, who writes it, who reads it, in which order.**
*Where.* Eight columns of `listing_profile` (0028), the raw inputs as the website gives them: `site_variant_status`,
`site_product_status`, `site_product_type`, `site_product_id`, `site_is_landing`, `site_is_default`, `site_product_link`, and ONE
date for all seven, `site_state_at` (as of when they were true). Each is NULL until known. Not in `features` (an identity change
wipes those, and a half-filled object breaks the item-card reader), not in the identity (`IDENTITY`) and in neither hash: a state
never makes a push look changed, never wipes the features and never moves a `map_version`. One index, on the product's number.
*Who writes it.* Only the listing intake (`ListingIngestService`), with what its caller supplies. (1) A push may carry the
optional object `website` (`variant_status`, `product_status`, `product_type`, `product_id`, `is_landing`, `is_default`,
`product_link`; not `site`, the word an export line uses for its store's code). It is read leniently (`SiteState::parse()`): a
value of the wrong type, or one that cannot be what it says, is ignored and counted in the audit row (`website_ignored`), never
a 400; something that is no object at all is ignored whole. No store sends it yet, and the stores' connector is not changed. The
API layer hands a pushed listing to the intake whole, so nothing had to be let through there. (2) `bin/import_listings.php` adds
it from the export line (`SiteState::fromExport()`; `fromExport()` of the intake is as its test pins it), dated with
`--exported-at`, else the time in the file's name. The state is attached to a profile AFTER both hashes are made
(`ListingIngestTest` pins both hashes to the values of before the check on arrival, with and without `website`). It is written in
the statement the intake runs anyway, in each of its three branches (created, changed, unchanged), and its date is moved on even
when it says the same. (3) The state-only load (below).
*Settled while building, about what is written.* A supplied state is WHOLE: what the object leaves out is not known from then
on, never kept from an older state under the new date (one date covers all seven values). An object with nothing usable in it
supplies no state: the stored one stays and grows old by itself. A state OLDER than the stored one is not written and is counted
(`website_older`): an old export loaded after a newer state must not put old values back; the cost is that going back to an
older file on purpose means clearing the columns by hand. An import of a file that has no date (no time in its name, no
`--exported-at`) works as before and writes NO state (`state_at=not_dated`): a state with no date is no state.
*The queue.* Two rules are added to the three of the mark (created, identity, address): a state that changed FROM A KNOWN VALUE
(one of the six values the readers use; not the product's address, which nothing reads yet) marks the profile "to check"
whatever its mark was; a state that was not known before marks it only when the profile already carries a mark. So the first
load of the state marks none of the 38,000 variants that were there before the check. In this build the check's rules do not
read the state, so a variant queued for its state gets the same answer again and nothing is written; the rule is here for 2b.
*Who reads it, in which order* (`SiteState::read()`, the one reader; the three SQL reads that named the features now select the
columns too: `BulkDecisions::prechecks()`, `Queries::newVariantRows()`, `Queries::barcodeElsewhere()`). (1) The stored columns:
a profile with a date has a stored state, and that is THE state, with what it does not know; the other two are not mixed into it.
(2) Else the stored features of a matching run (`variant_status`, `is_placeholder`). (3) Else what the open suggestion recorded
when the computer checked the variant (its evidence's `variant_status`). (4) None of the three: not known. One thing is still
asked of (2) and (3) beside a stored state, by the seed and by New Variants only: what they say AGAINST the variant
(`SiteState::against()`; "The review of build 2a" below, F1, which changed this on purpose).
*Not known is a state.* A missing value is never read as "on sale" and never as "not a page heading". A stored state older than
the setting `mapping.arrival_state_max_days` (30 days; 1 to 365; Settings › Matching products; provisional, for the owner to
confirm) reads as not known. A state from (2) or (3) has no date: it is neither fresh nor old and is relied on exactly as before
the columns were there, so nothing changes for the rows a matching run judged until their store's state is loaded.
*The page heading* of a stored state is the Normalizer's own answer: `SiteState::heading()` hands `Normalizer::normalize()` the
stored inputs (landing row, the product's type, default variant), the profile's titles, barcodes and units sold in the month,
and the number of published variants of the same product on the same store, counted from the database
(`SiteState::publishedSiblings()`, the new index, each row's listing by its primary key for the store), and returns its
`is_placeholder`. `SiteState` knows no part of the rule (`SiteStateTest` compares the two over 864 combinations); when one of the
inputs it hands over is missing the answer is "not known", for a landing row too. *Open:* a published variant under a product
that is not published is treated as not on sale; the export tool counts it the same way.

**The seed (`BulkDecisions::seedCheck()`): a tested rule is reversed on purpose.** Until this build a row marked New whose
state was "known from neither" was made (`BulkDecisionsTest` pinned `$plain => null`). Now, in the order the reasons are
recorded: `page_heading` for a heading the features recorded (as before); `not_published` when the variant's status is known
and is not Published (as before, now read from the stored state first) AND ALSO when its PRODUCT's status is known and is not
Published (the record says `of: product`; the words are the same, with the product's status); beside a stored state that does
not say so, `page_heading` and `not_published` for what the features and the record say against the variant, as before the state
was stored (the review below, F1); then the checks of before (no suggestion, not New, changed since the check, barcode
elsewhere); then, for a row that would be made and has a stored state, the
page heading worked out again at the click (`page_heading`: a product that gained a second published variant since the check
makes its default row a heading from then on); then **`state_not_known`**: no reader gives a state at all, or the stored state
lacks the variant's status, its product's status or an input of the heading, or it is older than the setting (the record says
`state`: `not_known` or `too_old`, with the date). A person opens such a variant and decides: the single page is untouched and
still makes its item. The tests that pinned the old rule say so where they changed (`BulkDecisionsTest`: `$plain`, `$odd`;
`BulkScreensTest`: `$unknown`); their other rows now carry a stored state, as every variant does once its store is loaded.
What an old stored state knows AGAINST a variant still counts (`not_published` is asked before the age).

**The state-only load** (`ListingIngestService::stateOnly()`; `php bin/import_listings.php --channel=<code> --file=<export>
--state-only [--apply]`). For the variants that are already there: the eight state columns and nothing else, and only where the
line IS the stored profile (the same `profile_hash`, after the tool's own barcode cleaning). A line that differs, a variant the
warehouse does not know, a line with no state and a line whose stored state is newer are counted, listed and left. It creates
no listing, moves no identity, no `map_version`, no features, no `pushed_at`, and never a mark of the check on arrival: it
queues nothing. Without `--apply` it reads without a lock or a transaction and writes nothing (`ImportToolsTest` compares the
checksum of every table); with it, one transaction and one audit row (`listing.website_state`) a batch. *Settled while
building:* (a) it never moves a mark, also not of a variant the check has already looked at whose state becomes known for the
first time (the scope's test says "never a mark"; the intake's queue rule would have marked it): build 2b must give those
variants their look another way; (b) the whole tool now reads its command line whole or not at all (`Cli::main(..., strict:
true)`, build 1's fix A): every documented call of it is written `--name=value` and survives; a misspelt `--state-only` would
otherwise have been the ordinary import, which changes profiles, and `--apply=false` an apply; (c) `--apply` without
`--state-only` is refused (the ordinary import always writes); (d) a date in the future is refused; (e) exit 1 when any line
was left.

**The check (`ArrivalCheck`): the state is recorded and decides nothing.** A suggestion's evidence gains `variant_status` (a
text, only when known) and `website` {`known`, `as_of`, `product_status`, `heading`}. *Settled while building:* `website` is
written into every suggestion, with `known: false` and nulls when the state is not known (not known is recorded as what it is);
`known` is true only for a stored state with the variant's status, its product's status and an answer for the heading. The
snapshot the write compares under the variant's lock holds the stored state's six values (not its date: the same state seen
again is no move): a state that moved between the look and the write means nothing is written and the variant stays to check
(the state-only load moves a state without touching the mark's number, so the number alone would not have shown it). No outcome
and no rule reads the state: a variant in the bin, one under a draft product and a page heading get the same match as one on
sale ("a match makes nothing"), and `ArrivalRules` is unchanged.

**U146. Words** (all in `Words`; variant and item; no code, no number of a setting). `BULK_SKIP['state_not_known']`: "The
warehouse does not know if it is on sale on the website now. Open it and decide." (`BY_ITEM_SKIP`: "… on its store now …"); one
sentence whether the state was never known or is too old. New Variants: under a row marked New that the seed would skip for it,
one line, "The warehouse does not know if it is on sale on the website now: open it to decide." (`NEW_VARIANTS['site_unknown']`);
the line beside the bar names the reason with the others. *Settled while building:* the row also says "A page heading on the
website…" for a heading worked out from its stored state, and "Not published on the website (Draft)." for a product that is not
published, so that a row and its skip cannot disagree (the list reads the state through the same functions as the seed:
`Queries::newVariantRows()` attaches them; one more indexed read for each row marked New, for its product's published variants;
since the review below, CS-A, the heading is said under every row still to match, for one such read a product);
the line about a state that is not known is shown only under rows marked New that are not already "made before" or "changed":
every other row is skipped by the seed for what it is, and thousands of "No suggestion" rows would otherwise all carry it. The
setting: "How old the website's state may be", with its help. The audit log: "Website state of a store's variants loaded"
(`listing.website_state`). *Not done here:* the design's line above the New Variants list ("the warehouse does not know which of
a store's variants are on sale… marks nothing New") and the outcomes `state_unknown`, `state_old`, `not_published` and
`page_heading` of the CHECK belong to 2b, where the check can say New; the match-strength lists and the variant's own page show
no state line (they showed none before).

**The migration.** As 0027, and for 0027's reasons (measured there; `Migration0027Test`'s second test still holds the server
to them): ONE statement, `ALGORITHM = COPY, LOCK = SHARED`, the eight columns and the index in one pass, written first in the
file; `Migration0028Test` holds the file to it (one ALTER in the whole file, no INSTANT, no INPLACE), shows the columns exactly,
that the profiles that were there come through with every other column as it was and no state, that the indexes of 0005 and 0027
still answer, and that the statements the code of before 0028 runs still work on the new schema. Reads go on during the copy; a
write to `listing_profile` waits (applying 0027 to staging took 17 seconds in all).

**Measured** (12 Oct 2026; nothing was written to `cw_staging` by the build). *Read only on staging*, one snapshot
(`/root/cw_work/runs/cw_arrival2_facts.php`, `arrival2_facts.log`): every line of the three export files in `/srv/cw-import` has
its `profile_hash` stored: Vape and Go 29,105 of 29,105, Electrofag 9,014 of 9,014, the Vape Big sample 40 of 40 (differs 0,
unknown 0, no line without a state, no value ignored). So the state-only load should write all of them and leave none. Of the
open "New" suggestions (Electrofag 119, Vape Big 11, the main store none), all 130 read their state from the features of their
matching run today, so the reversed rule changes nothing for them before the load; after the load all 130 read "on sale" from
the stored state (none not published, none a page heading); and from 26 Oct the 119 of Electrofag read "not known" (their file
is of 26 Sep; Vape Big's is of 10 Oct). The files say: Vape and Go 17,931 published variants, 1,318 of them under a product
that is not published, and 4,470 landing rows; Electrofag 8,304 published, 165 under such a product, 1,103 landing rows.
*A rehearsal on the test slot's schema* (`arrival2_rehearsal.log`): 300 real Electrofag lines imported from a file with no time
in its name, then the state-only load of the first 350 lines under the export's own name: the dry run counts 300 to write and 50
unknown and writes nothing; `--apply` writes the 300 in 1.2 seconds (about 4 ms a variant); a second run finds all 300 the
same; no listing is made and no mark moves. The seed's state questions over those 300 (as if each were marked New): 279 on
sale, 21 page headings (landing rows), 150 ms for all 300, the count of each product's published variants included.
*Each fix removed in turn* (`arrival2_mutate_one.py`, `arrival2_mutations.log`): 27 mutations, one at a time on a copy of the
worktree, each killed by the test named beside it (the state attached before the hash; a branch of the intake that does not
write it; each queue rule; the older state written; a 400 for a wrong type; the state-only load writing a line that differs,
writing without `--apply`, moving the mark, or reading its command line loosely; nothing known relied on; a state never too
old; the product's status not read; no heading at the click; a features-only state doubted; the features read first; the
variants of a product counted over every store or whatever their status; the evidence without the state; a moved state not
noticed; the state's date compared; the row not saying "not known", or every row saying it; a missing input read as "not a
heading"; the record not naming the product).

**Open, and for the reviewer first.** (1) The published variants of a product are counted from the stored states: a variant of
the product that arrived without a state is not counted, and a store that holds only a sample of its variants (Vape Big on
staging: 40 of 2,503) undercounts for every product. So "not a heading" can be said of a default row whose other variants the
warehouse cannot see. The seed works the heading out again at the click, which heals a count that was incomplete only for a
moment; it does not heal a sample. (Since the review below: a heading the features recorded is skipped beside a stored state
too, F1; and the Vape Big sample is left out of the load.)
(2) After the state-only load is applied, the rows a matching run judged New read their
STORED state: the files are of 26 Sep, so from 26 Oct (30 days) the seed skips them all as `state_not_known` until a fresher
export is loaded or the setting is raised. That is the rule working; it needs the owner's word on how the state is to be kept
fresh (the handoff's open question about refreshing staging's catalogues). (3) The state-only load never queues (above, a):
for 2b. (4) The ordinary import of a dated file now writes the state too, and so can queue (a state that changed from a known
value): a nightly refresh would queue the variants whose state changed, which is what 2b wants, and the queue alarm counts them.
(5) A features-only state never reads the features' `product_live`: on purpose, so that nothing changes before the load.
(6) The new reads name the new columns (the intake, a bulk action's pre-checks, New Variants, the check): between the copy of
the code and the end of the migration (the installer copies first, as build 1's review noted; the copy of the table takes
some seconds) those requests fail on staging; the command-line jobs refuse a schema that is behind the code and say so.
(7) `website` in a suggestion's evidence is written also when nothing is known (`known: false`); the scope's words were "when
known". (8) The state-only load exits 1 for a line that carries no state or whose stored state is newer, as for one that differs.

### The review of build 2a (12-13 Oct 2026, on `6002a73`)

Four reviewers, each with one question (does the seed do exactly what it should, and does nothing change for the owner before a
store's state is loaded; is the check still build 1's check plus the state, and are the new reads on the screens right, safe and
cheap; does the state-only load write only the state columns, only when told, and only for lines that are really the same
variant; is the ordinary intake unchanged except for the state, and are the migration and the deploy safe), then a refuter on
every finding; where the two differed the refuter's version was followed. No critical finding: before a store's state is loaded
nothing changes for the 130 rows marked New; a dry run of the load writes nothing, and an apply writes the eight columns of the
same variant and nothing else; both hashes are main's, with and without `website`; the check is build 1's plus the state
(`ar1.0`); the migration is one additive copy, and the code of before 0028 runs on the new schema. Two findings were important,
both about what a STORED state hides once a store is loaded, and both are fixed here. Their tests were pushed alone and seen to
fail (`/root/cw_work/runs/arrival2_fix_red.log`), then F1's code alone (`arrival2_fix_f1.log`: CS-A's rows still red), then
both (`arrival2_fix_green.log`); and each part of the two fixes was removed alone and killed by its test
(`arrival2_fix_mutate.py`, `arrival2_fix_mutations.log`: 14 mutations).

**Fixed (each with a test that failed first).**
- **F1. The seed is never less strict than it was before the state was stored. A decision of the build is changed on purpose.**
  The build had settled that a stored state is THE state and that the features and a suggestion's record are not read beside
  it, "even where it knows less" (M66, "Who reads it" (1); pinned as made by `$storedGood` and by row `7011`). With the count of
  Open (1) that let a row be MADE which the code before this build skips: the default row of a product whose features call it a
  page heading, when another variant of its product has no stored state (the count says one: no heading); and a variant that the
  features and the record of a LATER matching run call Draft, under the stored state of an older export that says Published.
  Neither is on staging today (every line's hash is stored, and the features of the 130 rows agree with their state). It takes a
  matching run imported after the stored state's export, from an export whose own state was not stored (a file with no time in
  its name, a line the state-only load left, the run's import without the listings'), or a variant of the product without a
  state. But the scope names only ADDED skips and one reversed rule, and an item is never deleted. Now `SiteState::against()`
  gives what the two readers that have no date say AGAINST a variant beside its stored state, and `seedCheck()` asks it right
  after the stored state's own status and before "no suggestion", where the features were asked before: `page_heading` when the
  features call it one, then `not_published` with the status the features, else the record, give when that is not Published.
  New Variants' row says the same two lines (`NewVariantsController::row()`), so a row and its skip agree. `SiteState::read()`
  is as it was (the check on arrival and "where else is this barcode" read the stored state alone), and nothing the two say FOR
  a variant is read beside a stored state: a stored "Bin" is not overruled. **The cost, a build decision:** a row whose OLD
  features say Draft or page heading stays one at a time although a newer stored state says it is on sale, exactly as on main
  today, until a matching run rewrites its features. Nothing changes for a row whose features and record agree with its stored
  state (all 130). Tests: `BulkDecisionsTest::testTheSeedReadsTheStoredWebsiteStateWorksTheHeadingOutAtTheClickAndSkipsWhatIsNotKnown`
  (`$storedGood` is now `page_heading`; new: `$draftSince` and `$binnedByRecord` are `not_published`, `$aloneHeading` and
  `$uncheckedHeading` are `page_heading`, `$agreed` is still made), `NewVariantsScreenTest::testARowMarkedNewSaysWhatTheSeedWillFindOfItsStateOnTheWebsite`
  (rows 7011, 7014 to 7016, 7029), `SiteStateTest::testWhatTheFeaturesAndTheRecordSayAgainstAVariantCountsBesideItsStoredState`.
- **CS-A. New Variants says "a page heading" under every row still to match, also once its store's state is loaded.** A stored
  state holds no heading (it is worked out), the build worked it out only for rows marked New (U146, to spare a read), and the
  features were not read beside a stored state. So after a load the line "A page heading on the website, not something that is
  sold." was gone from every "No suggestion" and "Suggested match" row: on the main store, its 4,470 landing rows. U133 promises
  that line under a row still to match; it is how a person knows which rows to Ignore (M62); and the variant's own page, where
  the item of such a row is made one at a time, says nothing of a heading. Now `Queries::newVariantRows()` works the heading out
  for every row still to match (`Queries::NEW_OPEN`: New, a suggested match, no suggestion) whose stored state holds the inputs,
  unless the row already says "not published" or "a page heading" without it (the stored status; the features and the record,
  through F1), and `row()` says it whenever it is true. "The warehouse does not know…" stays under rows marked New only, for
  U146's reason. The seed is not changed by this: it skips such a row for what it is (`not_checked`, `suggested_match`).
  *What the page costs now* (held in the test by the session's own statement counter): when a row of the page has a stored
  state, one read of the setting; and ONE count for each PRODUCT among the rows that need it (one range of the index on the
  product's number, each listing by its primary key: the plan `Migration0028Test` pins), remembered for the call. At most one a
  row: 50 a page, 500 a chunk of the CSV; the build asked the same count for the rows marked New only. A page heading of the
  main store has features that say so, so its landing rows cost nothing more; each count still reads its siblings' own profile
  rows (Left 3). Tests: `NewVariantsScreenTest::testTheFilterTheSearchAndWhatEachVariantIsInWords` (the Heading row, now with a
  stored state: the review's test, red on `6002a73`; F1 alone turns it green, because that row's features say heading) and
  `::testARowMarkedNewSaysWhatTheSeedWillFindOfItsStateOnTheWebsite`, rows 7022 to 7028 (a stored state and no features: a
  landing row under "No suggestion" and under a suggested match, a default row by the count, one by an old state, a binned one
  that says "not published" first, one that lacks an input and says nothing), with the counts of statements.

**Refuted (three; none is a fault of this build).** Two reviewers found that a state the state-only load commits while the check
writes a suggestion is not seen by that write: the end state is exactly "the check finished, then the load ran", which the build
accepts on purpose and hands to 2b ("The state-only load", (a); Open (3)); no rule reads the state in 2a. For 2b: `mark()` should
also ask the six state values. And an apply of the load also moves `listing_profile.updated_at`: that is the row's own change
stamp, MySQL moves it, nothing reads it, and holding it still would make it lie.

**Left, each confirmed and minor (for 2b or a small follow-up; none lets a bulk action make an item it must not).**
(1) From 26 Oct 2026 09:41:57 UTC the states loaded from the 26 Sep files are older than the 30 days and the seed skips every
loaded row marked New: the age limit is a build decision and is written down (Open (2)); left is that the skip's words do not
say it is an age limit or give the date its record holds, that a load applied after that moment switches the rows off at once,
that a later matching run does not bring them back, and that the load prints no warning for a file already past the limit.
(2) `BulkDecisionsTest`'s older row `$c` ("made before" is said first, also where "not published" would apply) had lost its
second reason to the new fixture default; fix F1 gives it back without a change of its own (its features say Draft beside a
stored state), and "made before asked after not published" is killed again (X14 of the mutations above).
(3) The count of a product's published variants reads each sibling's own wide profile row, and other stores' rows of the same
number, only to test a status: served by the index and bounded, not covered; an index on (`site_product_id`,
`site_variant_status`) can be added in place later (as 0020 did), and fix CS-A makes it worth more (the CSV of a whole store).
(4) A count that is short says "known, not a page heading" (a store held in part; a variant whose line the load left): counting
from the stored states is a build decision (Open (1)); before 2b, New must not be switched on for a store whose list is not
whole or whose load left lines.
(5) `Queries::barcodeElsewhere()` reads the stored state first, and no test fails when it reads the features alone.
(6) A time in a file's name that is no real time rolls over (`20260931T…` is read as 1 Oct) instead of being refused.
(7) A second run of the tool while another holds its job lock ends with exit 0 and "skipped", having written nothing (the
frame's rule, made for the timers): load the stores one after another.
(8) A file that is cut short can end with exit 0, and the manifest beside it is not compared: read `lines=` against the count
expected.
(9) No test would notice the row lock of the state-only apply gone; the code is right.
(10) `install_cron.sh` copies the code before it migrates (build 1's Left 5, older than both builds): this build's pages and
the intake name the new columns, so it must be run WITH `--migrate`, and they fail for the seconds of the copy (Open (6), which
did not name the variant's own page).
(11) The ordinary import's summary line prints no count of the variants it queued (the number is in its audit row only), and
this build adds one more way to queue.
(12) `--exported-at` wins over the time in the file's name and the two are not compared (the design's order, a build decision;
both are printed): a pasted option can date an old file as new.

**For the rollout** (`docs/ops.md`, "The website state and the state-only load"): `install_cron.sh` WITH `--migrate`; the Vape
Big sample is left OUT of the state-only load (40 of 2,503 variants: point (4)), so after the load Electrofag's 119 rows marked
New read their stored state and Vape Big's 11 keep reading their features as today; and the date of point (1).
## Stock › Counts: stock counting, pack A2a (slot `stocka2`, 12-13 Oct 2026)

The owner, 12 Oct 2026: "start inventory module", and to "which part?": "All of them, in order". The 8 Oct list asked for counting: "count
plan every 4 months (a setting), count sheets with scan / upload, variance review with a tolerance setting, `counted_at` rules"; the
module plan says the same in IM2 and its decision 6 ("the count screen warns first when goods arrive during a count"). The scope is
`/root/cw_work/Stock_A2a_scope_2026-10-12.md`; A2b (Quality) comes next. The count ENGINE existed and is not changed (`src/Movements.php`,
`src/Stock.php`, `tests/Integration/Stock/CountingTest.php`): this pack wires it to a document and adds the screens. Numbered 0029 and
CT: 0028, M66 and U146 are build 2a's. Code: `migrations/0029_stock_counts.sql`; `src/Counts/{CountSheets,CountSheetHandler,CountPosting,
CountTimes,CountTolerance,CountReviews,CountPlan,CountInvariants}.php` (new); `src/Documents/DocumentHandlers.php`, `src/Invariants.php`,
`src/Settings.php`, `src/Schema/Grants.php`, `src/Auth/Permissions.php`, `src/Ui/{Sections,Words,Context,Kernel}.php`; controllers
`Counts` (new), `Item`, `Documents`; templates `stock_counts`, `stock_count_sheets`, `stock_count_reviews`, `stock_count`,
`stock_count_before` (new); `public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`.

**CT1. A count sheet is a stock count record (CNT).** It is a `document` of type CNT (the warehouse counted, the UK day it was opened, a
note) on the document base: draft -> final ("made final"; a number `CNT-000123`) -> cancelled as a whole by a new record; a draft is
stopped, never deleted. Its header is `count_sheet` (kind `sheet`, an optional place inside the warehouse) and its lines `count_sheet_line`:
one per item (an item is on a sheet once), with what the system held when the line was put on the sheet, the quantity counted (empty =
not counted yet, nothing is booked for it; 0 = counted and none found), when it was counted, who entered it and how (typed or from a
file). `document_line` is written only at the posting: `CountSheets::post` makes the counted lines the record's lines and posts it
through `Documents::post` in ONE transaction, and `CountSheetHandler` books them through the engine (`Movements::bookForDocument` with
`count` movements: the as-of rule, "a later count wins", its two reviews, all unchanged). A refusal leaves the sheet as it was. Two other
kinds of CNT record exist: `reversal` (a whole sheet cancelled; the document base negates its stock) and `line_reversal` (CT7). A build
decision, for the owner: a sheet is entered and made final by the person who opened it (the document base's rule for a draft, I19); a
manager cannot prepare a sheet for a counter (each counter opens their own).

**CT2. Entering quantities.** A quantity is saved the moment Enter is pressed in its box: the form's own button, no script (the house
rule: app.js never talks to the network). Every box carries the value it was drawn with and the server keeps only the boxes changed on
that page: a page left open in another tab never empties or overwrites what was entered since. A line whose quantity is the one it holds
keeps the moment it was counted. A refused page saves nothing and shows what was typed again; nine or more digits in a box, or a value
of 4 to 8 digits that is a barcode CW knows (as typed, or as its barcode key: an EAN-8 that starts with 0, a short code of the shop's
own; review M-5 of 14 Oct 2026), are refused as "a barcode went into the quantity box" (a scanner fired while a quantity box had the
focus). app.js marks a box typed in and not saved yet, and the unsaved-changes guard asks before the scan box, the upload or "stop"
leaves the page. Each line keeps the moment its box was first typed into, not the moment Enter was pressed (review M-7: a counter who
moves with Tab and presses Enter once gave every line that one moment, so a dispatch between the real count and the save read as before
the count and the figure read high): app.js writes it into a hidden `at_<line>` as the page's drawn time (`data-drawn`, the server's
clock) plus how long ago the page was loaded (so the tablet's own clock does not matter); CountSheets refuses a moment after now or
before the line was put on the sheet (422 `bad_count_time`, nothing saved; Enter again saves with the time now); without one (no
script) the moment of the save counts, as before. A sheet holds at most 500 items
(`CountSheets::MAX_LINES`). Entering a quantity books nothing; every change moves the record's version, so "Before you make it final"
drawn before a change cannot post (409 `version_conflict`).

**CT3. Count times.** The engine takes ONE count time per movement and at most 20 movements a posting
(`Movements::MAX_DOCUMENT_MOVEMENTS`); a sheet has a time per line. `CountTimes::groups` books a line under an EARLIER line's time only when
nothing happened to its stock in between (no on-hand row, no later count) and the gap is at most the setting
`counts.time_window_max_minutes` (default 10, the engine's "near a count" window `Stock::NEAR_COUNT_SEC`; 0 to 60; review I-1 of 14 Oct
2026). The fewest such times are found (the textbook "fewest points that touch every interval"). The window is NEVER widened past the
setting: the first version doubled it until 20 times fitted (a day's sheet of 300 lines, one every 90 s, booked lines up to 39 minutes
before their own time; no limit at all past 366 days). A sheet that needs more than 20 times at the setting is refused (409
`too_many_times`, nothing booked), and "Before you make it final" marks the lines that started the earliest times (all but the newest 19):
"Count it again" on each, or one button that empties them all; counted again close together they share one new time and the sheet fits
(review M-2). At the moment of posting a shared time changes nothing the engine works out (no on-hand row lies in the gap). After booking,
the engine's answer per line is compared with what `CountPosting::plan` worked out before (left out or not, the difference): a mismatch
means stock moved in that instant, and the posting is refused whole (409 `moved_meanwhile`). What a shared time DOES change, afterwards:
the item's count time (`stock_balance.counted_at`) is the shared time T, not the line's own time, so the engine judges every dispatch or
reset reported LATER against T. Cost if wrong, both ways: a dispatch made in the gap (T, own time] and reported after the posting is taken
off once too often (the figure reads one LOW); a reset (a parcel back on the shelf) made in the gap and reported late is ADDED although the
count already had that unit (the figure reads one HIGH, the unsafe side). Both are within ten minutes of T while the setting is at most 10,
so the engine's own `ship_near_count` / `unship_near_count` review flags each, and Stock › Counts › Differences now lists them (accept only:
they are about a count's time, not a sheet line; whoever finds the figure wrong counts the item again). Above 10 minutes a late one in the
