gap may not be flagged (the setting's help says so). A second sheet's count of the same item made in the gap and made final later replaces
this line's count (it is not "older than the last count"): usually the arithmetic is still right as of its time. A line counted more than
a day before the posting is booked as a count typed in later (the engine's `backdated`, up to 90 days); older is refused (422
`count_too_old`). post() works the plan out again and gives the same 409 or 422 when stock moved after validate() (review M-3; the first
version threw an error page).

**CT4. The sheet, for a tablet and a scanner.** Each line shows the item (name, CW number, brand, its barcodes), its selling mode and
"stock now" (on hand at the sheet's warehouse, and how many are reserved for orders), and the quantity box. The setting
`counts.sheet_shows_stock` (default on: the module plan's choice; off = a blind count: the figure is shown once the line holds a quantity,
and the download leaves the column out). The scan box at the top: a barcode on the sheet goes to its line (that page, the line marked and
its box ready; an outer-case barcode says how many units it stands for); an item not on the sheet is offered ("Put it on the sheet"); a
barcode on no item, or on more than one item, or not usable, is said and nothing changes (it never guesses). Digits are always a barcode;
a CW number is typed with its letters.

**CT5. Warn first (decision 6 of the module plan).** "Before you make it final" lists every counted line with its difference (counted -
what the system holds now, after the engine's own rule: dispatches booked after the count come off it), the biggest first, the lines
above the limits, the lines a later count leaves out, and the lines whose stock moved after they were counted, with the newest five
movements and what keeping the count would do. Such a line blocks the posting until the person chooses: "Count it again" (the line is
empty again) or "Keep my count" (the choice names the newest movement the page showed; anything newer asks again, and a hand-made form
naming a movement that does not exist is refused). Nothing is adjusted behind the person's back; "Keep my count" lets the engine's as-of
rule do the arithmetic, and a count that overwrote stock that came in opens the engine's own review.

**CT6. Which differences a person looks at.** Two settings, in UNITS until costs exist (IM2): `counts.review_over_units` (default 5; 0 =
every difference) and `counts.review_over_percent` (default 10; 0 = not used). A booked line whose difference is MORE than either is
checked (`CountTolerance::over`); of an item the system held nothing of (or less), any difference is over the percent while it is used.
The check is kept on the sheet line (`count_sheet_line.review`: none, open, accepted, rejected; with the limits it was opened under), NOT
in `count_review`: a `count_review` row has a foreign key to `sku`, and inside a posting it may be written neither before the stock locks
(it would lock the item before its balance: I141/D15) nor after them (I21). The sheet's lines exist before the posting and are locked by
it first, so the posting adds no row. The counts are booked whatever the check says: the shelf figure is right at once (IM2).

**CT7. Accepting and rejecting.** Stock › Counts › Differences lists the open checks (the item, the sheet, what the system held, what was
counted, the difference, who counted, why it waits) and, beside them, the engine's own two kinds of review, which had no screen before
(`count_after_movements`: stock was booked after the count's time and the count overwrote it; `count_near_ship`: a parcel left within ten
minutes of the count). Every answer has a note (3 to 500 characters). Accept: the count stays, the row says who and why. Reject: that
LINE's count is put back by a new CNT record of the kind `line_reversal` (one line: the item and minus what the count changed, booked as
an `adjustment`; the engine can only negate a whole record, and a count movement would set a new count time), posted in the same
transaction; the sheet and its other lines stand; the balance's count time stays (as the engine's own reversal leaves it): the item is
counted again on a new sheet. A line is put back once (a UNIQUE key); putting it back settles every open review of the engine about that
count. A sheet with a line put back cannot be cancelled as a whole afterwards (409 `line_put_back`: it would put that line back twice), and
a line of a cancelled sheet cannot be rejected. A line is not put back after its item was counted again (409 `counted_again`; review C-1
of 14 Oct 2026): a put back is relative (minus what the count changed) and a later count is absolute (it set the figure again), so the old
difference would be added a second time (counted 0 of 500, counted again 480, the first rejected: the figure read 980). "Counted again" is
a `count` row of the item at that warehouse booked after the line's own (ledger ids of one balance follow its lock: D42's rule, as
Reservations reads it for VERIFY; a cancellation's copy of another count counts too, the safe side). It is said at once and checked again
by the handler under the item's stock lock, at the booking; the Differences row says "counted again since: accept it" instead of the reject
button. A whole sheet is not cancelled when any of its items was counted again since (409 `line_counted_again`: said at once, before a
cancellation waits for an OK, and again under the stock locks when a reviewer's OK books one that waited). Nor is a line put back while a
cancellation of its whole sheet waits for a reviewer's OK (409 `cancel_waiting`; review M-1: the OK would be refused for ever after). An
engine review of a count not made on a sheet can be accepted, not rejected. Cancelling
a whole sheet closes its open checks as rejected, naming the cancellation; a cancellation that puts more than the "stock put back" limit
back waits for a reviewer's OK first (the document base's rule, I32, as for any record): the person stays on the sheet, which links the
waiting record on History; the record gets its count header when it is booked.

**CT8. A second person: the existing rule on Settings › Approval Rules, switched OFF.** The CNT row of the Approval Rules page now means:
none = the person who counted may clear their own difference (the row says who did); "only over N units" = a difference of more than N
needs someone who neither counted the line nor opened or made the sheet final; "every one" = always (and the document base also opens its
own check of the whole sheet for a Reviewer, its rule for any record). The handler hands the base 0 units, so "over N" never opens a
whole-sheet check: differences are checked one by one. `CountReviews::refusal` gives the screen the same answer before the form is drawn,
and the tab's badge counts only what this person may answer. **0029 switches the rule off** (version N+1 of its history, `system:migrate`,
only when it is not off already): 0008 seeded it on (over 10 units) for a type that had no handler, so no record loses a check it had;
extra approvals start off (the owner's rule), and one person works on staging today, where a second-person rule would wait for ever. A
build decision, for the owner; the limit of 10 is kept for when it is switched on. The Approval Rules page and Settings say what the rule
means for a count (a second person who answers a count difference; "every one" also a reviewer's check of every count record) instead of
"a reviewer checks those over 10 items" (`Words::reviewRule`; review M-4 of 14 Oct 2026). **A stock count's Not OK only records it**
(`reject_action` record, in `DocumentRules::REJECT_RECORD_ONLY` beside the purchase order; 0029 sets it in the same version as the rule
switched off): with "every one" the base's own check of a record that puts a line back could not be said Not OK to (409 `not_reversible`)
nor that of a sheet with a line put back (409 `line_put_back`), and cancelling a count at review is exactly the put back after a later
count that CT7 refuses. A count is put right by counting again, or by answering its differences. A build decision, for the owner.

**CT9. Who.** `doc.CNT.post` (stock controller, warehouse; never admin, I12) opens, enters, makes final and answers differences;
`documents.view` looks (every GET). Each is checked again in the services inside the transaction (roles re-read). Staging, 12 Oct: nobody
holds either job yet (the one account is admin, reviewer and mapping lead), so nobody there can open a sheet until someone is given one.

**CT10. The plan.** One setting, `counts.plan_days` (default 120: "every 4 months"; 1 to 730, a rule of its own in `Settings::RULES`: a
`_days` key stops at 120 otherwise). The plan covers the items CW keeps a stock figure for at a warehouse (a `stock_balance` row; merged
items left out). An item counted within the days is inside the plan; never counted, or longer ago, is overdue. The tab shows four figures
for one warehouse (in the plan, inside, overdue, never counted) and "Next to count": never counted first (the best sellers first by
`reorder_demand.rate`, then the items without a sales figure by CW number), then the counted ones, the longest ago first. It is a work
list of the first 50, 100 or 200 (no later pages): what is counted leaves it. From it a person ticks items, takes "the next N", takes all
of a search (a brand, words of the name, a CW number; whatever their turn, and items with no figure at that warehouse too), or opens an
empty sheet (FormOnce: one sheet however often the form is sent).

**CT11. `counted_at` rules.** `stock_balance.counted_at` is the engine's (a posted count sets it, `Stock::setCountedAt`) and is what the
plan reads. `sku.counted_at` and the selling policy belong to the count gate (plan §7.4) and are NOT touched. The item page's "Stock last
counted" read `sku.counted_at`, which no count sets: it now shows the latest `stock_balance.counted_at` of the item (any warehouse).

**CT12. Download and upload.** A sheet downloads as a CSV (`CsvWriter`: formula-safe): line, cw_code, item, brand, barcodes, stock_now
(only while the setting shows it), counted. The counted quantities come back by upload: a PREVIEW first (what would be filled in, already
holding that quantity, empty, not on this sheet, cannot be read: no CW number, not a whole number, below zero, more than 10,000,000, the
item twice), which writes nothing (the test compares CHECKSUM TABLE of seven tables before and after); "Fill in the sheet" fills exactly
the sheet's own lines (nothing is added, nothing is made final). The upload asks when it was counted (default now; a UK date and time,
not after now, not even by a minute (review M-6 of 14 Oct 2026: the first version allowed the clock's 5 minutes, and a count time in the
future keeps the next dispatches on the figure), not more than 90 days back): a paper count typed in later keeps its true time, so "warn
first" sees what moved since.

**CT13. Every list read keeps to an index.** 0029 adds two, online (`ALGORITHM = INPLACE, LOCK = NONE`, not a rebuild): `stock_balance
(warehouse_id, counted_at, sku_id)` (the never counted, the oldest counts and the figures of one warehouse, from the index alone; a count
is the only thing that moves an entry) and `count_review (status, source, id)` (the open reviews of the two count kinds, newest first,
without the open reviews of every other kind). The new tables carry their own (`count_sheet_line (review, document_id, line_no)` for the
open checks, `(document_id, sku_id)` for the scan box). Every statement the tab sends was checked with EXPLAIN and timed on the test
schema (MySQL 8.4.8, 32 MB buffer pool, 13 Oct 2026) filled like staging: 15,000 items, 8,200 balances at MAIN (half never counted),
11,800 demand rows, 300,000 on-hand ledger rows (with no record, as nearly all of staging's are), 400 sheets of 40 lines, 20,000 count
reviews (`/root/cw_work/runs/a2_explain.txt`, script `/root/cw_work/a2b/a2_explain_script.php`). The plan's four figures: 37 ms (index only, 8,200
entries); Next to count reads 200 entries of the demand index backwards and 200 balances (6 ms); a sheet's page reads its lines by the
key; the differences and the badge are ranges of their two indexes. The first run found four reads that were not index-served and
they were changed: (1) the nightly C3 read the WHOLE ledger once per line (43.8 s): MySQL chose a full scan because nearly every
ledger row has no record; it now reads each final sheet's rows by the ledger's document index, named, and compares in PHP (the five
checks: 0.45 s); (2) the list of sheets sorted every header: now the ids first (the header key backwards, or the record index
(doc_type, status, id) with a state; 51 entries), then their details; (3) "sheets with this item" walked the whole (sheet, item) index:
the item index is named; (4) "Before you make it final" read every on-hand ledger entry of each line's balance (fine on staging
today, seconds for a busy item after a year of sales): each line is now a range of (warehouse, item, bucket, time) with its own
time as a value, 100 lines a statement. Known: the search by words (as Stock › Movements) reads the item names, 15,000 rows, 10-40
ms. Since the review of 14 Oct 2026 (CT7, CT16): "counted again since" reads the line's own count row by the ledger's document index,
then a range of the item's on-hand rows from that count time on (`ix_stock_ledger_effective`), stopping at the first count; Differences
does it per open row (at most 51 of each kind), the put back and the cancellation once per line; C6 only from the records that put
something back.

**CT14. The screens.** Stock › Counts is a tab with three segments: Next to count (CT10, with the split "New count sheet" button and a
"How counting works" fold), Count sheets (every count record as a board: open sheets, final, cancelled, records that put a count back,
stopped; Search by number or by an item on a sheet; Filter by state and warehouse; older pages by id; Export CSV, 5,000 rows at most),
Differences (CT7, its badge). A sheet's page (CT2, CT4, CT12, stop; once final: what each line booked and what became of its check,
cancel it as a whole) and "Before you make it final" (CT5). History's record page links a count to its sheet. The Dashboard lists the tab;
"stock counts" is no longer "coming later".

**CT15. Words.** Every word is in `Ui\Words` (new groups COUNTS, COUNT_HOW, COUNT_GROUP, COUNT_SHEET_GROUP, COUNT_KIND, COUNT_REVIEW,
COUNT_REVIEW_HELP, COUNT_SHOW, COUNT_LINE, COUNT_CHECK, COUNT_BAD, COUNT_NOTICE, COUNT_ERROR; additions to MENU, SEGMENT, NEW, MENU_HELP,
BADGE, PAGE_TITLE, PAGE_INTRO, SETTING, SETTING_HELP, SETTING_TOPIC, AUDIT_FAMILY, AUDIT_ACTION). One name for one thing: a "count sheet";
"made final" as every other record (never "posted"); the "difference"; a count "put back". The page intros never say "count" alone
(ReceivingWordsTest: a shelf count, stock counts). Every refusal says whether anything was saved.

**CT16. Nightly checks C1-C5 (`CountInvariants`, in `Invariants::check`).** C1 every final CNT record has its count header of the right
kind; C2 a final sheet's record lines are exactly its counted lines in order, each counted line says what the posting did with it, and a
sheet never made final holds nothing of a posting; C3 a line booked as counted has exactly one `count` movement of its item from that
record, of the difference it names, a line left out has none, and the record books nothing else; C4 a difference waits only on a final
sheet, and a rejected one names a final record that put it back; C5 a record that puts one line back is named by exactly that line, has
one line, booked exactly one adjustment of minus the difference, and its sheet is final (never cancelled as a whole as well); C6 nothing a
count booked was put back after its item was counted again (between a sheet's count row of an item and the row of the record that puts
it back, one line or the whole sheet, no other `count` row of that item and warehouse; review C-1 of 14 Oct 2026; from the few records
that put something back, by the document and balance indexes). They hold after every stock test.

## Stock › Sales: each store's orders, dispatch and returns, read only (slot `packd`, pack D, 14 Oct 2026)

The owner's module list of 8 Oct 2026: "Sales & Delivery: engine built; to add: sales and dispatch screens per store" and "Returns
Management: a list view only" (Q12: no new returns process; the stores' own return module restocks, and CW books what it sends). The
engine (`src/Reservations.php`) and the ledger writer (`src/Stock.php`) are unchanged: this pack only shows what they keep, and writes
no stock. Code: `migrations/0033_sales_dispatch_views.sql` (five settings, four indexes), `src/Ui/SalesViews.php`,
`src/Ui/Controller/{SalesController,DispatchController,SalesReturnsController}.php`, views `sales_orders`, `sales_order`,
`sales_dispatch`, `sales_returns` (new); `src/Ui/{Sections,Kernel,Words}.php`, `src/Settings.php`, `src/Auth/Permissions.php`, and
`ReservationViews::rows()` made public (marked blocks). Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/SalesScreensTest.php` (new) and the pinned
navigation, words and templates of `SectionsTest`, `WordsTest`, `UiTemplatesTest`, `StockScreensTest`, `ReservationsScreenTest`,
`StockOpsScreensTest`, `MenusTest`, `UiSecurityTest`.

**PD1. Where it lives: Stock › Sales, one tab with three segments.** Orders (`/ui/stock/sales`, its CSV, one order at
`/ui/stock/sales/{id}`), Dispatch (`/ui/stock/sales/dispatch`) and Returns (`/ui/stock/sales/returns`, its CSV), after Reservations and
before Quality. The store chosen travels through the three segments (`keep`). Not Reports: Reports holds figures (pack E builds
"Sales by Store" there as a report), while these are working lists of orders and units next to the stock they move. No new sidebar
item. The tab is named "Sales"; the segments "Orders", "Dispatch", "Returns" (page titles "Store orders", "Dispatch", "Returns and
cancels", so an order of a store is never confused with a purchase order). A build decision, for the owner to confirm.

**PD2. Who may open it: a permission of its own, `sales.view`** (provisional, owner to confirm): viewer, warehouse, manager, buyer,
purchasing manager, goods in, purchasing desk, stock controller, reviewer, accountant, auditor. Not the matching jobs (mapper,
matching lead: their work is the links) and not admin (people and roles only, I12). Its own permission, not `catalogue.view` as
Reservations (RS1), so that the roles screen pack E builds can switch it per job alone. Everything here is GET: a POST to any of its
addresses is 405, no page has a form that posts, and there is no button that changes an order (RS12 (4): the stores and the engine
are the only writers).

**PD3. Orders: a row is an order, and its state filter.** A row is one `reservation` (one order of one store), shown as Reservations
shows it (`ReservationViews::rows()`: products, warehouse units, items not linked, what became of it), plus when it was placed, paid
and how it came in. The state filter has seven values: Reserved, not paid (`held`); Paid (every sale: `committed`, whatever happened
next); With a unit sent / cancelled / returned (an order with at least one sold unit in that state, so these overlap with each other and
with Paid); Freed by the store (`released`); Ran out of time (`expired`). "Paid" is every paid order rather than "paid, not sent", so
that a period's sales can be listed at all; what waits to be sent is Dispatch's list. The way-in filter is `reservation.origin`
(Reserved first, Paid without a reservation, Open when the store joined).

**PD4. One order: each sold unit and its stock changes.** The facts (store, reference, state and what became of it, placed, paid, how it
came in, how long it has waited and whether that is late, store variants, warehouse units, a link to the reservation's page), then the
sold units a page at a time (by the store's unit number, `sales.page_size`): the warehouse item (a link to its card, its CW number,
"1 sold unit = N warehouse units"), the unit number, the store variant (its number and title), the warehouse, the state and when it was
sent; a unit not linked at the sale is named by the store's title and says that no stock is kept for it. Then "What happened to each
unit": the stock ledger's rows of each unit (`ix_stock_ledger_unit`), one step per call of the engine and warehouse, oldest first,
each with the change of each stock figure, who, when (the dispatch time for a sending) and "Open": Stock › Movements for the item, every
figure, starting at that step (`before` = its last ledger id + 1; Movements has no filter by order). A unit not linked moved no stock and
has no steps: the page says so. At most `sales.scan_max_rows` ledger rows are read for a page of units; the page says when it cut.

**PD5. Orders' days: when the order was placed, in UK days.** `reservation.created_at` (when the store first told CW: the checkout, or
the payment for an order paid without a reservation; an order open when the store joined shows the day it joined). The list opens with
the last `sales.default_days` days, today included; "Any time" and two dates of one's own (both days included) are offered. A day that
is not a real day, or a first day after the last, shows the default days and says so. Order ids follow the time of placing (the one
INSERT sets both), which the unit filters rely on (PD10).

**PD6. Dispatch: waiting, late, sent, undone.** Waiting to ship = the store's units in `allocated` (paid, not sent), listed per order,
oldest order first (by order id, i.e. the time of placing; the age shown and the late mark are from the payment, `committed_at`), with
the units still waiting, and "Sending was undone before" when the order's ledger has an `unship`. Late = paid more than
`sales.late_hours` hours ago and not sent; the figure looks at the oldest `sales.scan_max_rows` waiting orders of each store and says
when there were more. Sent today / Sent this week = orders with a unit whose dispatch time is since UK midnight / since Monday 00:00 UK
(a unit keeps its dispatch time when it is returned, so a return does not take it out of "sent"; a dispatch reset clears it). The week
starts on Monday (UK and ISO 8601): a fixed rule, not a number the owner set; say so and it becomes a setting. Sending undone = the
engine's `unship` rows of the ledger, newest first, one row per unit (its `allocated` row, which every reset books), with who and what
the unit is now; units not linked move no stock and are not in the ledger, and the list says so. Four figures and four lists
(`show`), each list paged by key.

**PD7. Returns: a list per unit, no process.** The units in `returned` (the customer sent them back; the store's return page called
`return`, and CW put them back in stock at the unit's warehouse) and in `cancelled` (the store cancelled them before sending), newest
order first, filtered by store and by kind. "Back on sale?" and "Where the stock is" are read back from the ledger by CW's own rules:
returned → back in stock at the warehouse; cancelled after payment, restockable → back on sale there; cancelled after payment, not
restockable (a transfer into VERIFY noted `cancel_not_restockable` after the unit's last cancel) → in VERIFY, with its recount's state
(open: waiting; resolved: done; dismissed: closed; `count_review` by its unique key `verify:<store>:<unit>`); cancelled before payment
→ the reservation was freed; not linked → no stock was kept. One figure: the cancelled units waiting in VERIFY for a recount (the open
`verify_recount` reviews, per store by their reference). Q11 (stock coming back from the sister stores, the shop units or trade
customers) is not an order of a store and is not here: that is Stock In's "a trade customer's return" (pack A1) and pack C's returns
to suppliers.

**PD8. Read only, no stock writes.** Every route is GET (`sales.view`); `CW\Reservations` stays the only writer of orders and units,
`CW\Stock` of the ledger. Changing an order (cancelling, re-sending, releasing a stuck hold) stays on the stores' own screens.

**PD9. Five settings, nothing hard-coded** (the owner's rule of 8 Oct 2026; each provisional, set on Settings › System › Settings with a
reason, version 1 in `config_change` from 0033, under the topic "Sales and dispatch"):
`sales.page_size` (50; 25, 50, 100 or 200) rows on a page of Orders, Dispatch and Returns, and sold units on an order's page;
`sales.default_days` (7; 1 to 365) the days Orders opens with; `sales.late_hours` (24; 1 to 720) when a waiting order is late;
`sales.csv_max_rows` (5,000; 100 to 50,000) the most rows of a CSV; `sales.scan_max_rows` (5,000; 500 to 50,000) the most rows a page
reads to fill itself where a filter is not in an index (PD10), and the most waiting orders the late figure and the ledger rows an
order's page read. They are read in one statement on every request; a stored value outside its rule (only admin SQL could write one)
reads as the migration's. The words never repeat a number: "longer than the hours set on the Settings page".

**PD10. Paging by key; the scan limit.** No list uses an OFFSET or a COUNT over a table that grows for ever. Orders by state and way
in: one range of `ix_reservation_store_placed` per (store, state, way in) asked for, each newest first and cut at a page, merged (at
most 3 stores x 4 states x 3 ways = 36 ranges of 51 entries); the next page starts after the last order shown (its placed time, then
its id: an exact boundary). Orders with a unit sent, cancelled or returned: the store's units in that state by order
(`ix_reservation_unit_store_state`, from the index alone), newest first, starting below the newest order placed before the period's end
(one look-up per range of the placed index); each order read is checked for the days and the way in; reading stops at the first order
placed before the period, when the page is full, or after `sales.scan_max_rows` orders: the page then says how many it read and
offers "Read on" from where it stopped (only when the index has more). Dispatch's waiting list after an order id; its sent lists before
an order (its sending time, then its id); its undone list before a ledger id; Returns after (order id, unit number); an order's units
after a unit number. The CSVs read the same way in batches of 500, up to `sales.csv_max_rows`, and say in a last row when they stopped.

**PD11. Four indexes, online (0033).** `reservation (channel_id, status, origin, created_at, id)`: Orders (0023's (channel_id, status,
id) has no time and no way in). `reservation_unit (channel_id, state, reservation_id, unit_id)`: a store's units of one state by order, for the
waiting list and its figures, Returns, and Orders' unit filters (the unit table's indexes start with the order or the item: RS7 left
the per-store waiting figure out for that reason; unit_id, the primary key's, is named so that (order, unit) is read in the index's order: left to the hidden primary key part, MySQL sorted the Returns page, EXPLAIN "Using filesort"). `reservation_unit (channel_id, state, dispatched_at, reservation_id)`: units sent in a
period, read from the index alone. `stock_ledger (channel_id, movement_type, id)`: sending undone, which nothing else keeps (the unit
goes back to waiting and its dispatch time is cleared); the week is turned into a ledger id through `ix_stock_ledger_created`. All
non-unique, `ALGORITHM = INPLACE, LOCK = NONE`, each named in an optimizer hint (ignored before the migration). Cost for the engine: one
more entry per order, two per sold unit, one per ledger row (about 25 bytes), moved when the indexed state changes; no new locks under
READ COMMITTED. The ledger index is the costliest (the ledger is the biggest table); it is also the index a "sales events per store over
time" report needs, so pack E should reuse it rather than add its own (a point for the merge).

**PD12. Every statement was checked with EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a filled schema** (14 Oct 2026, the slot's test schema `cw_test_packd` on
the staging cluster, MySQL 8.4.8, 32 MB buffer pool; the fill script is `/root/cw_work/runs/packd_explain.php`, its output
`runs/packd_explain2.log`): 3 stores (70% / 29% / 1%), 60,000 orders over 60 days, 120,000 sold units (98,530 sent, 5,338 waiting,
2,559 cancelled, 1,573 returned), 202,908 ledger rows (788 dispatch resets). Every list statement is a covering range of the index it
names, read in the index's order, cut at the page: Orders' range 51 entries (1 ms; an older page by key 8 ms cold); a store's
returned units by order, 801 entries for 500 orders; Dispatch's waiting orders 75 entries for 51 orders; Returns' (store, kind) range
51 entries; sending undone a reverse range of the ledger index; the week's first ledger id one entry of (created_at). The reads that
are bounded by what they count rather than by a page: a store's waiting units (3,835 index entries, 14 ms), the late figure (2,409
waiting orders, one primary-key look-up each, 94 ms cold), a week's sent units (2,246 index entries, 8 ms; the list groups and sorts
the week's 1,139 orders, 10 ms). End to end, each SalesViews read took 11 to 241 ms on this cold, shared machine (the 241 ms is the
first page of every store's last 7 days: 36 ranges, cold; the same shape warm 53 ms); a sparse filter (returned units of orders open
when the store joined) read 983 orders and ended at the index's end, under the scan limit. The new indexes on this fill: placed
2.5 MB, units by state 5.5 MB, units sent 6.5 MB, the ledger's 5.5 MB (about 27 bytes a row). Without 0033 the per-store waiting
figure and the Returns list would read every unit of the store (RS7). `SalesScreensTest` holds the plan of each statement shape (the
index named, no filesort where the order comes from the index, read from the index alone where it says so), so a later change cannot
silently fall back to a scan. The fill's ledger times are not in id order (rows were written kind by kind), so its "undone this week"
figure is not meaningful; on a real ledger `created_at` is the insert time and follows the id.

**PD13. Words and look.** Every word is in `Words` (new groups SALE, SALE_STATE, SALE_ORIGIN, SALE_ORDER, DISPATCH, DISPATCH_CHIP,
SALE_RETURNS, SALE_RETURN_KIND, SALE_RESTOCK, SALE_RESTOCK_TEXT; MENU, SEGMENT, MENU_HELP, PAGE_INTRO, HELP, SETTING, SETTING_TOPIC,
SETTING_HELP, PERMISSION and TONE entries), in the owner's terms (a warehouse ITEM, a store VARIANT, a sold UNIT). No new CSS and no
script: the v4 toolbar, tiles, pills, store selector, board groups and stacked cards of the neighbouring Stock pages; the templates
are in `UiTemplatesTest`'s lint (every value through a helper, no typed word, every table a `table.stack` with labelled cells).

**PD14. Left out, on purpose.** (1) A CSV of Dispatch (the stores' own dispatch screens print the picking lists). (2) Totals of
orders or money per state or period (no COUNT over the table; pack E's reports). (3) A search by product or by a part of an order
reference (Reservations searches the orders that hold a product now). (4) A days filter on Returns; and units not linked to a warehouse item
in Dispatch's "Sending undone" (they move no stock, so the ledger has no row of their reset). (5) A "late only" list (the waiting list is oldest first, so the late ones come
first). (6) The week's first day as a setting (PD6). (7) Anything that changes an order or the stock (PD8).

## Pack B: Item Management — items by hand, product families, multipacks and repack (slot `packb`, 14 Oct 2026)

The owner's 16-module list of 8 Oct 2026, module "Item Management", with the owner's answers of 7-8 Oct 2026: Q10 "create a product by hand
(second lead approves): yes"; Q4 "product families: yes"; Q3 "repack: yes ... link such multipack listings to the single item with units per
item 10 (two-person rule); add a multipack finder and relink step, plus the repack document", with the nuance of 8 Oct "suggest more than 1 unit
only when the pack is made of a single product that is ALSO sold separately; otherwise default to its own product, 1 unit; a person decides";
Q8 "leave it for now" (extra approvals off by default); Q9 "never delete". Built in parallel with packs C, D and E from main `a35ccff`.
Code: `migrations/0031_items_families_repack.sql` (0030 is reserved for A2b; the integrator may renumber), `src/Items/{HandMade,Families,Packs,
Repacks,RepackHandler,ItemsInvariants}.php` (new), `src/Mapping/DecisionService.php` (mintByHand), `src/Documents/DocumentHandlers.php`,
`src/Invariants.php`, `src/Auth/Permissions.php`, `src/Admin/{ApprovalRules,DocumentRules}.php`, `src/Settings.php`, `src/Schema/Grants.php`,
`src/Ui/{Sections,Words,Kernel,Queries}.php`, controllers `HandMade`, `Families`, `Packs`, `Repack` (new), `Item`, `ByProduct`, `Review`,
`Reference`; templates `item_new`, `families`, `family`, `packs`, `pack_links`, `repacks`, `item_groups` (new), `item`, `by_product`, `listing`.
Every number or rule a person may want changed is a setting with its baseline; every word is in `Ui\Words`; nothing is deleted.

**PB1. An item made by hand (Q10).** Products › Add Item (`/ui/items/new`): the identity (name, the one field needed; brand, range, flavour,
strength, nicotine type, kind, ml, puffs, pack size), the product card's fields (`ItemCards::FIELDS`, the box's brand and flavour apart from
the identity's), one barcode with its units per scan, and a family. `CW\Items\HandMade::create` does it in ONE transaction, checks first and
writes after: the barcode (refused, 409 `barcode_on_other_item`, when it is a barcode of another item in `sku_barcode` in any stored form, or
carried by a variant MATCHED to another item: that item's barcode not copied to it yet; an unmatched variant's barcode is no item's), the
same name AND the same identity (every identity field equal, an unknown equal only to an unknown, case and spaces ignored; items joined into
another left out): 409 `same_item_exists` naming the other items, unless the person ticks "it is a different item" (`anyway`, audited with the
items it named), the card's values (`ItemCards::check`), the family (switched on). Then the item through `DecisionService::mintByHand` — the
code rule "only DecisionService makes an item" holds: origin `manual` (an ENUM value since 0004), no origin listing, its code `CW-%06d` of its
id in the same transaction (the existing number series of items, D4) — its `item_by_hand` row, the barcode (`ItemBarcodes::add`), the family
(`Families::assign`) and the card (`ItemCards::save`, version 0, kind `change`) last, because a card whose block changes writes the stock feed,
the last lock of a transaction. Audit `item.create`. No listing, no link, no stock. The form carries a form key (one item however often it is
sent; a refusal stores nothing, so the same key is sent again after a correction or the tick).

**PB2. Who makes an item by hand (provisional, owner to confirm).** A new permission `items.create`, held by the catalogue team: exactly the
holders of `catalogue.edit` (mapping lead, stock controller, purchasing manager), who also fill in its card and barcodes (`ItemCards::editor`
checks each again). Never admin (I12: 403 `admin_cannot_edit`).

**PB3. The second lead's OK of Q10 is a check afterwards, off by default.** The owner's Q10 answer carries "(second lead approves)"; Q8 says
"leave it for now" and extra approvals start off. A build decision: a new approval switch `approvals.item_by_hand_check` (Approval rules ›
Items; OFF in 0031). While it is on, an item made by hand is `waiting` for a second person holding `items.create` who did not make it (403
`own_item`) to press "Checked: it is right" on Products › Add Item (`HandMade::check`, audit `item.check`); it is usable at once, so goods-in
never waits. While it is off the row says `not_asked`. A blocking OK would need the item to be unusable until then: put to the owner.

**PB4. Product families (Q4).** `item_family` (a name unique among the families switched on, ignoring case: `active_name`; a note; a version for
the forms) and `item_family_member` (one row per item ever put in a family; `sku` is not altered). A family is created, renamed, switched off
(it keeps its items, takes no new ones, leaves the choices) and on again (its name must be free); an item is put in, moved or taken out
(`family_id` NULL: the row stays). Never deleted; every change audited (`family.*`). Who: a new permission `families.manage` (provisional): the
catalogue team and the buyers (Q4 is about buyers seeing products together); never admin; everyone with `catalogue.view` reads. A move of
one item names the family the form showed (409 `family_moved` otherwise). Lock order: the family row, then the members in sku id order.

**PB5. A family's bulk change (the owner's skip-and-list rule).** On a family's page a pasted list of CW numbers or barcodes is put in at once,
and ticked items are taken out; ONE transaction each, at most `items.family_bulk_max_rows` (a new setting, 200, 1 to 1,000; 422
`too_many_rows`, nothing saved). Every sure line is done; a doubtful one is skipped and listed at the end with its reason: no item
(`not_found`), joined into another (`merged`), named twice (`repeated`), already in this family (`already_here`), in ANOTHER family
(`in_other_family`, named: moving it is a person's choice on the item's page, never done in bulk), and when taking out, no longer in this
family (`not_in_family`).

**PB6. Pack items (Q3).** `item_pack`: a pre-packed multipack item kept in stock as packs (a sealed box of 10 nic shots) = N x a single item.
Defined by the catalogue team (`catalogue.edit`, like a barcode's units per scan); one definition switched on per pack item (`active_pack`);
the two items differ and are not joined away; N is 2 to `DecisionService::MAX_UNITS`; no pack of packs either way (409 `pack_nested`). A
definition is never changed or deleted: it is switched off (repacks cannot use it; the records that used it keep it) and a new one defined.
The two item rows are locked FOR UPDATE in id order (after the definition's own row when one is switched) so two definitions of the same
items made at once are decided one after the other.

**PB7. The owner's rule "suggest more than 1 unit only when the single is sold separately" is a setting.** `items.pack_suggest_single_sold`
(on in 0031). Products › Multipacks suggests a pack item's variants (matched with 1 unit a sale) as N singles a sale ONLY while the single is
sold on its own — a variant is matched (mapped or quarantined) to the single with 1 unit a sale; off: for every pack item. A suggestion is a
link to each variant's page with the single picked; a person decides there and a second matching lead says OK (`approvals.match_multiple`,
unchanged). Nothing is relinked here, and nothing reads a pack from a name (the 8 Oct nuance: "pack of 3" coils are usually the maker's pack,
one stock unit: such a pack item's variants say "its own product, 1 unit a sale").

**PB8. The two ways of selling a pack, side by side; the matching unchanged.** A pack LINK (a variant matched with N units a sale: one sale
takes N singles) and a pack ITEM (its own stock) are shown together: on each pack item `single_sold`, `sold_both_ways` (a variant also sells N
singles a sale while the pack item keeps stock of its own: one pack's stock in two places), `pack_of_packs` (a variant sells more than one of
the pack a sale), `count_differs` (the identity cards' pack counts break the matching's own rule, pack = N x single); Multipacks › Pack links
lists every variant with more than 1 unit a sale (the range of the new index `ix_channel_listing_units`) with `pack_item_exists` (a pack item
of that N exists for its item) or `item_is_pack`. Nothing in DecisionService's rules, the matching or the check on arrival changes: a link
with units other than 1 still waits for a second matching lead, still sells N units a sale, and the arrival rules' pack answers are still "not
sure" (`PackLinksUnchangedTest`, `ArrivalRulesTest`).

**PB9. Repack, a document type (RPK, Stock › Repack).** 0031 seeds `RPK` (number series `RPK-000001`; no reviewer check, no blocking approval
of its own, the OK first for a big record available and OFF: `DocumentRules::SIZE_TYPES`; each on the Approval rules page). A record names the
pack definition, the way (`break` packs into singles, `make` packs from singles) and the packs (header `repack`, which also copies the units
and both items); its two lines are exactly `break`: pack -k, single +k x N; `make`: single -k x N, pack +k (`RepackHandler::lines`), checked
again at posting (422 `repack_lines`, `pack_off`). It books ONE `Movements::bookForDocument` call of signed `adjustment` rows — the movement a
stock in already books; `Stock.php` and `Movements.php` are not changed, and `adjustment` is a cost-carrying type (ck_stock_ledger_cost) — so on
hand moves on each item by exactly its line. Who: a new permission `doc.RPK.post` (provisional): the stock controller and the warehouse, who
move stock (as a transfer, `doc.TRF.post`); never admin. The screen books in ONE step (`Repacks::book`: draft, header, lines and posting in
one transaction, behind a form key); a draft left by an OK taken back is made final or stopped on the list.

**PB10. A repack carries the cost (a setting).** `items.repack_carry_cost` (on in 0031): the line that comes in carries the average cost so
far of the item taken apart (`CostHints::average`) times its units, divided by the units made, to 6 decimals, half up (a box of 10 at £12 ->
singles at £1.20). With no average known, or the setting off, no cost (valued at the average later, IM8). Neither way changes how any
existing record is valued.

**PB11. Below zero.** The stock records' rule (SO3) unchanged: a repack that would leave a protected item (strict or stopped) with less
available than nothing in its warehouse is refused (422 `below_zero`), checked before and again after booking on the locked balances; no
reason can allow it (a repack carries none, as a transfer); a legacy item may go below zero, as on every stock record (a count review opens).

**PB12. Where the family is shown.** The item page's new box "Family and packs" (the family with its form for `families.manage`, the pack
item it is or the pack items made of it, who made it by hand); Products › By Item ("Family: …" under the item); the matching's variant page
(the suggested or matched item's family). `Queries::skus()` and `productRows()` gain the family by two primary-key joins.

**PB13. A repack's record and its cancellation.** It opens on the generic record page (Approvals › History), where it is cancelled once final
(`Documents::reverse`: a new RPK record, the exact negation; `RepackHandler::reverse` copies the header). The document base's rule I32 applies
unchanged: a cancellation that puts more units back on hand than the "stock put back without a supplier document" limit (ADJ's, 10 by default)
waits for a reviewer's OK. On the item page a repack's rows link to their record.

**PB14. The nightly checks** (`CW\Items\ItemsInvariants`, from `Invariants::check`): B1 every posted or reversed repack has its header and the
header's items are its definition's; B2 its on-hand rows net, per item, to its lines and are all `adjustment` rows; B3 every `manual` item has
its `item_by_hand` row and the other way round.

**PB15. Grants.** `item_family`, `item_family_member`: no DELETE; `item_pack`: append-only but its switch columns; `item_by_hand`: append-only
but its check columns; `repack`: append-only; `item_name_guard` (PB17): no DELETE.

**PB16. Words that are provisional** (Ui\Words, the groups ITEM_NEW, ITEMS_NOTICE, ITEMS_ERROR, FAMILY, FAMILY_SKIP, PACKS, PACK_FLAG,
PACK_LINK_FLAG, REPACK, REPACK_DIRECTION, BY_HAND_STATE, and the pack's keys at the end of the shared lists): the tab names "Add Item",
"Families", "Multipacks" (segments "Pack items", "Pack links"), "Repack"; "pack item" for a sealed multipack kept as packs; "pack link" for a
variant matched with more than 1 unit a sale. A list's page size (50; 100 on a family's page) and the repack list's 200 are display numbers,
as on the other lists, not settings.

**PB17. The review of b62c69f (14 Oct 2026; four findings, all four real, each shown by a failing test first).**
(1) Two people making an item of the same name and identity at the same moment (no barcode) both passed the same-item check: neither
item existed yet, so there was no row to lock and each read missed the other. Making an item by hand now writes the name's guard row first
(`item_name_guard`, keyed by SHA2 of the name's `WEIGHT_STRING` under `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`, so case and accents compare as `sku.name`
does): the second waits for the first, then reads it and is warned (409 `same_item_exists`). Another name never waits. One row per name
ever made by hand; never deleted.
(2) The same-item check read the first 50 items of the name and compared the identity afterwards: the 51st namesake was missed. It now
compares every item of the name, read in pages of 500 on `ix_sku_name` (after the last id), and names at most 50 in the warning.
(3) Two first assignments of one item at the same moment (no member row to lock under READ COMMITTED) both inserted; the second met the
first's key and the error undid its whole list. The writes now go in item id order; an insert that meets another's key is undone alone, the
line is skipped and listed (`already_here`, or `in_other_family` with that family's name) and the rest of the list is done. One item at a
time: 409 `family_moved`.
(4) A cancellation waiting for an OK (I32), refused or taken back has no repack header until it is posted, and the Repack list was driven by
the headers, so it disappeared. The list is now read from the RPK records (`ix_document_type_status`, newest first), each with its own
header or, while it has none, the header of the record it cancels.
Tests: `tests/Integration/Items/ItemsRaceTest.php` (two worker processes, `items_worker.php`), `HandMadeTest` (60 items of one name),
`RepackTest` (the cancellation waiting for an OK, then taken back).

**Open, for the owner.** (1) PB2, PB4, PB9: who holds the three new permissions. (2) PB3: is the second lead's OK of Q10 a check afterwards
(built, off) or a block until then? (3) PB7: is "sold separately" right as "a variant matched with 1 unit a sale", or must that variant be on
sale (the website state of 0028)? (4) PB10: carry the cost, or value what a repack makes at the average later? (5) Families on the reorder
list, the purchase order editor and the reports (Q4's "order and see reports by product") are not built here: they come with those screens.

## Pack C: supplier invoices, the 3-way match, credit and debit notes, returns to suppliers (worktree `pack-c`, 14 Oct 2026)

<!-- Pack C block: decisions PC1-PC19. Kept as one block for the merge (Packs B, D and E are built at the same time). -->

Plan IM7 ("supplier invoices, credit/debit notes, supplier returns"; the owner's list of 8 Oct 2026: "Purchase & Replenishment: to add
(pack C): supplier invoices with 3-way match; returns to supplier / debit notes"). Code: `migrations/0032_supplier_invoices.sql` (after
0029 A2a, 0031 B and 0033 D; 0030 is reserved for A2b), `src/Invoices/{InvoiceMath,InvoiceMatch,SupplierInvoiceHandler,
SupplierInvoices,SupplierReturnHandler,SupplierReturns,InvoiceInvariants}.php` (new), `src/Ui/Controller/{Invoices,SupplierReturns}Controller.php`
and the templates `invoices`, `invoices_to_match`, `invoices_not_invoiced`, `supplier_invoice`, `supplier_returns`, `supplier_return` (new);
marked blocks in `src/Documents/DocumentHandlers.php`, `src/Documents/Documents.php` (two calls of the new optional `CancelHook`,
`src/Documents/CancelHook.php`), `src/Invariants.php`, `src/Receiving/GoodsReceiptHandler.php` (one call),
`src/Settings.php`, `src/Auth/Permissions.php`, `src/Schema/Grants.php`, `src/Admin/{DocumentRules,ApprovalRules}.php`,
`src/Ui/{Words,Sections,Context,Kernel}.php`, `src/Ui/Controller/{Approvals,Reviews,Documents,Reference}Controller.php`,
`src/Ui/views/document.php`. Tests: `tests/Unit/{InvoiceMath,InvoiceTemplates}Test.php`, `tests/Integration/Invoices/`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/InvoiceScreensTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Migration0032Test.php`, and the shared tests the new tabs, kinds
and words change.

**PC1. Three papers, each a document type.** The supplier invoice (SINV, 0008), the supplier's credit note (SCN, new in 0032: its own
number series `SCN-`; a credit note is not a negative invoice, so its number never mixes with the invoices') and the return to the supplier
(DN, 0008: "supplier return / debit note"). Each is a draft -> posted (a reviewer's OK first only when a rule asks) -> cancelled by its
reversal; a draft is stopped, never deleted. An invoice or credit note is a `document` (the supplier's number as `external_ref`, the date
on the paper as `doc_date`) with a `supplier_invoice` header (the supplier; net, VAT and net + VAT exactly as the paper states them; a
credit note's invoice and debit note; the stored match) and lines with a `sinv_line` (goods, freight, duty, service, other). A goods line
is packs x units per pack at a pack price, like a receipt line (the same formulas: `PoMath`), and names the delivery line and the order
line it bills. A return is a `document` with a `supplier_return` header and `dn_line`s (see PC13). `CW\Invoices\SupplierInvoices` and
`SupplierReturns` are the services; `SupplierInvoiceHandler` (registered for SINV and SCN) and `SupplierReturnHandler` (DN) post them.
The posted module content is anchored write-once in `purchase_doc_posting` (like `grn_posting`; V2).

**PC2. The 3-way match, per goods line (`InvoiceMatch`, `InvoiceMath`).** What a line bills: its units and amount, less what the
supplier's posted credit notes took off that line. What is there to invoice ("available"): the delivery line's units accepted into stock
(`grn_line.accepted_units` of a posted receipt), less the units posted returns took back beyond the line's exceptions (PC14), less what the
supplier's OTHER posted invoices bill of that delivery line (net of their credit notes), less what this invoice's earlier lines bill of it.
The reference price: the order line's (pack price / units per pack), else the delivery's provisional cost, else none. A line is
`matched` (no extra units, the price exact), `within` the tolerance, or `off`. One invoice line names at most one delivery line: several
deliveries on one invoice are several lines (the quick way adds a line per delivery line); one delivery over several invoices is the
"other invoices" term; a delivery billed twice shows on both invoices. A line of a paper that sums two deliveries is keyed as two lines
(a build decision: the alternative, one line allocated over several delivery lines, needs an allocation table and a screen to split).
Billing fewer units than are there is not a mismatch (a partial invoice): the rest waits on "Not invoiced yet".

**PC3. The tolerances are settings, with the plan's numbers (IM7 W2: "price ±2% or ±£5 per line; total ±£0.05 × lines").**
`invoices.price_tolerance_pct` 2 and `invoices.price_tolerance_gbp` 5.00: a line's price difference (its amount less the same units at the
reference price) is within when it is at most £5 OR at most 2 % of the expected amount ("or" read as: either is enough; 0 switches that
test off; both 0: exact; a build decision to put to the owner). `invoices.qty_tolerance_pct` 0: the plan gives no quantity tolerance, so
exact (the over-delivery tolerance of IM5/IM6, 10 %, is about receiving, not billing). `invoices.total_tolerance_per_line` 0.05: the
lines may differ from the stated net total by 5p a line; beyond it the posting is refused (422 `total_mismatch`: a typing error in a line,
corrected before posting), within it the invoice is `within_tolerance`. All provisional, on Settings > Supplier invoices.

**PC4. The invoice's state and the "To match" list.** `needs_review` when a goods line is off; `within_tolerance` when a line is within or
the total differs by rounding; else `matched`. The money a person looks at (`match_difference`): on the lines that are off, what is
charged above the units there at the reference price. The state of every posted invoice is stored (`supplier_invoice.match_*`, with the
tolerances it was worked out with), so "To match" is one read on `(match_state, document_id)` and the badge one COUNT. A person holding
`invoices.accept` accepts the differences with a reason (3-500 characters): `accepted`, kept while the match is exactly what they accepted:
the same lines off with the same figures (`accepted_fingerprint`: each off line's units, money, units there, reference price, extra units,
money above and why). Any other match drops the acceptance (columns cleared, audit `invoice.accept_dropped` keeps it), so it never covers
a later difference nobody looked at (review finding 4, 14 Oct: the count and the money alone could match another line's difference). "Check these again" works the listed invoices out with
the tolerances in force now (after a tolerance changed). A goods line billed before its delivery (from an order: `addOrder`) has nothing
there to invoice and needs review (`no_delivery`): the plan has the invoice entered with or after the delivery.

**PC5. When the stored match is worked out again.** Inside the transaction of every change it reads: the invoice's own posting and
reversal; the posting and reversal of another invoice, a credit note or a return on the same deliveries; and the reversal of a receipt
(`GoodsReceiptHandler::reverse` calls `InvoiceMatch::afterReceiptReversed`, one line: its invoices now bill units that are not there:
`delivery_reversed`). The nightly check V4 works every stored match out again with its stored tolerances (the newest 2,000 records), so a
change that forgot to do it is found.

**PC6. Second-person rules: all OFF by default, all on the Approval Rules page (the owner's rule).** (1) The reviewer check after
posting is `none` for SINV, DN and SCN: version 2 of SINV's and DN's rule (0008 seeded `all` as a placeholder before any screen; the
"To match" list is the check an invoice gets), SCN's baseline `none`. (2) The OK first for a big record (`size_approval`, the SIZE_TYPES of
pack A1) for the three, sizes kept for when it is switched on (SINV £5,000; DN 100 units or £500; SCN £1,000). (3) NEW: an invoice whose
match needs review and charges more than a limit over what was ordered and received waits for a reviewer's OK before it is posted
(`approval_rule` `over_difference`, its limit in whole pounds, 0: any; `approvalUnits` = the money to look at rounded up). (4) NEW switch
`approvals.invoice_accept_other`: the differences of an invoice are accepted by someone other than the person who posted it (403
`own_invoice`); off, the poster may accept them, and the acceptance records the version of the switch it relied on (`rule_evidence`).

**PC7. Who (provisional, owner to confirm).** `doc.SINV.post` and `doc.DN.post` stay the purchasing desk's and the purchasing manager's
(I16); `doc.SCN.post` the same people. `invoices.view` reads invoices, credit notes, "To match" and "Not invoiced yet": buyers, the desk,
the purchasing manager, reviewers, the accountant, the auditor, the manager; not goods in (money). `invoices.accept`: the desk, the
purchasing manager, a reviewer. `returns.view` reads returns: as invoices.view plus goods in and the stock controller (they pack the
goods). Never admin (I12). `Permissions::COMING_LATER` no longer names invoices and returns.

**PC8. Price differences, freight and duty: recorded for the value engine, which is not built.** The task: feed them into the existing
value engine as value-only events, but only if it already has the route. It does not: `stock_value_ledger` exists (C0, I5: kinds
`cost_adjust`, `landed`, `price_credit` among them) but nothing writes it, and `Valuation.php` (IM8) does not exist. So a posting records
them on the invoice, in `invoice_value_event` (append-only; a reversal records the negation; V5): `price_difference` (a goods line on a
delivery: its amount less the delivery's units at the delivery's provisional cost), `freight` and `duty` (an invoice's freight and duty
lines spread over its delivered goods lines, PC9), `credit` (a credit note's goods line on a delivery: minus its amount). Each names the
item, the delivery line, the units, the amount (signed), how it was worked out and the date on the paper (the valuation date). **What is
missing for IM8:** (1) `Valuation.php`, the only writer of `stock_value_ledger`: the moving average per (pool, item), consuming
`stock_value_seq` in seq order; (2) a consumer of `invoice_value_event` that posts each as a value-only entry (`price_credit` /
`cost_adjust` for a price difference or a credit, `landed` for freight and duty) at its `effective_on`, the part for units still held to
stock and the part for units sold since to cost of sales (FRS 102; the plan's A1 posting map); (3) a marker of which events it has
consumed (none exists: nothing reads them yet); (4) whether a return's claimed price (the cost on its `supplier_return` ledger rows,
"evidence for IM8", I1) or the average values the units going back. `Stock.php`'s locks and buckets are untouched.

**PC9. How freight and duty are spread (settings).** Over the same invoice's goods lines on a delivery (IM8 Must; "across different
invoices" is IM8 W2): freight by value (`invoices.freight_spread` value | ml), duty by the liquid (`invoices.duty_spread` ml | value: units x
the item card's ml), to the penny by the largest remainder (the shares add up exactly); an item card without ml counts 0 and, when no line
has any, the spread is by value. An invoice without delivered goods (a carrier's freight invoice) spreads nothing.

**PC10. Locks (no cycle with the postings).** A posting or reversal of an invoice, credit note or return locks, after its own document
row and its number series (Documents), the `document` rows of the deliveries it reads (`InvoiceMatch::lockReceipts`, FOR UPDATE, id order;
a credit note first its invoice's row; an invoice whose OK first for differences is switched on takes them before its number series, in
`approvalUnits`, so the decision is made with them held through the posting: review finding 1), then the `supplier_invoice` rows it rewrites (`refresh`, id order, never another invoice's
`document` row). A receipt's reversal holds its own document row and takes the `supplier_invoice` rows. So a receipt reversed while one of
its invoices is posted waits for the other, and the second sees what the first did. An invoice with a posted credit note is not reversed
(409 `has_credit_notes`: reverse the credit note first), so a credit note never reduces a reversed invoice.

**PC11. The nightly checks V1-V7 (`InvoiceInvariants`, called by `Invariants::check`).** V1 headers of their kind; V2 the posting anchor;
V3 invoice keys (live: the number's key; cancelled or reversed: none); V4 the stored match; V5 value events net to zero with their reversal;
V6 a posted return's claim is the sum of its lines; V7 what a delivery has left to invoice, as stored (PC18).

**PC12. One supplier's paper is booked once.** `UNIQUE (supplier_id, kind, invoice_key)`: the key is the number as receipts compare it
(`ReceiptMath::invoiceKey`: case and spaces ignored; hyphens and slashes kept, I176 (2) still open), held while the record is draft,
waiting or posted and freed when it is stopped, refused at its OK first (the document base's `CancelHook`, called by `cancelDraft` and
`reject`: review finding 5) or cancelled. A duplicate is 409 `duplicate_invoice` naming the earlier one ("SINV-000001",
or "draft invoice #12 (who keyed it)"). An invoice and a credit note of the same number are two papers; another supplier's number is
another paper. A receipt's own invoice number (IM6) is the same paper as the invoice booked from it: not a duplicate.

**PC13. A return to the supplier is our debit note.** A DN takes stock out through the stock writer (`Movements::bookForDocument`, movement
`supplier_return`, one per warehouse, LAST in the posting), each item line from the warehouse it names (MAIN, VERIFY, UNSTAMPED: our own
stock, switched on), at the price claimed per unit (the ledger row's cost, cost source `document`), with a reason offered for returns that
takes stock down (line or header; the Reasons page). A line's amount is units x price to the penny plus the duty claimed with it; a claim
without goods (a short delivery, an overcharge) is an amount and what it is for. Posted, its claim (`claim_total`, excl. VAT) is the debit
note. Never below zero for a protected product unless the reason allows it (pack A1's rule, checked again after booking); never more back
from where it leaves than the delivery line put there (VERIFY: its exceptions there; UNSTAMPED: its quarantined units; anywhere else: its
accepted units) over every posted return (422 `return_more_than_received`). A return about a delivery (its header names one) takes every
item from that delivery's lines: an item added by hand is given the line of that item with room (else its first line), one not on the
delivery is refused (422 `line_not_on_delivery`), and changing the delivery re-links the lines (review finding 2). Once:
posting it again is 409 `not_draft` and moves nothing. Cancelled by its reversal (the generic exact negation; above the "stock put back"
limit it waits for a reviewer's OK, I32). The quick way: "Return what a delivery put aside" (its VERIFY and UNSTAMPED units not gone back
yet, from where they are, at the delivery's price).

**PC14. A return before the invoice lowers what waits to be invoiced; stock value is never reduced twice.** Units returned on a delivery
line count against what it put where they leave from (`InvoiceMatch::EXCEPTION_WAREHOUSES`): from VERIFY or UNSTAMPED, its exceptions
(damaged, wrong item, over; unstamped: never accepted, never to be invoiced); from anywhere else, its accepted units. So returning the
damaged units changes nothing on the invoice side (the supplier's credit note does), and returning accepted units before the invoice leaves
fewer to invoice ("Not invoiced yet", the match). (First built as "exceptions first, whatever the warehouse": review finding 3, 14 Oct,
showed accepted units going back from MAIN were then not taken off.)

**PC15. Credit notes.** A credit note names the invoice it reduces (or none: a credit on account) and the return it answers (optional).
Each goods line credits units of one line of that invoice (it copies the line's delivery and order) and is billed less in the match (PC2);
never more than the line billed over every posted credit note (422 `credit_more_than_invoiced`). It lowers what is owed on the invoice
(the invoice's net + VAT less its posted credit notes' net + VAT; payments are not in CW). A return shows how its claim stands: not
credited yet, part credited, credited (the posted credit notes' net against the claim). "Book the supplier's credit note" on a return
starts one with a goods credit for each returned line its invoice bills (at most what is left to credit), the duty claimed, and the rest
of the claim as "other" lines.

**PC16. Duty in a claim.** A retailer cannot reclaim duty on damaged or destroyed stock, so the supplier's credit includes it (plan IM7).
The quick return fills the duty only when the supplier's invoice of that delivery charged duty on its own line (the receipt's expected
duty, pro rata to the units): when the pack price includes the duty, the claimed price already does, and adding it again would claim it
twice. The desk can change it.

**PC17. Screens (the v4 look; tabs inside Purchasing; no new sidebar item).** Purchasing › Invoices (segments: Invoices, To match with its
badge for the people who post or accept invoices, Not invoiced yet with "Book its invoice" on each delivery, Credit notes) and Purchasing ›
Returns. The quick way is "Book its invoice", on "Not invoiced yet" and on the delivery's own page in Goods In (which also names the
invoices that bill it): the invoice starts with the delivery's number (left empty with a notice
when an invoice of the supplier already has it), the date on its invoice, its invoice copy, and a line per delivery line still to
invoice; the desk checks the lines, types the total without VAT and the VAT, and posts. A record's generic page (Approvals › History) and
a review decision lead to its own page. Every word is in `Ui\Words` (INVOICES, INVOICE_KIND, ... RETURN_ERROR).

**PC18. "Not invoiced yet" reads stored figures; the list reads were measured.** Adding every delivery line up on each view took
1.4-3.4 s on a filled schema (a year of purchasing: 5,000 deliveries of 10 lines, 4,000 invoices, 300 credit notes, 500 returns; staging,
32 MB buffer pool) and 0.5 s for one supplier; per-line lookups and LATERAL were no better in the worst case (`packc_grni.txt`). So every
posting and reversal of an invoice, a credit note or a return stores, for the deliveries it names (locked, before any stock is booked),
what each still has to be invoiced (`grn_invoice_left`: units and their value at the delivery's provisional cost, `InvoiceMatch::
storeReceipts`); a delivery none has named has no row and everything it accepted is left. The list is then one read on the posted
deliveries, newest first. V7 checks the rows (the newest 2,000) and that every delivery named has one. The returns list's "credited" is
one grouped read of the credit notes that answer a return (a subquery per return chose a full scan of `supplier_invoice`: 2.2-2.9 s for
500 returns). Every other new read is an indexed one (`packc_explain.txt`, in the build's run folder, not committed).

**PC19. Owner, 15 Oct: the invoice price is the right price.** The owner's words: "end of the day whatever comes in purchase invoice is
the right price". A new switch, `invoices.check_price` (0040, a migration of its own: 0032 is applied on staging), **off**, not
provisional (the owner's own decision). Off: a goods line whose price differs from the order (else the delivery's price) is never
`within` or `off` for its price, whatever the size of the difference, so the price alone never puts an invoice on "To match"; the
difference stays on the line (`price_e2`, `price_note`) and the invoice's page says it as information ("Price differs from the order:
£0.15 more. The invoice price is used."); it is still recorded for the value engine exactly as before (`invoice_value_event`
`price_difference` against the delivery's provisional cost: the invoice's price is the cost carried forward, PC8). The quantity is
checked exactly as before: billing more units than arrived (beyond `invoices.qty_tolerance_pct`) still needs a person, and the money
shown for it is the extra units at the invoice's own price. On: the two price tolerances (PC3) apply unchanged. While it is off, the
Settings list greys the two price tolerances and says they are not used (`Settings::UNUSED_WHEN_OFF`); their values are kept. The
tolerances a stored match was worked out with now include the switch; a match stored before 0040 has none and reads as checked (V4).
"Check these again" on "To match" works the listed invoices out with the switch as it is now (the migration recomputes nothing).

**Not done (out of scope or left for the owner):** supplier payments, the ledger, bank, VAT returns and the accountant's files (scope);
the supplier item's "last price from the latest invoice" (IM4; I146's open item): an invoice records no `supplier_item_price` row, because a
price row cannot be taken back when the invoice is cancelled (append-only) and S4 would then keep a cancelled price: a decision for the
owner; a price-variance report as a file (the match is on each invoice and the "To match" list); an invoice line allocated over several
delivery lines (PC2); freight across invoices (IM8 W2); a foreign-currency invoice (GBP only, I1).

**Open for the owner:** PC3 ("or" in the price tolerance, which applies only with `invoices.check_price` on since PC19; the exact
quantity); PC6 (no reviewer check after posting by default for invoices
and returns); PC7 (who); the "last price" question above; whether a return's units are valued at the claimed price or the average (PC8 (4)).
## Going live, the CW side: the stores' queues, the relay intake, alerts, clean-up (pack F, slot `packf`, 14 Oct 2026)

Numbered PF1-PF14 (prefix PF: packs B-E, QC and arrival 2b are built at the same time). Source: the go-live plan part 6 ("The relay",
"Staff queue screens and their actions", "Alerts to a person", "Housekeeping on CW") and part 9 (lists A16, C2), the approved plan §2.2,
§3, §9, D14, D17, D18, H6, H8, R17, I144. Code: `migrations/0036_golive_queues_alerts.sql`, `src/Relay/{RelayLines,RelayIntake}.php`,
`src/Movements.php` (the per-line claim and `bookInTransaction`), `src/Queues/*`, `src/Ops/{ChannelHealth,Alerts,AlertDispatch,AlertTransport,AlertSender,Housekeeping}.php`,
`bin/{health_alert,housekeeping,channel_set}.php`, `src/ChannelAdmin.php` (relay grants), `src/Api/Controller/RelayController.php`,
`src/Ui/Controller/StoreQueuesController.php`, views `queue_*.php`, `src/Admin/Sites.php` (the Stores page's relay line). `src/Stock.php`
is not changed (its lock() and setPolicy steps are used as they are).

**PF1. A relayed document line is booked once, whatever key it comes under.** The plan's key is "document name + line index, never per
variant" (§9), but POST /v1/movements was idempotent per Idempotency-Key only: the same ERPNext purchase invoice re-sent under another key
(the store's queue after a restore, a worker that lost its answer) booked again; only its suspense lines were deduplicated. New table
`relay_line` (UNIQUE channel, kind, document, line). For a store's goods_in / supplier_return / erp_sale, `Movements::record` claims each
line inside the call's transaction, after the key and BEFORE any stock lock (INSERT … ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE; claims in line order, so two
calls never wait in a circle; a copy at the same moment waits for the first's commit and then finds it). A line already there is not booked:
the answer says `already_recorded` with what became of it the first time (`booked`, `suspense`), or `conflict` when the same document line now
carries other content (`line_hash`, the canonical line). What became of a claimed line (outcome, item, units, the suspense row) is written in
the same transaction; the rest of a row is frozen (Grants: append-only plus those columns), and rows are never pruned. A suspended line sent
again after its variant was matched stays in suspense: it is placed by a person, never booked twice. Staff movements are not keyed per line.
The response of a call with only new lines is unchanged; the canonical request (the idempotency hash) is unchanged.

**PF2. ERPNext's corrections go to the count-review queue (POST /v1/relay/reconciliations).** `{doc_ref, posted_at?, warehouse?, lines:
[{line_index?, variant_id | erp_item_code, qty, description?}]}`; qty is the figure ERPNext set, in the variant's units. Each line opens one
`count_review` (source `erp_reconciliation`, warehouse = the store's selling warehouse, `proposed_qty` = qty × units per item, `ref` = the
document, `detail` = the line, its units, the store and `posted_at`: when ERPNext set it, default when CW received it, at most 90 days old);
dedupe `erp_reconciliation:<channel>:<document>#<line>`. Nothing is booked ("ERPNext's pushes never become counts automatically"). A line CW
cannot place goes to goods-in suspense with movement type `erp_reconciliation` (doc type `stock_reconciliation`): picking its item there opens
the correction (PF6). The plan_final's "one queue entry per document" is not taken: a correction is answered per item (each line), which is
what a person can check on a shelf; the screen shows the document on every row.

**PF3. ERPNext's mode changes go to the policy-review queue, filtered (POST /v1/relay/modes).** `{doc_ref (the store's message id),
changed_at?, lines: [{line_index?, variant_id | erp_item_code, mode, low_stock?, previous_mode?, previous_low_stock?}]}`. The go-live plan's
queue filter (D14: "a push that changes nothing is logged and not shown"): a line is recorded as `no_change` when the store says the mode and
low-stock level were already so (`same_on_store`), when CW already has that mode (and level) for the item on this store (a legacy item:
`item_channel_mode`, else what `SellingModes::current` knows; `same_in_cw`), or when the stock rule it proposes is the item's already (a
protected item; `same_rule`). A variant CW does not know or that is not matched is recorded as `skipped` (no item to apply it to). The others
open a `policy_review` (source `erp_update_product`; `site_mode` = the ERPNext mode; `proposed_policy` from the settings `relay.mode_in_stock`
backorder, `relay.mode_from_warehouse` strict, `relay.mode_out_of_stock` stopped: the plan's map, now settings). A newer change of the same
variant replaces an older open one: settled `dismissed` / `superseded` with no person, never removed. Every line, queued or not, is in
`relay_line` (the "logged" of the filter) and the call's audit row.

**PF4. The relay permission: a tool, and the Stores page.** R17 left "changing it later is SQL for now". The grants are the store's
`channel.movement_types`, extended to five (`ChannelAdmin::RELAY_GRANTS` = `RelayLines::KINDS`: goods_in, supplier_return, erp_sale,
erp_reconciliation, erp_mode); `Movements::checkAllowed` is unchanged (only the three stock kinds may be sent as movements). `bin/channel_set.php
--relay=on|off|<grants>` (dry run unless --apply, `--actor`, audited `channel.relay` {from, to, by}; ending it warns that CW then answers 403
and stores nothing, the store keeps its messages). The Stores page shows "Messages from ERPNext: all received / none / received: …" and the
command in its folded technical details, like the other channel switches (a screen button was not added: the channel's switches are server
commands with the owner's sign-off, Y30). The two new routes answer 403 `relay_not_allowed` without their grant (not stored) and 409
`channel_off` while the store is off (the go-live plan: the store keeps ERPNext's messages and sends them later).

**PF5. Approvals › From the stores: one tab, four segments.** Lines to place (`goods_in_suspense`), ERPNext corrections (`count_review` of
source `erp_reconciliation` only: the count engine's own reviews stay on Stock › Counts › Differences, CT6), Mode changes (`policy_review` of
source `erp_update_product`), Oversold (`oversell_event`). Approvals because each is work waiting for a person's answer. Permissions
(provisional, owner to confirm; never admin, I12): `queues.view` (everyone who reads records, the auditor and the accountant), `queues.suspense`
(purchasing desk and manager, stock controller), `queues.corrections` (stock controller: it changes the figure without a count),
`queues.modes` (the people who set modes, I158: desk, purchasing manager, stock controller, manager), `queues.oversell` (desk, purchasing
manager, stock controller, manager). Each service re-reads the roles inside its transaction. Every answer needs a note (3-500 characters).
A row is settled once: the row is locked first, an answer on a row that is no longer open is 409 `queue_settled`; the two answers that book
stock run under the key `queue:<queue>:<id>`, so a second click replays the first answer and the same key with another item is 422
`idempotency_key_reused`; the job is checked before the key too (a person without the job hears that, not someone else's stored answer).
The four queue tables are NO_DELETE for the app login (D17: "rows are never deleted"). Badges count only what the
person may answer. Lists: open rows oldest first, a page of 50; a status filter (waiting, done, closed, all). The v4 cards of the incident
register (no new CSS, no script).

**PF6. Lines to place.** A person types the item's code and how many of its units one unit of the line is (1 unless the document counts
packs), and a note. A delivery, supplier return or ERPNext sale is booked NOW through the movement route (`Movements::bookInTransaction`: the
same checks and booking as record(), one lock and one flush, in the queue action's transaction, staff only; the ledger carries the ERPNext
document's name and the person) on the store's selling warehouse, and the row is resolved with the item, in one transaction. Locks: the row,
the item's balance (`Stock::lock`), then the row's update naming the item (its foreign key reads the item row: balances before the item,
`setPolicy`'s order), then the booking (the same balance, held) and the feed clock last. A relayed correction is not booked: its item opens
the correction (PF7). Close without booking: a note. The break-glass of I144 (a lead books against a named purchase invoice during a relay
outage, the later relay posts only the difference) is NOT built: it needs the shop-side relay.

**PF7. ERPNext corrections: confirm books the difference at the correction's moment, as an adjustment, not a count.** The go-live plan's
rule 1 (part 6, row 0.8): after a person confirms a correction, CW's figure for sale equals the number the shop was given at the moment it
applied it, and the item is NOT marked as counted by it. So: the shelf figure ERPNext meant = its number in CW's units, plus the units CW kept
then for paid orders not sent (`allocated`) when `relay.correction_is_for_sale` is on (on the website the number is the figure customers can
buy; default on). What CW held then is read from the ledger as booked at that moment (the last row created by then, then each bucket's
balance-after at or before it, `ix_stock_ledger_balance`). The difference is booked now as an `adjustment` (the ERPNext document's name on the
ledger), so what moved since (deliveries, parcels sent) is kept on top; 0 books nothing (`no_difference`). A count (`type count`) was not used:
it would set the balance's count time (the count plan's) and overwrite every movement since the correction (R13). The screen shows the
figures and what confirming books before the person answers. Close: a note, nothing booked. Unheld units (`held`) are not added: the store
takes stock off at payment.

**PF8. Mode changes: accept applies it by the item's state now.** A legacy item (not counted): the selling mode CW writes on THAT store
becomes ERPNext's mode, with the low-stock level when sent (`SiteModes::set`, IM10's switch, on the relaying store only, the person's note as
the reason); its stock rule stays legacy (only the count gate protects an item, §7.4). A protected item: its stock rule becomes the proposed
one, by `Stock::setPolicy`'s steps inside the review's transaction (its balances, then the item row, then the feed clock). The screen says
which before the person answers. Keep what CW has: a note.

**PF9. Oversold: mark handled, add notes.** Handled with how (sent later, refunded, nothing needed: `oversell_event.resolution`, the values
0001 names) and a note; settled once. Notes (open or handled) are rows of the new append-only `queue_note`, never changed or removed; the
card lists them with who and when.

**PF10. Alerts to a person.** `bin/health_alert.php` (H8's stub) now checks, each limit a setting (`alerts.*`): per store in watching or live
(its newest heartbeat): no report for `alerts.heartbeat_late_seconds` (180), outbox deeper than `alerts.outbox_max_depth` (500) or its oldest
message older than `alerts.outbox_max_age_seconds` (300: the go-live trigger "oldest waiting message over 5 minutes"), more than
