`alerts.dead_letters_max` (0: "any") failed for good, `alerts.feed_lag_max_seconds` (60) or more behind CW's change feed (at its last
heartbeat: from the first change after the seq it applied to the heartbeat), another mode than CW's; CW itself: its own answer time (a new
connection and the reads of a health call, `alerts.answer_probes` (3) times, the middle above `alerts.answer_max_ms` (1500, the go-live
"none over 1.5 s"); a probe that cannot connect is its own alert; measured on CW's server: what a store sees at Place order is read from its
connector log on the store, not built here), and the nightly safety check (`integrity_run`: the newest failed, or none finished for
`alerts.invariants_max_age_hours`, 36; a system where none ever ran is quiet, as Home is). `Ops\AlertDispatch` sends them to
`alerts.webhook_url` (https only: a JSON POST whose `text` a chat channel shows; redirects not followed) and/or `alerts.email_to` (PHP mail():
the server needs a mail transfer agent; staging has none known, so an e-mail address there reports "not taken"), BOTH EMPTY by default:
nothing is sent and no transport is called. Once per window (`alerts.repeat_minutes`, 60) per problem (`alert_state`), at once when it comes
back after clearing, and one "back to normal" line when a sent problem clears. A destination that fails is reported on stderr without its
address and the problems are tried again next run. One message per run. The job takes its lock now (it records what it sent). Scheduled every
2 minutes; `--no-send` checks and prints only (the installer's smoke). The CLI lines and the "ok" line are as before (OpsScriptsTest).
The address is a secret setting since PF15: masked on the screens, a fingerprint in the history and the audit log; only https to a public
server, pinned (PF15, 6 and 7).

**PF11. Clean-up.** `bin/housekeeping.php` (nightly 03:37): `idempotency` older than `housekeeping.idempotency_keep_days` (30, the floor D14
sets), `channel_health` older than `housekeeping.channel_health_keep_days` (30, D18) except each store's newest row (the Stores page and the
alerts read it: a store silent for longer still reads "last contact <date>"), `audit_log` older than `housekeeping.audit_keep_years` (7, its
floor: records are kept "year end + 6 years"; when unsure, 7). Chunks of `housekeeping.chunk_rows` (1000), each an autocommit DELETE … ORDER BY
… LIMIT on the table's time index, until done or `housekeeping.max_seconds` (300; the rest the next night). A retention below its floor is
never used, even if the row were changed by hand. The grants decide the audit part: the app login has no DELETE on `audit_log` (append-only),
so with it (the cron) the database refuses and the run reports "kept"; only `--admin` (a person's decision) removes audit rows. A key pruned
and sent again is still held by `relay_line` (PF1) or by its queue row's status (PF5). `--dry-run` counts only.

**PF12. Cron.** `deploy/staging/cw-staging.cron`: health_alert every 2 minutes (it was commented out, H6), housekeeping at 03:37; the
installer's smoke runs `health_alert.php --no-send` and `housekeeping.php --dry-run`. Not done: the jobs still run as root on staging (H6's
"production should run them as a dedicated user": production is not provisioned).

**PF13. Plans (EXPLAIN on a filled schema, `QueueListPlansTest`).** Every queue list (open rows) reads its (status, created_at) index, or
count_review's (status, source, id), with no file sort; the badge counts the same indexes; the notes (queue_name, row_id, id); the alerts'
latest heartbeat (channel_id, id) and feed-lag read (the primary key); the correction's ledger reads (created_at; (warehouse, item, id) forced);
the clean-up's deletes (their time indexes; the heartbeat chunks read the primary key's range below each store's newest row: ids grow
with time, so the oldest rows come first and a chunk stops at its LIMIT); the relay claim its unique key. The corrections and oversold lists
join the item and the warehouse with STRAIGHT_JOIN: on a small item table the optimizer drove the join from `sku` and sorted the open rows in
a temporary table (found by this test). Figures (3,000 rows per queue, 50 open): every list `ref` on its index, 50 rows examined, no file
sort. No new index.

**PF14. Not built, or left for the owner.** (1) The shop-side relay (the connector's part: sending these messages, its outbox while off, the
company filter, the break-glass of I144). (2) The connector-log alerts (answer time at Place order, PHP errors naming the connector, the
hourly order job, the e-mail count, an outside check of CW): the go-live plan's step 0.6, shop side. (3) An e-mail sender on the CW server.
(4) A screen button to give or end the relay (a server command, like the other channel switches). (5) Every number above is provisional, a
setting with a reason on Settings › System › Settings; the permissions are provisional (owner to confirm). (6) Production's jobs as a
dedicated user (H6).

**PF15. The Codex review of 14 Oct 2026 (`/root/cw_work/runs/packf_codex_review.txt`, nine findings, all real) and what changed.** Each was
first shown by a failing test (`runs/packf_r1_red.log`: ten tests, all red on the unfixed code), then fixed.
1. *Corrections confirmed late compounded* (20 -> 10 -> 8, both waiting, booked -10 and -12: -2; reproduced exactly). What CW held at a
   correction's moment now also counts the corrections of the same item and place made at or before it and booked after it (their
   delta and booking time are written on the row, `detail.booked`); an older correction confirmed after a newer one is refused (409
   `newer_correction`, the screen says to close it). The item's balance is locked before the reading, so two confirmations queue (PF7).
2. *Queue keys were cut at 191 bytes*, so a 191-byte document name dropped the line: two lines shared a key and the second was lost. A
   key that does not fit is now the kind and a sha256 of the whole (store, kind, document, line) (`Movements::queueKey`; goods-in
   suspense, corrections, mode changes).
3. *A newer change that changes nothing left the older request open*: it now closes it (`superseded`) (PF3).
4. *Arrival order, not change time, decided the supersession*: a change is compared by its `changed_at` (the relayed time, else when it
   arrived); a change older than one already known for the variant (open, answered or replaced) is recorded `no_change` /
   `older_than_known` and replaces nothing.
5. *An item-only change of one store closed another store's request*: requests named by an ERPNext item alone are compared within their
   store (detail.channel_id). The requests of one variant are locked while a message decides.
6. *The web address (it can hold a token) showed on the settings pages, in the setting's history and in the audit log.* `Settings::SECRET`
   (`alerts.webhook_url`): the pages and bin/settings.php show "https://host/…"; the history and the audit log keep a fingerprint
   (`hidden:sha256:…`), applied alike to the live row and the versions, so the nightly K checks still compare; the form sent back with the
   masked value keeps the address; the alert sender reads it whole.
7. *The web address could reach a private service (SSRF).* `AlertSender::destination()`: https only, a server name (no IP literal), every
   address it resolves to must be public (private, loopback, link-local, reserved, shared and benchmarking ranges refused), and the request
   is pinned to the address checked (curl RESOLVE; without curl, the address itself with the name for TLS).
8. *A "back to normal" that could not be sent was lost*: it is owed (`alert_state.clear_sent_at`, added to 0036, which no shared schema
   has applied) and sent on a later run, once; a problem that comes back first makes it moot.
9. *The clean-up's time limit was checked after a chunk*: it is checked before every chunk (each table and store included); an
   injectable monotonic clock tests it.
Tests: `StoreQueuesTest::testDelayedCorrectionsOfOneItemDoNotCompound`, `RelayIntakeTest::{testALongDocumentNameKeepsEveryLineApart,
testANewerChangeThatChangesNothingClosesTheOlderRequest, testAnOlderChangeArrivingLateNeverReplacesANewerOne,
testItemOnlyChangesOfTwoStoresStayApart}`, `AlertsTest::{testABackToNormalThatFailedIsSentOnTheNextRun,
testTheWebAddressIsNeverShownOrKeptInHistory}`, `StoreQueuesScreensTest::testTheSettingsPagesNeverShowTheWebAddressWhole`,
`GoLiveQueuesUnitTest::testTheWebAddressMustLeadToAPublicServer`, `HousekeepingTest::testTheTimeLimitIsCheckedBeforeEveryChunk`.



<!-- ==== Pack E (worktree cw-packe, branch pack-e; migration 0034, may be renumbered at merge) ==== -->
## Pack E: Reports, and who can do what changed on the screen (slot `packe`, 14 Oct 2026)

The owner's module list of 8 Oct 2026: "Reports & Analytics: Stock by Store, Sales by Store, Low Stock (threshold setting), stock value,
slow / dead stock"; "Inventory Valuation: stock value report (average cost, £)"; "Inventory Settings: an editable Roles and permissions
screen". Code: `migrations/0034_reports_roles.sql`; `src/Auth/{Permissions,RoleMap}.php`, `src/Admin/RolePermissions.php`;
`src/Reports/{ReportRefresh,ReportViews}.php`, `bin/refresh_reports.php`, `deploy/staging/cw-staging.cron`;
`src/Ui/Controller/{ReportsController,AccessController}.php`, views `report_{store,sales,low,value,slow}`, `access_permission`, `access`;
the marked blocks of `Words`, `Settings`, `Sections`, `Permissions`. Tests: `tests/Unit/{RoleMapTest,ReportsUnitTest}.php`,
`tests/Integration/Admin/RolePermissionsTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Reports/ReportRefreshTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/{RolesScreenTest,ReportsScreenTest}.php`; `tests/perf/report_explain.php` (EXPLAIN on a filled schema).
Every decision below is a build decision put to the owner, not the owner's.

**PE1. Two new permissions, both read only.** `reports.view` (Stock by Store, Sales by Store, Low Stock, Slow Stock: stock and sales
figures, no money): warehouse, manager, buyer, purchasing_manager, goods_in, purchasing_desk, stock_controller, reviewer, accountant,
auditor. `values.view` (Stock Value: pounds): purchasing_manager, reviewer, accountant, auditor; Slow Stock shows its value column only to
them. Never admin (I12: admin manages people), never the matching-only jobs. The five reports are tabs of the existing Reports section,
before the Audit Log, each a GET page and the same list as a CSV (`/ui/reports/<page>.csv`, the CsvWriter's safe cells); no POST route.

**PE2. Who holds each permission is kept in the database.** `role_permission`, one row per permission, the jobs in `Permissions::ROLES`
order, comma-separated; 0034 seeds it from `Permissions::MAP` exactly as the code had it (RoleMapTest holds the seed and the code
together), so nothing changes on deploy. It is read on every /ui request (`Auth\RoleMap::load` in `Ui\Kernel`, before the session's
roles are checked) and again wherever a service re-reads a person's roles inside its transaction (`Staff\StaffRoles::active`), so a
permission taken away stops working on the next page and the next action, as a role taken away does (I11). `Permissions::can()` and
every caller are unchanged: they read the map in force (`Permissions::map()`); `Permissions::MAP` stays the code's list of permissions
and the default of a permission that has no row. The app login may read, add and change rows, never delete them (`Grants::NO_DELETE`).

**PE3. A permission another pack adds to the code works at once, with its safe default.** A key in `MAP` without a row reads as MAP
says (sanitised, PE4): a pack that adds `items.create => [...]` needs no migration of its own for it, and the screen lists it as "as the
system was delivered". The first change on the screen inserts its row, with version 1 a baseline of MAP's holders and version 2 the
change (`ConfigHistory::record`), so the nightly checks hold. Two guards for the merge: RoleMapTest fails (a) if a pack changes the
holders of a permission 0034 seeds (update 0034's seed while it is not applied anywhere, or add a migration), and (b) if a permission in
the code breaks a rule of PE4 (for example an acting permission given to the auditor). Once a row exists it wins over MAP: a later change
of MAP for that permission needs a migration.

**PE4. The rules hold whatever the table says** (`Permissions::sanitise`, read fail-closed; `Permissions::problems`, the screen's
refusals): (1) LOCKED, never changed on the screen and read as MAP whatever the row: `catalogue.view`, `reference.view` (every job: Home
and the settings pages), `staff.manage`, `settings.manage` (stays admin plus reviewer, Y1), `staff.approve` (only a Reviewer loosens a
rule, I1), `mapping.decide`, `mapping.approve` (DecisionService and KeySample read the matching leads by job name), `company.edit`,
`company.confirm` (CompanyDetails and CompanyInvariants read their holders by job name); (2) a permission is read-only exactly when its
key ends in ".view"; one that changes anything is never held by admin or by the look-only jobs admin may be combined with (viewer,
accountant, auditor), so "admin never holds a working job" (I12) cannot be undone through the map; (3) REQUIRED: admin always keeps
`staff.view`, the reviewer always keeps `documents.review`, `documents.approve` and `suppliers.approve`; (4) an unknown job in a row is
dropped; a row emptied by SQL means nobody (except the required jobs).

**PE5. Who changes it, and only a Reviewer gives.** An admin or a reviewer (`settings.manage`, re-read inside the transaction), as every
setting (Y1). Giving a job a permission is loosening and needs a Reviewer (`staff.approve`, `ApprovalRules::authoriseLoosening`, I1,
Y45); taking one away is tightening and needs `settings.manage` only. A change that gives one job and takes another is a give. The
owner's staging account (Admin + Reviewer + Matching lead) cannot give, because its Reviewer job is off while it holds Admin.

**PE6. Nobody gives a permission to a job they hold** (403 `own_job`): the editor's live jobs (all of them, switched off or not) are
re-read inside the transaction; a change that gives any of them is refused whole. So a person never grants themselves more rights.
Consequence: every person who may give holds the Reviewer job, so on the screen the reviewer job can lose permissions but never gain
one; a server tool (a system caller) can (the break-glass; no tool is built for it, PE14).

**PE7. Every task keeps at least one job** (422 `no_holders`): an empty list is never what a person means; to stop a task, leave it with
the fewest jobs. Every page refusal says what went wrong and that nothing was saved, with the ticks kept (`Words::ROLES_ERROR`).

**PE8. Audited like the settings.** `config_change` gains the subject type `permission` (the ENUM member added at the end, in place):
one version per change with the jobs before and after, the reason (3-500 characters) and who; the form carries the version it was
drawn with (409 `changed_meanwhile`); `audit_log` gets `permission.change` {permission, before, after, added, removed, reason, version,
loosened}. The nightly K1-K4 cover the new subject. The task's page (Settings › Users › Roles and permissions › a task) shows its
history. The sentences that name the jobs of a task (`Words::whoCan`) keep the code's order, so they read as before until someone
changes the map.

**PE9. Low Stock.** A product is low when the units the stores can sell (the sellable warehouses' on hand less reserved) are at or
below its own "least stock to keep" (`item_reorder.min_stock`, set on its reorder page: the per-item level that already exists; the item
card has none, so none was added), else the setting `reports.low_stock_default` (5 units). The websites' own low-stock level that
the stock writer sends (`item_channel_mode.low_stock_threshold`, IM10) is per store and is what a website shows its customers; it is
not used here, because this list is per product across the stores. Only products a store sells (matched on a
store), not merged into another, not marked discontinued on their card. Two lists: Low (above zero) and None left (zero or less).

**PE10. Stock Value at average cost.** The average cost of an item is the existing estimate of the value engine,
`StockOps\CostHints::average`: the weighted average of every unit that came in with a cost (an on-hand rise with `unit_cost`), rounded
half up to 6 decimals; the report job keeps its two sums per item (`report_item.in_units`, `in_value`) from the item's value sequence,
never by scanning the ledger. The value of an item in a warehouse is its units there (above zero) times that cost, rounded half up to
pennies; a product, a brand, a warehouse and the whole stock are sums of those, so they add up exactly. Another account's warehouses are
shown apart and never in our value; items with stock and no cost are counted and listed. **The value at a past date is not built**: the
value ledger (`stock_value_ledger`, IM8) is still empty, so the engine has no valuation at a date to read.

**PE11. Slow and dead stock.** Two settings: `reports.slow_after_days` (60) and `reports.dead_after_days` (180, at least the slow days).
A sale is a paid store order (a unit allocated, sent or returned), a sale booked through ERPNext or to a trade customer (the value
sequence), or a day of the sales history loaded from the websites (Reorder's import, so the report is useful before the stores are
live); a product never sold counts from the first day its stock came in. A product the job has not read yet is left out.

**PE12. The report job: on by default, because it writes only its own tables.** `bin/refresh_reports.php`, every 15 minutes
(`deploy/staging/cw-staging.cron`, one line; the installer's smoke runs `--status`, which writes nothing), the Cli job lock (one run at a
time), switched by `reports.refresh_on` (true). It writes only `report_item`, `report_sales_day` and `report_refresh`, which nothing else
reads and `--rebuild` empties; each run reads at most `reports.refresh_max_rows` value-sequence rows (50,000) and
`reports.refresh_max_days` days of store sales (31). Exact whatever was read before: (A) per item, from its value sequence (gap-free per
item, in commit order, I3) up to its clock; (B) per UK day and store, each day worked out whole again (orders paid by
`reservation.committed_at`, served by the new index `ix_reservation_committed (status, committed_at, channel_id)`; sends, cancels and
returns by the ledger's `created_at`, read as one range of ids found through `ix_stock_ledger_created`), from the day of the last run
less an hour (a transaction that began before a run and committed after it) to today; (C) the imported sales history batch by batch in
id order, stopping at a batch still loading.

**PE13. Sales by Store.** Per UK day and store: orders paid that day; units sold (warehouse units: a pack of 3 counts 3; every unit of a
paid order, also one cancelled later); units sent, cancelled and returned, each on the day the store told CW. A store product not
matched to a warehouse product moves no stock: its units count as sold but never as sent, cancelled or returned. Sales booked through
ERPNext are not store orders and are not here (they count as a last sale, PE11). The period: last 7 or 30 days, this or last month, or
chosen days, at most `reports.sales_max_days` (366) at once (the last days are kept, and the page says so).

**PE15. Measured on a filled schema** (`tests/perf/report_explain.php`, slot `packe`, 14 Oct 2026; logs `runs/packe_explain.log`, `runs/packe_explain2.log`:
20,000 items, 28,666 store products, 335,000 ledger rows, 165,000 value-sequence rows, 100,000 paid orders with 200,000 units, 100,000
days of sales history, on the staging cluster with its 32 MB buffer pool). No page reads the ledger. Each list is read ONCE: the page's
rows and the list's counts come from one statement (window functions over the inner query), as the EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows. Times of a
page's reads: Stock by Store 0.36-0.76 s for the list plus 0.42 s for the three stores' figures (every matched product of every store
and its balance: the heaviest page, the same kind of read as Stock › Overview); Low Stock 0.43-0.47 s; Stock Value 0.11-0.29 s; Slow
Stock 0.12 s; Sales by Store 5-10 ms (the summary table's primary key, a year at once); the map of permissions 10 ms. The job: a quiet
run (nothing new but today's orders) 0.2-0.44 s, served by indexes throughout (`ix_reservation_committed` covering the day's paid
orders, `ix_stock_ledger_created` with the id range for the day's ledger rows); the catch-up from nothing took 8 runs of at most 35 s.

**PE14. Not done in pack E** (each would be a decision for the owner): the stock value at a past date (PE10); an editable list of the
guarded jobs (`ApprovalRules::GUARDED_ROLES`: making it shorter would loosen the staff-grant rule; admin and reviewer stay its floor); a
server tool to change the map (the break-glass is SQL with the admin login, which the read fail-closes, PE4); new jobs (the job list is
the `staff_role` ENUM: a new job needs a migration); low levels per store; plain-words column names in the CSV files (they use column
names, as the other CSV downloads do); the per-store figures of Stock by Store kept by the job (they are read live, PE15); the People form's
one-line job descriptions (`Permissions::DESCRIPTIONS`) stay code text and do not follow a change of the map (the Roles and permissions
page does).
### The Codex review of pack E (on `71b8fc0`; `runs/packe_codex_review.txt`): three findings, all real, each fixed test-first

**PE16. A job given a Reviewer's or an Admin's power is guarded like them** (finding 1, high). With `approvals.staff_grant` on, a
Reviewer could give `documents.approve` to Warehouse staff on the Roles and permissions page, and an admin could then give Warehouse to
anyone at once: the staff-grant and staff-reset rules guarded the two job names only. Now `ApprovalRules::guardedRoles()` reads the
guarded jobs from the map in force (re-read inside the transaction): Admin and Reviewer, plus every job that holds one of the powers the
code keeps for them (`Permissions::guardedPowers()`: every permission whose holders in MAP are Admin and Reviewer only; today
staff.manage, settings.manage, staff.approve, documents.review, documents.approve, suppliers.approve, company.edit, company.confirm, and
any such permission a later pack adds). It is used for giving a job (setRoles), setting a person up (enrol), the request's guarded list,
and resets. With the map as delivered the set is Admin and Reviewer, as before. Not every job holding any acting permission: that would
make nearly every job's grant wait (buyers, matchers) whenever the owner switches the rule on, which is not the rule's meaning (the
second person's powers). The rule's words now say so.

**PE17. The map is never guessed** (finding 2, high). A missing `role_permission` table read as the code's defaults, which would give back
a permission someone took away on the screen. Now any failure of the read (a missing table included) puts "nothing allowed" in force
(`Permissions::denyAll`) and fails the request: a page answers 503, a service's action fails. The application has no pre-migration mode (the
jobs refuse a schema that is behind; a page served in the seconds of a deploy before `--migrate` gets 503 instead of guessed rights).
The one explicit way to run today's code without the table is `RoleMap::runWithoutTable(true)`, which the migration tests call for
their scratch schemas of before 0034 (`Migration0013Test`); it is never inferred from an error. The nightly configuration check
compares no `permission` rows on a schema that has no such table (K2 still finds the baselines of a table gone missing).

**PE18. A failed history batch holds the later ones back** (finding 3, medium). The import retries a failed export under the same batch
id, so passing a failed batch over skipped its days for good. The job now stops at a batch that is still loading or failed, and its run
note says which batch it waits for ("history waits for batch N (failed)"). The cost: a failed batch that is never retried holds the
history back until it is retried (`bin/refresh_reports.php --status` shows it); the stock and sales parts of the job are not held.
<!-- ==== end Pack E ==== -->

## Pack I: the opening stock and opening cost migrated FROM ERPNext (slot `packi`, 14 Oct 2026)

The owner's decision of 14 Oct 2026: CW's opening stock is migrated FROM ERPNext, not taken from the stores' own figures (it replaces the
opening of D40a, `bin/import_opening_estimate.php`, as the source of the figure). This pack is the import, for the quantity and the opening
average cost (the opening-cost half of IM8 / E16: "opening average cost from ERPNext's Stock Balance rates; blank and £1 placeholder costs
re-costed"). Code: `bin/import_erp_opening.php`, `src/Ops/{ErpOpening,ErpOpeningFiles,ErpOpeningRules,ErpItemResolver}.php` (new),
`migrations/0039_erp_opening_import.sql` (numbered 0039: 0030-0038 are other packs'), marked blocks in `src/Movements.php`
(`recordOpening`), `src/Output/CsvReader.php` (`records`), `src/Output/XlsxReader.php` (`$maxRowIndex`), `src/Settings.php` (RULES),
`src/Ui/Words.php` (SETTING, SETTING_TOPIC, SETTING_HELP), `src/Schema/Grants.php` (UPDATE_COLUMNS); tests
`tests/Integration/Stock/ErpOpeningTest.php`, `tests/Unit/ErpOpeningFilesTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Migration0039Test.php`; the staff
steps in `docs/ops.md` "The opening stock from ERPNext". Every rule below that the owner may want otherwise is an `erp_opening.*` setting
(provisional, a build decision put to the owner).

**PI1. Where and how it is booked.** One `adjustment` per CW item at the warehouse `erp_opening.cw_warehouse` (baseline MAIN), through the
one stock writer (Movements → Stock; Stock.php's locks and buckets untouched), actor `system:opening_estimate` (the actor of every opening,
D40a: so the stores' estimate tool sees an ERPNext-opened item as an `earlier_opening` and never books it again, and the T0 rebase sees it as
`other_opening`), cost source `estimate` (PI7), Idempotency-Key `<doc_ref>:<sku_id>`, the as-of moment, the file hash, the source, the
below-zero rule, whether the sales on their way were taken off and who approved in the note. The doc_ref is given (`--doc-ref`,
compared byte for byte), e.g. `erp-opening:vapeandgo:2026-10-31`. An opening is not a count: `counted_at` is never touched.

**PI2. Which ERPNext rows are read: the main warehouse only, never VPG 2.** `erp_opening.warehouses` (baseline `Stores - VPG`, one name per
line) and, when the file has a Company column, `erp_opening.companies` (baseline `VAPE AND GO`; empty: the company is not checked).
`erp_opening.blocked_names` (baseline `VPG 2`): a company or warehouse whose name CONTAINS one of them, spaces and case ignored, is never
read, whatever the two lists say (`VPG 2 Main warehouse - VPG2` and `Stores - VPG2` both stop); a list that names one is refused as a
setting mistake (409 `bad_setting`), and a file exported for such a company (its own `company` filter line) is refused whole
(`wrong_company`). Rows left out are counted per reason (`blocked`, `other_company`, `other_warehouse`) with their units and names. Names are
compared as ERPNext compares them (case and runs of spaces ignored).

**PI3. An ERPNext item reaches a CW item by one route or not at all (`ErpItemResolver`).** First CW's own ERPNext link (`sku_erp_item`, ×
its `units_per_item`; plan §5 keeps it as the override); else the item list's Product ID (the custom Item field that holds the Vape and Go
variant number, docs/ops.md "ERPNext open POs") names a listing of the store `erp_opening.listing_store` (baseline `vapeandgo`), which must
be `mapped`: its item × the listing's `units_per_item` (plan §9: ERPNext resolves through Vape and Go's link). Otherwise the line is
UNRESOLVED, counted and listed with its reason, never guessed: `no_item_code`, `bad_qty`, `fractional_qty`, `no_item_list`, `no_product_id`,
`ambiguous_product_id` (the item list gives two), `no_listing_store`, `unknown_listing`, `unlinked_listing`, `quarantined_listing`,
`merged_item`. Two ERPNext items of one CW item (the `P47074` / `47074` naming split, a single and a pack) are summed and counted
(`fed_by_several_erp_items`). **Assumption, to be confirmed on the first real export:** one unit of an ERPNext item's stock UOM is one unit
of the variant its Product ID names (the summary lists the stock UOMs seen).

**PI4. Below zero (the plan's D36; about 707 ERPNext items).** Per CW item, after the sales on their way are taken off: `erp_opening.below_zero`
`zero` (baseline: open at nothing, as D40b's max(S, 0) and D36 A) or `carry` (book the minus, as D36 B; CW allows an uncounted item below
zero, D1, SO3). The summary gives the lines below zero (rows, units), the items below zero (items, units), what the rule did (units not
carried, or carried) and the items one by one.

**PI5. The opening cost: ERPNext's Valuation Rate, never a placeholder.** A central unit's cost = the line's rate ÷ u, averaged over the
item's lines weighted by their central units: the lines on the side of the item's figure (above zero for a plus), else any line with a real
rate. A blank rate, one that is not a number or below zero, and one of `erp_opening.placeholder_costs` (baseline `0,1`: £0 and the £1
placeholder Vape and Go's cost field holds, I1) are never used: the summary counts those lines, an item with no other rate opens WITHOUT a
cost and is listed for re-costing (items, units, its lines), and an item costed from its other lines only is counted (`mixed`). Rates keep 6
decimals (half up). The summary gives the opening's value at these costs and, for comparison, ERPNext's own Balance Value of the resolved
lines. A carried minus carries its cost too (value below zero).

**PI6. The sales still on their way to ERPNext.** Website sales reach ERPNext through a queue (pending and failed rows), so ERPNext's figure
still holds units a store has sold. An optional file lists them (Variant ID or Product ID, or Item Code; Qty, or one row a unit); each row
resolves like PI3 (a variant directly through the store's link) and its central units are taken off the item; rows that do not resolve are
listed, not taken off. Without the file the summary says in capitals that the correction is still OPEN. `erp_opening.require_pending_sales`
(baseline on): `--apply` refuses to book without it; an empty file (its header only) says there are none. Writing that file from the
website's queue is the integrator's (the query is not part of this pack).

**PI7. `Movements::recordOpening`.** record() for a system job, `adjustment` only, whose line costs are stored with cost source `estimate` (I1
reserved it for the opening cost load; until now nothing wrote it). The canonical request carries `cost_source`, so a key used by record()
is never replayed by it nor the other way round (422), and every request record() hashes is unchanged (I6, MovementHashCompatTest). Staff
and sites never reach it (LogicException).

**PI8. The files are what staff download; CW never connects to ERPNext.** Never its stock feed (`get_product_stock_sync` marks pending
purchase invoices Synced: 200 units on 5 Oct). The stock file is the Stock Balance report (CSV or Excel), read by its column names (Item,
Warehouse, Balance Qty, Valuation Rate required; Company, Balance Value, Stock UOM, Item Name used when present); a Report-view export of the
Bin list (Item Code, Warehouse, Actual Quantity, Valuation Rate, Stock Value) reads the same way. An export made with "Include filters"
starts with its filter lines: kept, and the `company` and `to_date` ones are checked (PI2, PI9). The report's Total line is checked against
the sum of the lines (`total_mismatch`: edited, filtered in the grid or cut short) and left out; a line after it, the same item and
warehouse twice, or no line at all refuse the file. Quantities are whole numbers (`12.0` is 12; a fraction is the line's `fractional_qty`).

**PI9. What CW already knows about an item wins.** Skipped and listed (with the figure ERPNext gives): `counted` (a count replaced any
opening), `earlier_opening` (any opening row under another doc_ref, or at another warehouse), `moved_before_as_of` (an on-hand row of
anyone else before `--as-of`: ERPNext's figure already holds it). On-hand rows after `--as-of` are fine: the opening sits under them. When
the file carries its To Date, `--as-of` must fall on that UK day (`as_of_mismatch`). An item already booked under this doc_ref with the same
figure AND cost is left alone; another figure or cost under the same doc_ref refuses the whole run before anything is booked
(`opening_conflict`): a second `--apply` of the same files books nothing, a different file needs a deliberate new doc_ref.

**PI10. Two additions to shared readers.** `CsvReader::records()` gives every record with no header rule (the filter lines come first);
`XlsxReader::read()` takes an optional `$maxRowIndex` (an ERPNext stock export runs past row 10,000). Neither changes what an existing caller
reads.

**PI11. `--replaces=<doc_ref>`: replacing the stores' estimate.** Where the stores' estimate of D40a was already booked (cw_staging holds
`opening:vapeandgo:2026-10-01T00:00+01:00`), the ERPNext figure can replace exactly that one opening: the item's row then holds two lines,
the earlier opening taken back (line 1, no cost) and the ERPNext figure with its cost (line 0), so the item's openings add up to the ERPNext
figure and the value is the ERPNext figure × its cost. An item of the replaced opening that the ERPNext file does not lead to is skipped
(`not_in_erp_file`), never written down to nothing. Without `--replaces` such items are `earlier_opening`.

**PI12. The dry run writes nothing.** The default; it reads, plans and prints the summary (and `--report=<csv>`, one row per stock line
and what became of it, when asked). `--apply` (with `--sha256` of the archived stock file and `--approved-by`) books and records the run in
`erp_opening_run` (0039: what the run was on, frozen; its status, summary and end the only columns the app login may change; never
removed). The command line is read strictly (a misspelt option ends it before anything is read) and one run at a time (the job lock).

**PI13. The value engine has no route yet: what exactly is missing.** IM8 is not built: nothing writes `stock_value_ledger` (I5: IM8's
`Valuation.php` is to be its only writer; this pack does not write it). What is in place: the opening cost on the ledger row (`unit_cost`,
`cost_source = 'estimate'`), numbered in the item's value sequence (`stock_value_seq`, I3) like every on-hand row, and read today by the
screens' "average cost so far" (`CostHints::average`, SO6). Missing, for IM8: (1) the consumer that walks each item's value sequence; (2)
its rule that an on-hand row of actor `system:opening_estimate` with cost source `estimate` is the item's `opening` entry (qty, unit cost,
value, `effective_at` the as-of moment written in the note, pool `default`); (3) the value of an item opened without a cost (PI5: it waits
for a cost typed by a person or the first delivery at a price); (4) the value of a carried minus (plan §15.3 "true-up at the next
receipt"); (5) the opening valuation saved on the switch day for the accountant (plan part 2). None of these needs a change here.

**PI14. A store's T0 after an ERPNext opening: the units-only rebase (built in the review round of 14 Oct 2026).** ERPNext's figure, once
the sales on their way are taken off, is free stock: every sale is out of it, as the store's own figure was in D40a. At the store's T0,

the figure to the store's own (against the owner's decision), or skip every ERPNext-opened item as `other_opening`. So
`bin/import_opening_estimate.php --rebase --units-only --estimate-doc-ref=<the ERPNext opening's doc_ref>` (`OpeningRebase::plan(...,
unitsOnly: true)`): target = the item's rows under that doc_ref + the units term of D40b (the channel's committed `origin = opening` units ×
u); delta = the units term. No file is read (no `--csv`, no `--sha256`; giving one is a usage error), the T0 checks and `--as-of` for a real
run stay. The skips that judge the store's figure (`no_t0_figure`, `quarantined_listing`, `no_mapped_listing`) do not apply; every other one
does (`counted`, `other_opening`, `moved`, `units_elsewhere`, `merged_item`; a conflict under the same doc_ref refuses). An item ERPNext opened
at zero (below zero) gets its open units, as max(S, 0) + units in D40b. The summary says how many items carry the named opening. After it,
available = the ERPNext figure (× u) and, once the opening units have shipped, on-hand = the ERPNext figure. Still to confirm: that the
website's sales invoice reaches ERPNext at payment (read in the code 14 Oct: payment completed sets `ord_is_syncable`, PI20), so ERPNext's
figure is free stock and not on-hand.

**PI15. Not built.** The small Stock screen of the last import's summary (optional in the brief): left out to keep this pack off the shared
screen files that six packs change at once; `ErpOpening::lastRun()` gives what it would show.

**PI16. Tests.** `ErpOpeningTest`: only the main warehouse is read and VPG 2 never is (also when a list names it, and a file exported for
it); unresolved lines listed by reason with nothing guessed (and without the item list); below zero by both rules; blank, £0 and £1 costs
flagged and passed over, the weighted average over a single and a 10-pack; the same file again books nothing, other figures or another cost
under the same doc_ref are refused, the same file under another doc_ref books nothing; the sales on their way taken off (a 10-pack variant ×
10), listed when they do not resolve, and reported open when not given; the dry run through the command line leaves every table's row
count as it was, `--apply` refuses without the hash or the pending-sales file, books once and records its run, and the same command again
books nothing; `--replaces` of a D40a estimate; counted and moved items skipped; an XLSX export, an edited Total line, a doubled line, no
rate column, the To Date check; `recordOpening`'s cost source and refusals. `ErpOpeningFilesTest` (unit): numbers, rates, the filter lines,
the Bin export, the item list, the pending-sales file, the rules, the words of the eight settings. `Migration0039Test`: the settings, their
versions and rules, the run table and its grants.

**PI17. One opening lock, and a re-check inside each booking (review of 14 Oct 2026, finding 1).** The estimate tool and the ERPNext
import had their own job locks, so both could plan the same item and both book it (an estimate of 8 and ERPNext's 11 made 19). Now (1)

**PI18. ERPNext item codes keep their inner spaces (finding 2).** Item codes were compared with the name key that also folds runs of spaces,
so the CW links `ABC DEF` and `ABC  DEF` overwrote each other and either could win. Now `ErpOpeningRules::itemKey()` ignores letter case and
the spaces at the ends only (ERPNext's own rule for names); the warehouse and company names keep the folding key. Two CW links that still

**PI19. A re-run that leaves out a booked item is refused (finding 3).** The history read now loads every item already booked under the
doc_ref, not only the planned ones, so a file under the same doc_ref without an item booked earlier (left out of the file or of the item

**PI20. The sales not yet in ERPNext: `bin/erp_pending_sales.php` (`SitePendingSales`).** Read in App/App_proto on 14 Oct 2026: payment
completed sets `orders_master.ord_is_syncable = 1`; `salesorder.php` makes one `data_sync` row per order (`ds_type = 'sales_invoice'`,
PENDING; `items[]` = one `{item_code: ordi_prodt_id, qty: 1}` per `orders_items` row, none left out) and sets

PENDING or FAILED (any retry count: a stuck one is surely not in ERPNext), or SUCCESS within `--success-grace-minutes` (10, as the store's own
reconciler), and is its order's newest such row (`source_ord_id`: a re-queued order counts once); plus the `orders_items` of orders paid but
not queued yet. Cancel and refund rows still on their way put units BACK in ERPNext: counted and printed as "NOT NETTED", never guessed
into the figure. Read only: SELECT statements only (checked before each runs), `SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY` and `START TRANSACTION
READ ONLY`, `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` on the session and in every statement (`--max-ms`, 30,000 by default, 100 to 600,000), rolled back at the end;
the connection comes from an env file (`--site-env`, KEY=VALUE, parsed never sourced, refused unless chmod 600, nothing of it printed),
TLS required as every CW connection. Output: the pending-sales file `variant_id,qty` (`--out`, made 0600) and a summary on stderr. Tested
only on made-up tables in a scratch schema; never run against a live database by the build.

**PI21. Tests of the review round.** `ErpOpeningTest`: an opening booked by the other tool, or a count, between a run's plan and its apply
stops the item (both directions); the tools share one lock (both refused while it is held, the dry run not); item codes with inner spaces
and an ambiguous link; a re-run that leaves out a booked item, through the file and through the item list. `ErpOpeningT0Test`: the
units-only rebase with the opening_orders flow (ERPNext opening, open paid units, a ship before the rebase, available = the ERPNext figure,
on-hand = it once shipped, a 10-pack, an item opened at zero, a re-run, the refusals), the skips, and the command line without a file.
`SitePendingSalesTest`: the figures on made-up tables, the read-only session (a write refused, 1792), the statements, the grace, the script,
its env-file rules and the file the opening import reads. The three findings' tests were run first on the unfixed tree and failed.

## Purchasing › Reorder: the full reorder engine and the buying data around it, pack G (slot `packg`, 14 Oct 2026)

Pack G replaces ERPNext's E4 (the PO "Fetch Item" suggestion and "Download Items"), E10 (pack sizes), E11 (the monthly average-sales
and safety-stock job, about 17,600 variants), E12 ("Items Below Safety Stock", the Item Management page), E22 (enable / disable) and
E23 (brand as a filter) (`/root/cw_work/golive/plan_final.md` part 3b; `docs/inventory-modules-plan.md` IM9, IM4, IM5). The basic
engine of I60-I89 stays as it was built; this pack adds what the "full engine" needed. Numbered PG1-PG16. Code: `migrations/0037_reorder_engine.sql`;
`src/Reorder/{SalesFold,ReorderRefresh,ReorderLines,ReorderJobs,LowStockLevels}.php` (new); changed `src/Reorder/{DemandBuilder,DemandMath,
ReorderMath,ReorderList,ReorderSettings,DraftPos}.php`, `src/SiteWriter/SiteView.php` and `src/Availability.php` (one field passed),
`src/Ui/{Controller/ReorderController,Controller/SellingModeController,ReorderWhy,Kernel,Sections,Words}.php`, `src/Ui/Controller/ReorderEngineController.php`
(new), views `reorder_suppliers`, `reorder_low_stock` (new), `reorder`, `reorder_item`, `item`; `src/Settings.php`, `src/Schema/Grants.php`;
`bin/reorder_refresh.php` and its cron line; tests below (PG14).

**PG1. CW's own record of each store's sales (`reorder_sales_day`, `SalesFold`).** Once a store is connected, its orders reach CW through
the connector, and the stock ledger holds every sale. The fold reads the ledger by UK day and writes one row per (store, variant, UK day)
in the variant's own units, so the demand build and every page read a small table, never the ledger. What counts: the ledger rows on the
`allocated` bucket of a sale (`commit`, +u), a cancellation (`cancel`, -u) and an uncancellation (`uncancel`, +u), joined through the sold
unit (`reservation_unit`, primary key) to its order and its variant (both by primary key), divided by the units per sale the unit was sold
with. Left out: an opening order (placed before the store connected: the imported history has it), and a sale of a variant that was not
linked (it moved no stock, so it has no ledger row; the import also counts it as unlinked). The day is the UK date of the ledger row: a
cancellation lands on the day it happened (a day may go below 0; it reads as nothing sold). Each UK day is read in ledger-id ranges (its
first id from `ix_stock_ledger_created`, then the primary key in steps of 20,000) and written in ONE short transaction: the day's rows set
to 0, then the new figures upserted. Nothing is ever deleted. The days due: every UK day from the first (the UK date of the earliest
store connect moment `channel_opening.t0_at`, at most a year back) to yesterday that was never folded, and each of the last
`reorder.fold_refold_days` days once more on a later UK day (a late write lands); at most `reorder.fold_days_per_run` days a run, oldest
first. `reorder_fold_day` says what was folded, when, how often and how much. *Why by day and not by a ledger-id watermark:* ids are not
promised in commit order, so a watermark can skip a row written by a slower transaction; a day folded again cannot.

**PG2. Which sales the demand uses (`DemandBuilder::channels()`).** For a store named in the setting `reorder.own_sales_stores`
(channel codes; **empty by default: the imported history only, as before**) that has connected, its days from the first whole UK day
after its connect moment come from CW's own record, up to the newest day folded; its earlier days come from the imported history. A day
inside the store's span that neither source has (the import ended before the record began) is "no data" (`DemandMath::listing`'s new
`$gap`), never a day without sales. All the rest of I62 holds (windows, exclusions, spike cap, blend). *Build decision, provisional:* the
setting is empty until the owner names a store; the go-live list gets one step: name Vape and Go on its switch day, and Electrofag and
Vape Big when their connectors go live. Known limits on the record's days, for the owner: promotions are not detected there (the
connector's sale message carries no price yet, D41/F1-lite), and sold-out days are not left out there (CW holds no daily site snapshot);
anomaly windows apply as before.

**PG3. The list is worked out ahead of the page (`reorder_line`, `reorder_line_detail`, `ReorderLines`).** E11's job, ahead of time: every
item of the list (demand, a smallest stock, or a low-stock figure) has its line stored. `reorder_line` holds the few columns the list
filters and sorts by (listed, to buy, urgent, below the safety stock, never suggested, days left, value, brand, main supplier, safety
stock, stock, low-stock figure) with an index in list order (`ix_reorder_line_need`, `ix_reorder_line_all`, DESC parts); `reorder_line_detail`
the whole line as JSON. A page reads the 200 ids of its page from the compact rows, then those 200 lines by primary key: never the whole
list, never the ledger, never every PO line. The download reads the ids in list order, then the lines a thousand at a time. The
website-stock view (`stock=site`, before go-live only) is still worked out on the page as before.

**PG4. The refresh and the schedule (`ReorderRefresh`, `ReorderJobs`, `bin/reorder_refresh.php`).** The refresh works the lines out in
chunks of `reorder.refresh_chunk_items` (500) items in id order, each chunk read and then written in one short transaction, and writes
only lines whose sha1 changed. An item that left the list is unlisted (`listed = 0`), never deleted. Each row keeps when its figures were
read (`read_at`): a write of figures read earlier never overwrites later ones (a long run that read a chunk before a draft was made cannot
undo the draft's line). One full run at a time (`GET_LOCK('cw_reorder_lines:<schema>', 0)`: 409 `refresh_running`). The schedule: one
cron line every 5 minutes runs what is due: the fold when a UK day waits; the demand once a UK day from the hour `reorder.demand_hour`
(4, UK time), again after a failure only after `reorder.refresh_minutes`; the list after the demand and every `reorder.refresh_minutes`
(15). Each step's last run (start, end, last good end, time, result, error) is kept in `reorder_job`; the list says "Figures worked out on
...", and says so when the last run went wrong. At once, without waiting: after "create draft orders" (its items, in its transaction),
after an item's settings, after a brand's or a supplier's spare days (their items, up to `reorder.refresh_inline_max_items`, 2,000; more
wait for the schedule), after a low-stock click, after "Work out sales again", and with the new button "Work out the list again now"
(reorder.manage; above the same number it works out the products of the page shown, the rest at the next run).
`bin/reorder_demand.php` still rebuilds the demand alone.

**PG5. The safety stock and "below the safety stock" (`ReorderMath`).** Safety stock = ⌈sales a day × spare days⌉, at least the item's

(ERPNext's "Items Below Safety Stock" reads the stock now). An item never suggested is never below. The filter "Below safety stock only"
shows those items whatever there is to buy (it overrides "Products to buy" / "Every product"), on the list, in its download and on
Low-stock warnings. Each line says its safety stock, and the "Why" says how it is made.

The slot's test schema on the staging database server (MySQL 8.4.8, **32 MB buffer pool**) filled like the live catalogue: 17,600

**PG17. The independent review of 14 Oct 2026 (Codex, `runs/packg_codex_review.txt`): three findings, each shown by a test that failed
first (`runs/packg_fix_red.log`), then fixed.**
- *Finding 1 (an unchanged read was not recorded):* a refresh that found a line unchanged wrote nothing, so a slower refresh that had read
  older figures could still put them over it. Now each chunk locks its items' stored rows in item order and decides every line against
  them: a row read later wins; an unchanged line moves its `read_at` on (its `changed_at` stays); the rest is written, both tables
  together. Test `ReorderEngineTest::testALineReadEarlierNeverOverwritesOneFoundUnchangedLater`. Cost: one UPDATE of the read time per
  chunk of unchanged lines.
- *Finding 2 (the full run's clean-up hid an item added while it ran):* the clean-up now unlists only lines read before the run read the
  list's ids (`$baseAt`), and only items still off the list when it unlists them. Test
  `ReorderEngineTest::testAnItemAddedDuringAFullRefreshStaysListed` (the item is added and refreshed between two chunks).
- *Finding 3 (the demand built on a part-folded record, then not again that day):* while the fold has days left after
  `reorder.fold_days_per_run`, or another run is folding, the demand step says "waiting for the fold"; the run that finishes the fold
  builds it, the same day. Test `ReorderJobsTest::testTheDemandWaitsUntilTheFoldHasCaughtUp`.
- Also: the low-stock click now works its items' stored lines out before it writes the feed rows, so the feed clock stays the last lock
  and is held for the shortest time.

  `role_permission` takes the defaults).

## Pack H: hand-overs, the company's VAT code and currency, the duty register (slot `packh`, 14 Oct 2026)

<!-- ---- Pack H (0038): PH1-PH20. ---- -->
The ERPNext functions E26 and E47 (the staff sales invoices that move stock to Electrofag, Vape Big, the shop units and trade customers,
and the selling price list behind their rates; module IM11), E34 (the company, its VAT code and currency on CW's orders and invoices) and
E45 (the vaping duty register built from the receipts; module IM13), from `/root/cw_work/golive/plan_final.md` part 3b. Built from main
`8c54425` in `/root/cw-packh` (branch `pack-h`), migration `0038_handovers_company_duty.sql`. Code: `src/Handovers/{Handovers,
HandoverHandler,HandoverMath,Counterparties,CounterpartyAccounts,HandoverPdf,HandoverInvariants}.php`, `src/Duty/DutyRegister.php`,
`src/Ui/Controller/{Handovers,Duty}Controller.php`, views `handovers`, `handover`, `handover_fields`, `handover_customers`,
`handover_customer`, `handover_customer_fields`, `handover_balances`, `duty_register` (new); changed: `src/Company/{CompanyDetails,
CompanyInvariants}.php`, `src/Ui/Controller/{Company,Reviews}Controller.php`, views `company`, `company_form`, `src/Documents/
DocumentHandlers.php`, `src/Invariants.php`, and one marked block each in `Words`, `Settings`, `Sections`, `Permissions`, `Grants`, `Kernel`.
Every number below is a setting or a rule on a screen unless it says otherwise; every setting is a build decision put to the owner.

**PH1. A hand-over is a TRD document (0008's "Trade / inter-site issue", never live until now).** Draft -> make it final (a reviewer's OK
first only when a rule on the Approval Rules page asks) -> cancelled by a new record that puts everything back; a draft is stopped, never
deleted (the document base, I17-I21, SO1). Its header extension `handover` names the customer and the VAT code chosen; its lines are an
item, units above zero and the price of a unit before VAT (`document_line.unit_cost`, as the release keeps its agreed price, SO1). Posting
(`HandoverHandler`) writes the module rows first (the invoice's sums and snapshots, the remembered prices, what the customer owes) and
books the stock last, ONE `Movements::bookForDocument` of `trade_sale` (0006, I8: on hand down, no cost: issued at the average) from the
hand-over's warehouse (ours, switched on; MAIN by default). Stock.php is not touched. A protected item (strict, stopped) never goes below
zero (the stock out's rule, SO3; a hand-over carries no reason that could allow it), checked in validate() and again after booking on the
balances the posting holds. The same form sent twice books once: the second posting finds no draft (409 `not_draft`); the create form is
FormOnce (one draft however often it is sent). A cancellation that puts more units back than the "stock put back" limit waits for an OK
(the document base's I32, unchanged).

**PH2. The customers (`counterparty`).** One list for the three kinds the plan names: a sister shop (another company: Electrofag, Vape Big
-- Vape Big without a connector is "treated as a trade customer", decision 5, which this is), one of our shop units (Unit 6, Unit 7,
Ashton: decision 10, "shop units handled as issues"), a trade customer. Name (printed on the invoice, unique whatever its case),
address (8 lines of 100), company and VAT numbers (the company details' rules), an optional VAT code of their own, e-mail, phone, note.
Switched off, never deleted; the form carries the version (409 `customer_changed`); every change audited with what changed. No rows are
seeded: the plan names the customers but not their legal names or addresses, and CW invents none.

**PH3. The company details gain the VAT code of our invoices and the currency (E34).** Two more fields on every `company_profile`
version (0038, ALTER of a small table): `vat_code` (a code of `vat_code`; NULL = not said yet, which every existing version keeps --
nobody confirmed a code, so none is put into a confirmed version) and `currency` (pounds only, owner answer Q13; a CHECK, as
`purchase_order.currency`). They are fields like the others: changing one makes the details unconfirmed again, so every PO PDF says "do
not send" and every hand-over invoice waits until a reviewer confirms them (I94 unchanged). The VAT code is not needed to CONFIRM the
details (a company that is not VAT registered has none; and the PO's lines carry their own codes): it is needed to print a hand-over
invoice of a VAT registered company (PH8). C2 compares the two new fields too. The PO's snapshot now carries them; its PDF is unchanged.

**PH4. Which VAT code a hand-over is invoiced with.** The one chosen on the hand-over, else the customer's, else our company's. None when
our company said it is not VAT registered (no VAT is charged). When none is known and the company is, or may be, VAT registered, making
it final is refused (422 `vat_code_required`): the balance owed needs the total. A code no longer in use is refused (422 `vat_code_off`).
One code per hand-over (ERPNext's sales invoice had one taxes template); per-line codes are not built.

**PH5. The sums.** Each line: units x price to the penny, half up (`CostHints::amount`, the release's rule). Net: their sum. VAT: net x
rate / 100 to the penny, half up, ONCE on the invoice (not per line). Gross = net + VAT: what the customer owes. A cancellation's sums are
the original's negated (never computed again). Pounds only. Whether invoice-level rounding suits the accountant is put to them.

**PH6. Prices remembered (E47; setting `handovers.price_fallback`, `none`).** `counterparty_price` holds the price a customer last paid for
an item: written when a hand-over is made final (each item's last line), unless a price from a later day is there already (the hand-over's
date decides, so a back-dated hand-over does not overwrite a newer price). A cancelled hand-over leaves the price (a price agreed is still
the price). A new line takes the customer's remembered price; when there is none, `none` leaves it empty for the person (making it final
refuses a line without a price, 422 `price_required`), `cost` fills the last supplier price, else the average cost so far (CostHints, the
release's default). No FK to `sku` (written inside the posting before the stock locks, as `incident`, I127); H5 checks the ids.

**PH7. The past trade-invoice prices from a file (setting `handovers.price_import_max_rows`, 5,000).** Customers > "Load the prices of old
trade invoices": a CSV with the columns customer, item, price and, if there, date and invoice (ERPNext's export spellings accepted: Item
Code, Rate, Posting Date, Sales Invoice). The customer by its exact name (case does not matter; the import never creates one: the 12
are typed with their addresses). The item by its CW number, a usable barcode of ONE unit, an ERPNext item code's override
(`sku_erp_item`, one unit), else the one item every mapped website variant with that code points at (one unit each). The owner's rule:
a row that cannot be read for sure (unknown customer or item, a case barcode or a pack, two items, a bad price or date) is skipped and
listed with its reason; the rest are loaded. For one customer and item the newest row wins; a price remembered from a later day is kept.
Audit `counterparty.price_import` with the file's sha256 and the counts.

**PH8. The invoice PDF waits for confirmed company details (setting `handovers.pdf_needs_confirmed_company`, true).** The task's "the PDF is
refused until the company details are confirmed", and the plan's gate (step 0.2b) for E34: while on, the invoice PDF is refused (409
`company_not_confirmed`, in words on the hand-over's page, which says so beside the link before anyone presses it) when the details it
prints were not confirmed: a draft prints the details in use; a final hand-over the snapshot its posting took (`company_snapshot`,
`company_version`, `company_confirmed`). A hand-over made final before the confirmation therefore never prints under the rule: it is
copied into a new draft ("Make it again": the same customer, warehouse, VAT code, lines and prices) and cancelled -- the purchase order's
"cancel and copy" (I96), so a final invoice never changes its seller's details. Also refused while on: a VAT registered company with no VAT
code that applies (409 `vat_code_missing`). Off: it prints, with "COMPANY DETAILS NOT CONFIRMED -- DO NOT SEND", as a purchase order does.
Making a hand-over final never waits for the company details: stock flow is not stopped by paperwork.

**PH9. What the invoice says, and what it does not.** "Invoice TRD-000123": from (our company as printed, "[to be confirmed]" for an
empty field), to (the customer as printed), its number and date, the customer's reference, the currency (pounds), each line (CW number,
item, units, price, VAT code, amount), the units, the total before VAT, the VAT at its rate and the total; a draft says "DRAFT -- NOT AN
INVOICE", a cancelled one "CANCELLED -- see TRD-x". CW invents no legal wording (the owner's rule): it does not call it a "VAT invoice",
prints no tax point and no payment terms of its own; `handovers.invoice_terms` (empty) holds the words the owner or the accountant
types. TO BE CONFIRMED with the accountant (decision 13, open): whether this invoice serves as the VAT invoice; whether a cancellation
needs a credit note (a cancellation record prints nothing of its own: 409 `no_invoice`); the rounding of PH5. The delivery-note PDF IM11
also names is not built (the invoice lists the items and units).

**PH10. What each customer owes (the VPG 2 release's pattern, SO8, the other way round).** `counterparty_entry` (append-only): + a
hand-over's gross, - its cancellation's, - a payment received, + a payment's reversal; the balance is their sum, per customer.
Hand-overs > Balances shows each customer's balance (a credit when negative), what was handed over this UK month, the last payment and
every entry with links. The receivables stay with the accountant (IM11: "in ERPNext they were never settled: Alectrofag GBP 169k, Vape Big
GBP 125k"): the page says this is CW's own record of hand-overs and the payments people tell it about. Nothing is brought across from
ERPNext's unsettled balances.

**PH11. Payments received and their locks.** "Record a payment received" (amount, the day it arrived, up to today; the bank reference; a
note) and "Reverse this payment" (a reason; once) by `handovers.pay`. A payment locks the customer's row FOR UPDATE; a hand-over's posting
reads it FOR SHARE (after the document and the number series, before the stock), so a payment's "more than owed" sees a hand-over made
final at the same moment. No cycle: no payment path touches a document or the stock.

**PH12. A payment more than owed (setting `handovers.allow_overpayment`, false).** Refused (409 `more_than_owed`, "nothing_owed" when
nothing is), so a zero too many is caught (SO8's rule). On: recorded, and the customer has a credit.

**PH13. Who and where (provisional, owner to confirm).** `doc.TRD.post` (0007: the purchasing desk and manager, who key trade sales
today) makes, finishes, cancels and copies hand-overs; `handovers.customers` (the same two jobs) keeps the customer list and loads old
prices; `handovers.pay` (the same two jobs) records payments received; `duty.view` (goods in, the purchasing desk and manager, the stock
controller, the reviewer, the accountant, the auditor, the stock manager) reads the duty register. Everyone with `documents.view` reads
hand-overs, customers and balances. Never admin (I12): every service re-checks the roles inside its transaction. Screens: Stock >
Hand-overs (a new tab after Stock Out, the v4 look) with the segments Hand-overs, Customers, Balances; Purchasing > Goods In > Duty
register (a segment after Issues). A hand-over's check, when a rule asks one, is decided on its own page (Approvals > Waiting for me links
there, and the decision comes back). Home no longer names trade sales as "coming later". Not built: a badge on the tab (the check is off).

**PH14. The nightly checks H1-H5 (`HandoverInvariants`, in `Invariants::check`).** H1 every TRD has its header; a final hand-over its sums
and exactly one `handover` entry of its gross on its customer; a posted cancellation the negated header and exactly one
`handover_reversal` entry; a draft or a stopped one neither. H2 every entry names a final hand-over or a posted cancellation of one, of
the right kind. H3 net = the lines' units x price to the penny, VAT = net x rate to the penny, gross = net + VAT. H4 a final hand-over
books only `trade_sale` on hand at its warehouse, per item the negation of its lines. H5 a payment reversal mirrors a payment of its
customer; a remembered price names an item, and one from a hand-over a final one of the same customer.

**PH15. The duty register is built from the receipts, at read time (IM13; setting `duty.register_lines`, `stamp`).** No table: each line of
the register IS a line of a final goods receipt (`goods_receipt` + `grn_line` + `document_line`, the posted fields of I127-I135), so the
register can never disagree with the receipts. Listed: the lines that needed the duty-stamp check (`stamp_required`, I134; `all`: every

barcode, the units on the paperwork and where they went (in, held back in UNSTAMPED, refused), the liquid per unit and the expected duty
(for information, I135), the bench's stamp check (on the outer pack and sealing it, its type, a scanned code, who checked), the unstamped
units and what happened to them, the supplier's declaration that unstamped stock was made or brought in before 1 Oct 2026 (the bench's
`pre_october_evidence`) and whether a file of it is kept with the delivery, the incidents. The stamp state: stamped, unstamped (held back
or refused), declared made before 1 Oct 2026, not checked, no stamp needed. A reversed receipt stays listed, marked "cancelled" (a filter
leaves it out). Filters: the arrival days, the supplier, the stamp state, booked in or cancelled, words. The columns follow the owner's
spreadsheet register (`/root/cw_work/duty/Vaping_Duty_Goods-In_Register_v2.xlsx`, "Goods-in register" tab); its "Duty on invoice" and
"Supplier checked" columns have no source in CW yet (IM7, IM4).

**PH16. The unstamped stock and where it is (settings `duty.unstamped_warehouses`, `UNSTAMPED`; `duty.unstamped_zero_from`, 2027-04-01).**
The register's page shows what the named warehouses hold now (item, units, warehouse) and the units taken in unstamped on a supplier's
declaration (per item: the units, the receipts, the last arrival, the warehouse they went into and what it holds of the item now; the

held in those warehouses is a red alarm ("holding them is an offence"), before it a note ("must be empty by"): the date and the words are

and the supplier-checks-due list are not built (left, PH20).

**PH17. Page and download sizes (settings `duty.page_rows`, 200 in 50/100/200/500; `duty.export_max_rows`, 20,000 in 100-100,000).** The
register pages newest first; the download (CSV, formula-safe, UTC times as every CW file) holds at most the setting's lines, read 1,000 at a

packh_explain.php`; 15,000 items, 300 customers, 3,000 hand-overs of 10 lines, 30,000 remembered prices, 5,000 receipts of 10 lines; on

**PH18. Words.** Every word on the new screens is in `Ui\Words` (HANDOVER, HANDOVER_HOW, HANDOVER_NOTICE, HANDOVER_ERROR, HANDOVER_PDF,
CUSTOMER, CUSTOMER_KIND, CUSTOMER_FIELD_ERROR, CUSTOMER_ERROR, CUSTOMER_NOTICE, PRICE_SKIP, BALANCE, BALANCE_KIND, BALANCE_NOTICE,

**PH19. The hand-over's reviewer check starts off.** 0008 seeded TRD with the check `all`; no TRD could be made before this pack (no

rule's history, written only when the rule was not already like that. Both are switched on the Approval Rules page.

**PH20. Provisional and left out.** Provisional: every setting above; the jobs of PH13; one VAT code per hand-over; invoice-level VAT
rounding; a back-dated hand-over keeps the newer remembered price; the overpayment refusal. Left: (1) IM11's "allocation" (moving the site

The monthly inter-company statement (IM11 W2: the hand-overs list filtered by customer, and its CSV, cover it now). (4) IM13's

**PH21. The review of `094b20c` (Codex, 14 Oct 2026; six findings, all MEDIUM, each proved first by a test that failed on that commit).**
(1) An older price import could overwrite a newer price written meanwhile by another session: under READ COMMITTED a locking read
locks nothing where no row is yet. The day is now compared inside the write (`INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` keeps a price from a
later day, as the hand-over's own write does), and the row it leaves says whether the import's price was taken
(`HandoversTest::testAnOlderImportNeverOverwritesANewerPriceWrittenMeanwhile`, the other session's write put between the import's
read and write with `tests/Support/HookedStatement`). (2) A deadlock retry could not read the file again (its rows were a generator,
empty on the second run): the whole file, bounded by `handovers.price_import_max_rows`, is read before the transaction, and the prices
are written in one order (customer, then item) so two imports lock the same rows in the same order (`testAnImportIsRetriedWholeAfterA
Deadlock`). (3) `/ui/documents/{id}/pdf` printed a final hand-over's generic record PDF, prices included, while its company details were
not confirmed: a hand-over now prints there only as its invoice, through the same rule (PH8;
`HandoverScreensTest::testTheRecordsPdfOfAHandoverWaitsForTheCompanyDetailsToo`). (4) The register counted an unstamped delivery's
damaged units as stamped and left its unstamped extras out: stamped and unstamped are now counted as the receipt booked them
(`DutyRegister::stampUnits`, `ReceiptMath::extras`, I167: 100 on paper, 10 damaged, 5 over, 20 unstamped quarantined = 70 stamped, 35
unstamped; `DutyRegisterTest::testTheDamagedAndOverUnitsOfAnUnstampedDeliveryAreUnstamped`); the page and the download show the whole
unstamped figure. (5) An item code longer than the key it is compared with matched its first 140 (ERPNext item code) or 64 (website
variant id) characters: a longer text names no item, and a match must be the same text exactly (the columns' collation ignores case;
the import compares the text itself), and an invoice number over 100 characters skips the row instead of being cut
(`testOnlyAWholeIdentifierNamesAnItem`; PRICE_SKIP `bad_reference`). (6) The total taken in on a declaration added up only the 500
items listed: it is now summed over every line, the page says when a list stops at its limit, and shows both totals
(`testTheDeclarationTotalCountsEveryLineNotOnlyTheListedItems`).
