## Pack J: the owner's day-one purchasing workflow -- invoices made final at a set time, goods on their way, claims (worktree `pack-j`, 15 Oct 2026)

<!-- ---- Pack J (0041): PJ1-PJ16. ---- -->
The owner's words (15 Oct 2026, relayed in the brief): a purchase placed today usually arrives the next day; they want it on the websites
the same day, so customers order overnight and the orders go out when the stock lands. Today in ERPNext they book the purchase invoice and
schedule its submit for a time they choose. Something missing on arrival is a return or claim. When they are 100% sure of the quantity
they skip the count. Built from main `552851a` in `/root/cw-packj` (branch `pack-j`), migration `0041_incoming_stock.sql`. Code:
`src/Arrivals/{Arrivals,ArrivalBooking,InvoiceSchedule,ArrivalInvariants}.php`, `bin/submit_invoices.php` (new);
`src/Ui/Controller/ArrivalsController.php`, views `arrivals`, `invoices_timed` (new); changed: `Stock`, `Movements`, `Availability`,
`Reservations`, `SiteWriter/SiteView`, `Invariants`, `Mapping/DecisionService` (one guard), `Invoices/{SupplierInvoices,
SupplierInvoiceHandler,InvoiceMatch}`, `Receiving/{GoodsReceiptHandler,ReceivingInvariants}`, `Ops/{Alerts,AlertDispatch}`, the
invoice, receipt, supplier and item pages, and one marked block each in `Words`, `Settings`, `Sections`, `Grants`, `Kernel`, `Context`,
the staging cron. Every number below is a setting; the three settings are build decisions put to the owner (provisional).

**PJ1. Goods on their way are a fourth bucket of a balance, `stock_balance.incoming` (a build decision).** available = on_hand +
incoming - allocated - held, everywhere the figure is worked out (`Stock::available`, `Availability`, `Reservations`' read, the site
writer's view and its moves, the staff screens). Stock.php stays the only writer; a change of incoming is a ledger row (bucket
`incoming`) like every bucket; never below zero (a CHECK). Two document-only movement types move it: `incoming` (+, the invoice made
final) and `arrive` (-, the receipt that takes them in), booked through `Movements::bookForDocument` (one lock and one flush per
document). Why a bucket and not a warehouse "on the way": the units stay on the same `(warehouse, item)` row the sites already sell from,
so the lock order is unchanged (no new row locked, nothing after the feed clock), the change feed tells the sites the new figure by
itself (the flush's feed rows), the oversell flags of a falling figure work unchanged (`flagShortfalls`), and the connector's writer
(IM10, `App_proto/src/central_warehouse/lib/writer.php`) writes CW's figure, which now includes incoming: **writer.php needed no change**
(read, not edited). The cost: the ledger's `bucket` ENUM gains a value, and MySQL 8.4 will not do that in place for a column two CHECKs
name (probed: INPLACE and INSTANT refused; re-adding an enforced CHECK copies too), so 0041 copies `stock_ledger` and `stock_balance` once,
ALGORITHM=COPY, LOCK=SHARED: reads go on, stock writes wait. Measured on the test server: 7.6 s per 200,000 ledger rows, 41.5 s per
1,000,000 (about 40 microseconds a row). Apply it before go-live while the ledger is small, or out of trading hours. A merge of an item
with units on their way is refused (409 `incoming_on_item`): they are received first (the receipt books them on the invoice's item).

**PJ2. "Count on arrival": the invoice made final puts its goods on their way.** For each goods line no delivery names, an
`invoice_arrival` row (the item, MAIN, the units, `sellable`, state open); the sellable rows' units go into Incoming, booked LAST in the
invoice's posting (the module rows first, I21). Lines a delivery already names are matched as before (pack C).

**PJ3. Goods In receives against the invoice.** Goods In › Arriving, "Receive": a receipt draft made from what is still on its way (its
order when there is exactly one receivable, the invoice number as its reference, the invoice's files copied, linked in
`goods_receipt_invoice`); one live draft per invoice (pressed again: the same draft). It goes through the usual bench and stamp check and
posting. Its posting (step 5b of `GoodsReceiptHandler::post`) closes every open row of that invoice: received, linked to the receipt's
line of the same item (none when the item did not come), and takes the sellable rows' units out of Incoming (`arrive`) in the same
document booking that puts what came on hand (an item on several invoice lines: its receipt lines are given to them one to one, in
line order). So a short delivery lowers the figure at once by what did not come, and when the websites
had sold it the oversell event is raised by the same flush (`movement_short`, pack F's queue). **One receipt closes the whole invoice (a
build decision):** what it did not bring is short, not "still coming"; a second delivery of the rest is a new receipt and a new invoice
line, or a credit. The receipt's reversal reopens the rows (the units on their way again).

**PJ4. Reversals.** An invoice whose goods a receipt took in is not reversed (409 `arrived`: reverse the receipt first); otherwise its
open rows are cancelled and the generic negation takes the units out of Incoming. A receipt's reversal: PJ3.

**PJ5. "Sell before it arrives", a supplier's switch (setting `arrivals.sell_before_default`, on, the brief's default).** A supplier's own
choice (`supplier_arrival_pref`, the supplier page's "Goods on their way" card, `suppliers.manage`, audited `supplier.arrivals`, not
changed while the supplier waits for a reviewer's OK, as its other details) else the setting. Off: the rows are kept (shown on Arriving)
but nothing goes into Incoming. Read when the invoice is made final and kept on the row: changing the switch later does not change
invoices already final.

**PJ6. The way per invoice, with a default per supplier (setting `arrivals.default_mode`, `count`; a build decision).** A new invoice
takes the supplier's default, else the setting; the person changes it on the draft ("How its goods come in"). A credit note has none.
Invoices made before 0041 have none (NULL): pack C's rules unchanged for them.

**PJ7. The claim of what did not come.** On a receipt made from an invoice, "What did not come" lists each item short (units and the
invoice's amount for them) and "Claim the missing units" (doc.DN.post) makes a draft return to the supplier: reason supplier_error, linked
to the receipt and the invoice, lines with no item and the amount only, so its posting moves NO stock (pack C's DN/SCN machinery). One live
claim per receipt (pressed again: the same one; 409 `not_from_invoice`, 422 `nothing_missing`). Damaged units go through the bench's
existing set-aside / return flow.

**PJ8. The 3-way match.** A goods line on its way counts as delivered for the match until it is received (billed as ordered: matched); once
received, it bills the receipt line its arrival row names (none: 0 delivered, so a line that did not come is off). A receipt taken in from
an invoice counts as invoiced by it ("Not invoiced yet" does not list it).

**PJ9. "Book as received (no count)".** For goods the person is sure of: when the invoice is made final, a receipt is booked and posted at
once (benched: paperwork OK, the stamp answers) and the invoice's lines are linked to it, so the units go straight on hand; no Arriving, no
bench. The duty stamp is asked on the invoice (`sinv_line.stamp_answer`, digital or transitional, for each line whose item needs a stamp,
`ItemCompliance::receiving` as the bench asks it), and the invoice copy must be attached: until then making it final is refused with the
problems listed. Two transactions (the receipt, then the invoice); `submit_receipt_id` makes a retry post the invoice, never a second
receipt. A posting of such an invoice whose lines no receipt names is refused (409 `receive_first`). Later corrections are the usual
adjustments and counts.

**PJ10. "Make it final later": the time is the person's.** On a draft invoice: a date and time (UK time, stored UTC; only a time still to
come, 422 `bad_submit_at`; one that comes twice when the clocks go back is chosen, BST or GMT, by the person), "Take the time off", or
"Make it final" now. Until then the draft is changed, re-timed or stopped as any
draft; a stopped draft keeps no time. `bin/submit_invoices.php` (cron every minute; one run at a time per schema, Ops\Cli's named lock)
makes the due ones final through `SupplierInvoices::submit` as the person who set the time (their roles checked again then), oldest
first. A draft made final meanwhile is skipped, never posted twice (the posting locks the draft and checks its version). With an approval
rule on, it goes to the reviewer as a person's posting would, and its time is used up. Purchasing › Invoices › Timed lists the waiting ones.

**PJ11. A timed posting that fails** keeps its reason on the invoice (`submit_failed_at`, `submit_error`), is audited
(`invoice.submit_failed`), listed first on Timed, counted on its badge and named by the alerts (`invoice_submit_failed`, pack F), and is
not tried again until a person sets the time again (or makes it final, or stops it). The job exits 1 on the run that saw the failure.

**PJ12. Late (setting `arrivals.late_hours`, 24, 1-720; a build decision).** An invoice whose goods are still on their way that many hours
after it was made final is "late" on Arriving (and counted on its badge).

**PJ13. The nightly checks (`ArrivalInvariants`, in `Invariants::check`).** J1 every balance's incoming equals its open sellable arrival
rows; J2 an open row belongs to a final invoice, a received one to a final receipt; J3 an invoice booked as received leaves no goods line
without a receipt; J4 what a final receipt took out of Incoming equals the sellable rows it received. Receiving's G4 leaves out the
`arrive` rows (J4 checks them).

**PJ14. The screens.** Purchasing › Goods In › Arriving (receiving.view; "Receive" for doc.GRN.post): per supplier and invoice, the units,
how many the websites sell, since when, late. Purchasing › Invoices › Timed (invoices.view). The invoice page: "How its goods come in"
(the way, and the stamp per line for book as received) and "Make it final later" on a draft; "Its goods" once final. The receipt page:
"Received against the supplier invoice", "What did not come" and the claim. The supplier page: "Goods on their way". The item page: an
"On its way" column. Every POST carries the CSRF token; every service checks the person again.

**PJ15. Known limits (build decisions, for the owner to accept or change).** Incoming does not change an item's selling mode: a legacy
item whose website mode is "Out Of Stock" stays off sale until the receipt. Reports, the reorder engine and the duty register count
on_hand only (units on their way are not stock yet; the reorder list may suggest buying what is already on its way). No partial
deliveries (PJ3). "Book as received" is two transactions (PJ9). A merge waits for the units on their way (PJ1). The stock
records' "a protected item never goes below zero" checks (stock out, transfer, repack, hand-over) still count on hand - allocated - held
without Incoming: units on their way never let shelf units leave. So when the websites sold units on their way beyond the shelf, taking
shelf units of a strict item out is refused until the delivery is received (stricter than needed, never a negative shelf).

**PJ16. Not changed.** The connector's writer (PJ1), pack C's rules for invoices without a way (NULL, before 0041), the bench and its
stamp rules, the receipt's own posting order (the arrival step is 5b, before the stock), the lock order.

**Open for the owner:** PJ5's default (on), PJ6's default (count on arrival), PJ12's 24 hours, PJ3's "one receipt closes the invoice",
PJ15's limits, and when 0041 is applied (PJ1: the ledger copy).
### The Codex review of pack J (on `cd3868f`; `runs/packj_codex_review.txt`): seven findings, all real, each fixed test-first

The tests are in `tests/Integration/Arrivals/ArrivalsReviewTest.php` (finding 6 in `ArrivalScreensTest`); each failed before its fix.
(1) Two invoice lines of the same item were both linked to the receipt's first line of that item, so the second looked short, the
match went off and the receipt's second line stayed "not invoiced": the receipt's lines of an item are now given to the invoice's rows
of that item one to one in line order (the receipt is made line for line from the invoice), a row left over sharing the item's last
line (`testTwoLinesOfOneItemAreReceivedLineByLine`). (2) "Make it final" on a book-as-received invoice checked the version before
booking the receipt but not under the lock, so a new time set in between still booked the stock: `Arrivals::bookAsReceived` now takes
the expected version and checks it under the invoice's lock before anything is booked (`testAStaleMakeItFinalBooksNoReceipt`). (3) The
right to make the invoice final was checked only when the invoice was posted, after its receipt: it is now checked first in `submit()`
and again under the lock (`testMakeItFinalWithoutTheInvoiceRightBooksNoReceipt`). (4) A timed attempt overtaken by a new time marked the
new time as failed, so it never ran: the failure is recorded only while the draft is still the version and time the run read, under the
draft's lock; otherwise the attempt is skipped (`testAnAttemptOvertakenByANewTimeLeavesTheNewTimeAlone`). (5) A receipt books up to
four rows a line (on hand, set aside, quarantine, out of Incoming), so a large invoice with exceptions on every line passed the 2,000
rows of `Movements::bookForDocument`: a receipt's own bound is `GoodsReceiptHandler::MAX_BOOKED_LINES` (3 x 2,000 receipt lines + 1,000
invoice lines; `testALargeReceiptFromAnInvoiceIsBookedWhole`, 667 lines, 2,001 rows). (6) A UK time typed in the hour the clocks go
back was read as the second one (GMT): such a time is now never guessed; both are shown ("01:30 BST: the first one", "01:30 GMT: the
second one, an hour later") and the person chooses (422 `ambiguous_submit_at` until then); the time set is shown with its clock
(`CW\Arrivals\UkTime`; `testATimeThatComesTwiceIsChosenByThePerson`). (7) The merge guard read only the incoming bucket, so an item
whose goods were on their way from a supplier that does not sell before arrival could be merged and its receipt then refused: an open
arrival row of the item refuses the merge too, checked before the early return for items without a balance
(`testAnItemOnItsWayUnsoldIsNotMerged`). Also: the two race tests now start the checkout hold only once the posting holds its stock rows
(the worker waits on performance_schema), instead of a fixed 0.2 s that a busy machine could outrun.

## Pack PO: "select or add new" on the purchase order, and the Codex review of the PO module (worktree `pack-po`, 15 Oct 2026)

<!-- ---- Pack PO (0042): PO1-PO12. ---- -->
Built from main `552851a` in `/root/cw-packpo` (branch `pack-po`), migration `0042_po_select_or_add.sql`. The owner, 15 Oct 2026: "In purchase
order view: select or add new option." And the eight findings of the Codex review of the PO module (`runs/po_module_codex_review.txt`), each
proved first by a test that failed on `552851a` (`runs/packpo_red_552851a.log`). New: `src/Ui/Controller/PoSelectOrAddController.php`, views
`purchase_order_new_item`, `po_supplier_needs`, `receipt_split`; changed: `PurchaseOrders`, `PurchaseOrderHandler`, `PoLinesFile`, `DraftPos`,
`PurchaseOrdersController`, `ReorderController`, `ReceivingController` (marked blocks), `GoodsReceipts`, `GoodsReceiptHandler`, `ReceiptPlan`
(marked blocks), `ReceiptWords`, the views of the order, the editor, the list, the reorder list and the delivery, `Words` (group `PO_ADD` and
marked keys), `Kernel` (five routes), `app.js` (the list's search box), `app.css`.

**PO1. The request.** Wherever a purchase order chooses something, the person picks one that is there or adds a new one, without leaving the
order: the supplier (the list's "Start a new order", and a draft that has no products yet: the supplier of a draft with products stays fixed,
I-2) and the product of a line. A build decision put to the owner: the inline supplier form asks the name (the only field the supplier record
needs) and, optionally, an e-mail and a phone; everything else is filled in on the supplier's own page.

**PO2. The supplier: select or add.** The supplier list gets a search box (`input[data-filter-select]`, shown by `app.js`; without the script
the list works as before, a select is searched by its first letters). "Supplier not in the list? Add a new supplier" is a small form of its own
(never inside the order's one form). On the list it makes the supplier and a draft order for it in ONE transaction
(`PurchaseOrders::createWithNewSupplier`, FormOnce: one of each however often it is sent); on a draft without products it makes the supplier
and puts it on the draft (`setNewSupplier`, at the draft's version: the draft's row is locked first, then the supplier is written, the order of
`saveDraft`). The supplier is made by `Suppliers::create` exactly as the supplier screens make one: a DRAFT supplier, its checks, its audit
(`supplier.create`); its approval rules are not changed. Who: the routes ask `suppliers.manage`, the services check it and `doc.PO.post`.

**PO3. A supplier not usable yet.** The draft may be saved with a supplier that is a draft or waits for approval (as before); confirming it is
refused as before (`PurchaseOrderHandler::validate`, 422 `supplier_not_active`). The editor and the order's page now say plainly what is still
needed, in steps, with a link to the supplier ("Supplier waiting for approval": fill in its details, naming the ones `Suppliers::missing`
lists; ask for its approval; a reviewer approves it; then confirm the order). While the second person for a supplier is switched off on the
Approval Rules page (`approvals.supplier_activation`), the steps say that its buyer makes it usable on its page. The general warning "you cannot
confirm it until a reviewer approves X" is then not said twice.

**PO4. The product of a line: scan, search, or add a new item.** The scan box is unchanged. Next to it, "Add a new item" (a button of the
order's one form: it saves the table like Save, then opens the step `/ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/new-item` with what is in the scan box: digits
fill the barcode, words the name, and the packs). The step makes, in ONE transaction (`PurchaseOrders::addNewItem`: the draft locked first,
creator, its version): the item by hand with Pack B's rules (`HandMade::create`: a barcode on another item refused, 409
`barcode_on_other_item`; the same name and identity answered with the items that are there and a "different item" box, 409
`same_item_exists`), this supplier's supplier item when a supplier code, a price or a pack of more than 1 is given (`SupplierItems::create`,
preferred when the item has no main supply yet; the price recorded as its first price), and the line (as a scan adds one). Audit `item.create`,
`supplier_item.create`, `po.new_item`. A refusal offers the existing item: "Add that item to the order instead" / "Add this one to the order"
(a small form to the order's `/lines` with `add_sku`). FormOnce: one item however often the step is sent. Back on the order: "The new item was
made and added to the order."

**PO5. Who sees the "add" options.** Supplier: `suppliers.manage` (Buyers, Purchasing managers). Item: `items.create` (Matching leads, Stock
controllers, Purchasing managers: Pack B, PB1). People without them never see the option: the screen names who can ("Product not found?
Matching leads, Stock controllers and Purchasing managers can add a new item: ask them.", from the permission map in force). **Open for the
owner:** a Buyer cannot make items (items.create is the catalogue team's), so on a Buyer's draft "Add a new item" is not offered; give Buyers
items.create on the Roles and permissions page if they should.

**PO6. Without the script, and the CSP.** Every form works without `app.js` (the search box stays hidden; "Add a new item" is a step that
returns to the order); one stylesheet and one script, no inline code; every word from `Words` (`PO_ADD`); the new templates are held to the
buying and delivery pages' rules (`UiTemplatesTest`).

**PO7. Review findings 1, 5 and 8 (the editor).** (1) HIGH, real: with the orders' "OK first" switched off the editor printed the limit note with
`null` (a TypeError, HTTP 500): the note now says no order needs an OK first (`PurchaseOrderFixesScreensTest::
testTheDraftEditorOpensWithTheOrdersOkFirstSwitchedOff`). (5) MEDIUM, real: a refused save or confirm lost the charge being added, the scan text
and its packs: they are shown again with the table's edits (nothing was saved, so nothing is added twice; after a version conflict they are not:
the page is as it is now). (8) LOW, real: a charge line has its own "Remove this charge" box (`line_N_remove`; `editorFields` counts it).

**PO8. Review finding 2 (HIGH, real): a delivery of an order closed afterwards.** It was refused (409 `po_closed`, I145; owner question I176
(1)): a wrong delivery could be neither reversed nor rejected at review. Now it is taken back like any other (`PurchaseOrders::reverseReceipt`
accepts a closed order): the order stays closed while some of it is still delivered (its "the rest is not coming" stands), and with nothing
delivered it is open again (sent or approved: "closed" means the rest of a part delivery is not coming), its close cleared, the close reason kept
in the audit row (`po.receipt` `reopened_from_closed`; P5 holds either way). The delivery's review box offers "Not OK" again and says what it does
to the order. And "Reopen order" (`PurchaseOrders::reopen`, `POST /ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/reopen`, buyers): a closed order waits for the rest
again; a reason of 3-500 characters, the version, audit `po.reopen` with the close reason it undoes; it can be closed again later.

**PO9. Review findings 3 and 7 (MEDIUM, real).** (3) An order's own lines file did not import again when its item is sold in several packs:
the CW number named the preferred pack and contradicted the supplier code of the box. A row's identifiers now name its line from the most
precise (`PoLinesFile::PRECEDENCE`: supplier code, then barcode, then CW number); the others are resolved within it and must name the same item,
a case barcode the same pack ("is a case of 12, but supplier_code names a pack of 6"). Without a supplier code the CW number still names the
preferred pack. (7) Changing "Terms printed on orders" changed the PDF of orders approved before: the terms are kept at approval
(`purchase_order.terms_snapshot`, 0042; in the order's anchor, P2, when present); an order approved before 0042 prints the version of the
setting in force at its approval (its history), else the setting.

**PO10. Review finding 6 (MEDIUM, real): one supplier invoice for several deliveries.** A delivery may use the invoice number (and the same invoice
copy) of another delivery when the person says so ("Yes: this is a later delivery on the same invoice", a second step offered after the
refusal; `GoodsReceipts::setInvoice` `invoice_split`) AND every live delivery with that number is against the same order (not none) AND none has
the same delivery note (the same delivery keyed twice: 409 `duplicate_invoice`, `why` same_delivery_note). It is then part 2, 3, ... of the
invoice (`goods_receipt.invoice_part`, 0042; the UNIQUE key of a live number is (supplier, number, part)). Everything else stays refused as before:
the number alone, another order's number, no order. A later part keeps its order (409 `invoice_shared` until its number changes); posting
re-checks it (plan problem `invoice_shared`). Left for pack J / pack C: the invoice "the quick way from a delivery" of the second delivery finds
the number taken and starts an invoice without a number; the desk adds the second delivery to the invoice of the first instead.

**PO11. Review finding 4 (MEDIUM, real): the reorder list orders what it showed.** Each ticked line sends the supplier item and the pack it showed
(`si_N`, `upp_N`); when the item's main supply changed meanwhile (another supplier, another pack, none) the line is not ordered: it is skipped
and listed ("its main supplier or pack changed after the list was shown ... look at it again and tick it again"; the owner's rule: skip anything
doubtful, finish the rest). A pick without them (the API, older callers) takes the main supply as it is, as before.

**PO12. "Make all flow easy" (relayed by the build's coordinator, 15 Oct 2026).** Found: the owner, holding Reviewer, can already do the whole flow
alone. (a) A new supplier: the second person is the switch `approvals.supplier_activation` on the Approval Rules page; switched off, "ask for
approval" makes a complete supplier usable at once, recorded as approved alone (`supplier.activate_alone`); CW holds no bank details (decision
25). (b) The company details: a Reviewer edits and confirms them alone; the check of one's own change of watched details
(`approvals.company_own_change`) opens a review afterwards and never blocks. (c) The reviewer check after an order is confirmed is the PO rule's
review rule on the same page; the OK first over the value limit is separate. (d) A new line already takes the supplier's VAT code and the
supplier item's last price (`PoSelectOrAddTest::testANewLineTakesTheSuppliersVatCodeAndTheLastPrice`). **Not done in this build:** changing the
seeded defaults of (a) and (c) to off; it is put to the owner, who can switch both on the Approval Rules page today.

## Pack RB: the rollback file, the smallest switch-over tool (worktree `rollback-export`, 17 Oct 2026; RB1-RB34)

The go-live plan (step 5.2, "the ERP way back" step 4; IM15) needs, if the switch is rolled back, a file that brings ERPNext level with what
CW booked since the switch, plus the lists ERPNext needs, written every night of the rollback window. `bin/rollback_export.php` makes it;
`CW\Ops\RollbackExport` has the rules. The owner's condition for the switch (Vape and Go first, at least 3 listening days) stays; this pack only
makes the way back possible.

**RB1. Read only, one moment, never overwritten.** Everything is read in ONE consistent snapshot (`Snapshot::read`: REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY);
nothing is written to the database and nothing connects to ERPNext. The files go into a NEW directory (one that exists is refused, exit 2), 0700,
each file 0600 (umask 0077 before the first write), `manifest.json` last: the format, when it was made (the database's clock), the schema, the
cut-off and where it came from, the settings used, the item list's name and sha256, each file's rows, bytes and sha256, and the counts. A run
stopped halfway leaves a directory without a manifest: it is not used, a new one is made (never delete). The cut-off is `--since` (UTC, to the
microsecond), else the as-of moment of the EARLIEST finished ERPNext opening (`erp_opening_run`, pack I; RB13): the moment ERPNext's figures
describe. The settings are read in the same snapshot (RB17).

**RB2. Which stock rows are carried.** Every `on_hand` row booked (`created_at`) at or after the cut-off at a warehouse of the setting
`rollback.cw_warehouses` (baseline `MAIN,VERIFY`), except, each listed in `movements.csv` with why (`Words::ROLLBACK_REASON`):
- the website's order flow (`RollbackExport::WEBSITE_TYPES`: reserve ... return): the website sends its own sales, cancels and returns to
  ERPNext; these rows are not read, only counted per type (`website_rows`);
- rows a website (channel) booked: the ERP relay types (goods in, supplier returns, sales booked in ERPNext) are `in_erpnext`; anything else a
  website booked (a doubtful cancel moved into VERIFY) is `from_website`;
- a person's booking OF an ERPNext queue row (its Idempotency-Key is the row's, `Corrections::KEY` / `Suspense::KEY`, for the same item;
  RB15), and any `erp_sale`: `in_erpnext` (ERPNext made them);
- a join of duplicates and its undoing: `cw_join` (RB14); a row booked at or before an ERPNext "set to this number" of its item and
  warehouse: `before_erp_correction` (RB12); a website event a count took in gives its units back to that count (RB11);
- opening rows (actor `system:opening_estimate`: the ERPNext opening, the estimate, the units-only rebase; or type `opening`): `opening`;
- a row at another warehouse: `other_warehouse`; a type this file does not know (`CARRIED_TYPES` lists the ones it does): `unknown_type`.
Why VERIFY is carried by default: a website's cancel moves units MAIN -> VERIFY (not carried: the website's), and ERPNext never took them out; a
person's recount VERIFY -> MAIN then adds up to nothing inside its document. With VERIFY not carried, that recount would add the units to ERPNext
a second time. UNSTAMPED is not carried by default: stock moved there by the duty sweep cannot be sold, so ERPNext's figure loses it (a setting).

**RB3. Which ERPNext item a CW item is, never a guess.** The candidates of an item: every ERPNext code CW knows (its ERPNext links,
`sku_erp_item`, and, when the ERPNext item list is given, `--item-list`, the same file the opening used, its codes) that the opening's own
resolver (`ErpItemResolver`: the link first, else the Product ID through the store `erp_opening.listing_store`'s match) makes this item, with
its units per ERPNext item (RB10); item codes compared as ERPNext compares them (`ErpOpeningRules::itemKey`), written as ERPNext wrote them
(`ErpOpeningFiles::itemMap` now also returns `codes`). One candidate: that one. Several: the one of one unit, when exactly one is; else
`ambiguous_erp_item`. None: `no_erp_item`. A net that is not a whole number of ERPNext items: `fractional_qty`. A code the spreadsheet guard
would change (`CsvWriter::safeText`: it starts like a formula): `unsafe_text`, since ERPNext would get a different code. Each is listed with its
units; nothing is carried for it (the owner's rule: skip anything doubtful and list it).

**RB4. One entry per document, added up per item.** The rows of one document and its reversal (`reverses_id`), or of one movement a person typed
(its Idempotency-Key), are added up per item first; what adds up to nothing is `netted_out` (a document and its cancelling, a move between two
carried warehouses). The rest of a document becomes a Material Receipt (more) and/or a Material Issue (less) in `erpnext_stock_entry.csv`, in
ERPNext's Data Import layout ("Insert New Records": the entry's fields on its first row, the item fields as "Field (Items)" on every row), in the
ERPNext company `rollback.erp_company` and warehouse `rollback.erp_warehouse` (baselines `VAPE AND GO` and `Stores - VPG`, the names the
opening import reads), posted at the earliest moment of its rows (`effective_at`, else `created_at`) in UK time with "Set Posting Time" on. A
receipt's Basic Rate is the cost a central unit CW valued the rows at (the value ledger's, else the row's own), averaged over the rows weighted by
units, times the units per ERPNext item, to 6 decimals; none known: left empty and counted (`receipt_lines_without_rate`). An issue carries no
rate: ERPNext values it at its own average. The Remarks name the entry ("CW rollback entry N"), the CW document numbers and the movement types;
`movements.csv` names each row's entry. The two ERPNext files have no byte-order mark (ERPNext's importer reads plain UTF-8); the lists keep
the mark (people open them in Excel).

**RB5. A hand-over is a Sales Invoice.** The units out of a hand-over document (`TRD`) are a line of `erpnext_sales_invoice.csv`: Customer (the
customer's name in CW, which ERPNext must have: `customers.csv`), Update Stock on, the ERPNext item and its quantity, Rate = the hand-over's price
a unit (averaged as in RB4) times the units per ERPNext item, in the same warehouse. VAT is not on the file: ERPNext applies its tax template. A
customer name the spreadsheet guard would change, or a reversal whose original lies before the cut-off (units back in), goes to the stock entry
file instead.

**RB6. The selling modes.** `selling_modes.csv`: every item's mode on the store (`item_channel_mode`: the mode, the mode before Out-Of-Stock, the
low-stock figure CW writes, who set it, when) as CW last wrote it, one row per ERPNext item of the item (each of them takes the mode), with the
store's variants; an item without an ERPNext item is listed with why. Honest limit: while the writer is off, the store may hold other modes;
this file is what CW last wrote.

**RB7. The lists.** `purchase_orders.csv`: every order made, or approved, since the cut-off (RB18), or received against since (a goods receipt posted since),
one row per item line: units ordered, received and still to come (none once received, closed or cancelled), the pack price and VAT code, and the
ERPNext item. `suppliers.csv`, `customers.csv`, `items.csv`: those made since the cut-off (an item with its ERPNext items, `code (units)` when not
one, its variants, and what it was joined into), so ERPNext gets them before the entries that name them.

**RB8. Settings (0046).** `rollback.cw_warehouses` (warehouse codes, comma-separated; each must be a CW warehouse when the file is made),
`rollback.erp_warehouse`, `rollback.erp_company` (the names as ERPNext writes them; a name starting like a formula is refused; empty: the file is
not made, exit 2), and `rollback.max_rows` (RB28). All four provisional: put to the owner. Topic "Way back to ERPNext"; words in `Words::SETTING`, `SETTING_HELP`, and
`ROLLBACK_REASON` for the reasons.

**RB9. Not in this pack.** The nightly run and the copy off CW (write-once storage) of plan step 5.2 are set up on the production server, with
its backups (handoff 17 Oct, §6.4): the command is ready for a cron line. The Data Import layout is proved only by the practice switch night on
the ERPNext test copy (plan part 3, "the ERP way back after two weeks"): if ERPNext v16's template names a column differently, the titles are in
`RollbackExport::STOCK_ENTRY_COLUMNS` and `SALES_INVOICE_COLUMNS` (one place).

Tests: `RollbackExportTest` (a goods-in a person typed as a Material Receipt at its cost in UK time; units in ERPNext items and every reason a
row is not carried; what ERPNext or a website already has; a document and its reversal, a move between carried warehouses; a hand-over as a
Sales Invoice; the item list and the modes file; the settings; the script: a new directory once, 0700/0600, the manifest's sha256, the cut-off
from the latest opening), `RollbackListsTest` (the orders, suppliers, customers and items made since), `Migration0046Test`.
### The Codex review of pack RB (on `269909d`; `runs/rbx_codex_review.txt`): ten findings, all real, each shown by a test first

The key question put to the reviewer: after a rollback, is ERPNext's stock of each item CW's stock in the carried warehouses, every change
carried once, at the right ERPNext item? Each finding below has a test that failed on `269909d` (`runs/rbx_red.log`: 8 failures, the 10 earlier
tests passing) and passes now. RB1-RB9 above stand as amended here.

**RB10. Finding 1 (HIGH): an ERPNext item is the CW item the opening import makes it.** A link (`sku_erp_item` BOX = 6 units) and the item list
(BOX's Product ID is a single's listing) were added side by side, and "the one of one unit" then wrote 12 BOX for 12 units. Now every code CW
knows (its links, the item list's codes) is resolved by `ErpItemResolver`, exactly as the opening resolves it (the link first, else the Product
ID through the store's match; a merged item, an unmatched or quarantined listing and a code two links share resolve to nothing). One code is one
CW item with one unit count; only then is the item's code chosen (RB3). `RollbackExport::productCodes()` is gone; the constructor takes the
item list itself. Test: `testAnErpnextLinkKeepsItsUnitsWhenTheItemListAlsoReachesTheItem`.

**RB11. Finding 2 (HIGH): a website event a count already took in.** A dispatch dated before a count but sent after it books only
`allocated -u` (note `pre_count`, Reservations::ship); the count's own on_hand change already took the units off, and the website still tells
ERPNext of the sale: carrying the count took them off ERPNext twice. The same for a reset (unship) the count put back. Such a row is now read
(`bucket = 'allocated'`, `ship`/`unship`, note `pre_count`) and gives its units back to the count that took them in (the latest count of the
item and warehouse in the window, dated at or after it): in the count's family they add up to the count's true change. A count the file does
not carry passes its reason on; none in the window: `count_before_cut` (the item's ERPNext figure was never CW's: set by hand). Test:
`testADispatchOrResetACountAlreadyTookInIsNotCarriedTwice`.

**RB12. Finding 3 (HIGH): ERPNext's "set to this number" makes its figure whole.** A reconciliation sets ERPNext's figure absolutely, so what
CW alone booked before its moment is inside it (CW's confirmation books the difference against its own figure then, Corrections::effect). A
row booked (`created_at`) at or before the latest ERPNext correction of its item and warehouse (`Corrections::at`, any state) is not carried:
`before_erp_correction`. A correction CW did not take (open, dismissed) is named in the counts (`erp_corrections_not_taken`; the command says how
many): ERPNext's figure of that item is then not CW's. Test: `testAnErpnextCorrectionTakesInWhatCwBookedBeforeIt`.

**RB13. Finding 4 (HIGH): the cut-off is the EARLIEST finished ERPNext opening.** A later run books only items that had not moved, so it can
never move the cut-off; choosing the latest hid the CW changes between the two. Every finished run is named in the manifest
(`opening_runs`), and the command says so when there are several. Test: `testTheEarliestFinishedOpeningIsTheCutOff`.

**RB14. Finding 5 (HIGH): a join of duplicates is CW's own.** Carried, a join moved ERPNext's units between two ERPNext items while the moved
listing's website sales went on to the old item in ERPNext. ERPNext never joins its items: the join rows (`JOIN_TYPES`: merge and split) are
not carried (`cw_join`), so each ERPNext item keeps what its own website listing sells from; the total over the two stays CW's. Test:
`testAJoinOfDuplicatesIsNotCarriedAndAMovementUnderTheSameKeyStaysItsOwn`.

**RB15. Finding 6 (MEDIUM): only a booking OF an ERPNext queue row is ERPNext's.** A document name shared with an ERPNext queue row hid a
person's own goods-in. Now a row is ERPNext's when its Idempotency-Key is the queue row's (`Corrections::KEY`, `Suspense::KEY`, now constants
used by the queues themselves) for the same item. Test: `testAMovementThatOnlySharesAnErpnextDocumentsNameIsCarried`.

**RB16. Finding 7 (MEDIUM): one typed movement is its booker, its type and its key.** A join's generated key could equal a typed key. The family
of a row without a document is now `(actor, type, Idempotency-Key)`; joins are not carried anyway (RB14). Same test as RB14.

**RB17. Finding 8 (MEDIUM): the settings are of the same moment.** `RollbackExport::run()` reads the settings, the cut-off and the stock in one
snapshot; the command calls it and writes the settings it used into the manifest. Test: `testTheSettingsAreReadInTheSnapshotOfTheStock`
(every read of `app_setting` happens inside the transaction).

**RB18. Finding 9 (MEDIUM): an order approved since the cut-off is listed** even when its draft is older (`document.posted_at`). Test:
`RollbackListsTest::testAnOrderDraftedBeforeTheCutOffAndApprovedAfterIsListed`.

**RB19. Finding 10 (MEDIUM): memory.** The rows were all kept as arrays until the end. Now they are read twice in the same snapshot, by id in
chunks: the first pass keeps only each family's sums per item (one small array; a family's types and documents once), the second writes
movements.csv. Measured with a probe not kept in the tests (`runs/rbx_memory_probe*.txt`; peak above the start, the old code against the new on
the same rows): 3,000 rows at a warehouse not carried 10.6 MB -> 6.8 MB (a row not carried now costs only its line in movements.csv); 3,000
rows each its own carried item 10.0 MB -> 11.3 MB (about the same: one sum per document and item instead of one row). Honest limit (corrected
by RB22): memory grows with the carried documents and items (their sums, outcomes and entries) and with the files, not only with the CSV bytes.
### The second Codex review (on `5e96333`; `runs/rbx_codex_review2.txt`): six of the ten fixed, four more, each shown by a test first

Codex checked each fix against its finding: RB10, RB11, RB12, RB13, RB17 and RB18 fixed; four were not complete. The tests below failed on
`5e96333` (`runs/rbx_red3.log`) or, for RB23, on `269909d` (`runs/rbx_red2.log`), and pass now.

**RB20. (HIGH) Joins, and the items entries cannot make level, are set to CW's figure. Withdrawn by RB24: see there.** Not carrying a join (RB14) kept each ERPNext item's
own figure, but an ERPNext correction of the kept item afterwards (30 + 8 joined, ERPNext sets the kept one to 20) left the joined item's 8 in
ERPNext: 28 against CW's 20. Entries cannot fix that, nor an ERPNext correction CW did not take (RB12), nor the website events of a count before
the cut-off (RB11). So the file now has `erpnext_stock_reconciliation.csv`: ONE Stock Reconciliation, at the moment of the file, that sets each
such item to CW's figure as ERPNext counts it: its units at the carried warehouses less the paid units not yet sent (`allocated`: ERPNext takes
a sale off when it is paid; the opening's units-only rebase, PI14, is the same relation), in its ERPNext item, at CW's average cost; every other
ERPNext item of it, and a joined item's own links (which the opening no longer reads), to nothing. ERPNext imports it LAST: an absolute figure
at that moment overrides every entry before it. An item it cannot set (no or several ERPNext items, not whole ERPNext items, a figure below
zero, a code like a formula) is named in `counts.reconciliation.not_set`, never guessed. Of several ERPNext items of one unit, CW's own link
(a person's decision) is the item's (a join leaves the kept item with its own link and, through the moved listing, the joined one's). Honest
limit: a website sale paid but not yet in ERPNext at that moment is counted twice for these items (minutes; the same as the opening's pending
sales). Test: `testAJoinOfDuplicatesIsNotCarriedAndBothItemsAreSetToCwsFigure`.

**RB21. (MEDIUM) A queue booking is the person who settled the row.** A key and an item did not prove the row booked that queue row: a job
can use `queue:correction:7` in its own scope (Idempotency: staff and each job have their own). A row is ERPNext's booking only when the queue
row is settled, the row's booker is the person who settled it (`resolved_by`), its type is the queue's (an adjustment; the suspense row's
type) and its item (and, for a correction, its warehouse) are the queue row's. Test: `testAJobsMovementUnderAQueueRowsKeyIsCarried`.

**RB22. (MEDIUM) Memory, measured and said honestly.** Codex measured a file of 30,000 distinct carried documents at about 148 MB above the
start (it did not fit in 128 MB): about 5 KB a carried document and item. A window of 100,000 of them would need about 500 MB; the expected
window is far smaller (6 weeks: about 300 receipts, 100 corrections, the counts of 6 to 8 weeks, plan §5.2 and §8.3), and the production
server has 4 GB with PHP's command line unlimited. Each run writes `peak_memory_bytes` into its manifest, so the nightly runs show the job
growing long before it would not fit; bounding it further (streaming the entries) is left until a run shows the need.

**RB23. (MEDIUM) The test that isolates RB16.** Two movements under one key from two scopes (a person's +6 and a job's -1 of an item of six
units) stay two families: one box, and the job's unit listed as not whole. With the old grouping by the key alone they added up to 5 and both
were listed. Test: `testTwoMovementsUnderOneKeyFromTwoScopesStayApart`.
### The third Codex review (on `433ff14`; `runs/rbx_codex_review3.txt`): RB21 and RB23 confirmed; the stock reconciliation withdrawn

Codex confirmed RB21 and RB23, and RB20 for the case it was written for, but showed that a figure set by a program erases what it does not
see. The tests below failed on `433ff14` (`runs/rbx_red4.log`) and pass now.

**RB24. (HIGH) Nothing sets ERPNext's figures by itself: the items entries cannot make level are listed, to be set by hand.** RB20's Stock
Reconciliation set a joined item to nothing although units held on it stayed its own (38 in ERPNext became 36); a count dated a minute ahead
was counted twice (the reconciliation, then the later entry); the reconciliation's clock was later than the snapshot (a sale between the two
was overwritten); a merged item's link bypassed the check of two links reading as one code; a code shared by two items took the last item's
rate; a merged item's one link of a box was called ambiguous. Each is a way a program's absolute figure goes wrong. So
`erpnext_stock_reconciliation.csv` is gone; `to_set_by_hand.csv` lists both items of every join (the item joined, the one it went into, each
marking the other), every item ERPNext set to a number CW did not take, and every item a count before the cut-off took website events in for:
the item, why (`Words::ROLLBACK_SET`), CW's figure as ERPNext counts it (units on hand at the carried warehouses less the paid units not yet
sent: ERPNext takes a sale off when it is paid, the relation of the opening's units-only rebase, PI14), both parts, every ERPNext item known for
it (the codes the opening reads, a joined item's own links, with their units), and the item it was joined with. The ERPNext admin sets them
after the import, so that each pair together holds CW's figures (the owner's rule: anything doubtful is listed, never guessed). The command
says how many; `counts.to_set_by_hand` holds the number. Tests: `testAJoinOfDuplicatesIsNotCarriedAndBothItemsAreListedToBeSetByHand` (the 30
+ 8 join, then ERPNext sets the kept item to 20: no entry, both listed at 20 and 0), `testAJoinThatLeavesHeldUnitsOnTheJoinedItemListsBothFigures`
(36 and 2: the held units are not paid, ERPNext still counts them).

**RB25. (HIGH) Two ERPNext items of one unit are never chosen between.** RB20's tie-break (CW's own link wins) could take a sale off an
ERPNext item that holds none: a link says how its own code maps into CW, not which of two ERPNext items is the item's. Withdrawn: such an
item's rows are `ambiguous_erp_item`, as before RB20. Test: `testTwoErpnextItemsOfOneUnitAreNeverChosenBetween`.

**RB26, RB27.** Withdrawn with the reconciliation (RB24): the rate of a code shared by two items (finding 7) and the one link of a box
(finding 8) were the reconciliation's alone; the hand list shows every code with its units and sets nothing.

**RB28. (MEDIUM) A window too big for the machine stops before it is read.** The aggregation is still unbounded by design (RB22's numbers:
about 5 KB a carried row). The new setting `rollback.max_rows` (0046; baseline 200,000, provisional) stops the first pass at the first row past
it, before any file is written (exit 3, the directory not made), and says how to go on: raise the setting when the machine has the memory, or
make the file from a later moment. Test: `testARunThatWouldReadMoreRowsThanTheLimitStopsAndSaysWhy` (a limit of 2 with 3 rows stops, through
`run()` and through the command; 3 reads them).
### The fourth Codex review (on `5264689`; `runs/rbx_codex_review4.txt`): RB24-RB28 answered; the hand list told more

Codex found the nine points of its third review answered, and four things the person setting the list, or a big window, still needed. The tests
below failed on `5264689` (`runs/rbx_red5.log`) and pass now.

**RB29. (HIGH) A joined item's ERPNext item from before the join.** When ERPNext reaches the joined item only through its listing, the join
moved that listing to the kept item, so the code showed under the kept item and the joined item's held units had none. A listing whose present
link a join opened (`listing_map_history` opened by an applied `merge_skus` decision, `DecisionService::openPeriod`) belonged to the joined
item: its code is shown under the kept item as "came with <item> in the join" and under the joined item as "its own before the join". Test:
`testAJoinThatLeavesHeldUnitsOnTheJoinedItemListsBothFiguresAndItsOwnErpnextItem` (the joined item's code through its listing only; 36 and 2).

**RB30. (HIGH) A code two CW links read as one is shown with its other owner.** A joined item's own link (` Shared`) and another item's
(`Shared`) are one ERPNext item; the opening's resolver refuses both, but the list showed the code under the joined item alone, and setting it
to that item's figure would have erased the other's units. Every code in the list now says which other CW items link it ("also linked to ...:
settle which item it is first"). Test: `testACodeTwoLinksReadAsOneIsShownWithItsOtherOwner`.

**RB31. (MEDIUM) The limit is checked on a count, before a row is read.** The first pass counted as it went, so a window far over the limit
could run out of memory (exit 255) before reaching it. The rows are counted first (the same reading's condition, on the `created_at` index); a
window over `rollback.max_rows` stops with exit 3 before any row is read, and a window within it raises PHP's memory limit, when it is set lower,
to what it may need (RB22's 5 KB a row, and room to start). Test: the limit test now also proves no row was read (`StatementHook`).

**RB32. (MEDIUM) Many joins stay within MySQL's limit of bound values.** The hand list's look-up of joined pairs named every item twice in one
statement (65,536 values for 32,768 items); it now reads in chunks of 1,000, each side on its own, like the other look-ups. Not covered by a
test (it needs 16,384 joins); the chunking is the same as `loadSkus()`'s.
### The fifth Codex review (on `2ed488b`; `runs/rbx_codex_review5.txt`): RB30-RB32 answered; one more, then fit to merge

**RB33. (HIGH) Through a chain of joins each code goes back to the item it belonged to first.** RB29 read only the newest period of a
listing's link: after A was joined into B and B into C, A's code showed under B ("its own before the join") while A, still holding two units
held for a checkout, showed none, and setting B would have erased them. The listing's periods are now walked from the newest back: each period a
join opened names the item it came from, as long as it follows on from the period before it (the walk stops at a period a person's decision
opened, or a link changed in between); the item of the first join is the code's own. Test: `testAChainOfJoinsGivesEachCodeBackToTheItemItBelongedToFirst`
(A into B into C, two units held on A: A 2 with its code, B 0 with its code, C 13 with both "came with").
### The sixth Codex review (on `1b41917`; `runs/rbx_codex_review6.txt`): RB33 confirmed; a join undone

**RB34. (HIGH) A join undone is stepped over; history that cannot be followed is said so.** After A into B into C, splitting B back out of C
opened new periods for B's listings, and the walk stopped there: A's code showed under B with no word, and A's two held units had none. A
period a split back to the former item opened (`match_decision` action `split`, `detail.split_to = former`) now sends the walk back past every
period down to the one the join it undoes opened (`detail.undoes_decision_id`), and on from the period before it, which must be of the same item.
A history that cannot be followed (a split to a new item, or the join a split undoes not among the listing's periods) is not guessed: the code
is shown with "its joins cannot be followed: check which item it belongs to". The walk is `RollbackExport::firstOwner()`. Test:
`testAJoinUndoneIsSteppedOverAndTheEarlierJoinsCodeStaysItsOwn` (A into B into C, then B split back: A 2 with "its own before the join", B 3
with A's code as "came with A in the join" and its own, C 10).

## Design v5: the owner's monday.com-like brief (worktree `ui-v5`, 19 Oct 2026; V5.1-V5.9)

The owner pasted a design brief from another project ("ui posible to follow this style") and chose, when asked: light only (no dark
mode), the icons as a same-origin SVG sprite, a deep plum (#2a0a24) sign-in panel, and the three missing Poppins weights downloaded from
@fontsource/poppins 5.2.7 (the 500 already here is byte-identical to that package's). The brief is kept at
`/root/cw_work/ui5/design_brief_owner_2026-10-19.md` on the main server. It is a re-skin: no route, permission, service or word of a
rule changed.

**V5.1. Tokens.** Section 1 of `app.css` holds the brief's tokens (surfaces, ink, lines, the accent #c90e9f, the brand gradient, the
eight solid status colours, the soft tags, radius 8/10/12/14/16/999, the spacing scale) and defines every older token name the page
bodies use from them, so the screens' own parts kept their rules. One font, Poppins 400-700 (Figtree is gone). Light only:
`color-scheme: light`, no dark block. Two deviations, both for contrast: the open sidebar item's words are the darker accent #8f0a71
on the accent's tint (the accent itself is 4.3:1 there), and a field's edge (`--field`) is the brief's muted ink #6c6577, not the
1 px hairline (1.2:1) nor "ink faint" #9a92a6 (2.95:1), so a field is visible (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1; V5.10).

**V5.2. The statement.** Every page template opens with `$head(...)` (`Ui\View::head`, drawn by `Ui\Html::statement` and
`views/page_frame.php`): the section's name as the UPPERCASE eyebrow (the Dashboard: today's date; outside every section the system's
name; an error page "Error 404"), the page's heading, its state chips, the page's sentence and, muted under it, what to do (or "You can
look; … change this."): `Words::introParts`, the same PAGE_INTRO pair as before, so the words did not change. The full stop is drawn by
the stylesheet after `.stmt.stop` (not after a heading that ends in its own punctuation), so the heading's text stays the page's name for
the tab title, a screen reader and the tests. The page's create button sits on the right of the statement; the section's tabs, the
buying flow, the segmented filter and the "switched off" strip come under it. The section's one-line description (`SECTION_DESC`) is no
longer shown (one sentence per page). A template that draws no statement still gets the frame from the layout (`.frame-only`).

**V5.3. Icons.** `public/ui/assets/icons.svg`: 24 outline icons, one `<view>` each (an "SVG stack": no style, no script, nothing
fetched), served by `Ui\Assets` as `image/svg+xml` under the same CSP and caching as the stylesheet. `app.css` draws `.ico .ico-<name>`
as a mask of `icons.svg?v=<first 16 of its sha256>#<name>` in the text colour, so a page still holds no `<svg>` and no image
(`UiSecurityTest::assertInert` unchanged). `UiUnitTest::testTheIconSpriteIsCurrentAndHasEveryIconAPageNames` keeps the version current
and every icon a page names in the sprite.

**V5.4. The shell.** A white sidebar (248 px, from 700 px up): the CW tile and name, the bell (everything waiting for the person, on the
Dashboard; the sum of the sidebar's counts) and the help; "Find a product"; MENU; the seven sections; the person (gradient avatar,
name, jobs) with a menu (`details.user-menu`: Change password, Sign out). Under 700 px: a sticky top bar (the tile, the open tab's
name, find, the bell, Menu) and the bottom bar the owner approved in v3 (kept: the brief does not forbid it and the phone users rely on
it). The change notice is a toast at the bottom right (`p.notice.toast`), fading after 8 seconds with app.js.

**V5.5. Components restyled in place** (the markup and the tests that pin it unchanged): status pills (solid, white 12 px semi-bold,
radius 6, at least 110 px; the tones keep their names: needs amber, done green, waiting grey, blocked red, info blue, review purple, off
navy), soft tags, KPI tiles (radius 16, a 10 px coloured square before the label, 32 px figure), board groups (a coloured chevron and
17 px title, a muted count, then the table in a white card), tables (in a white card with a hairline and radius 14, sideways scroll
inside it, a 12 px muted head, soft row dividers, numbers on the right, ticked rows #fdf3fb, rows needing a look #fdf6ec), quick-filter
chips, segmented filters (the chosen one dark), underline tabs, buttons (44/36/30 px; primary, secondary, dark, danger, danger outline,
success, ghost, dashed), forms (label above, 44 px fields, radius 10, a 2 px accent focus ring; a form of several fieldsets numbers them),
notices (info, warning, problem, done, each with its badge), the bulk bar (dark, the count in pink, dark secondary buttons, the main
action pink with dark words), histories as a timeline, empty states centred.

**V5.6. Drawers.** A list page's "New …" fold (`details.drawer#new`: purchase orders and the other create forms) is, with app.js and
from 700 px, a panel sliding in from the right (560-760 px, radius 16): its summary is the sticky header with a close mark, the form's
buttons a sticky footer, the page dimmed behind it (`body::after`). Esc, a click on the dimmed page and the header close it; Tab stays
inside; focus goes to its first field and back to what opened it (else to its header). While open it is moved to the end of `<body>`
and back to its place when it closes or the screen narrows under 700 px (and lifted again when it widens): the page column is a CSS
container (its lists turn into cards), and a container keeps what is fixed inside it under the dimmed layer. A fold the server sends
open (a refused form, whose error is above it, or an empty list) stays a fold in the page (`is-inline`) until it is closed and opened
again (V5.10). Without the script, or on a phone, it is the fold it was.

**V5.7. Sign-in.** Two halves (stacked under 900 px): the brand half (#2a0a24, two soft glows in the brand gradient's colours, faint
large shapes at 16%, a dot grid, the CW tile on a white tile, an eyebrow, the headline "One stock figure for every shop.", one line, four
short bars, "Powered by Floverfy") and the 420 px form ("Sign in.", the sentence, e-mail, password with Show, the 6-digit code, the full-
width button, "or", "Set up my sign-in", who to ask). The words are new `Words::SIGN_IN` entries.

**V5.8. Left out of the brief, on purpose.** Google Fonts and Alpine.js (CSP and the vanilla app.js); the cookie banner (CW sets only
its session cookie); a footer privacy link (no such page); "Keep me signed in", "Forgot password?" and a code-only sign-in (they would
be new services; who to ask is said instead); the "Live · updated" badge with 30-second refresh (app.js never talks to the network);
the context switcher card, the inline assign panel, the approvals split layout and paging every group by 10 (each a change of what the
pages do, not of their look); a modal (CW has no modal: its confirmations are steps on the page); "−£" in red for negative money
(`Html::money` is shared with files and stays "-£").

**V5.9. Tests.** UiTemplatesTest (the layout: sidebar, bell, person's menu, top bar, statement before the tabs, the create button on the
right; `testEveryPageOpensWithItsStatement`: no template writes an `<h1>`, every page template draws `$head`, the helper's parts
escaped and in order, the drawn full stop), UiUnitTest (the sprite served and current; the error pages' heading), UiSecurityTest (the
sprite and the four Poppins files served, nothing else), KernelUiTestCase::sectionTabs (the tabs are under the statement now).

**V5.10.** (1, MEDIUM) A create form refused with an error was sent open and became a drawer over the error above it: a fold the server
sends open now stays in the page (`is-inline`; the drawer rules skip it). (2, MEDIUM) A drawer opened under 700 px and widened past it

section 22 still had v4's `.bulkbar-choice` rule after the new one (dark words on the dark bar, 1:1): one rule now. (4, LOW) a field's
edge was 2.95:1: `--field` is the muted ink (5.6:1). (5, LOW) the template lint took `$head(...)` as a helper call, so a raw value in its
`chips`, `meta` or `aside` (printed as they are) would have passed: `UiTemplatesTest::testTheStatementsRawPartsAreOnlyHelperOutput` parses
those arguments and allows only helper calls, string literals, `.`, parentheses and ternaries whose branches are such (none of the 117
calls failed it). Tests: `UiUnitTest::testTheDesignTokensMeetTheContrastTheyAreUsedFor` (the field edge on a card and the page, muted and
body words, the eyebrow, the open sidebar item, white on every status colour, the one bulk-bar rule) and
`testACreateDrawerTheServerOpenedStaysInThePageAndFollowsTheBreakpoint`; the drawer's behaviour itself was checked in a browser (no
script test runner in CW).

### The second Codex review (on `bf28321`, rebased onto main `de196e3`; `runs/ui5_codex_review2.txt`): 3 fixed, 2 partly, 3 more

**V5.11.** Findings 1, 3 and 4 fixed; 2 and 5 partly, and three more, all real, each answered:
- (LOW, finding 5 again) the lint read a `$head` argument by its text, so `/* note */ meta: $row['name']` or the raw parts given by position
  (`$head('P', null, null, $row['name'])`) slipped past: the arguments are now read from their tokens (comments dropped), and one

- (MEDIUM) after Esc or a click on the dimmed page, the toolbar's "New …" link could not open the drawer again (the address already
