The drawer's behaviour was checked in a browser (the viewport emulation used sends no resize event, so the breakpoint was driven by a
resize event fired by hand); `UiUnitTest::testACreateDrawerTheServerOpenedStaysInThePageAndFollowsTheBreakpoint` pins the script's parts.

### The third Codex review (on `b96c828`; `runs/ui5_codex_review3.txt`): every MEDIUM fixed, three LOW more, each answered

**V5.12.** (LOW) The lint still missed `$head('P', ...['meta' => $row['name']])` and a comment holding brackets before a name: the calls
are now found with PHP's own tokenizer (a bracket in a string or a comment is never the end of a call; markup is never read), and an
unpacked argument is refused (which parameter it fills is unknown). (LOW) A Ctrl, Cmd, Shift or Alt click on a "New …" link (a new tab)
also opened the drawer here: only a plain click that stays in this tab opens it (not another button, a `target`, a `download`).
(LOW) A link to an ordinary fold could be kept as a drawer's opener: a link is an opener only for a drawer and only from outside it,
and when what opened a drawer is gone or hidden the focus goes back to the fold's header. Tests: the lint's own cases
(`testTheStatementsRawPartsAreOnlyHelperOutput`) and the script's parts
(`testACreateDrawerTheServerOpenedStaysInThePageAndFollowsTheBreakpoint`), red on `b96c828` first.

### The fourth Codex review (on `a156b50`; `runs/ui5_codex_review4.txt`): two of three fixed, the lint once more

**V5.13.** (LOW) A bracket inside a double-quoted string (`$head("$title)", meta: $row['name'])`) still ended a call early for the lint,
so what came after it was never read. The lint now refuses any `$head` call it cannot read whole: one holding a double-quoted,
backquoted or heredoc string (none of the 117 calls does) or one that never closes (`UiTemplatesTest::UNREADABLE`); Codex's three cases,
a `{$x}` case, a heredoc and an unclosed call are in the lint's own test. The fifth review (on `39a50c1`; `runs/ui5_codex_review5.txt`)
found the same gap through an attribute (`#[A] fn() => …`, whose `#[` is one token): instead of one token more, a `$head` call may now
hold only the parts the templates use (`HEAD_TOKENS`, `HEAD_CHARS`: variables, names, single-quoted strings, numbers, comparisons,
`??`, casts, `->`, `::`, brackets, `.`, `?`, `:`, `!`); anything else (an attribute, a closure, `match`, braces, a backquote) makes it
unreadable, and the lint fails.

### The sixth Codex review (on `2fadf6d`; `runs/ui5_codex_review6.txt`): the attribute case fixed; one older gap closed at its source

**V5.14.** (LOW, older than this commit) The `$partial` helper drew any template with the values given, the layout too, whose `body`
is printed as it is: `$partial('layout', ['body' => $row['name']])` passed both lints. The helper now refuses the layout (only
`View::page()` draws it; `UiTemplatesTest::testThePartialHelperNeverDrawsTheLayout`, red first), and `$head`'s raw parts may not use
`$partial` at all (none did).

### The seventh Codex review (on `17d47d5`; `runs/ui5_codex_review7.txt`): `$partial` fixed, no other helper route; the echo lint read whole

**V5.15.** (LOW, older than this commit) The echo lint (`UiTemplatesTest::onlyHelperCalls`) read an echo by its characters, so brackets
in a comment could make a raw value look like part of a helper call (`<?= $e(/* ( */'') . $row['name'] // ) ?>`). It now reads the
echo's PHP tokens (comments and whitespace dropped; the text of a double-quoted string never counts as a bracket) and wants every term
to be one whole helper call ending at depth 0; the raw-part checker got the same end check (a term left open is refused). Codex's case,
an interpolated bracket and an unclosed call are in the lint's own test; every echo of every template still passes.

### The eighth Codex review (on `92cd9fd`; `runs/ui5_codex_review8.txt`): V5.15 fixed; one NEW gap it opened, closed

**V5.16.** (LOW, NEW in V5.15) The echoes were still cut out with a regex up to the first `?>`, also one inside a block comment (which
PHP does not end there), and the tokenized lint then dropped the unfinished comment: `<?= $e('') /* ?> */ . $row['name'] ?>` passed.
Every `<?= ... ?>` and `<?php ... ?>` block is now read with PHP's own tokenizer, up to the closing tag PHP itself ends it with
(`UiTemplatesTest::blocks()`, `echoes()`, `phpBlocks()`); Codex's template is in the lint's own test.

### The ninth Codex review (on `ebc6f9f`; `runs/ui5_codex_review9.txt`): its older LOW, closed after the merge (branch `lint-helper-calls`)

**V5.17.** (LOW, older than design v5) The echo lint trusts a helper by its variable's name, so a template that rebinds one prints what
it likes: `<?php $e = static fn ($v) => $v; ?><?= $e($row['name']) ?>` passed every template lint and printed a raw value. In a
template's code a helper variable is now only ever called (`$e(`), read with PHP's tokenizer (`UiTemplatesTest::helperMisuse()`,
`testAHelperIsOnlyEverCalled`, red first: main's lints accepted all 56 cases). Every other use is refused: an assignment of any kind,
a `foreach`, `catch` or parameter variable, `&$e`, destructuring, `global`/`static`, a closure's `use`, `unset`, a by-reference
argument. So is what writes a variable by its name: `extract()`, also through `call_user_func(_array)` or a name PHP folds from
literals (`('ext' . 'ract')(...)`; PHP itself refuses it through a variable), `$$x` and `${'e'}`. One template wrote a helper:
reasons.php looped `foreach ($uses as $u)` over the `$u` URL helper (nothing called `$u` after the loop); the loop variable is `$use`.
Codex's review of this change (`runs/lintgap_codex_review.txt`) found a route that replaces what a helper runs instead of rebinding it:
`<?php namespace CW\Ui; function htmlspecialchars($v, ...$o) { return $v; } ?><?= $e($row['name']) ?>` printed `<b>RAW</b>` (Html::e's
unqualified `htmlspecialchars()` resolves in CW\Ui first), and `define('CW\Ui\ENT_QUOTES', 0)` left quotes unescaped. A template now
declares nothing: no namespace, named function, class, interface, trait or enum, no `define()` or `class_alias()` (none did). Its false
positive, `if ($ok) ($x = 1);` read as a call of a computed name, is fixed: a `)` that closes a control structure's condition is no
callee. Both red first (`runs/lintgap_red2.log`, `lintgap_red2_cases.txt`). Its second review (`runs/lintgap_codex_review2.txt`) found
both fixed and no other way to rebind or replace a helper; two false positives it named are fixed too (red first,
`runs/lintgap_red3.log`): a closure returning by reference (`function &() { ... }`: PHP gives that `&` its own token) and an anonymous
class with a modifier or an attribute (`new readonly class { }`) declare no name; only `class` followed by a name is a declaration.
Known, outside this lint and left for a follow-up: the code lint refuses functions by name only, so a function reached through a string
variable (`$f = 'sys' . 'tem'; $f(...)`) or an output-buffer callback (`ob_start(fn ($b) => html_entity_decode($b))` with
`ob_end_flush()`, which prints a raw value) passes; an allowlist of the plain functions templates call would close both.

## How long a person stays signed in (worktree `staff-session-limits`, 20 Oct 2026; SL1-SL5)

The owner, 20 Oct 2026: "we face session time out easily, once logged in don't time out". A session ended after 30 minutes without a page
or 12 hours after signing in (U2), both fixed in `Auth\Sessions`, and its cookie had no lifetime, so closing the browser signed the person
out too. The limits are now settings; nothing changes until someone raises them.

**SL1. Two settings (0047).** `session.idle_minutes` (int, baseline 30; `Settings::RULES` 30 to 43,200 = 30 days) and
`session.absolute_hours` (int, baseline 12; 12 to 2,160 = 90 days), both provisional, with their `config_change` baselines (dev.md rule 5).
The shortest each may be is the limit of before: a setting can only make sessions longer. They are changed on the Settings page (topic
Staff) with a reason, like every other setting; this change sets no value on any server. An idle limit longer than the absolute one is
allowed and simply never decides (the absolute limit ends the session first).

**SL2. Read once per request; a bad value is the limit of before.** `Sessions::limits()` reads both in one statement, once per instance;
the kernel makes one `Sessions` per request and hands it to the controllers (`Ui\Context::sessions()`: the sign-in, the password change,
the finished set-up, the Users page's devices and its actions through `Staff\StaffAdmin`, the end of a set-up through `Staff\Enrolment`),
so a request sees one set (a tool on the server, `bin/reset_staff.php`, makes its own). A setting that is missing (a schema before 0047), not a whole
number, or outside its rule (only SQL could store one) reads as its default (`IDLE_SECONDS` = 1800, `ABSOLUTE_SECONDS` = 43200), each
on its own. `Sessions::liveSql()` is the one condition of a live session: `resolve()`, `revokeAll()` (what "signed out N devices" counts)
and `Staff\StaffSessions::live()` (Settings > Users, signed-in devices) all use it. A change applies to the next request of everyone
signed in: a session idle or old beyond a lowered limit ends at its next page, one within a raised limit carries on.

**SL3. The cookie lives as long as the absolute limit.** The session cookie (`HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ui`, `Secure` over HTTPS,
as U2) now carries `Max-Age` = the absolute limit in seconds at sign-in, at a password change and at the end of a set-up
(`AuthController::withSession`), so closing the browser does not sign the person out. The server still decides: either limit, signing
out (POST, revokes the row, `Max-Age=0`), a password change (every session revoked, this browser gets a new one), an admin's sign-out,
switching the account off, and the kernel clears a cookie that resolves to nobody on whatever it answers next (a public page too,
unless the answer sets a new one: `Kernel::dispatch`). Nothing about session fixation
changed: every sign-in makes a new random token and revokes the one the browser brought. A raised absolute limit reaches a cookie at the
person's next sign-in (the browser keeps the Max-Age it was given); cookies issued before this change have no Max-Age and still end
with the browser.

**SL4. Words.** `Words::UI['signed_out']` names no number ("you were away for too long, your sign-in reached its time limit, or your
password changed"), true for any setting. The two settings have a name and a help text under Staff (`SETTING_TOPIC['session']`); the
help gives the day and the week in the unit of the setting and never repeats the value (rule 20), and says that on a shared computer a
person should sign out themselves.

**SL5. What a longer session costs.** A copied cookie, or an unattended shared computer, stays signed in for as long as the settings
allow. What stays in place: the cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, the CSRF token is bound to the session, Settings > Users lists
every signed-in device with an admin's "sign out", a password change signs out everywhere, and the sign-in still needs the password and
the code. There is no "signed in until" column on the Users page (it lists when each device signed in and was last active); none was
added.

### The Codex review (on `5dbba5b`, the same patch as `37ed1fe` rebased onto main `f471402`; `runs/sessions_codex_review1.txt`): two findings, both fixed test-first

No serious security or expiry defect. Both tests failed first (`runs/sessions1_review1_red.log`) and pass now.

**SL6. Finding 1 (MEDIUM): some requests read the limits twice.** `StaffAdmin` (an admin's sign-out, the resets, switching an account
off) and `Enrolment` (the end of a set-up) made their own `Sessions`, so such a request read the limits a second time: a change made
between the two reads could count a live session under one value and judge it under another (the "signed out N devices" notice and its
audit row). Both take the request's `Sessions` now (an optional last constructor argument; `PeopleController` and `AuthController` pass
`$ctx->sessions()`). `SessionLimitsTest::testTheLimitsAreReadOncePerRequestWhateverTheRequestDoes` counts the reads of a request
(`HookedStatement` on the kernel's own connection): one for a page, a sign-in (with and without a live cookie), signing someone out
everywhere, a reset, switching an account off, a password change and the end of a set-up; none for a page without a cookie.

**SL7. Finding 2 (LOW): a public page left an ended cookie behind.** Only the pages that need a session cleared a cookie that resolved
to nobody; the sign-in page opened after the session ended (or a failed sign-in) left it, and with Max-Age it now outlives the browser.
`Kernel::dispatch` clears it on every answer that sets no session cookie of its own (a successful sign-in sets only the new one); the
protected branch no longer clears it itself. Server-side revocation was never bypassed. `testAnEndedCookieIsClearedOnThePublicPagesToo`.

**SL8. A failure page clears an ended cookie too (the second review's low finding, on `902a281`; `runs/sessions1_codex_review.txt`).**
SL7 cleared it only on the answers `dispatch()` returns; a 500 or 503 after the cookie was checked (a sign-in whose database work
failed) left it in the browser (it gave no access). `Kernel::handle()` now clears a cookie that resolved to nobody on whatever it answers,
a failure page included, unless the answer sets a session cookie of its own; a cookie the request never got to check (a 404, a failure
before or while it was checked) is left alone, since it may be live.
`SessionLimitsTest::testAFailurePageClearsAnEndedCookieButNeverALiveOne` (red first: `runs/sessions2_red_kept.log`).

## 2-step verification switched off for a while (branch `staff-session-limits`, 20 Oct 2026; TF1-TF6)

The owner's decision of 20 Oct 2026: "turn 2-step verification off temporarily, I will tell you when to turn it back on". We advised
against it; the owner chose it. What was built is a switch with an end: it cannot be left off by forgetting it.

**TF1. One setting, a UK time (0048).** `auth.totp_off_until` (string, baseline empty, provisional; topic Staff on the Settings page,
changed like every setting: settings.manage, a reason, a version, an audit row). It holds a UK time as typed, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`
(`Auth\SecondStep`). The request was for a UTC time; it is a UK time because the screens never show UTC (dev.md rule 10) and a person
types the time on the clock: a UTC value typed as a UK time in summer would keep the code off an hour longer than meant. CW turns it into
one moment (`SecondStep::moment`, `Arrivals\UkTime`) and compares moments.

**TF2. The bound, and failing closed.** `Settings::RULES` (`pattern`, `uk_time`, `ahead_max_days` 90) refuses, when it is saved, a time
more than 90 days ahead, one not in that form or not real, and one that happens twice or not at all that day in the UK (the hours the
clocks change); a time already past is allowed and simply means "on". `SecondStep::offUntil()` reads it fresh on every call and asks
for the code (returns null) when the value is empty, past, unreadable, not a text, more than 90 days ahead (only SQL could store
that), or missing (a schema before 0048).

**TF3. The sign-in without the code.** `Auth\Login`: the throttle and its named locks, the password check, an active account and a
sign-in that is set up (a sign-up sheet's account never signs in at /ui/login, whatever its password) stay as they are; then, while the
switch is on (`SecondStep::offUntil`, read inside the locks), the 6-digit step is skipped and a code sent anyway is ignored
(`Login::withoutCode`): the old cookie's session revoked, a new session (`Sessions::create` sets `mfa_at`, which a live session needs),
a successful `login_attempt` (step `password`; it resets the account's failures like any completed sign-in), `last_login_at`, and audit
`login.ok` with `without_code: true`, `code_off_until` and the note "signed in without the 2-step code: switched off until … (UK
time)". `staff_session` has no field for it, so none is written there (the audit row and the session's id prefix tie them). A one-time
password still leads to choosing a new one first; a "new sign-in code" waiting (an admin's reset) does not block the sign-in, and its
set-up waits for the code to be back. /ui/enrol and /ui/new-code still need a code (setting up is still offered). Sessions, their limits,
signing out, a password change and every revocation are unchanged.

**TF4. The sign-in page.** While it is on, the form has no code field and says one line: "2-step verification is switched off until 27
Oct 2026, 18:00. Sign in with your e-mail and password." (`Words::SIGN_IN['code_off']`, the moment in UK time). A failed sign-in says
"Check your e-mail and password" without the words about codes (`failed_no_code`).

**TF5. The warnings.** On the Dashboard, the people who can switch it back on (settings.manage: Admins and Reviewers) see the card
"2-step verification is OFF until …" first (`HomeTasks` `code_off`, rank 3, tone blocked), which opens the setting; Settings › System
(the settings list) shows the same warning at the top to everyone who opens it. Both go by themselves at the time.

**TF6. What it costs, and what is left as it is.** While it is on, a password alone signs in: a leaked or guessed password is enough,
within the throttle (10 failures an account, 30 an address, in 15 minutes). A session made while it was on keeps going after it ends,
up to its own limits (SL1; with raised limits that can be long): to end them at once, an admin signs people out on Users ("Sign them out
everywhere"). Ending sessions made without the code when the switch ends was not built (the request kept everything else as it is); it
would need a mark on the session row.

### The Codex review of the switch (on `43bb353`; `runs/sessions2_codex_review.txt`): three findings, all fixed; the two races shown by a test first

The reviewer found no other serious defect: the ordinary path keeps the password, account and throttle checks, every sign-in without the
code leaves its audit row, the UK times that happen twice or not at all are refused, the permission is checked on the server, and the
baseline follows rule 5. Both race tests failed on `43bb353` (`runs/sessions2_review1_red.log`) and pass now.

**TF7. Finding 1 (HIGH): a password reset between the password check and the new session.** The password was checked on a read
without locks; the limiter's named locks do not stop an admin's reset. A reset (or the account switched off) that committed between the
check and the session left a live session made with the old password. Both ways of signing in now hold the account's row lock (`SELECT
... FOR UPDATE`, the lock the resets and switching an account off take) from a check that it is still the account that was verified
(`Login::unchanged`: the same password hash, the same secret and state, active) to the session and its audit row, in one transaction;
a reset that waits for it then ends that session with the others. The sign-in with the code had the same race on main (a session after a
reset, with the old password and a valid code); it is closed too. `TotpOffTest::testAResetOrSwitchOffBetweenThePasswordCheckAndTheSessionWins`
and `...TheCodeCheckAndTheSessionWins` step in with `HookedStatement`.

**TF8. Finding 2 (MEDIUM): a sign-in that waited could cross the end of the switch.** The switch was read once, before the writes. In
the same transaction, after the row lock, it is now read again with `FOR SHARE` (`SecondStep::offUntil($db, null, true)`): a change made
before is seen, a change made after waits for the sign-in. If it ended or was emptied meanwhile, everything the sign-in wrote is rolled
back and it is refused as a sign-in without the code it now needs. `testTheSwitchEndingWhileASignInIsUnderWayAsksForTheCode`.

**TF9. Finding 3 (LOW): words that promised the code.** The idle limit's help said "They sign in again with their password and code";
it says "and signs in again". The sign-in page's own sentence while the switch is on is "Use your e-mail and your password"
(`PAGE_INTRO['login_no_code']`).

### The second Codex review of the switch (on `e367271`, rebased onto `0a32e63`; `runs/sessions3_codex_review.txt`): four findings, all fixed test-first

Each test failed on `e367271` (`runs/sessions2_review2_red_kept.log`) and passes now; no other serious issue was found (cookie handling,
audit, throttle, replay guard, UK times, the bound, permissions, grants, the baseline).

**TF10. Finding 2 (HIGH, older than the switch): the hand-off to a "new sign-in code" step had no lock.** For an account with a new
sign-in code waiting, the step (the rotate-and-confirm page, `Enrolment::beginFromLogin`) was started after checks made without locks: a
password set or a sheet replaced on the server in between still started a step with what was replaced, and the step then gave a session.
The hand-off now runs in the transaction and under the account's row lock of TF7 (`Login::unchanged`).
`testANewSignInCodeHandOffAfterTheAccountChangedIsRefused`.

**TF11. Finding 1 (HIGH): a password change left a waiting step behind.** With the switch on, an account with a new sign-in code waiting
can hold a session (TF3); someone who knew the old password and the sheet's code could start the code's step later, and confirm it after
the person changed the password, getting a session without the new password. `Login::changePassword` now ends a waiting step in the
same statement (`StaffAdmin::CLEAR_NEXT`). If that step had already taken the sheet's secret, the person asks an admin for a new
sign-in code once the code is back. `testAPasswordChangeEndsAWaitingNewSignInCodeStep`.

**TF12. Finding 3 (MEDIUM): time passes while a sign-in waits for a lock.** The share lock of TF8 stops changes of the setting, not the
clock: the session without the code is now made by one statement that also checks the database's clock is still before the end
(`Sessions::createBefore`: `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOW(6) < ?`); after the end, everything is rolled back and the code is asked for.

**TF13. Finding 4 (LOW): the locks in the order of a settings change.** The sign-in without the code held the account's row and waited
for the setting's row, while a settings change by the same person holds the setting's row and then the person's (the history's foreign
key): a deadlock (retried, but avoidable). The sign-in now locks the setting's row first, then the account's. The test checks the order of
the two reads (`testASessionWithoutTheCodeIsMadeOnlyBeforeTheEndByTheDatabaseClockAndTheLocksKeepTheirOrder`, which also proves
`createBefore` on both sides of the end); a two-process deadlock test was not written.

### The third Codex review of the switch (on `737b3f1`; `runs/sessions4_codex_review.txt`): TF10-TF13 close their races; one older race, fixed

**TF14. (HIGH, older than the switch) A password change that waited could undo a reset.** `Login::changePassword` checked the current
password, let the limiter's locks go, then wrote the new password and a new session unconditionally: a reset by an admin, another
change, or a sign-out of the session it came from, made in between, was overwritten (the waiting request got a fresh session). Signing in
without the code makes that first session easy to get, so it is closed here. The write now runs only if, under the account's row lock,
the stored password is still the one checked, the account is active and the session the change came from is still live (its row locked
too, in the order of the resets: the account, then its sessions); otherwise nothing is written and the answer is `wrong_current`.
`testAPasswordChangeThatWaitedDoesNotUndoWhatHappenedMeanwhile` (red first: `runs/sessions2_review3_red_kept.log`).

### The fourth Codex review of the switch (on `7c72a37`; `runs/sessions5_codex_review.txt`): no high or medium finding

TF10-TF14 close the reported races; no password bypass, lock-order cycle, missing grant of the app login, unaudited sign-in without the
code or cookie regression was found.

**TF15. (LOW) Words that promised the code.** The Users pages said "They can sign in again straight away with their password and code"
(Sign them out everywhere) and "They sign in with their own password and the code on their phone" (switching an account back on); both
now say "as usual", true either way. Left as the reviewer noted them, not built: a test that expires the switch inside a whole sign-in
(TF12 is tested on `Sessions::createBefore` itself and on the order of the locks), and tests with two processes really blocked on each
other's locks (the races are tested by stepping in between the statements with `HookedStatement`).

## The decide guard: what the pages only hid is refused by the service (worktree `mapping-decide-guard-2`, 20 Oct 2026; DG1-DG5)

Staff will drive CW with their own Claude in Chrome, which may send a form straight to the server. Three rules of the matching pages
were kept only by the page not drawing a form (the staff Claude guide, section 8; a Codex review of the quick-pick branch): a spot
check's match was the owner's on the page (U47, U64, U71: "the service still takes such a POST, as before"), a variant held back (M30),
a spot check's match and a variant found on arrival (M64) were decided one at a time on their own page while no other page offered them
(OneAtATime, M63; By Item's quick match, docs/dev.md "The quick match", hides its "Match to …" for them), and "No, wrong product" sent twice was recorded twice
(the decide form has no one-time key, and a reject does not move map_version). Numbered DG (not M67: the stopped branch
`mapping-arrival-2b` uses that number). Code: `src/Mapping/{DecisionService,KeySample,OneAtATime,BulkDecisions}.php`,
`src/Ui/Controller/{ReviewController,DuplicatesController}.php`, `src/Ui/views/{listing_form,listing_decide}.php`, `src/Ui/Words.php`.
Tests: new cases in `tests/Integration/Mapping/{KeyBulkTest,KeyBulkHoldTest,DecisionServiceTest}.php`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/{KeySampleScreenTest,OneAtATimeScreenTest,BehaviourItemsTest}.php` and `tests/Unit/WordsTest.php`.

**DG1. A spot check's match is its owner's in the service (amends U47, U64, U71).** `DecisionService::run`, inside the decision's
transaction and right after the listing's lock, asks `KeySample::keeping()` for a person's decision (every action but the system's
`suggest`, every caller: the variant's page, a direct POST, the quick match, a ticked list, Duplicates, the tools): is the listing one of
the matches (with a position) of a spot check that has not failed? Then only its owner (`key_sample.created_by`) decides it; anyone else
gets **403 `spot_check_other`** with the listing, the spot check, its owner and `done` (answered already), and nothing is written.
- "Open" is "not failed": while a spot check waits, each match is still to answer or confirmed by its owner, and any other person's
  decision fails it for good (`confirmed_by_other`, `decided_otherwise`, `changed_since`). A complete spot check keeps its confirmed
  matches too (a change would fail it after all). A failed one keeps nothing: there is nothing more to lose, and its matches are still
  one at a time on the screens (DG2). Neither does one whose owner can no longer answer it (switched off, or without a matching lead's
  job): no confirmation of theirs would count, so it can never be completed, and its matches would be stuck, decidable by nobody (the
  page still shows others no form there; a lead can now decide such a match). A listing that is a match of two spot checks (the older
  failed when its suggestion was replaced) is kept by the newest that keeps it.
- A decision that waits for a second person is applied (`approve()`, under the listing's lock) only with the owner as its decider or
  its approver. The owner's own change of a confirmed match (a relink with 2 per sale, say) is the owner's decision, and the two-person
  rule wants another lead's second OK: it applies, and the spot check fails (the page warns the owner first, U71). Such a waiting change
  names no suggestion, so the spot check has not failed while it waits. A change asked for by two other people is refused.
- A merge moves every listing of the item it joins away (M31), named or not: `merge()` asks the same for each listing it moves, with
  the decider (or, for a pending merge, the approver and the decider) as the people one of whom must be the owner. The Duplicates page
  shows `DUP_ERROR['spot_check_other']`.
- `BulkDecisions` already skips a spot check's matches before a row is sent (OneAtATime); a spot check drawn between that check and the
  row's decision now ends as the same skip (`in_spot_check`, with the spot check's name), not as "refused".
- The page is unchanged: it already showed anyone else no form (U47, U71). The words: `MATCH_ERROR['spot_check_other']` ("Not saved:
  <owner> is checking this one in a spot check. A decision by anyone else would fail the spot check.") and `spot_check_other_done`
  for an answered one.

**DG2. A variant decided one at a time is decided from its own page as it is now (amends M30 "the screens", M63, M64).**
`OneAtATime::seen()` says what a variant's page shows of it, by `of()`'s rule and order: `held:<hold id>`, `in_spot_check:<spot check
id>`, `on_arrival:<suggestion id>`, or nothing. The review page puts it into every decision form it draws (the answers, the quick yes,
the spot check's yes and its "Not a match", "Change this match"; a hidden `seen`, drawn only when there is something to say), and the
decide route always sends it (empty: the page showed none). `DecisionService` reads `seen()` again under the listing's lock: when the
variant is one of these now and the form names anything else, **409 `one_at_a_time`**, nothing written, and the page is drawn again as
it is now (with the hold's note, the spot check's box or the check on arrival's clue), so the next send is the page's own.
- What it stops: a form made by hand or by a script, another page's button (By Item's "Match to …" sends the decision's fields and
  its way back, no `seen`; a fold drawn before the variant became one of these still has the button), a made-up value, a page drawn before the variant was set aside (a hold does not move
  map_version, so nothing else noticed: the person never saw the note), a hold released and written again since (another hold id).
- What it keeps: a hold does not stop a person's decision (M30): anyone who may decide answers a held variant on its page, as before.
  The spot check's owner answers its matches on the variant's page as before. Only the decide route sends `seen`: the service's other
  callers keep their own rules (BulkDecisions skips these variants itself, the bulk confirm leaves a held listing out by its
  eligibility and refuses `held_meanwhile`, the tools are the leads').
- Why a field and not a refusal of the kinds: the rule is "on its own page", and only the page can say it was there. `seen` is checked
  like `expected_map_version` and `proposal_id` (design I7: what the person saw); it is not a secret (a person can copy it), it stops the
  accidental paths. `MATCH_ERROR['one_at_a_time']`: "Not saved: this website product is decided one at a time, on its own page. The page
  now shows why. Read it, then answer again."

**DG3. The same "No, wrong product" twice is recorded once.** A reject does not move map_version, so a double click (or a script that
sends again) wrote a second decision and audit row. Now, under the listing's lock, a person's reject that is exactly the listing's
latest decision again (same person, same item, same suggestion, same note, the same map_version as that decision, not in a ticked
list's batch) writes nothing and answers as the first did (the same decision id, `repeated`); the screen shows the same page and
notice, so a double click is no error. That holds too when the first send settled the suggestion it named (a merge suggestion's
"different products", M34): the replay answers before the suggestion is called closed; anything else naming it is still 409
`proposal_closed`. Chosen over
a refusal because the person did nothing wrong (the browser shows the second answer: "Not saved" would say the first failed) and
over a one-time key because the form has none and the rest of the decide form needs none (every other answer moves map_version, so a
second send is refused as stale). Anything else is still a new answer, recorded as before: another person's "No", another note, another
item, a ticked list's, or the same once something else was decided on the listing since.

**DG4. The other POST routes under /ui/review, checked.**
- `decision/{id}/approve` and `/withdraw`: an approval re-asks DG1 under the listing's lock (the owner as decider or approver), for the
  listing and for every listing a merge moves (DG1 above). A pending decision that names a spot check's suggestion has failed it already
  (`waiting_second`); one that names none (a change of a confirmed match) has not, which is why the approval asks. A withdrawal changes
  no link. Seen in passing, not changed: withdrawing a waiting decision that named a match's suggestion puts that match back to "to
  answer" (KeySample reads only `pending_second` rows), so a spot check failed by such a decision is waiting again.
- `bulk` (the lists, Store Products, New Variants) and `products/bulk/apply` (By Item): every row through `BulkDecisions`, which skips
  held back, a spot check's matches and the check on arrival's before and under the row's lock (M63, M64); the preview saves nothing. No
  gap; DG1's mapping above for the race.
- `duplicates/{id}/decide` and `/split`: lead only, a one-time `form_key`; every request through `DecisionService` (DG1, including
  the listings a merge moves). A split moves back only listings the merge moved, which a spot check drawn later cannot have confirmed.
- `/ui/items/barcodes/{id}/decide` (not under /ui/review): barcode rulings, no listing's link; a one-time `form_key`. No gap.
- Left open: **a matched variant (U69, behaviour item 13)**. The page shows a Matcher no form on a matched variant ("Ask a matching lead
  to change it"), and the route and the service still take a Matcher's unlink or relink, as U69 recorded on purpose. Not a one-at-a-time
  rule and not a spot check: a policy for the owner (a 403 for a Matcher's change of a match would also apply to every other caller).

**DG5. Tests.** Red first (`runs/decideguard2_red1.log` to `red4.log`; red4 on the quick-pick code, 0a32e63): another lead's and a Matcher's answer to a
spot check's match were saved, a held variant's bare form was saved, a merge moved a confirmed match, the same "No" was written twice.
Green after the change. `KeyBulkTest::testOnlyTheOwnerDecidesASpotChecksMatchWhileItIsOpen` (every answer by another lead and a
Matcher, open and answered, then after the failure), `testAMergeThatMovesAnOpenSpotChecksConfirmedMatchIsTheOwnersAlone`;
`KeyBulkHoldTest::testAPageDecisionOnAHeldListingNeedsTheHoldThePageShowed` (none, made up, a type, released and held again; not held;
not a page); `DecisionServiceTest::testTheSameNoTwiceIsRecordedOnce`; `KeySampleScreenTest::testAnAnswerToAnotherLeadsSpotCheckIsRefusedWhateverItCarries`
(the owner's own form posted by others, the owner's hand-made form, the owner's page form: saved; after the failure) and
`testAHeldVariantIsDecidedOnlyFromItsOwnPage` (a script, By Item's quick match fields, a made-up note, a page drawn before the hold, the
page's own form by a Matcher, a variant not held); `OneAtATimeScreenTest` (a variant found on arrival: the page's form carries
`on_arrival:<id>`, a form without it is refused, the page's is saved); `BehaviourItemsTest::testASecondNoWrongProductForTheSameProductSavesNothingMore`;
`ByProductScreenTest::testAStaleMatchButtonOnAnotherLeadsSpotCheckOrAHeldVariantIsRefusedOnTheVariantsPage` (a fold drawn before
the spot check and the hold: another lead's and a Matcher's button 403, the owner's and a held variant's 409, each on the variant's page
with its words and the way back; the page's own form and a free variant's button saved); `WordsTest` (the new codes have words; `plain()` names the owner, or the job when no name is known).

### The first Codex review (on `3707add`; `runs/decideguard2_codex_review.txt`): no HIGH, two MEDIUM and one LOW, fixed test-first

Each new test failed first (`runs/decideguard2_r1_red.log`) and passes now.
- **MEDIUM: a new answer after the listing changed was taken for a repeat.** `sameNoAgain()` did not compare map_version: a "No"
  after the website changed the variant's identity (map_version moved on; the person looked again) wrote nothing. It now needs the
  first reject's `expected_map_version` (`DecisionServiceTest::testTheSameNoTwiceIsRecordedOnce`, its end).
- **MEDIUM: the same "No" to a merge suggestion was refused.** Its first send settles the suggestion, so the replay hit 409
  `proposal_closed` before DG3. The replay is now recognised there (`testTheSameNoTwiceToAMergeSuggestionAnswersAsTheFirst`).
- **LOW: DG1's edges were not pinned.** `KeyBulkTest::testACompleteSpotChecksConfirmedMatchesStayTheOwners`, and in
  `testAMergeThatMovesAnOpenSpotChecksConfirmedMatchIsTheOwnersAlone` a Matcher's pending merge refused at another lead's approval and
  applied at the owner's. The bulk race (a spot check drawn between a list's checks and the row's decision) is pinned in the second
  round's tests, below.
- Found while fixing: a spot check whose owner can no longer answer it kept its matches for nobody
  (`testASpotCheckWhoseOwnerCanNoLongerAnswerItKeepsNothing`; DG1 above).

### The second Codex review (on `c864fb5`; `runs/decideguard2_codex_review2.txt`): no HIGH or MEDIUM, one LOW, pinned

The first round's fixes were found present and correct. **LOW: the "under the listing's lock" of DG2 was not pinned** (the tests would
pass with `seen()` read before the lock). Two tests force the overlap with a second session and a worker process (`OpWorkers`, as
`testAHoldThatCommitsWhileTheBulkIsLinkingItsListingWins`): `KeyBulkHoldTest::testAHoldThatCommitsWhileAPageDecisionWaitsForTheListingIsSeen`
(a hold commits while a page decision waits for the listing: 409 `one_at_a_time`, nothing written) and
`testASpotCheckDrawnWhileATickedBatchRunsSkipsItsMatch` (a spot check drawn while a ticked batch's row waits: skipped `in_spot_check`
with its name, nothing decided). Both pass, and both fail on a copy with the read moved before the lock and with BulkDecisions' mapping
removed (`runs/decideguard2_mut1.log`).

### The third Codex review (on `0c6ce17`; `runs/decideguard2_codex_review3.txt`): no HIGH, one MEDIUM and one LOW, fixed test-first

- **MEDIUM: an approval did not ask DG1.** A change of a confirmed match that waits for a second person names no suggestion, so
  KeySample does not count it and the spot check still keeps the match; `approve()` did not ask who the owner is, so a change asked
  for by someone else (made while the owner could not answer, or before this guard) could be approved by any other lead. It now asks

### The fourth Codex review (on `8e044a0`; `runs/decideguard2_codex_review4.txt`): no HIGH or MEDIUM, two LOW

- **LOW: the spot check owner's forms behind their warnings were not sent as drawn.** `KeySampleScreenTest::testAnAnswerToAnotherLeadsSpotCheckIsRefusedWhateverItCarries`
  now sends the owner's own "Change this match" and "Not a match" forms as the page draws them (each carries `seen`); it fails on a
