## Check & match on the lists: a clean likely match found on arrival is answered from the list (branch `list-quick-match`, 21 Oct 2026; CM1-CM4)

The owner, on Store Products ("Electrofag: website products"), on a row found by the check on arrival with "Likely match – check it"
and CW-003906 suggested (20 Oct 2026): "why can't we add a match button here so no need to go inside the page. makes it easier to map".
Production maps with the check on arrival and no AI (M63, M64), so about 3,300 Electrofag and 3,200 Vape Big Likely rows are such rows,
and each had to be opened on its own page (DG2). The owner chose the scope "Clean Likely only". Numbered CM (Check & match): DG, TF, SL
and M1-M67 are taken. Code: `src/Ui/Controller/{ReviewController,StoreProductsController}.php`, `src/Ui/StoreContext.php`,
`src/Ui/views/{check_fold,listing_check,queue,store_products}.php`, `src/Mapping/DecisionService.php` (decide()'s `recheck`), `src/Ui/Words.php`
(`CHECK`, `MATCH_ERROR['check_changed']`), `public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`. Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/CheckMatchScreenTest.php`,
`tests/Unit/{UiUnitTest,UiTemplatesTest,WordsTest}.php`.

**CM1. The fold (amends M63, M64 and DG2).** On To review's Likely list and on Store Products, a row that waits for its match, found by the
check on arrival (`OneAtATime::of()` says `on_arrival`: not held back, not a spot check's match), whose open suggestion is a Likely match
(`Check`) of an item, has "Check & match" under its line, for someone who may decide (`ReviewController::foldOffered`). It is a
`<details>` that opens in place, like By Item's quick match: app.js fetches `GET /ui/review/listing/{id}/check` (read only,
`mapping.decide`), parses it inert and shows it only when its root carries `data-lc-fragment`; anything else shows `CHECK['failed']`
beside the variant page's link, which is also all the fold offers without app.js. Nothing is computed for the list's 50 rows: whether a
row is clean is the fragment's answer, asked when it opens (`foldFacts()`). The fragment shows the website variant against the warehouse
item side by side (names; Compare::rows' brand, strength, nicotine type, range, kind, flavour, size, puffs, pack units and barcodes, each
with the variant page's same / different / unknown chip; price; units sold in 30 days and a year, from the sales history as the page
reads them), the strength with its help, the reasons, and every "Watch out" and red "cannot be the same" line. The page's lines and the
fold's come from ONE function (`ReviewController::whyOf()`, taken out of `show()` unchanged), so they cannot disagree.

A row is **clean** when none of `FOLD_BLOCKS` applies: it waits for its match; `OneAtATime::seen()` says `on_arrival`; the band is
`Check` (Conflict says a matching lead decides it); no decision waits for a second OK; the item is not joined into another and nobody
said "not this product" to it for this variant (a "No" keeps the suggestion open, M8); no "Watch out" line of the variant page
(`whyOf()`: watch and cannot) and none of the list row's own (`flagWords()` of its flags: "A detail needs a look" of a match the check
wrote with a warning, which the page has no line for when the item had nothing to compare with); the barcodes are not different (the
same, or not on both); and 1 sale = 1 (`unitsOf()`, as the page offers). A clean row has two plain POST forms of the decide route:
"Yes, match to CW-… (1 sale = 1 product)" (`link`, the item, `units_per_item=1`) and "No, wrong product" (`reject`), each with csrf,
`expected_map_version`, `proposal_id`, `seen` (`OneAtATime::seen`, computed by the fragment), `from=check` and the list's way back
(CM3). Any other row gets the facts, why in words, and "Open to decide" (the variant's page): no form, and no `seen`. The root, the forms
and their buttons carry `data-listing-id`, `data-sku-id`, `data-channel` (and `data-answer`, `data-clean`) for a staff member's own Claude.
Held back and spot-check variants are still decided only on their own page; so is everything not clean.

**CM2. The decide route asks the fold's question again under the lock.** A decision from the fold goes through every check a decision
gets (DecisionService, under the listing's lock: map_version, the suggestion it names, Conflict for a matching lead only, DG1, DG2's
`seen`): a variant held back or put in a spot check after the fold was drawn is refused 409 `one_at_a_time`, a replaced suggestion 409
`proposal_closed`, a Conflict re-band 403 `lead_required` for a Matcher. Then, because `from=check`, `ReviewController::foldRecheck()` runs
inside the same transaction (`DecisionService::decide(..., $recheck)`, after those checks and before anything is written): `foldFacts()`
again, and the answer must be one of the fold's two as drawn (its item, its suggestion, `units_per_item = 1` for a match). Anything else
(a re-band in place for a lead, the barcodes different now, a hand-made `from=check` form with 3 per sale, another item or another
action) is **409 `check_changed`** (`MATCH_ERROR['check_changed']`), nothing is written, and the variant's page is drawn with the words,
to answer there. Without `from=check` the decide route is as it was (a form with the page's `seen` is the page's, DG2).

**CM3. The way back.** To review's fold carries the list's QueueContext and its page (`lp`); Store Products' carries a StoreContext
(`via=store`, a store's code that must name a store, a state and a sort that must be the list's, the search `lq`, the page `lp`: built
like ByProductContext, never a return address). Both carry the next row of the page (`nx`, a number, an anchor only). After a success
the person is back on the same page of the list at `#l-<next row>` (the rows are `id="l-<listing id>"`; the decided row may have left
the list) with the usual notice (a toast, wherever the page is scrolled). A refusal lands on the variant's page with its words; from
Store Products that page has Back to the list and its own forms lead back there too (decide()'s StoreContext redirect, at the row).
To review's variant page without `from=check` still goes on to the next one in the list.

**CM4. Left out on purpose.** New Variants draws the same rows with the same line (one_at_a_time.php) but its rows carry no band and
its way back is another context: no fold there yet. The "may duplicate" box of the variant's page (the barcode on another product) is not
part of the clean rule (the owner's scope); the fold leads to the page for it. The rule is the owner's: no setting.

### The Codex review (on `300657f`; `runs/listmatch_codex_review.txt`): no HIGH, one MEDIUM fixed test-first, two LOW

No bypass of the decide guard found: the recheck runs under the listing's lock before any write, and DG1, DG2, the two-person rule,
Conflict for a lead only, map_version and the suggestion are checked as before.
- **MEDIUM, fixed: on a phone the open fold stayed in the card's name column** (beside Store Products' status chip), with 110 px chips
  in its label column. As a card the open fold's name cell now spans the row (the status chip goes under it), each fact's name is on
  its own line above the two values, and the fold's chips are as narrow as their words (`UiUnitTest::testTheCheckFoldTakesTheWholeCardOnAPhone`,
  red first: `runs/listmatch_r1_red.log`).
- **LOW, fixed because CM3 promises it: Store Products drew no notice**, so a row that left the Suggested filter (or a match that waits
  for a second OK) went without a word. Store Products now shows `ReviewController::notice()` as By Item does (CheckMatchScreenTest:
  the applied, the reject and the pending notice after the redirect).
- **LOW, left open: the fold's same "No" sent twice is 409 `check_changed`**, not DG3's quiet answer: the first "No" is a reject of
  this item, so the second finds the row no longer clean. Nothing is written either way; the variant's page says why.

### A detail that is different is not clean (branch `check-match-differs`, 21 Oct 2026; CM5)

The fold showed the website variant and the warehouse item side by side, each compared detail with its chip, but its clean rule (CM1)
asked only for the barcodes, the warnings, 1 sale = 1, the band and the row's state. So a row could be clean, with "Yes, match to CW-…",
while its Strength or Flavour said "Different". The owner's scope is "clean Likely only".

**CM5. A compared detail that is Different makes the row not clean (amends CM1 and CM2).** A row is clean only when none of the details
the fold draws (Compare::rows' brand, strength, nicotine type, range, kind, flavour, size, puffs and pack size; the barcodes keep their own
reason) is `differs`. The rule reads the very rows the fragment draws (`foldFacts()`'s `compare`), so the chips and the answer cannot
disagree. "Written differently" (`alike`, a brand spelt another way) and "Not stated" (`unknown`, one side does not say) stay fine. The
reason (`FOLD_BLOCKS` `differs`, `CHECK['differs']`) names the details by their names on the fold, in its order: "Some details are
different: Strength (mg), Flavour." The fold then has no form and no `seen`, only "Open to decide". The recheck under the listing's lock
(CM2) is `foldFacts()` again, so a fold drawn clean before the website's (or the item's) details changed to Different is refused 409
`check_changed` for its Yes and its No, and nothing is written. The variant's own page is unchanged: it still decides such a row.
Tests first (`runs/cleanfix_red1.log`, red on `afb6760`): CheckMatchScreenTest `testARowWithADifferentDetailHasNoAnswerAndSaysWhichDetails`,
`testDetailsTheSameWrittenDifferentlyOrNotStatedKeepTheAnswers` (green on the base too: it guards the other side of the rule) and
`testAFoldDrawnBeforeADetailBecameDifferentIsRefusedAndNothingIsSaved`.

## Search and matching for normal staff: one forgiving search, hints, progress (branch `search-match-ux`, 21 Oct 2026; SX1-SX8)

A review as a first-time staff member (`/root/cw_work/SEARCH_MATCH_UX_REVIEW.md`, production looked at read only) found the product
searches of the matching pages each reading the text their own way: the match-strength lists, Store Products and New Variants
searched the WHOLE text as one phrase ("hayati strawberry kiwi" found nothing, "tahiti 20mg" nothing, the CW number printed on every
row nothing), no search forgave "R&M" / "R and M" / "RandM", "Elfbar" / "Elf Bar" or "cw 3906", a barcode was found on a website
product only as the website stored it, and every box said only "Search". Only SAFE-UI changes were built (words, layout, search
forgiveness, hints, counters, keyboard): nothing that is saved, no rule of matching, no POST field, data-* attribute or fragment marker
changed. Code: `src/Ui/SearchText.php` (new), `src/Ui/Queries.php`, `src/Ui/Controller/{Review,StoreProducts,ByProduct,Search}Controller.php`,
`src/Ui/views/{search_note (new),queue,store_products,new_variants,by_product,search,listing,check_fold}.php`, `src/Ui/Words.php`
(`FIND`, `QUEUE` `left_*` `today_*`, `CHECK['next_open']`, `SEARCH['capped']`, `PAGE_INTRO['queue_Check']`), `public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`
(one commented block each). Tests: `tests/Unit/SearchTextTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Mapping/ForgivingSearchTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/SearchHintsScreenTest.php` (new); `CheckMatchScreenTest`, `WordsTest`, `UiTemplatesTest`.

**SX1. One reading of a search (`Ui\SearchText`).** Every product search of the matching pages (Find a product, "Pick a different
product", By Item, its picker and quick match, the match-strength lists, Store Products, New Variants; and through `searchSkus` the item
searches of the stock, purchasing and supplier pages) reads the text the same way: every word must be found, in any order (at most
6); case and accents by the columns' collation (`utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`); slashes, bars, commas and brackets separate words; "20 mg",
"10 ml", "0.8 ohm", "7000 puffs" are one word, and so are "R and M", "R & M"; a lone "and" / "&" and punctuation are no word (such a
text finds nothing, as By Item's already did, U116); a CW number however it is written ("CW-003906", "cw 3906", "CW3906", "#3906", or
a bare number); a code (the whole text, at most 64 characters, as a barcode may be: letters, digits, a space) with the barcode
forms of a number (`Gtin::forms`: with or without its leading zeros).

**SX2. Where it is cheap, the words are forgiving: three kinds, the cheapest asked first.** (1) a short word of letters (at most 4) or a
number: in the text as it is; (2) a longer word of letters: in the text as it is, or in the brand with its spaces and hyphens left out
("elfbar" finds the brand "Elf Bar": a joined word is nearly always a brand, and the brand is short); (3) any other word (typed with a
hyphen or "&", a number and its unit, letters and digits, "R and M"): in the whole text with its spaces and hyphens left out
(`REPLACE(REPLACE(…, ' ', ''), '-', '')`), two short names joined by "and" / "&" in both spellings. Each kind only adds to what the word
found before (a word found as it is is found with the spaces and hyphens left out on both sides: the mapping goes character by
character); the two merges ask for the number and its unit (the two names) together instead of anywhere apart. Measured first with
every word of kind 3 and three REPLACEs (with "&" → "and"): on the profiles of a 29,000-variant store that cost as much as the old
JSON parse of every row's barcodes, and twice the old cost on the 15,000 items; the kinds bring it back (SX8).

**SX3. Codes and CW numbers by their indexes, never in a scan.** The lists' search (`Queries::listingText`, shared by the
match-strength lists, Store Products, New Variants and Find's website products): the option number as typed; a code's barcode forms by
the multi-valued index of 0005 (`JSON_OVERLAPS`, as `barcodeElsewhere`); a CW number ("CW-…", "cw …", or a bare number of up to 6
digits) as the website products matched to that item (`ix_channel_listing_sku_channel`) or with an open suggestion of it
(`ix_match_proposal_open_sku`): looked up BEFORE the statement, of the store the list is of (every store for Find), with no cap, and
named by id; or every word in the product's title, the option's title and the brand. The old `JSON_SEARCH(lp.barcodes, …)` parsed every profile's barcodes in the scan; it is gone
from the lists and from the quick match's whole-text test (the quick match still looks for any PART of a barcode, per word, as before).
A text written as a CW number has no word search. Store Products and New Variants read a search's ids in ONE pass (count and page from
it; two passes before). No schema change.

**SX4. The Likely list's first sentence.** "The AI found a likely product, …" became "The computer found a likely product, …": most of
these rows were found by the check on arrival and say "no AI has looked at it" (production, Electrofag: all 530).

**SX5. Every box says what to type, what it found, and clears the search alone.** A placeholder (`Words::FIND`, at most 40 characters:
"Name, barcode, option or CW number"; By Item and New Variants in their own words, item and variant); while a search is on, under the
toolbar: `12 found for "hayati kiwi".` and **Clear the search** (the store, the state, the sort, the period and the filter stay;
`search_note.php`); an empty result adds "Check the spelling, or use fewer words. You can also type a barcode, an option number or a CW
number." to the page's own empty state (whose "Clear filters" is unchanged); Find says that words can be in any order and that "R&M",
"R and M", "RandM" are the same, and when its 20 / 30 rows are full, "The first 20 are shown. Add a word to see fewer."; "/" puts the
cursor in the page's search box (`data-page-search`, `aria-keyshortcuts="/"`; not while typing in a field, nor with Ctrl, Cmd or Alt;
the variant page's folded "Pick a different product" is opened first).

**SX6. The progress line.** A match-strength list says, under its count, "530 left on this list. You answered 23 today." and so does a
variant's page opened from one (`p.progress-line[data-progress]`): the list's own count in the store (as the strength legend counts it,
not narrowed by a search; `Queries::listLeft` for the page), and the person's decisions since midnight UK time (`Queries::answeredToday`,
one range of `ix_match_decision_decided_by (decided_by, created_at)`; every answer, a ticked list's rows and the ones waiting for a second
OK included). Someone who can only look is told the first sentence only. It counts only the person's own work: a team table or a target
is the owner's call (not built).

**SX7. Check & match is the one filled button of its row, and the next one opens by itself.** On To review's lists a row with Check &
match draws its Open as the plain (secondary) button (Store Products' was already); the words, the link and every data-* stay. After an
answer from the fold CW comes back to the list at the next row (unchanged: `#l-<id>` with `notice` and `prev`); app.js then opens that
row's fold (the same GET a press does; nothing is answered), moves the focus to its heading, and adds "The next one is open below." to
the "Done" notice (`data-opened` on the fold, from `Words::CHECK`). A decision is still one press of Yes or No after reading the fold.

**SX8. Measured** (`tests/perf/search_perf.php`, not committed: the slot's test schema filled like production, 15,000 items and 38,000
website variants of three stores with profiles about as wide as the real ones (120 MB), the old `Queries` of `5e68ee8` and the new one
run in turn in one process, the median of four warm runs, cw-test MySQL 8.4.8; `runs/searchux_perf_ab3.txt`): see the table in the
branch's report; Store Products and New Variants got faster (one pass), the lists' and the item searches stayed within a few ms, Find's
website-product part and the quick match within about a tenth. Still slow, and not for this branch: every search of website products
by words reads the profile of every variant it may find (Find: all 38,000; Store Products: the store's). A narrow, normalised search
column or a FULLTEXT index on the names is a schema change (a table copy of `listing_profile`) and the owner's decision.

**Not changed, on purpose.** DecisionService, the decide route and its guards (DG1-DG5), the Check & match clean rule and its recheck
(CM1-CM5), held back, spot checks and Clues disagree; every POST field; the markers the staff Claude guide reads (`data-check-fold`,
`data-check`, `data-lc-fragment`, `data-qp-fragment`, `data-qp-q`, `data-answer`, `data-clean`, `p.notice[role="status"]`, the rows'
`tr#l-<id>`, `.qp-*`, `.lc-*`). The band names (provisional, U70) and the other NEEDS-OWNER items of the review.

### The Codex review (on `f46d19b`; `runs/searchux_codex_review.txt`): no HIGH, three MEDIUM and one LOW, fixed test-first

Each new test failed first (`runs/searchux_r1_red.log`) and passes now.
- **MEDIUM: a barcode with no digit was no longer found.** A code needed a digit and no space; the old exact `JSON_SEARCH` found any
  barcode as stored, and the intake takes any 64 printable characters. Now the whole text is a code when it is at most 64 characters
  (and UTF-8). `ForgivingSearchTest::testCodexR1AlphabeticBarcodesManySharersAndMergedWordsWithOtherSeparators`.
- **MEDIUM: the 500-id caps of the look-ups were of every store.** 501 variants of another store with the same barcode could hide this
  store's. The look-ups are now of the store the list is of (each by its index, then by primary key), with no cap (the same test).
- **MEDIUM: a merged word lost an exact phrase.** "20 mg" with a no-break space or a bracket between the number and the unit was asked
  as "20mg" only, which `sql()` does not make of "20 (mg)". A merged word keeps what was typed between its parts and is also asked so in
  the text as it is (`SearchText::merged()`, `wordSql()`; the same test and `SearchTextTest`).
- **LOW: someone who can only look had no progress line on a variant's page.** They now get its first sentence, as on the list
  (`SearchHintsScreenTest::testTheProgressLineSaysWhatIsLeftAndWhatIAnsweredToday`).
- Found by the full suite (`runs/searchux_full1_b.log`): `ByProductScreenTest::testTheFragmentReadsTheSpotChecksOfItsRowsInOneGoHoweverManyThereAre`
  counts the quick match's statements for a search by an option number and one by words; with a code looked up for every text of at
  most 64 characters the two send the same statements again (it failed while only a text with a digit was looked up).

## The website products' search by an index (branch `search-index`, on `search-match-ux`, 21 Oct 2026; SI1-SI6)

The owner said yes (21 Oct 2026) to item 1 of the review's NEEDS-OWNER list: make the website-product searches index-fast. Before,
every word search of website products read and compared the text of every profile it might find (SX8: 250-500 ms on the test server
for a 29,000-variant store or Find's 38,000), and SX2 had to choose cheaper, less forgiving comparisons to stay there. Code:
`migrations/0049_search_index.sql`, `src/Ui/Queries.php` (`searchedIds`, `idsIn`, `waitingWords`; `listingText`, `storeProducts`,
`newVariants`, `searchListings`, `waitingListings`), `src/Ui/SearchText.php` (`storedPatterns`, `allStored`). Tests:
`tests/Integration/Migration0049Test.php`, `tests/Integration/Mapping/SearchIndexTest.php` (new); `ForgivingSearchTest` and the
screens' tests unchanged, and green.

**SI1. What was measured, and the choice.** On the slot's test schema filled like production (`tests/perf/index_probe*.php`, not
committed; `runs/searchux_index_probe*.txt`): (a) stored generated columns of the normal text with B-tree indexes, read by a covering
scan of the index (5.5 MB for the names, 12 MB for everything the quick match reads, against the profiles' 120 MB): 15-30 ms for the
scan of 38,000 entries, 40-90 ms with the LIKEs of three words, under load; the ALTER 8-14 s; (b) a FULLTEXT index with the ngram
parser: 33 ms for a rare word but 220-380 ms for a common one ("20mg": 12,700 of 38,000), stopwords to switch off at creation,
one-letter words it cannot find, its boolean operators to escape, and changes seen only after commit; (c) a narrow side table written
by code: the same reads as (a) but kept in step by every writer, and every test's fixture that writes a profile, by hand. (a) is
chosen: MySQL keeps the columns in step itself, LIKE keeps exactly the forgiving search's meaning, and the index read is cheap
whatever the word.

**SI2. The stored text, and why a search still finds everything it found.** `search_names` = the product's title, the option's title
and the brand; `search_all` = those, the website's product number, the web address, the barcodes, the attributes and
the flavour, range and number features (the attributes' JSON without its keys, `REGEXP_REPLACE`: every name and value JSON_SEARCH read,
and none of the keys, which ByProductScreenTest holds); both made normal as `SearchText::norm()` makes a word (spaces and hyphens left out, "&" as
"and"; case and accents by the column's collation, `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`), cut at 760 characters (an index entry's 3,072 bytes).
A word is asked as its normal form, a merged word also as what was typed between its parts made normal (`storedPatterns()`). Every
form the forgiving search asks a word in (SX2's three kinds, both spellings of "&", the merged word as typed) is in the normal text
whenever it is in the text (the mapping goes character by character), so the stored search finds a superset: what SX found and,
since every word is now compared without spaces and hyphens on the whole text, joined words anywhere ("bluerazz", "promax"). A profile
whose stored text is not the whole truth (`search_on_row = 1`, by its index: longer than the column, or a JSON value with an escape in it,
which JSON_SEARCH read decoded and the JSON text writes escaped; none in the test data, a handful at most) is asked as before, on its row.

**SI3. The reads.** `searchedIds()` gives every website product a search finds, as ids, by indexes only: the option number as typed
(`uq_channel_listing_variant`), a code (the barcode index of 0005), a CW number (the item's website products, SX3), every word in the
stored text (one covering scan of `ix_listing_profile_search_names`; for the quick match, the store's waiting variants by the covering
`(channel_id, status)` index, each one's text by a look-up in `ix_listing_profile_search_all (listing_id, search_all)`: its text is
four times as long, and reading only one store's entries is cheaper than scanning every store's, `runs/searchux_comp_probe.txt`), the long
rows on their rows, and for the quick match the variants whose option number holds a word or the start of one (the option number lives in
`channel_listing`; a covering scan of the store's part of `uq_channel_listing_variant`, then each word in the option number joined to
the stored text, as the old joined text had them, also for a variant with no profile). Store Products, New Variants, Find and the quick match then read `cl.id IN (…)` of those ids (written into the
statement as integers this code read: a common word finds thousands) with the units from `ix_listing_profile_units` alone, and Find
its 30 best sellers' rows only. The match-strength lists read their own few thousand rows with the profile anyway, so they ask
`lp.search_names` on the row (with the long rows' old conditions). The quick match's statements are the same for every search (By
Item's statement-count test).

**SI4. In step, and the backfill.** The columns are STORED GENERATED: MySQL computes them with every INSERT and UPDATE of a profile,
whoever writes it (the listing intake and import, `ListingIngestService`; the tools that write features; a test's fixture), and refuses
a statement that writes one (3105). The ALTER's copy computes them for every profile that is there: that is the backfill, in the
migration; no tool. `SearchIndexTest` pins a push that renames a variant (found by the new words at once, no longer by the old) on
every search.

**SI5. The migration.** One statement, `ALGORITHM = COPY, LOCK = SHARED`, as 0027 and 0028 (this server copies the table for any new
column of `listing_profile`): 14 s for 38,000 profiles of 120 MB on the test server; reads go on, a push waits. It runs in
`install_cron.sh --migrate` with the public vhost off (`docs/ops.md`, "The website products' search index"). No grant changes: no new
table, and nobody writes a generated column. `Migration0049Test` holds the file to this and checks the backfill, the old code's
statements on the new schema, the normal text, the cut and the covering reads.

**SI6. Left out.** Items (`sku`): their word search reads 15,000 narrow rows (55-120 ms on the test server, SX8), not the wide
profiles; the same columns there would cost a copy of `sku` (referenced by most tables) for tens of milliseconds, so not now. And the
quick match, in theory: a typed word that runs out of an option number that ends in a letter into the product's title, with no space
between (the old joined text found "a12bmango" for option "A12B" and "Mango"; the option branch asks the starts of a word's leading
digits only).

### The Codex review (on `7307ab1`; `runs/searchix_codex_review.txt`): no HIGH, three MEDIUM and one LOW, fixed test-first

The new test failed first (`runs/searchix_r1_red.log`) and passes now:
`SearchIndexTest::testCodexR1EscapedJsonValuesProfilelessOptionsAmpersandOptionsAndWordsAcrossTheOptionNumber`.
- **MEDIUM: a JSON value with an escape was missed.** JSON_SEARCH read the decoded value ("abc\def", a tab); the stored text has the
  JSON text, which writes them escaped. Such a profile is now flagged too (`search_long` became `search_on_row`: longer than the column,
  or a backslash in the JSON text of its attributes, barcodes or features) and asked on its row as before.
- **MEDIUM: a part of the option number of a variant with no profile was missed** (the option branch joined the profile). It is a LEFT
  JOIN now: the option number alone finds it.
- **MEDIUM: an option number with "&" was missed for "randm"** (the old text kept "&" and asked both spellings). The option number is
  made normal like the stored text ("&" as "and").
- **LOW: a word running from the option number into the title ("27electrofag") was missed.** The option branch now keeps every option
  number that holds a word or ends with the start of its leading digits (option numbers are the websites' numbers of their variants:
  digits; asking every start of every word cost 100-200 ms a search, `runs/searchix_perf2.txt`), and asks each word in the option number
  joined to the stored text, as the old joined text had them. What is left of SI6's exception: a word that runs out of an option
  number ENDING IN A LETTER into the title (no store has such option numbers today).
- Also, before this round (measured, `runs/searchux_comp_probe.txt`): the quick match reads only its store's waiting variants' entries
  (`ix_listing_profile_search_all` is `(listing_id, search_all)`), and New Variants reads a search's ids by the primary key, not the
  period's index.


## Landing pages are not products (branch `landing-pages`, on `search-index`, 22 Oct 2026; LP1-LP12)

The owner (21-22 Oct 2026): "Landing pages are not real products. Even if you see any sale on it, that only means something is broken
and somehow customers were able to add the landing pages to cart. So a proper fix is needed about the landing pages in Central
Warehouse live." A one-off clean-up list was rejected ("won't help in the long run"). The facts, the measure and the open choices:
`/root/cw_work/LANDING_PAGES_DESIGN.md`. In short: a shop keeps a product's landing page (the page where the customer picks 10mg or
20mg) as one more option row (`product_types_and_pricing.prodt_islanding = 1`, nearly always also the default row); the connector
(0.4.6, in the shops' admin trees, not in this repo) pushes every option row, landing rows included, and sends no `website` object;
the shop's `add_cart()` reads the flag but inserts the row before it throws (`Website/config/modules/cart.php:55-69`), and nothing
after the cart checks it. Code: `migrations/0050_landing_pages.sql`, `src/Mapping/LandingRule.php`, `src/Mapping/LandingPages.php`,
`bin/landing_pages.php` (new), `src/Mapping/DecisionService.php`, `src/Mapping/ListingIngestService.php`, `src/Reservations.php`,
`src/Queues/LandingOrders.php` (new), `src/Queues/QueueRules.php`, `src/Schema/Grants.php`, `src/Ops/Alerts.php`,
`src/Ops/AlertDispatch.php`, `src/Ui/Queries.php`, the controllers of Store Products, the variant's page and the stores' queues,
`src/Ui/HomeTasks.php`, `src/Ui/HomeCounts.php`, `src/Ui/Context.php`, `src/Ui/Sections.php`, `src/Ui/Words.php`, the views
`store_products`, `listing`, `queue_landing` (new). Tests: `tests/Unit/LandingRuleTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Migration0050Test.php`,
`tests/Integration/Mapping/LandingPagesTest.php`, `tests/Integration/Stock/LandingOrderTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/UiKernel/LandingPagesScreenTest.php` (new).

**LP1. A kind of its own: `channel_listing.status = 'landing'`** ("Landing page (not a product)"). No item (the CHECK of 0001 holds).
Not `ignored`: the reports and people tell the two apart. 0050 adds the value, the two decisions, the website-bug table and one
setting, and classifies no row. Both altered tables are copied once, said out loud: this server refuses the ENUM change of
`channel_listing` in place (the column is named by a CHECK), and `match_decision`'s replaced CHECK is checked against every row.

**LP2. Two decisions, through DecisionService** (still the only writer of a listing's status), like ignore / unignore (M48).
`landing`: by the SYSTEM (on arrival, or the classifying tool; `decided_by` NULL, the 0050 CHECK allows a system `suggest` or
`landing` only) with why in `match_decision.detail.landing` (`reason` website_flag / same_page / person, `rule` lp1, `source`
arrival / tool, `evidence`), or by a person who may decide (the variant's page: "Is this a landing page?"). Only an unlinked
product (`unmapped`, `suggested`; `ignored` when asked): a linked one is refused (409 `linked`: unlinking changes a stock link,
a person does it on its page). The system settles whichever suggestion is open under the lock (a suggestion of the check on arrival too: a mark confirms no
match); a person names it (I7). The system leaves a product a person held back, and a spot check's match, to a person (409
`one_at_a_time`; measured on staging: 287 of Electrofag's 1,103 landing rows carry such an arrival suggestion, and would otherwise
all have waited for a person). `not_landing` ("This is a real product"): a MATCHING LEAD only (403 `lead_required`), with a note (the page asks
for it); back to its list (suggested when a suggestion is open, else not matched). Every other decision on a landing page is refused
(409 `landing_page`): nothing is matched to it, made of it or rejected for it until a lead says it is real.

**LP3. Never back and forth.** The system only ever marks, never unmarks. It never marks again a product a person said is real (an
applied `not_landing`: 409 `said_real`), whatever the rule or the website's flag says later; a person may. A landing page the rule or
the flag no longer finds stays one (the tool lists it as `no_longer`). A later rule is a new version (`lp1` is recorded with each
mark), so its marks can be told from these; it does not undo them.

**LP4. On arrival.** After a listing push (`ListingIngestService::push()`), outside its transaction, the pushed products whose profile
was created or changed, or whose website state says something new, AND the other products of their pages are classified
(`LandingPages::onArrival()`): a landing page that arrived before its options is found when they arrive. Each mark is a decision of its
own; a failure is logged and never costs the push; the answer to the site is unchanged. The website's flag always marks; the rule only
while `mapping.landing_rule_on_arrival` is on (Settings › Matching products; on; provisional). The import of export files does not
classify: the tool does. A mark a push could not make (a failure is only logged) is made by the hourly cron line
`bin/landing_pages.php --recent-hours=48 --apply`: every store's website products first seen in the last two days and the other products
of their pages, as on arrival; older products are the owner's dry run and `--apply` (Codex review R5).

**LP5. Existing rows: `php bin/landing_pages.php --channel=<code> [--dry-run | --apply] [--include-ignored] [--list]`.** A dry run by
default (no write, no lock): what it would mark and why, what it leaves and why (linked, said_real, one_at_a_time, waiting,
ignored, no_longer), why the others are not landing pages. `--apply`: each mark a decision (actor `system:landing_pages`), one
`landing.run` audit row with the counts. Re-runnable: a second run finds nothing new. The owner runs it per store after the deploy.

**LP6. Out of every matching list, count and progress line.** They read `unmapped` / `suggested` (the match-strength lists and their
counts, Home's, New Variants' "still to match", the pickers, the bulk lists, the check on arrival); a mark also settles the
suggestion. Store Products gains the state "Landing pages" (its count, its filter, why each is one and who marked it when); New
Variants a kind of the same name; coverage (Matching progress, the Dashboard) and the "By store" figures leave landing pages out.

**LP7. An order for a landing page is a website bug, never a stock event.** Its line is an unlinked line as before (no bucket, never
refused, the same answer to the site), and `Reservations::flagLandingLines()` writes one `landing_order` row per order and landing
page in the order's own transaction (a hold, a payment, an opening order). A later call adds the reservation, the units and the
payment; a payment that comes after a person handled the row while it was unpaid opens it again (audit `landing_order.reopened`).
The R4 adoption is unchanged: if a lead later says the page is a real product and it is matched, its old units are adopted as any
unlinked units are.

When a product is MARKED, its orders still open (units held or allocated) go to the list too (Codex review R1): a unit sold while the
product was linked by mistake keeps the item it was sold under (I14) and a person sorts that order out. An ERPNext line (the relay) that
names a store's landing page waits in Lines to place (`landing_page`) even when ERPNext's item code names an item (Codex review R2).

**LP8. Approvals › From the stores › Website bugs** (`/ui/queues/landing`): each order with its store, number, the landing page and its
option number, the units, paid or not, "No stock moved for it"; marked handled (fixed by hand, refunded, nothing needed) with a note,
once. Who: `queues.oversell` (the people who sort orders out with the customer; looking: `queues.view`). The badge and a Home card
("Website bugs: orders for a landing page") count the open ones for them.

**LP9. The alert.** `bin/health_alert.php` (every 2 minutes; Settings › Alerts' web address and e-mail) has the problem
`landing_order:<store>` while one is open: "Website bug: an order on <store> for the landing page <title> (option <n>, order <ref>)",
with how many are open. One alert per store, sent again at most once per `alerts.repeat_minutes`, "back to normal" when all are handled.

**LP10.** An unmatched REAL product behaves exactly as before: in its lists, its order lines unlinked, adopted on its link.

**LP11. The rule, measured** (blind, against the shops' own flag; the design file). Page found by the product number: Vape and Go
4,111 called landing pages, 4,109 right, 2 binned parent rows the shop did not flag, 361 missed (titles edited); Electrofag 1,078 of
1,103, none wrong. By the web address alone (what a bare push gives): Vape and Go 1,343 of 4,470, 1 wrong (the same binned row);
Electrofag 874 of 1,103, none wrong. Not one product with a single option was called one (Vape and Go 3,386, Electrofag 205). Rejected:
"the same product title on the store" as the page (6 real single-option products would have been marked).

**LP12. Open, for the owner** (NEEDS-OWNER in the design file): connector 0.4.7 sending `website` (it is in the shops' trees; deployed
per box); the shop's own fix; whether landing pages staff ignored are moved (`--include-ignored`); linked landing pages (listed, a
person unlinks); refusing a landing page at checkout on a Live store (not done: recorded and alerted only); hourly reminders.

### The Codex review (on `560b0ef`; `runs/landing_codex_review.txt`): three HIGH, four MEDIUM, three LOW, all fixed test-first

The new tests failed first (`/root/cw_work/landing/landing_codex_red.log`, 10 failures) and pass now.
- **HIGH R1: a mark left the page's open orders off the list** (a landing page linked by mistake took an order; units keep their sale-time
  item). Now `Reservations::flagOpenOrdersOf()` lists every open order of the product when it is marked (`LandingOrderTest` …CodexR1).
- **HIGH R2: an ERPNext item code booked a line that names a landing page.** The relay's and the movements' resolve now park such a line
  in Lines to place, reason `landing_page` (…CodexR2). The "ERP item code wins" rule stands for every other line.
- **HIGH R3: an address could pull in an option of ANOTHER product number** (a real single-option product marked). An option found by the
  address counts only when its own product number is not known or is the same (`LandingPagesTest` …CodexR3).
- **MEDIUM R4: a plan read before a change could still mark** (a website state does not move a map_version). `apply()` asks the plan's
  question again under the listing's lock (DecisionService's `$recheck`); a different answer is refused `landing_changed` (…CodexR4).
- **MEDIUM R5: a failed classification on arrival was never tried again.** The hourly `--recent-hours=48` run (LP4; …CodexR5).
- **MEDIUM R6: an answer given while the order was unpaid could close it once paid.** The form carries what the person saw (`paid`);
  a different one is refused `queue_changed` (…CodexR6).
- **MEDIUM R7: "This is a real product" carried no `seen`**, so a held-back landing page could not be put back. It does now.
- **LOW R8-R10:** the Website bugs title links to the variant's page only for people who may open it; the units line keeps its words;
  Find shows a landing page's chip.
- Settled while fixing (the staging rehearsal of the dry run, `landing/staging_plan.out`): the system's mark settles a suggestion of the
  check on arrival (it confirms no match); only a held-back product and a spot check's match wait for a person. Before it, 287 of
  Electrofag's 1,103 landing rows would have waited.

## Create new warehouse products for a ticked family (branch `bulk-new-items`, on `landing-pages`, 22 Oct 2026; NF1-NF8)

The owner (22 Oct 2026): Vape Big's best sellers include whole families that Vape and Go never sold, so no warehouse product exists to
match them to (measured on production, top 600 Vape Big sellers by 30-day units: Hayati Pro Max 4000 49 rows / 1,977 units, Elux ENE
Legend 4000 14 / 1,801, Elux FireRose EX4500 3 / 199, Crystal Pro Max 4000 14 / 163: about 32% of its sales). Each one was opened and
"Create a new product" pressed one by one. The owner chose: "tick a whole family, then create new products for these in one go; better
for future Vape Big-only products too". Code: `src/Mapping/BulkDecisions.php` (the list context `store_new`), `src/Ui/Controller/
StoreNewItemsController.php` (new), `src/Ui/Controller/{StoreProducts,Bulk}Controller.php`, `src/Ui/Kernel.php`, views
`store_new_preview` (new), `store_products`, `bulk_bar`, `bulk_result`, `src/Ui/Words.php` (STORE_NEW; BULK_SKIP and BY_ITEM_SKIP gain
six reasons; PAGE_INTRO, AUDIT_ACTION), `public/ui/assets/app.css`. No migration: `mapping_batch` already takes source `store` with
action `new_item`. `DecisionService` is not changed. Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/StoreNewItemsScreenTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/Mapping/StoreNewItemsTest.php` (new).

**NF1. Where: Store Products, its existing filter and bar.** The filter the brief asked for is there already: "Not matched"
(`state=not_matched`, `Queries::STATE_WHERE`) lists the rows that are unmatched or suggested with NO open suggestion and no decision
waiting, so never a landing page, an ignored, matched or on-hold one; with the forgiving search (SI, SX) "hayati pro max 4000" narrows it
to the family. The action is a new button of the existing bar, "Create new warehouse products for these", for a matching lead only, with
a line above the list on "Not matched" saying how to use it. The bar hosts it cleanly: the button carries `formaction` (CSP-safe, no
script; it works without app.js), so the same ticks (`pick_`, `ver_`, `prop_`) go to the preview, and Ignore… / Take off the ignored
list / Send back for matching… keep the list's own route. `POST /ui/review/bulk` never makes items from Store Products (`store` has no
`new_item`: 400 `bad_action`), so the preview cannot be skipped.

**NF2. What it takes and what it skips (`BulkDecisions::newChecks()`, one rule for the preview and the apply).** It takes a website
product of the store with NO open suggestion, or one whose suggestion says "new product" (band `New item` and `proposed_new_item`). It
does not ask for the computer's "new" as the seed of M61 does: the person looked at the family. It skips, first match recorded:
`unknown_listing`, `other_store`; `held`, `in_spot_check`, `on_arrival` (OneAtATime, as every bulk action); `changed` (the version the page
showed), `pending_second`, `suggestion_changed`; `landing_page`; `linked` (matched or on hold); `not_waiting` (ignored); `made_before` (an
item was made from it before); `match_instead` (its open suggestion names an item: "match it to that one instead"), `match_no_item`,
`not_new` (any other suggestion); `page_heading`, `not_published` (known not to be sold, SiteState as the seed reads it; a state the
warehouse does not know is no reason here); `no_name`; `barcode_on_item` (a barcode, in any stored form, that an item has, or that a
variant MATCHED to an item carries: PB1's rule; a barcode on a variant nobody matched is no item's); `name_elsewhere` (an item not joined
into another has the same name, or the same set of words in any order, case and accents apart: `nameWords()`, "Hayati Pro Max 4000
Apple" = "APPLE - hayati pro max 4000", "Apple Ice" is another); `name_waiting` (a new product waiting for a second OK has that name:
not an item yet, so the item table cannot say it); then among the rows left `name_twice` (two ticked rows with the same words) and
`barcode_twice` (a barcode in common): every row of such a group, so neither of two that would make one product is made; and
`barcode_waiting` (a new product waiting for a second OK has the barcode; added by the review below). Each reason has
words (`Words::BULK_SKIP`, `BY_ITEM_SKIP`). The item names are read once a request (`itemWords()`: the ids, names and joins of the item
table, about 15,000 rows on staging); just before each row's decision the name is read again, exactly (`namesTaken`, as M61) and as
words among the items made since (`wordsSince()`, by primary key), so another person's create in between is found too. Not a lock: two
creates of one name in the same instant can both make an item, as M61 says.

**NF3. Who: a matching lead.** Today a new product one at a time is `mapping.decide` (Matcher, Matching lead), and the screens' bulk
actions are `mapping.decide` too (M49, also the seed's "Create as new"). The stricter is chosen: M7's rule for a bulk mint that no
computer check vouches for (`mintAndLink`, the seed) is a matching lead's, and so is this (both routes `Route::LEAD`, i.e.
`mapping.approve`, and `BulkDecisions::checked()` refuses anyone else, 403 `lead_required`, before anything is read for a row). No new
permission. A matcher still creates one at a time on the variant's page, unchanged; a viewer is refused (403) everywhere.

**NF4. Preview first, then the apply; one batch however often it is sent.** `POST /ui/review/store/new-items` (`preview()`, writes
nothing: no batch, no lock, no audit row) shows, for each ticked row, "Will create", "Will wait for a second OK" (with the reasons) or
"Will skip" (with why), and the new product exactly as the single "Create a new product" makes it with nothing typed over
(`DecisionService::cardFrom` of its profile and features: name, brand, strength, nicotine type, range, kind, flavour, size, puffs, pack
size), and 1 sale = 1. At most `mapping.bulk_max_rows` rows (100 by default; 422 whole, as every bulk action). Its form carries each
row again (`row_<listing>` = suggestion . version . shown-as-done . the fingerprint of its details, `cardHash()`) and a form key
(`FormOnce::newKey()`). The apply (`POST /ui/review/store/new-items/apply`) checks everything again: a row the preview skipped is never
made (it keeps the reason it has now, or is `changed`), and one whose details are not the ones shown (`card_changed`: a matching run
rewrote its features, which does not move its version) neither; each row is ONE `DecisionService::decide` `new_item` with the
suggestion and version shown, units 1 and the card as shown, under its listing's lock, in its own transaction with its batch row, in
listing id order, with `bulk_batch_id = screen:<batch>` (M47, M52; the decision and its audit row name the batch); the hold, spot check
and check on arrival are read again under the lock (M51). The batch row is opened through `Idempotency` under `bulk:<staff>:<form key>`:
the same form again (double click, Back and send) lands on the same batch page and does nothing; the same key with other rows is refused
(422), a malformed key 400. Only the batch's own row is in the idempotent unit, so a request that stopped half-way is shown as such
(M47's "fewer rows than ticked") and is not finished by a re-send.

**NF5. The two-person rule and the single action are DecisionService's, unchanged.** Every rule of a single new product applies to each
row; while the owner's switch `approvals.mapping_bulk_second_ok` is on each row waits for a second matching lead ("Confirmed from a
ticked list"), nothing is made until one says yes, and the decider cannot approve their own. `predict()` now says that of a new product
too (it said it of a confirm only). A row DecisionService refuses is recorded as skipped with its code (M51).

**NF6. The result page.** The batch page (M47): "Created N new warehouse products, K wait for a second OK, M skipped.", a list of the new
products with links to their pages, the skipped ones each with why and a link, every row with its decision now; the CW number of a
matched row links to its item on every batch page. "Back to Store Products".

**NF7. Words and look.** `Words::STORE_NEW` (the button, the line above the list, the preview, its button "Yes, create these N new
warehouse products", the refusals, the result page), `PAGE_INTRO['store_new_preview']`, `AUDIT_ACTION['mapping.bulk_start']` (the
idempotency record's audit row). The preview is a `table.stack` (one card a row on a phone), the new product's details a small `dl`, the
button at the bottom of the screen (`actions sticky`).

**NF8. Not done, and open.** No typing over a detail in bulk (open the product and create it there; the preview says so). The name a new
item gets is the variant's own title (`cardFrom`, M9): on a store that titles its options with the flavour only, the preview shows that

### The Codex review (on `dc7e49c`; `runs/bulknew_codex_review.txt`): three HIGH, four MEDIUM, all fixed test-first

The new tests failed first (`runs/bulknew_codex_red.log`) and pass now (`StoreNewItemsTest`, `tests/Unit/NameWordsTest.php`).
- **HIGH 1: the words of a name were never read again before a row** (the row's transaction did not take them). `one()` now asks
  `newMeanwhile()` inside each row's transaction, after the exact name: an item made since with the same words (`wordsSince()`).
- **HIGH 2: a barcode put on an item, or a same-named product sent to Second approval, while the batch ran was not seen.**
  `newMeanwhile()` reads them again too (`barcode_on_item`, `name_waiting`, `barcode_waiting`). `…WhatChangesWhileTheBatchRunsIsReadAgain…`
  makes the other person's change with a trigger inside the first row's transaction.
- **HIGH 3: a new product waiting for a second OK did not keep its barcode.** A new reason `barcode_waiting` ("A new product with the same
  barcode already waits for a second OK"), in the checks of the request and before each row. Approval itself is unchanged (DecisionService
  is not touched): the second lead sees each one.
- **MEDIUM 4: a barcode typed with spaces on a matched variant was missed** (the intake keeps a barcode as sent; `Gtin::forms` finds leading
  zeros only). `oddBarcodeItems()` reads, once a request, the matched variants' barcodes that hold a sign other than a digit and compares
  them by their digits.
- **MEDIUM 5: the mark of `wordsSince()` was read after the names**, so an item made in between was in neither. The mark is read first, and
  the 50 ids below it are read again (`SKU_OVERLAP`: an id given out before the mark and committed after the names).
- **MEDIUM 6: accents were folded by intl only**, which the web server's PHP lacks. `foldAccents()` (a fixed table of the Latin letters) runs
  first in every PHP; intl, where there, folds the rest.
- **MEDIUM 7: a page heading known from the stored website state only was not skipped.** `newRowSkip()` works it out as the seed does
  (`SiteState::heading()` with the published variants of its product).

needs a migration (rule 20 allows it to become one if he wants to change it). Each row is `id="m-<sku id>"` (the way back from Apply);
on a phone each row is a card (`table.stack`) and each cell is named by its store.

**SM3. A store's cell: what is matched there.** Every website product matched to the row's product on that store (`productCells`'
`matched`, the best seller first), then every match of it that waits for a second OK (`waiting`), each with its name on the store
(product title and option title), "ID <the store's option number>" and, where it applies, "Waiting for a second OK", "1 sale = N
products" and "On hold". The name opens the website product's own page, where a match is changed or undone (U69: a matching lead's);
this page has no change and no unmatch.

**SM4. The one box: a plain dropdown.** For someone who may decide (`mapping.decide`: Matcher, Matching lead) a cell has ONE box and
Apply: shown at once in an empty cell, behind "+" (a `<details>`, no script) in a cell that already has a product, for a second page of
the same store (a duplicate). The box is an `<input list>` with its own `<datalist>`. app.js fills the list from `GET /ui/match/options
?sku=&channel=&q=` (`Route::DECIDE`, read only): a fragment marked `data-sm-fragment` (`FRAGMENTS`, the one fetch of app.js, parsed
inert), whose choices are that store's products still waiting for a match (unmatched or suggested, no decision waiting for a second
OK, never ignored, a landing page or another store's: `Queries::waitingListings`, the quick match's search by every word of the names
and what else it reads, or the exact option number; the product whose option number is exactly the text first (`listingByOption()`), then
best sellers first), at most `OPTIONS_MAX` = 20; for an empty box (on focus) the
computer's suggestions of this product on that store (`suggestedFor`). Each choice reads "<name> · ID <option>" and carries what Apply
sends (`data-listing-id`, `data-map-version`, `data-proposal-id`: the listing's open suggestion of ANY product, which the decision must
name, I7), and says "decided on its own page" (OneAtATime: held back, a spot check's match, found on arrival) or, for a Matcher, "a
matching lead decides it" (Conflict). Typing waits for 2 letters (one digit is an ID: asked at once) and 300 ms. A choice fills the form's
hidden fields; a typed ID that is
exactly one choice's ID is that choice; a choice stays as its list showed it (no search is started while the box names it, and one
still on its way is not drawn, so no newer version or suggestion takes its place; when the words change, no answer asked for before them
is drawn; focusing a box with no choice behind it looks for its words: the suggestions for an empty box, the words a refusal kept);
Apply with
nothing chosen says "Choose one from the list first." and sends nothing (checked in the
capture phase, before the "send once" of every form), except when the list could not be loaded: then the typed text goes to the server
as without the script. Without app.js the box is the store's ID (SM5).

**SM5. Apply: one more match, through the decide route's request and DecisionService.** `POST /ui/match/apply` (`Route::DECIDE`, CSRF):
`sku_id`, `channel`, `listing_id`, `expected_map_version`, `proposal_id`, `pick` (the box), and the list's `q` and `page`. An unknown store
or product is the 404 page; a product joined into another one meanwhile is `gone`. The website product is the one chosen; with no
`listing_id` (no script) nothing is decided: the store's product whose option number is exactly what was typed (`listingByOption()`, the
unique (channel_id, external_variant_id) index), when it still waits for a match, comes back chosen in the cell's box (`confirm`, with its
version and suggestion as that page shows them, and in the box's list so app.js keeps the choice) under "Is this the one? Press Apply to
match it.", and only that second Apply decides, against what that page showed (I7); else "Choose one from the list", with what was typed
kept. A chosen product must be the store's (`other_store`) and still wait for a match (`not_waiting`), and the version the form names
must be the one that waiting state was read with (`changed`): this page never changes or moves a match. The box must still name that
product (its words as its list shows them, or its ID): a box whose text was changed after the choice is taken as typed (a unique waiting
ID comes back to be confirmed; anything else is "Choose one from the list"), never as the product the hidden fields carry. The units are
what this product's own open suggestion gives (`ai_units_per_item`, as By Item's quick match), else 1. Then the request is the decide
route's `link`, built by ONE method, `ReviewController::decisionRequest()` (the checks `decide()` made, moved out unchanged and used by
both), with `seen` empty and `SimpleMatchController::addOnly()` as the decision's recheck (under the lock, after every other check and
before anything is written: still that store's and still `unmapped` or `suggested`, else 409 `not_waiting`): `DecisionService::decide`
checks everything again under the listing's lock (the person on the decision and its
audit row, map_version, the suggestion, Conflict for a matching lead, a spot check's owner (DG1), a product decided one at a time from its
own page (DG2: 409 `one_at_a_time`), the second OK of a store that already sells warehouse stock, a multiple, a pair marked not a match
before). Back to `/ui/match` with the search and the page, at `#m-<sku>`, with the matching pages' notice (`notice=decided_link` "Done:
"…" is matched to CW-…", or `pending_second` "Saved, not live yet: … needs a matching lead's second OK"; `ReviewController::notice()`,
whitelisted) and the row marked.

**SM6. Who.** No new permission: the page is `linking.view`, the choices and Apply `mapping.decide`, as By Item's picker and the decide
route (a viewer gets 403 on both). A Conflict is a matching lead's and a spot check's match its owner's, as everywhere (DecisionService).

**SM7. A refusal in words, in its cell.** The address names a refusal by its code only (`said`, one of `SimpleMatchController::SAID`; never
a text), with the row (`at`), the store (`ch`), the website product (`prev`) and what the box held (`t`, up to 300 characters, put back
in the open box after any refusal, with no choice behind it: rule 7; a choice's words kept so are found again by the ID in them,
`idOf()`). `saidOf()` turns DecisionService's code into one: map_version_conflict, proposal_changed, proposal_closed → `changed` ("someone
changed this product just now. Choose it again, then press Apply."); one_at_a_time → `own_page` ("this product is decided on its own
page" with "Open its page"); lead_required, spot_check_other, role_not_allowed → `not_allowed` ("you may not match this one. Its page says
who decides it." with the link); pending_second_exists, landing_page, no_change, not_waiting (addOnly) → `not_waiting`; sku_merged →
`gone`; anything else `other` with the link. Each starts with "Nothing was saved" (rule 7) and is drawn as a red line in the cell it was
about (never the green "done" toast), or above the list when that row is not on the page.

**SM8. Store Products' Previous and Next lost the page number (the owner hit it).** `$pageQuery = $base + ['page' => null]`, then
`$pageQuery + ['page' => N]`: PHP's `+` keeps the left side's key, so every link was the first page (Next on page 1 and on page 2 both
opened page 1). The links are now `$base + ['page' => N]` (`$base` holds no page). Every controller and view that adds `['page' => …]`
with `+` was read (Stock, the four reports, Mapping's lists, Packs, Families, Counts, New Variants, By Item, Duty, Hand-made, Documents,
Reorder, Low stock levels, All Products, the contexts): none other had a base that already held `page`, so only Store Products changed.
`StoreProductsPagerTest` (red on main): page 1's Next is page 2, page 2's Next page 3 and its Previous page 1, page 3's Previous page 2,
and the state, sort and search travel with the page.

**SM9. Left out, and open.** No change or unmatch of a match here (the product's page, leads). No CSV, no filters. A product decided one
at a time is refused here with the way to its page: on production that is every product the check on arrival found while
`mapping.arrival_bulk_confirm` is off (CM: about 3,300 Electrofag and 3,200 Vape Big rows), which Store Products' Check & match or the
product's own page answers; the dropdown says "decided on its own page" before Apply. A browser filters a `<datalist>` by the typed text
as one piece, so of the server's choices it may show only those whose name holds the words in the order typed (an ID or a run of the
name always works). The store order is a constant (SM2).

### The Codex review (on `8171a46`; `runs/simple_codex_review.txt`): one HIGH, two MEDIUM, one LOW, all fixed test-first

The new tests failed first (`runs/simple_codex_red1.log`) and pass now (`SimpleMatchScreenTest`, `UiUnitTest`).
- **HIGH 1: an ID typed without the script was decided against the product as it was when the request arrived** (its version and open
  suggestion read by Apply), so a product renamed on its website, or given a new suggestion, after the person typed its ID was matched
  and that suggestion settled unseen (I7). Now a typed ID is never decided at once: the product comes back chosen in the cell's box with
  "Is this the one? Press Apply to match it." and the version and suggestion that page shows; only that second Apply decides (SM5).
  `testATypedIdWithoutTheScriptWorksOnlyForOneWaitingProductOfThatStore` (the confirmation), `testATypedIdIsDecidedAgainstThePageThatShowedIt`
  (renamed, then a newer suggestion, after the confirmation: refused, nothing saved).
- **MEDIUM 2: "only adds a match" held only before the lock.** A hand-made form naming the version another person's match would leave
  behind, sent while that match was being written, passed the waiting check (the old version) and then relinked the product under the
  lock (red: the relink was applied). Now the form's version must be the one the waiting state was read with, and `addOnly()` asks
  again under the lock (DecisionService's recheck). `testAProductMatchedWhileApplyWaitsForItIsNotChanged` (a second session writes the
  match and commits a second later, a stored procedure, while Apply runs), `testUnderTheLockApplyOnlyAddsAMatchToAWaitingProductOfThatStore`.
- **MEDIUM 3: the line under the box could not wrap on a phone** (it shared `.sm-note`, one line, with a matched product's notes). It is
  `.sm-msg` now and wraps; only a matched product's short spans keep to one line
  (`UiUnitTest::testSimpleMatchingsBoxAsksAOneDigitIdAndItsLineWraps`).
- **LOW 4: a one-digit ID was never asked with the script**, and a short ID could be missing from the 20 choices behind products whose
  numbers hold it and sell more. One digit is asked at once, and the product whose ID is exactly the text comes first
  (`testTheProductWhoseIdWasTypedIsOfferedFirst`).

The review found the `decide()` refactor identical to the base (every validation combination it tried), the pager fix right and no other
pager with the bug, and no permission, CSRF, escaping, CSP or units issue.

### The second Codex review (on `466f506`; `runs/simple_codex_review2.txt`): one HIGH, one MEDIUM, both fixed test-first

The first round's fixes were checked again. Red first (`runs/simple_codex_red2.log`), green after.
- **HIGH: a confirmation edited without the script still matched the product it showed.** The hidden fields kept the confirmed product
  while the person typed another ID over it (or emptied the box), and Apply matched the first one. Now the box must name the product the
  hidden fields carry (its words as its list shows them, or its ID); otherwise what it holds is taken as typed: another unique waiting ID
  comes back to be confirmed, anything else is "Choose one from the list". `testAChoiceWhoseTextWasChangedIsNotApplied`; the refusal tests
  send the product's ID in the box, as app.js does.
- **MEDIUM: a search on its way could erase a choice just made** (app.js): the late answer replaced the list and cleared the hidden fields,
  so Apply refused a choice the box still showed. A choice now makes any search on its way not drawn (`turn++`). Pinned by a string
  in `UiUnitTest::testSimpleMatchingsBoxAsksAOneDigitIdAndItsLineWraps`, and checked in headless Chrome against the rendered page with
  the fetch of "50" held until after the choice: red on `466f506` ("CHOICE LOST": the hidden fields empty, Apply refused), green after
  ("CHOICE KEPT"). The repo has no browser tests; the harness stayed outside it.

### The third Codex review (on `e10d86b`; `runs/simple_codex_review3.txt`): one HIGH, fixed test-first

The second round's fixes were found right. **HIGH (app.js): an ID typed whole that is one of the list's products could take a newer
version or suggestion.** Typing "5001" chose that product as the list showed it, but the box's text was not the choice's words, so a
search for "5001" was still started; its answer, drawn after the product changed, chose the product again with its new version and
suggestion, and Apply would have matched it against what the person never saw (I7). Now any choice, an ID too, stops the searching
while the box names it, and a search on its way is not drawn. Red first (`UiUnitTest::testSimpleMatchingsBoxAsksAOneDigitIdAndItsLineWraps`,
`runs/simple_codex_red3.log`; the same harness in headless Chrome with the answer to "5001" carrying version 3 and a suggestion: "CHOICE
SUBSTITUTED" on `e10d86b`, "CHOICE KEPT AS SHOWN" after; the second round's race "CHOICE LOST" on `466f506`, kept since).

### The fourth Codex review (on `3dc44c2`; `runs/simple_codex_review4.txt`): one HIGH, fixed test-first

The third round's fix was found right, and the server side (the confirmation, the add-only check under the lock) correct. **HIGH
(app.js): an answer asked for before the words changed could still choose.** Focus an empty box (its suggestions are asked for), type
"5001" before they arrive: the suggestions chose the product with the version they gave, and the search for "5001", already waiting its

Chrome with the suggestions held until "5001" was typed: the hidden fields held "0/" then "3/77", CHOICE SUBSTITUTED on `3dc44c2`; one
choice after), and the three earlier browser cases still pass.

The browser checks (not in the repo; `runs/simple_js_harness/`): the page as the kernel renders it, served with app.js and a stub of the
choices route, driven by a script in headless Chrome: the box, the list, the choice, Apply refused with nothing chosen and its button not

### The fifth Codex review (on `c2edb27`; `runs/simple_codex_review5.txt`): no HIGH or MEDIUM, one LOW, fixed test-first

The four earlier rounds' fixes held, the box's input, timer and answer races included. **LOW: a refusal emptied the box** (only "Choose one
from the list" kept what was typed), against rule 7. Now every refusal puts back what the box held (`t`, up to 300 characters), with no
choice behind it; such words, a choice's ("<name> · ID 5001"), are found again by the ID in them (`SimpleMatchController::idOf()`, the words
around the ID taken from `Words::SIMPLE_MATCH['option']`), and focusing a box with no choice behind it looks for its words (an empty box:

The fifth round's fix held (the kept words, `idOf()`, the focus search), with every interleaving of input, focus, the timer and the answers

### SM10. A choice starts with what tells it apart (branch `simple-match-labels`, 26 Oct 2026)

The owner, on production the day Simple matching went live: two choices of a Hayati Pro Max nic salt looked the same in the dropdown
("Hayati Pro Max Blueberry Cherry Cranberry Nic Salt 10ml Blueberry C…" twice). A browser cuts a long choice at its end, and the end was
what told them apart (10mg or 20mg, and the ID). A choice now reads **"ID <option> · <strength> · <its own name> · <the product's name>"**
(`SimpleMatchController::choiceName()`, `Words::SIMPLE_MATCH['option']` with positional placeholders):

- the store's ID first, then a held-back / spot-check / lead's mark when there is one ("ID 5001 · decided on its own page · …");
- the strength the matching reads (`DecisionService::cardFrom`), else the last "<n>mg" the store's option name (then its product name)
  says, left out when the name already starts with it ("10mg | Black Mamba");
- the option's own name without the product's name when it repeats it ("Red Edition · IVG 2400 4 in 1 …", not "IVG 2400 4 in 1 … IVG
  2400 4 in 1 … - Red Edition"), then the product's name once.

`idOf()` reads the ID from the start of a choice's words (a name with "ID" in it cannot hide it). The matched cells are unchanged (their
lines wrap). `testAChoiceStartsWithItsIdAndStrengthAndNamesTheProductOnce` (red first: `runs/smlabel_sm.log`); the tests that name a
choice's words follow the new order.

The Codex review of c330f42 (two LOW, fixed test-first; the old code gave "Café Salt - Blue" and a broken "�5 Edition"): the product's
name is taken out of the option's name whatever its case, accents included ("CAFÉ SALT" in "Café Salt - Blue" gives "Blue · CAFÉ
SALT"; `str_ireplace()` missed it although `mb_stripos()` found it), and what stands between the two is trimmed by whole characters
(a byte mask with "·" in it cut the first byte of a "£": "Brand Kit - £5 Edition" now gives "£5 Edition · Brand Kit"). Both in
`testAChoiceStartsWithItsIdAndStrengthAndNamesTheProductOnce`.

### SM11. The full name on two lines, and each product's status on its store (branch `simple-match-labels`, 26 Oct 2026)

The owner, on the live page the day after SM10: "I want to still see the full name ... maybe take the dropdown a little to the left,
or use two lines ... and I need also the status of the variant shown there from each shop, the same way you show the ID". A browser's
`<datalist>` popup is one line as wide as the box and cannot be styled, so it cut long names whatever their order.

- **The box's own list.** A cell's box is a plain text box with a list `app.js` draws itself, at the page's top level (no table, card
  or scrolling box cuts it): under the box (above it when there is more room there), 36rem wide where the screen allows and never
  narrower than the box, opening to the LEFT near the screen's right edge, the full width but the gutter on a phone, as tall as the
  room it has with its own scroll. Down and Up move in it, Enter chooses and sends nothing while it is open, Escape, a press elsewhere
  or leaving the box shut it, a click or a tap chooses. A choice still puts SM10's words in the box (what Apply compares, `idOf()`)
  and fills the same hidden fields; a stale answer is still never drawn over a newer one. Without the script the box is a plain text
  box and a typed ID is confirmed by the server, as before (SM4).
- **Two lines per choice:** its FULL name on the store (never cut; the same words as a matched cell), then "ID <option> · <its status
  on the store> · <strength>" and the held-back / spot-check / lead's mark when there is one. Built as text from the fragment's
  `data-label` and its two lines (`.sm-opt-name`, `.sm-opt-meta`) as text: nothing of the fragment's markup is kept.
- **The status** is the website state CW stores (`SiteState::read`, M66): the stored state, else what a matching run recorded
  (`features.variant_status`), else what the computer's check recorded in the open suggestion; in the store's own word (Published, Bin,
  Draft…); "<status> · product <status>" when the product itself is not published; `Words::SIMPLE_MATCH['status_unknown']` ("status
  not known") when nothing is known or the stored state is older than `mapping.arrival_state_max_days`. The matched cells say it too,
  after the ID ("ID 5001 · Published"). `Queries::SITE_STATUS_COLUMNS` is the one place the columns are read, by primary key with the
  rows the page reads anyway (no extra statement).

Tests: `testEachChoiceHasTheFullNameThenItsIdAndItsStatusOnTheStore`, `testAMatchedCellSaysEachProductsStatusOnItsStoreAfterItsId`,
`UiUnitTest::testSimpleMatchingsListIsThePagesOwnOnTwoLinesAndOpensToTheLeft` (red first: `runs/smlabel_sm11_red.log`, 16 failures);
the browser checks (two lines, the full name, the list to the left near the right edge, a phone, the keys, a tap) in a real Chrome on
staging, screenshots in `runs/smlabel_shots/`.

## PO on one page (branch `po-one-page`, 26 Oct 2026; PX1-PX10)

The owner, 26 Oct 2026: "this purchase order all this related all operation i need single view like in purchase order module have supplier
choose option add new button in this dropdown. dont need multiple step". The plan he approved: "New purchase order" opens ONE page at once;
the supplier is one dropdown you can type in whose last line is "+ Add new supplier" (a small form there: name, e-mail, phone); the product is
one search/scan box whose last line is "+ Add new item"; the lines, the delivery charge, the totals, Save or Confirm on the same page; sending
the PDF, goods in and invoices stay as they are. Later the same day (relayed by the build's coordinator): "ui follow monday.com design and user
experience, dont make over complicated" (PX10). Built from main `2f8873a` (SM11 merged) in `/root/cw-poone`. No migration, no new permission,
no service rule changed. Code: `src/Ui/Controller/PurchaseOrdersController.php` (newPage, create, products, lines, apply, oneData),
`src/Ui/Controller/PoAddNew.php` (was `PoSelectOrAddController`, now without routes), `src/PurchaseOrders/PurchaseOrders.php` (`newSupplier`,
`setNewSupplier`'s header and lines), views `purchase_order_edit` (the one page), `po_products` (new), `po_supplier_needs`, `purchase_orders`,
`supplier`; `src/Ui/{Kernel,Sections,Words}.php`, `public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`. Removed: the view `purchase_order_new_item`, the routes
`POST /ui/purchasing/orders/new-supplier`, `POST /ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/new-supplier`, `GET|POST /ui/purchasing/orders/{id}/new-item`, the
list's side panel ("Start a new order", "Supplier not in the list?"), the supplier list's search box (`data-filter-select`).

**PX1. One page at once.** `GET /ui/purchasing/orders/new` (`doc.PO.post`) is the page: the list's "New purchase order" button (`Sections`),
its "+ New purchase order" row and the supplier card's link (`?supplier=`) lead to it; the list keeps its table. A draft opens as the same page
(`purchase_order_edit`, `PurchaseOrdersController::oneData()` for both), with its products; others still get the read-only view (drafts belong
to their creator, unchanged).

**PX2. When the draft is made (the decision the brief asked for).** Opening the page writes nothing. The page's one form posts to
`POST /ui/purchasing/orders`; with a supplier chosen and something to keep (Add with a product, "+ Add new item", Save, Confirm) the draft is
made AND the form applied to it in ONE transaction (`createDraft`, then `apply()`: `saveDraft` with the details and the charge, then the
action), under FormOnce (the page's `form_key`): the same form sent twice makes one draft. Anything that leaves nothing to keep rolls the whole
transaction back, so no draft is left: no supplier ("Choose the supplier first.", 422), Add with nothing to add (422), not found, a search with
several products (the choices are shown on the same page; their buttons post again), a refused item, a refused Confirm (an empty order: 422
`no_lines`). Save with only a supplier makes an empty draft: the person asked for it. Why this one: the simplest safe design: no "page draft"
state, no clean-up job, no draft made by a click on a supplier; an empty page left alone leaves nothing behind.

**PX3. "+ Add new supplier".** Before the order exists it makes the supplier alone (`PurchaseOrders::newSupplier`: `doc.PO.post`, then
`Suppliers::create` as the supplier screens make one: a DRAFT supplier, `suppliers.manage`, its checks and `supplier.create`; FormOnce) and the
page comes back with it chosen (`/new?supplier=ID`, `notice=supplier_added`, what was typed carried: `CARRIED`); no order is made by it. On a
draft without products it is `setNewSupplier` (the draft locked first, then the supplier; now also with the details and the delivery charge
typed with it; an item line is refused, `supplier_has_lines`), under FormOnce and the draft's version. With products the supplier is fixed (no
box). Confirm stays refused in plain words while the supplier is not approved (`PurchaseOrderHandler::validate`, 422 `supplier_not_active`);
the page says it in one line with a link to the supplier (`supplierNeeds()`, `PO_ONE not_approved / waiting`; the steps of PO3 are gone).

**PX4. The products: a board, its last row the scan box; "+ Add new item".** The lines are a board (`table.stack.list.board`): packs, the price
(and items per pack for a product not set up with the supplier) edited in place; each row has a remove (×, `remove_line`: a Save without that
row, notice `removed`); the last row is "+ Add product": the scan box, its packs and Add. Enter anywhere is Add (a first, visually hidden
button), so a scan with Enter adds as before. "+ Add new item" is the item_* fields of the same form (`action=new_item`): `apply()` saves the
table and then `addNewItem` (Pack B's `HandMade::create`: a barcode on another item 409, the same name 409 with the items there and the "it is a
different item" box; the supplier item when a code, a pack or a price is given; the line), under FormOnce and the version. A refusal is said in
that form, open, with what was typed (the table's edits too: nothing was saved), the item that has the barcode or the items of the same name
each with a button that adds it (`add_sku`, a button of the same form). A draft's "+ Add new supplier" / "+ Add new item" carry the page's
`form_key` (FormOnce) besides the version; Add, Save and Confirm carry the version only, as before.

**PX5. Who sees "+ Add new".** `suppliers.manage` for the supplier, `items.create` for the item, from the permission map in force. The others
see one short line instead, as the dropdown's last line (not a choice) and without the script under the box: `Words::askToAdd()`, "Ask a buyer to
add it." (the first job that holds it, in the code's order: "Ask a matching lead to add it." for an item). The action sent anyway is refused
403 before anything is read (`denied()`, `Kernel::refusal`), and the services check again. PO5's open item stands: a Buyer has no
`items.create`, so a Buyer is told to ask; give Buyers items.create on the Roles and permissions page if they should add items.

**PX6. One dropdown for the site.** SM11's list is now one engine in app.js, `combo(input, list, cfg)`: the list at the page's top level, its
placement, Down/Up/Enter/Escape, a tap, one list open at a time, following its box. Simple matching's cells, the order's supplier box and its
product box all use it (no second dropdown). The supplier: the plain select becomes a box whose list is its options (the name; a supplier not
usable yet says so on the second line), the ones holding every typed word, then the last line; a choice sets the select; Enter there never
sends the order. The product: typing (2 letters, 300 ms) asks `GET /ui/purchasing/orders/products` (PX8; one more marker in `FRAGMENTS`, the one
