## The matching lists leave out what does not matter (branch `hide-unsold`, 26 Oct 2026; HU1-HU9)

The owner approved on 26 Oct 2026 ("Yes, build it"): hide the website products with no sales in the last year from the matching lists, so
staff only see what matters (about 12,900 rows on production by the earlier count of "not matched, nothing sold in a year"); and never offer
a warehouse product that is not sold any more, or joined into another one, as one to match to (he also approved marking the 50 duplicate
"Crystal Pro Max 4000" items not sold any more on their cards after this ships). Built from main `2febd84` in `/root/cw-hideold`, rebased on
`e5da244` (PX11). Migration `0051_hide_unsold.sql` (two indexes and a column of `channel` in place, each store's first load, one setting);
`bin/import_listings.php` records a new store's first load (HU9); no new permission; `DecisionService` not changed; nothing in the data is deleted
or changed (the lists read one more condition). Code: `src/Ui/Queries.php` (its HU block: `UNSOLD_SETTING`, `UNSOLD_HIDDEN_SQL`,
`STOPPED_SQL`, `unsoldBefore()`, `unsoldShown()`, `exactIds()`, `unsoldHidden()`, `unsoldOfState()`; and the lists that use them),
`src/Ui/Controller/{StoreProductsController,SimpleMatchController,ReviewController}.php`, views `store_products`, `simple_match`, `listing`,
`src/Settings.php` (one rule), `src/Ui/Words.php` (marked HU blocks). Tests: `tests/Integration/UiKernel/HideUnsoldScreenTest.php`,
`tests/Integration/Migration0051Test.php`, `ImportToolsTest::testTheFirstImportOfANewStoreRecordsItsFirstLoad`,
`WordsTest::testTheProductsTheMatchingListsLeaveOutAreSaidInPlainWords` (red first: `runs/hideold_red1.log`, 12 failing, and for HU9 and the
Codex finding `runs/hideold_b_red.log`; green: `runs/hideold_green2.log`, `runs/hideold_b_green2.log`).

**HU1. Which website products are hidden, and the one setting.** A website product (a `channel_listing` row) that is not matched yet
(`unmapped` or `suggested`, with no decision waiting for a second OK), sold nothing in the last year (`listing_profile.units_365d` is 0 or
NULL, or it has no profile), and is OLD: first seen by the warehouse system more than 365 days ago, or at or before the end of its store's
first load (HU9, the owner's answer "b"). "First seen" is `channel_listing.created_at`:
when CW made the row (the store's push, or the load of its list), never changed after; it is the earliest date CW keeps of a product that
never sold (the profile's own date is the same moment or later; the stores' "added" date is in their export, `prodt_added_date`, but never
stored; the imported sales history starts on 1 Oct 2025 for Vape and Go and on 8 May 2026 for Electrofag, and says nothing of a product that
never sold). A product added after its store's first load with no sales yet is therefore never hidden before it is a year old. (As first
approved, with the year alone, the rule hid nothing on production until about October 2027: every product there was first seen when its
store's list was loaded, in October 2026. HU9 answers that.) The setting
`mapping.hide_unsold_days` (Settings › Matching products; 365 = on, the default; 0 = off; empty = not set = off; a schema before 0051 = off):
an on/off switch in days, because the stores send the units of the last 30 days and of the last 365 days only, so "nothing sold in N days" can
be known for a year and for no other N (`Settings::RULES` allows 0 and 365; the words say the 365 days, which cannot change). Read once per
request with the stores' first loads (`Queries::unsoldBefore($store)`: the later of now minus the days and just after the store's first load,
UTC; one value per store, never worked out per row).

**HU2. Where.** The lists staff browse to match: Products › Store Products (its Not matched and Suggested states and All, with their counts);
Mapping › To review (every match-strength list, its count, the legend's counts and "N left", the next one after a decision; the same
`bandCounts()` gives the badge and tiles of Home and the Dashboard, so they count the same rows); New Variants (its counts, list and CSV; only
"Any time" can hold such a product, the page's periods being a year at most, so a shorter period runs the statement of before); Simple
matching's choices for a cell (the search, and an empty box's suggestions of the item). Never hidden: a matched, on-hold, ignored or landing
product, or one waiting for a second OK (Store Products' All and New Variants' All keep them). Left as they were: By Item and its picker (a
matching lead's page), the website product's own page, Find, Duplicates, the "By store" overview's coverage figures (`coverage()`,
`unproposed()`, `storeBands()`: figures of the whole catalogue), and the bulk actions (they act on the ticked rows of a page).

**HU3. Store Products' one quiet line.** At the end of the list, before the pager, one plain paragraph (`p.muted.unsold-line`): "N products
not sold in a year are hidden. Show them" (one: "1 product not sold in a year is hidden. Show it"), the owner's words; nothing when none is.
It counts the rows of the state and search shown (a search's own one pass says of each id it finds whether it is hidden: no second pass).
"Show them" is the same list with `unsold=1`: every product, the raw counts, and the line "Products not sold in a year are shown. Hide them";
the states, the sort, the search and the pager keep `unsold=1`. A bulk action's way back and the Check & match fold's way back (StoreContext)
do not carry it: they come back with them hidden, the quiet default. No filter chip, no help paragraph (the owner: pages simple, in the
monday.com style). With the setting off there is no line at all.

**HU4. A hidden product is found by its exact store ID or barcode.** On every list of HU2, a search whose text is the product's option number
as typed (the unique (store, option number) index) or one of its barcodes (the index of 0005, every form a number may be stored in:
`Gtin::forms`) lists it (`Queries::exactIds()`, an exception in `unsoldShown()`); the words of its name do not bring it back (else every word
search would show them again). Simple matching already offered the product whose ID is typed first (`listingByOption`, SM4); a barcode now
finds a hidden one there too.

**HU5. A warehouse product not sold any more, or joined into another, is not offered to match to.** "Not sold any more" is its product card's
flag (`item_card.discontinued` = 1, the card's "Not sold any more: never suggest it on Reorder"); "joined" is `sku.merged_into_sku_id`.
- Simple matching's list leaves out both (joined ones were left out already), and counts what it lists (`productTotal(true)`: the products
  not joined, minus `STOPPED_SQL`). A CW number written as one ("CW-000123", "cw 123", "#123"; not a bare number, a barcode or a word) shows
  that product whatever it is, read only: under its name "Not sold any more (product card): it is not matched here." or "Joined into
  CW-…: match that one instead.", no box, "+" or Apply in any cell; what is matched to it is still listed. Its choices (a hand-made request)
  are none, with that line; Apply refuses `stopped` ("Nothing was saved: …", said above the list) before anything is decided. What Simple
  matching did for a joined product before is unchanged (options 404 `item_joined`, Apply `gone`, DecisionService `sku_merged`). The
  check is the page's, not a rule under the lock: a card marked while Apply runs is no stock rule, and the product's own page (a matching
  lead's) can still match one on purpose.
- The website product's page, "Pick a different product" (`searchSkus(…, matching: true)`): the same rule; its exact CW number lists it with no
  "Use" and "Not sold any more (product card)" or "Joined into CW-…". A `pick` that names one (an old link) is said
  ("That warehouse product is not sold any more …") and not compared, as a joined one always was; the evidence's "Use" links (candidates,
  the AI's pick, the closest) leave it out. Not changed: a suggestion the computer made of such an item is still shown on its page.
- The 50 "Crystal Pro Max 4000" items leave Simple matching and the picker the moment their cards say "Not sold any more" (nothing is cached).

**HU6. The counts stay cheap.** Store Products' and New Variants' hidden counts are ONE statement (`UNSOLD_HIDDEN_SQL`: one range of the new
index, its units from the narrow index of 0020, its waiting decision and open suggestion from their unique indexes), taken off the store's
three narrow counts (`storeStateCounts`) by kind (`unsoldOfState()`; New Variants splits New / Suggested / Not checked by its `n_new` and
`n_open`). To review's counts add one condition to the statements they already run. Simple matching's total is two index counts.

**HU7. How the condition is read (EXPLAIN on the test machine, `runs/hideold_explain.txt`: two stores of 400 website products, 40 items).**
The condition that keeps a row (`unsoldShown()`) asks the cheap things first: the status (lists of every state), then `created_at >=` the date,
and only then, for an old row, a sold unit (a dependent subquery on `ix_listing_profile_units`, "Using index": never the profile's wide row).
With HU9 every product still to match on production is old (it was there at the first load), so each one's units are asked once, of
that narrow index (about a megabyte for the stores' 90,000), as the list's own sort already reads it. Plans: the hidden count `cl range
ix_channel_listing_unsold Using index`, `lu ref ix_listing_profile_units Using index`, the decision and suggestions `eq_ref` by their unique
keys (NO_SEMIJOIN on the decision: else MySQL read every decision's entry of that index first); Store Products' lists `cl ref/range
ix_channel_listing_unsold Using index` (hinted while the condition applies: the index holds the store, the status, the date and the id; not for
a search, which reads its ids by the primary key), `lp ref ix_listing_profile_units Using index`; To review's list and counts `p ref
ix_match_proposal_open_band`, `cl eq_ref PRIMARY` as before, plus the dependent `lu`; New Variants' "any time" `cl ref ix_channel_listing_seen
Backward index scan` as before; Simple matching's choices `cl ref` as before plus `lu`; `STOPPED_SQL` `c ref ix_item_card_discontinued Using
index`; Simple matching's list `s ref ix_sku_merged_into`, the card by `ix_item_card_discontinued`.

**HU8. The two indexes of 0051, in place.** `channel_listing (channel_id, status, created_at)` (`ix_channel_listing_unsold`: a store's
products still to match first seen before a date, one range; 0001's (channel_id, status) is a part of it and stays, the code names it in
hints) and `item_card (discontinued)` (`ix_item_card_discontinued`: the handful not sold any more). Each `ALGORITHM = INPLACE, LOCK = NONE`
(no table copy: `Migration0051Test` holds the tables' InnoDB ids), the ALTERs first; not unique; the old code runs on the new schema; the code
names them in hints, ignored before the migration. And `channel.first_load_at` (HU9), added in place to a table of a handful of rows.

**HU9. Answered: a product already on its store at the store's first load counts as old (the owner's answer "b", "Hide them now", 26 Oct
2026).** The question: as first approved (the year alone) the rule hid nothing on production until about October 2027, because CW first saw
every product when the stores were loaded. Offered: (a) keep it; (b) treat a product that was already there when its store was first loaded as
old; (c) keep the shops' own "added" date. The owner chose (b): the about 12,900 not matched and unsold are hidden now; a product added after
the load is shown until it is a year old; a hidden one is still found by its exact ID or barcode and comes back on its first sale; a product
the shop added in the year before the load and never sold is hidden too (the price of "now").
- **Old** is: `created_at <= channel.first_load_at` OR `created_at < now - 365 days`. Per store that is ONE moment, the later of the year and
  just after the first load (`unsoldBefore($store)`, + 1 microsecond: a product first seen AT the load is one of it), read once per request
  with the setting; a list of one store compares `created_at >=` it (one `?`), a list of every store (To review with no store chosen, the
  band counts) a CASE of the stores' ids and their moments (a handful, written in the statement), else the year; never a join or a sum per row.
- **The first load, recorded once.** `channel.first_load_at` (0051), the end of the store's first list load. The most reliable source CW has is
  the stores' own rows: the import runs leave no record of a run (an audit row per batch, with no run, and nothing for a push), while the rows
  of a load are made one after another, batch by batch. So 0051 sets it to the end of the store's first run of website products made with no
  gap of more than 30 minutes between two (the batches of an import, or a connector's first full push), at most a day after the store's
  first product, by window functions in one UPDATE; a store with no product stays NULL (the year alone). `bin/import_listings.php` records a
  NEW store's at the end of its first run that makes products (`ListingIngestService::recordFirstLoad`: the store's last product then; only
  while NULL, never moved after; printed `first_load=`). A store first filled by its connector's pushes stays NULL (the year alone), the safe
  side. A load split over runs more than 30 minutes apart (0051), or over several tool runs (a new store), keeps the first run's end: the rest
  count as new until a year old, also the safe side; a migration can set another time.
- Pinned: `HideUnsoldScreenTest::testAProductAlreadyThereAtItsStoresFirstLoadCountsAsOld` (a product first seen AT the load hidden, after it
  shown, a store with no load recorded by the year, the lists of every store each with its own moment, the counts, exact ID and barcode, the year
  after an old load, the first sale), `Migration0051Test::testTheMigrationRecordsEachStoresFirstLoad` (a load of batches, a slow load, a store
  with none, a load capped at a day), `ImportToolsTest::testTheFirstImportOfANewStoreRecordsItsFirstLoad`.

Still open: (1) By Item's picker lists every product, as before (a lead's page); it can take the same rule with one argument. (2) The words
("not sold in a year", "Show them", "Hide them") are provisional, as every word (U70); change them in `Words` only.

### PI19. The item list is read by ERPNext's "Variant ID" (27 Oct 2026)

A read of the live ERPNext (27 Oct 2026) showed the Vape and Go variant number in the Item field `custom_variant_id` (label
"Variant ID"); `custom_product_id` ("Product ID") is empty on every item. The import read only a "Product ID" column, so an item list

The owner, 29 Oct 2026: "purchase order / purchase invoice / sales invoice — keep always user experience much good" and "and professional:
refer Zoho Inventory and make it professional". The brief (`runs/pione_brief.txt`): the purchase invoice on ONE page like the order's (PX1-PX11),
laid out as Zoho Inventory's "New Bill"; the same look for the order's and the invoice's list, new/edit page and saved document; Zoho as the
reference for layout, spacing and hierarchy only (CW's own colours, type and words; no Zoho name, logo or icon); sales invoices not built, but
the layout pieces shared for them. Built from main `e52154f` in `/root/cw-pione`. Code: `src/Ui/Controller/InvoiceOnePage.php` (new),
`InvoicesController` (routes, the saved document's data, the list's due date and balance), `PurchaseOrdersController` (the saved order's
data, the list's search), `ReceivingController` (one line: `?po=`), `src/Invoices/SupplierInvoices.php` (the due date, a line as a pack of the
supplier, `creditedOn`), `migrations/0052_invoice_due_date.sql`, views `invoice_edit` (new), `doc_totals`, `doc_party`, `doc_bar` (new,
shared), `invoices`, `supplier_invoice`, `purchase_orders`, `purchase_order`, `purchase_order_edit`; `src/Ui/{Sections,Words}.php`,
`public/ui/assets/app.{js,css}`. No new permission; every service rule of pack C and pack J unchanged.

**PV1. One page at once.** `GET /ui/purchasing/invoices/new` (`doc.SINV.post`) is the page: the list's "New supplier invoice" button (the
statement's create button, `Sections`; the list's fold "Book an invoice by hand" is gone for invoices) and a confirmed order's "Record its
invoice" lead to it (`?supplier=&from=po:<id>`). Opening it writes nothing. A credit note keeps its fold and its forms (pack C).

**PV2. When the draft is made.** The page's one form posts to `POST /ui/purchasing/invoices`; with a supplier and anything to keep (a line,
"From", a charge, "+ Add new item", "Save as draft", "Save and make final") the draft is made and everything applied in ONE transaction under
FormOnce (`InvoiceOnePage::create`): the same form sent twice makes one draft. Every refusal rolls it all back: no supplier (422
`need_supplier`), Add with nothing (422 `need_product`), "Fill the lines" with nothing chosen (422 `need_source`), a duplicate supplier number
(409, PC12's words), another supplier's delivery, an item search with several answers (the choices on the page) or none: nothing is left,
what was typed comes back. "Save as draft" with only a supplier makes an empty draft. "Save and make final" is the save, then the posting
(PV16): a refused posting keeps the saved draft, never a half-final invoice.

**PV3. The draft is the same page.** Its creator's draft opens as the one page (`InvoicesController::page` hands it to
`InvoiceOnePage::editPage`); its one form posts to the draft's `/lines` (version and line count first), saved in one transaction: the header
fields it sent, the lines as edited (each row's ×: `remove_line`, not read), "From", the action, the file; "make final" comes after that
transaction (PV16). A refusal of the save saves nothing. "+ Add new item" also runs through FormOnce (it makes an item). A form of the old
lines table (no action) saves its rows as before; Add with nothing on a draft saves the form (Enter in a field). Anyone else sees the saved document (PV12); their POST is refused by the service (403 `not_creator`).

**PV4. "From".** A plain select of the open deliveries (`SupplierInvoices::notInvoiced`) and the open orders (approved, sent, part received)
of every supplier while the supplier can still change, the new page, even when the address chose one (each option names its supplier,
`data-supplier`; the script keeps the chosen supplier's and follows a change of supplier, so the plain select works without it: the Codex
review of 6418b15, finding 5); a draft's, its supplier's only. "Fill the lines" (or any other action with one chosen) applies it. On the new page a
delivery is the existing quick way (`createFromReceipt`: its number, date, copy and lines), then what was typed wins; an order is
`createDraft` + `addOrder`. On a draft: `addReceipt` / `addOrder`. Another supplier's document is refused by those services (422, in words).
A received order is not offered: its deliveries are.

**PV5. The supplier.** The order page's dropdown (`select[data-po-supplier]`, the same `combo()`), every supplier (one switched off since
can still send an invoice, as before; one not approved yet or switched off says so on its second line), its payment terms on its option.
"+ Add new supplier" is the order page's small form (`PoAddNew`): `Suppliers::create` (a draft supplier, `suppliers.manage`), FormOnce, the
page back with it chosen and what was typed carried, the item chosen in the box as its item (`pick_sku` with the item's own words: a pack of
the supplier before is not the new one's; the order page's `carriedPick()`, the Codex review of 6418b15, finding 6); the others see "Ask a
buyer to add it." (403 if sent anyway). Once the draft exists its
supplier is fixed: no service changes an invoice's supplier (stop the draft and start again).

**PV6. The lines.** Item, Qty (packs, the pack under it), Price (a pack's), Amount, ×. **No VAT column** (a decision against the brief's
list): an invoice's VAT is one figure typed exactly as the paper states it, and CW never works VAT out (PC1, the column comment of
`vat_total`); a VAT per line would be a second VAT that can disagree with the paper's. "+ Add line" is the order page's item box (the same
engine, its fragment `po_products` from the invoice desk's own route `GET /ui/purchasing/invoices/products`, `doc.SINV.post`;
`app.js` `ALSO` lets that one route's answers through `fragment()`): a choice of one of this supplier's packs adds that pack
(`SupplierInvoices::addItem`'s new `$supplierItemId`; another supplier's pack: 422 `unknown_supplier_item`), else as the old Add did
(StockOps::resolve). "+ Add new item" is the order page's form: Pack B's item (`items.create`), this supplier's pack when a code, a pack or a
price is typed (as PX4), its line (the items per pack typed: `addItem`'s new `$unitsPerPack`). A charge (delivery, duty, service, other: the
kinds the rules allow) is a fold under the lines; a charge typed is kept with whatever is pressed (as the order page's delivery charge, PX10),
and never typed again after an Add that found several items. "Save and make final" with words left in the item box is refused (422
`scan_pending`, as the order's Confirm: what is made final is what the person sees); "Save as draft" leaves the box alone.

**PV7. The totals.** On the right: Sub total (the lines), "Total without VAT on the paper" and "VAT on the paper" (typed; the match's total
check needs the paper's figure, PC3), Total (the paper's total without VAT, else the lines, plus the VAT). A draft says in one line how it
would match now (pack C's preview), above the lines; its problems are listed above the form.

**PV8. The due date (0052).** `supplier_invoice.due_date` (DATE NULL, added in place). The invoice date plus the supplier's
`payment_terms_days` when CW has them: on the new page (drawn when both are known, and by the script while the box is empty or still holds
the date it filled), and by the service when a draft is made without one (`createDraft`: "Book its invoice", and the new page's first form
when no date was shown; the new page sends `due_shown`, what its box showed, so a date cleared there is kept cleared). A saved draft shows its
own: a due date the person cleared stays empty when drawn again and on the next save (the Codex review of 6418b15, finding 4). Editable;
never before the invoice date (422 `due_before_date`); a date that is not one is refused in words (`bad_date`, finding 8); none on a credit
note (400). It changes nothing in the match, the postings or the stock; the document and the list show it.

**PV9. Notes and the file.** The note is a text area. The file is part of the one form (multipart), with what it is (the supplier's paper by
default): attached in the save and committed with it, before "make final" (PV16), so "book as received" finds its copy and a refused posting
keeps the file with the draft. Only a commit that fails after the bytes are stored leaves a file without a row: `FileStore`'s stance for every
attachment (append-only storage; `verify()` counts orphans; harmless). A file refused (type, size) is said, nothing saved.

**PV10. The bar at the bottom.** It stays on the screen while the form is (`position: sticky`; on a phone it takes the tab bar's place):
"Leave without saving" (a link), "Save as draft", "Save and make final" (the one primary button). The brief's "Save" for posting is worded
"Save and make final": the order page's "Save" keeps a draft, and one word must mean one thing (writing rule 13). A draft's "Make it final
later" (pack J) is a fold above the bar whose controls name the form `pi-schedule` (forms do not nest); "How its goods come in" and "Stop
this draft" are folds after the form, as their own forms.

**PV11. The lists.** One clean table: Date, Number (theirs under it), Supplier, Status (the solid pill), Total (with VAT), and for invoices
Due date and Balance (the total less the final credit notes: `SupplierInvoices::creditedOn`, one grouped read; payments are not in CW), for
orders Expected. One search box (orders: now the supplier's name too), a status select, "+ New …" at the right; a row opens its paper (a
stretched link). The URL's other filters (supplier, match, stopped; sent back, with the cancellation records) ride as hidden fields, so a
search keeps them (the Codex review of 6418b15, finding 7). The order list's grouping by state with group totals and its "how it works" fold are gone; drafts stay hidden for goods in
and the desk (behaviour item 8); the URL's other filters still work. (Amended by PV18: the lists are boards grouped by status.)

**PV12. The saved document.** Its actions in one bar at the top (`.doc-actions`; a step that needs a reason or a choice is a fold that opens
under the bar), the supplier's block beside the facts (`doc_party`), the lines, the totals on the right (`doc_totals`), then the rest as
before. An invoice: accept the differences (`invoices.accept`), book its credit note, take it back, attach a file, cancel it. An order:
Confirm, Take back, Send, the PDF, "Receive the goods" (Goods In's new delivery with the order chosen: `?po=`, `doc.GRN.post`), "Record its
invoice" (PV1, `doc.SINV.post`), Copy, Correct, Close, Reopen, Cancel. The short help lines under the order's actions and the big buttons'
second lines are left out (the owner's "no help paragraphs"). (Amended by PV19: the next step in the accent, the rest under More.)

**PV13. The order's page in the same look, behaving as before.** The head fields in the shared grid, the board with its headings, the totals
on the right, the bar at the bottom (`doc_bar` inside the summary section, which is `display: contents`, so the bar sticks for the whole
form). Every PX pin holds (the summary's two buttons, "Cancel draft" in it, two folds, no help line, the board's last row).

**PV14. Shared for the sales invoice.** Plain CSS classes and three partials, listed in `docs/dev.md`: `.doc-grid`, `.doc-lines`,
`.doc-foot`, `.doc-totals`, `.doc-bar`, `.doc-list` + `a.row-link`, `.doc-actions` + `details.doc-act`, `.doc-view`, `.doc-meta`, the
status pill `.chip` (`$chip`/`$stateChip`); `doc_totals`, `doc_party`, `doc_bar`; words `Words::DOC`, `Words::DOC_LIST`.

**PV15. Not changed, and known limits.** Credit notes (their pages and forms), every service rule (doc.SINV.post, invoices.accept, the
duplicate number, VAT as stated, the 3-way match and its tolerances, FormOnce, versions, the creator's drafts, pack J). The totals are worked
out when the page is drawn (no sums in the browser). "From" lists at most `SupplierInvoices::LIST_LIMIT` deliveries and orders (every
supplier's while the supplier can still change, PV4). A pack chosen in the item box is that pack; typed words with Enter still find the
supplier's preferred pack (as before). An invoice with more lines than the form can carry shows them read-only (PV17): its existing lines are
then not changed or removed from the page.

### The Codex review of 6418b15 (`runs/pione_codex_review.txt`): six MEDIUM, two LOW, all real, each shown failing first

Red on 6418b15: `runs/pione_codex_red.log` (InvoiceOnePageScreensTest: findings 1-7) and `runs/pione_codex_red8.log` (finding 8, a 500); the
JavaScript in node: `runs/pione_js.log` (`runs/pione_js_harness/`, outside the repo: 6418b15's app.js fails 3 due-date checks, the new one
passes all 16). Green after: `runs/pione_codex_green.log`, `runs/pione_codex_green2.log`.

**PV16. "Save and make final" is the save, then the posting (finding 1).** Making it final inside the save's transaction put pack J's "book as
received" (its receipt's stock and feed locks) before the SINV number series, while a "count on arrival" posting holds the series and then
asks for the feed: a lock cycle between two postings. Now the save commits first (a new draft under FormOnce, with its file), then
`SupplierInvoices::submit` runs exactly as pack C and pack J post (its own transactions; the receipt before the invoice, PJ9), so no lock is
taken out of the order those postings keep. A refused posting leaves the draft saved and says so: "Saved as a draft, not made final: …" with
the problems (422); never a half-final invoice. The same form sent twice: one draft (FormOnce), and the second lands on the invoice already
final. The race itself is not re-run by a test here (it needs two posting workers holding the series and the feed); the order is the one
pack J's race tests prove. `testASupplierAndALineMakeOneDraftOnceAndARefusalMakesNone` (a refused posting keeps the draft and the edits),
`testMakeFinalSentTwiceIsOnceAndARefusalKeepsTheFile`.

**Finding 2 (an orphan file on a refused posting)** is gone with PV16: the file's rows commit with the save (PV9). Same test.

**PV17. A big invoice (finding 3).** The one form sends 2 fields a line plus `InvoiceOnePage::FIXED_FIELDS` (48, with room to spare); when
that reaches PHP's `max_input_vars` (read on the server, `UiRequest::maxInputVars()`) the lines are shown read-only with one line saying so,
and the form carries no line rows (no `line_count`: the lines are not saved again); the head, the totals, "+ Add line", a charge and the bar
work, so it is saved and made final from the page. `testABigInvoiceShowsItsLinesReadOnlyAndIsStillMadeFinal` (a draft of max_input_vars / 2
+ 10 lines: 400 form_truncated before).

**Finding 4 (a cleared due date came back), finding 8 (a date that is not one: 500), finding 5 ("From" after another supplier), finding 6 (the
item chosen lost through "+ Add new supplier"), finding 7 (a search dropped the other filters):** PV8, PV4, PV5, PV11 as amended above.
`testAClearedDueDateStaysClearedAndTheTermsFillANewOne`, `testADateThatIsNotARealDateIsRefusedInWords`,
`testFromADeliveryOrAnOrderFillsTheLinesAndAnotherSuppliersIsRefused`, `testTheItemChosenGoesThroughANewSupplier`,
`testASearchKeepsTheOtherFilters`; the due date's script: `UiUnitTest::testTheInvoicePageUsesTheOrdersDropdownsAndTheSharedLayout` and the
node harness (the old script filled a date the person had cleared again, and overwrote a saved date when the invoice date changed).

## The approved design: boards, saved documents and the new pages (branch `pi-one-page`, second commit, 29 Oct 2026; PV18-PV20)

The owner said "yes" to the Claude Design canvas on 29 Oct 2026 ("monday.com design style and color follow"; the canvas pages Main = the
order list, PO_New, PO_View, PI_List, PI_New, PI_View, PI_New_Phone). Its layout is copied into plain shared classes in `app.css` (the block
"pi-design"), with CW's own tokens (the `--st-*` status colours through the tone classes' `--t-fill`, the magenta accent) and no inline
style (CSP); every word is in `Words`. No rule, route, permission or posting changed; the PO page's PX1-PX11 behaviour and words are as they
were (only where things sit). The sales invoice pages (SI_*) are not built.

**PV18. A list is a board grouped by status.** Each group is a coloured heading with its count (it folds: app.js's `.grp-toggle`), over a
white card with the group's colour on a 6 px left edge; the status cell is filled with its colour, white words, centred (about 160 px); the
last row of the Draft group is "+ New ...". The toolbar has one search and one Show menu (no chips, no state select); the URL's other filters
(status, supplier, match, stopped, sent back) still work and ride with a search as hidden fields (PV11, finding 7).
- Orders (`PurchaseOrdersController::BOARD`, `boardGroups()`): Waiting for approval (purple), On the way = confirmed, sent and part received
  (blue; each status cell keeps its own colour), Draft (grey), Received or closed (green: delivered or closed within `po.board_recent_days`
  days, read on `purchase_order.updated_at`). Show: Open orders (the default), All orders (every order and the cancellation records: the old
  `show=all`), Closed and cancelled. Columns: Order (number and date), Status, Supplier, Expected, Received (a thin bar and "160 / 240"),
  Total (with VAT). The CSV keeps its own default (every order but the cancellation records); Show's "all" and "closed" narrow it the same way.
  Behaviour item 8 (goods in and the desk see no drafts unless they ask) holds.
- **The setting `po.board_recent_days`** (migration 0053; 14, 1-365, provisional, decided here): how long a delivered or closed order stays on
  the open board. The owner's rule (no hard-coded number): it is on the Settings page with a reason. The code reads it with a default of 14,
  so the code may run a moment before the migration.
- Supplier invoices (`InvoicesController::BOARD`, `boardGroups()`): Needs a look (amber: final, the 3-way match needs review), Draft (grey),
  Final (green); cancelled and reversed ones and their records only under Show (Open / All / Cancelled; the old `cancelled=1` still means
  All). No Overdue or Paid group and no money summary (payments are not in CW). Columns: Invoice (the supplier's number; under it the order or
  delivery it is for, `SupplierInvoices::refsOf`, one read for the page), Status, Supplier, Match (a soft tag: Matches / N differences /
  Accepted / Not checked yet, from the stored match), Due (red when passed and a balance is left: `td.late`), Total, Balance. Credit notes:
  the same board with Credit note / Status / Supplier / Reduces / Total.

**PV19. A saved order or invoice.** Its status is a solid block with 8 px corners beside the title (`.doc-head`); a second state (the order's
reviewer check, the invoice's match) is a soft tag beside it. One action bar on the right: the next step in the accent, the rest under
"More" (`details.doc-more`, a menu; a step that needs a reason or a choice still opens its fold). The choice is fixed in code and changes no
permission: an order's next step is Confirm, else Send (confirmed, not sent), Receive the goods, Record its invoice, Take back, Send again,
Copy (`PurchaseOrdersController::actions()`); an invoice's is Accept the differences (needs a look), else Take back, Book the credit note,
Attach a file (`InvoicesController::page()`). The partials `po_action` and `si_action` draw one action either way, with the forms, fields and
routes the pages had.
- The order's progress strip (`.doc-progress`): Ordered; Received ("0 of 3" and a bar); Invoiced (the final invoices' goods units on this
  order, net of their credit notes: one indexed read on `ix_sinv_line_po`; a bar); Expected and "N still to come". Not for a draft or a
  cancelled order.
- The invoice that needs a look starts with the differences panel (`.doc-diff`, amber left edge): "N lines differ from what was ordered and
  received", the total difference, and a 3-way table (Item, Ordered, Received, Invoiced, Order price, Invoice price, Difference) with the
  cells that differ tinted (`td.diff`). It shows the stored match (`InvoiceMatch`'s lines, the order's and delivery's figures): no new rule.
  The old match section below the paper is folded into it.
- Then the paper (`article.doc-view`): the supplier's block, the facts (dates, For the order / the delivery as links, Entered by), the
  Balance large on the right (`doc_party`'s `big`), the lines, the notes and files with the dashed attach box, the totals; the history last.

**PV20. The new pages.** "From" has its own full-width row with a soft "Fill the lines" button (`.btn.soft`); under the due date a hint
says where it came from ("From the supplier's terms: 30 days.", app.js keeps it with the supplier chosen; hidden without terms); the attach
box is a dashed drop area (`.doc-drop`; a plain file input, no drag script). On a phone the lines are stacked cards with Qty, Price and
Amount side by side, and the bottom bar's two buttons are equal.

Tests (red first: `runs/pione_design_red.log`, on the first commit): `InvoiceOnePageScreensTest::testThePurchaseOrderScreensShareTheLook`
(the board's groups, colours, columns, the status cell, received of ordered, "+ New" in Draft, Show and what it shows, the saved order's

drop area, the terms hint), `testASearchKeepsTheOtherFilters` (Show is the toolbar's own menu now), `Migration0053Test`,
